<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for "metaphysical separation." While the previous page established the theoretical framework—arguing that the purer "quintessence" can be drawn from the four elements—this page provides a practical, laboratory example using the transformation of grain into a "philosophical wine" and its subsequent salts.</meta>

-># CRAFTSMANSHIP<-

<meta>catchword: Concerning</meta>

...I judged it better to set aside, rather than repeating one and the same thing in different places. Now, however, because this separation cannot easily be performed from certain bodies without a "vehicle" <note>original: "vehiculo"; a medium or solvent used to carry or extract a substance</note>, we shall also demonstrate this way through examples. Through these, you may be able to learn better than by rules alone, especially since we have already made mention of **philosophical wine** <note>original: "vini philosophici"; a potent spirit or solvent used in alchemical extractions</note>.

Take grains of wheat, barley, or rye. These should first be soaked in pure water so that they swell; then, they are to be removed from the water and gathered together in a heap on the ground, so that after several nights and days they may grow warm and begin to sprout. Once this is observed, spread them out so they may dry. Or, if necessity urges, they may be spread out in a wide basket woven of wicker, placed over a furnace resembling an inverted chimney—that is, narrow at the bottom and wide at the top—and dried by the smoke stirred up below, until they appear half-toasted (though not scorched) and of a reddish color. Meanwhile, care must be taken that the basket does not catch fire, but is elevated far enough from the flame. This grain should then be ground in a mill—not too finely—or coarsely broken, not into flour, but into small fragments. 

Afterward, let it be placed in a wooden vessel, and let the hottest water, which has boiled for a long time, be poured over it; let the vessel then be very well covered. After it has cooled and settled, the liquor should be poured out through a hair-sieve or a sack, so that the fragments do not mix with it. Once you have separated this first water, pour on other boiling water as before, and strain it. Repeat this same process several times, until you see that all the substance from the grain has passed into the waters; you will easily perceive this by the taste of the liquor and the grain. Finally, take all the liquors and boil them in a cauldron for as long as it takes to reduce them to the thickness of yellow, skimmed honey. 

Then, you shall distill the liquid placed in a vessel, and from that **honey** and **philosophical wine** you shall separate the **soul** with its **spirit** <note>original: "animam cum suo spiritu"; the volatile, active components separated from the physical dregs</note>, and you shall sublimate it as many times as necessary until they are freed from all <term>phlegm<note>The watery, tasteless, and inert part of a distillate.</note></term>. Whatever residue of the body remains sinking at the bottom of the distillation vessel, you shall remove and dry in the shade, or by evaporating the moisture. At last, you shall reduce it by a most violent fire into very dry ashes. Over these ashes, you shall pour boiling water and let it boil for a very long time, so that you may obtain from it a very sharp <term>capitellum<note>A strong lye or alkaline solution extracted from ashes.</note></term> (as they say). This clear liquid floating on top you shall separate from the ashes by tilting the vessel; pour water similar to the first over the remaining ashes, boil it, and repeat what I have already said, until no sharpness remains in the final lye, which you may then discard. 

Pass this and all the preceding liquids through a filter-sleeve until you have a most clear liquor, and let this evaporate in glass vessels, so that you may have our <term>tartar<note>A crystalline salt residue, historically associated with the sediment in wine or the salts derived from plants.</term></note> and the **natural salt of all things**. This can be resolved upon a marble stone in a damp, cold place into **tartaric water**, etc.

# SUPERNATURAL

->*Concerning the second separation.*<-
### CHAP. III.

After you have successfully refined the **quintessence** <note>The "fifth essence," a substance's purest and most potent form beyond the four elements of earth, air, fire, and water.</note> from the **philosophical wine** <note>original: "vino philosophico"; not ordinary wine, but a powerful alchemical spirit or solvent</note>—or from a common wine of any color, provided it is pure and very potent—as I have taught in my chemical books, you must reduce this juice to its highest state of simplicity. This is done through continuous movements of **rotation** <note>original: "rotationis"; a process of circulating or redistilling a liquid in a closed vessel, often called "circulation."</note> as described in those same books. When the cycle of the wheel is finished, you will see the pure once again separated from the impure; the pure part will float on top with a color as clear as the serene sky. Separate this from the impure part by **decanting** <note>original: "inclinationem"; the act of carefully tilting the vessel to pour off the top layer</note> and save it. Until now, you have seen a "naked" heaven; now you will be able to adorn it with "lower stars," just as the heaven above is adorned with the higher stars. Will the Natural Philosophers who imitate the Greeks now wonder that we can touch the heaven and the stars with our hands, or will they deny this like they deny everything else? It matters very little what they do.

->*Concerning the ornament of the metaphysical heaven.*<-
### CHAP. IV.

For us, these "lower stars" are any individual things produced by nature in this lower world through the joining of the higher stars and heaven with the lower elements. Now I hear the voices of those growling against us, saying: "Bah! Away with such men, who presume they can join heaven to earth!" Let them shout until they are hoarse; they will be forced to hear even greater things. Heaven is celestial matter and a **universal form** <note>In alchemical philosophy, "form" is the organizing principle or "soul" that gives matter its specific identity.</note>, containing within itself all distinct forms, yet all of them proceed from a single universal form. Therefore, whoever knows how individual things can be reduced to their **most general essence** <note>original: "genus generalissimum"; the most fundamental category of existence</note> through the metaphysical art, and can afterwards fix one or more special virtues into that essence, will easily discover the **universal medicine**. This medicine will be able to remove all corruptions and diseases, whether they affect a specific part or the whole body. Since there is a single beginning for all decay, there is also a single source for the virtues that renew and give life. Who then, unless they are a philosopher who has lost their mind, could doubt this? But because many philosophers have already described very clearly how this is done, I will not press the point further. Instead, I will move on to the things they have described more obscurely, so that I may clarify them and promote this study. There is no benefit to readers in treating things already done by others in the same manner. Read, therefore, what they themselves have written on this matter, and compare it with what is here, so that you may hold onto what is useful.

->*Concerning the definitions and several divisions of the terms which we use in describing this treatise.*<-

# THE ARTIFICE
<note>original: "ARTIFICIUM"; refers to the alchemical craft or the skillful operation of the Great Work.</note>

...of the two of all mediums. In this place, **Chaos** is properly defined as the confusion of particular forms and their own materials with their universal form and its material. This is considered in various ways: First, as the confusion of the understanding of men who do not comprehend this art. Second, for the confusion of the parts that constitute this first extreme. Third, for the confusion in which they stand confusedly with their extremes, and successively each medium, one to the other by potential, as well as to all things, in whatever way, in whatever things, and those existing in any. Fourth, just as nature is a medium between the elements: not differently is the craftsman in this art held as a medium between Chaos, the operations, the **perfect medicine**, and the **most perfect medicine**. From these four it can easily be understood that the said medicines are brought from their potential into act, by means of matter, form, heaven, and intermediate operations. For once movement is excited by the craftsman, Chaos passes to the second extreme, which is the perfect medicine, and that to the most perfect, according to the order and disposition of the physicians. To perceive the matter more sharply, our **chaos** is a universal thing, containing within itself all that we work upon, from whose belly the ingenious craftsman must draw out matter, its form, heaven, and elements, so that from these he may fashion the medicines which were mentioned. 

**Metaphysical matter** is called the first and universal matter, or **Mercury** moving toward growth <note>original: "vegetationem"; in alchemy, the life-like growth or multiplication of minerals.</note> and extracting the first matter of a particular form from the form itself. It is considered in three ways here: First indeed as a passive subject, which undergoes movement under the excitation of the craftsman through the required mediums; from the operations of all these, the **heaven** <note>In alchemy, the "heaven" often refers to the purest, most volatile part of a substance, such as a highly rectified spirit.</note> arises from its matter. Second, it is considered as any sick body, which receives the form of medicines, just as elementary things receive the vegetable form. Third, for the form or the material of the form, like the first matter subjected to the actions of the heaven; for otherwise it obtains the power of form, as will be explained more broadly later. For by this reasoning, the heaven—which is the subject for the actions of these forms, by which it is turned into a **white or red tincture** <note>original: "tincturam"; the alchemical substance capable of transforming metals, usually "white" for silver and "red" for gold.</note>—can be said to have the nature of matter and form, since it moves the said form or form toward the perfect or most perfect medicine by its action, as will appear more fully below. From this you can have the best knowledge of our Chaos, because one and the same substance, yet through different reasons, behaves passively toward another, and actively toward the same, and then the reverse. Hitherto very few have had knowledge of metaphysical matter, from which the metaphysical heaven arises. For account must be taken of the simple and the composite reduced to simplicity through alteration, mixing, and so forth.

The **form of things** is the **generative virtue** <note>original: "virtus generativa"; the innate power or soul-like quality that directs growth and determines the identity of a species.</note> by which each thing can produce its own likeness: as the form of man lies hidden in man, and not in another:

...another: a tree within a tree, and likewise a metal within a metal: the raw material must not enter the work, but must be evacuated through **sublimation** <term>sublimation: the process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then collects as a solid on the cooler parts of the vessel, effectively purifying it</term> to the sides of the sublimation vessel, so that it may be free from its useless and superfluous earth. For this reason, it is called "intellectual" because of its incorruptibility, and for the same reason that we say heaven itself "understands," just like a man who is both sensory and intellectual. For it has within itself the property of an incorruptible spirit, which is like a soul having within itself the conditions of a body: because it generates and produces seed from itself like a woman. In this way, it differs from other things entering into this mastery. And because it is perceived by the senses, it is called "sensory Mercury." This, as a moving cause, draws out the potential within the form (or the form previously existing) toward the Red or White act: and it carries them in its womb no differently than a wife carries an infant conceived from her husband. From this it can be gathered that our heaven has an action upon the form, and the heaven of these things (and all things hidden within them) draws them out from potentiality into manifest action. For in it consists the power both of generating and of nourishing, just as in the menstrual blood of the masculine-feminine <note>original: "menstruali sanguine masculini feminis"; likely referring to the Rebis or the androgynous principle of the alchemical vessel</note>: for this reason it is called the **menstruum** <term>menstruum: in alchemy, a solvent that also acts as a "nurturing blood" for the developing Stone</term> in this art, and "heaven" by reason of its motion. For no differently than the celestial heaven moves the universal form, prime matter, elements, and species toward elemental compounds and individuals, our heaven also moves our forms toward the four elements, and from there to the **perfect medicine**, and the **more-than-perfect medicine**. Sometimes it is called "blood," because it is nutritive, and it causes the said forms to vegetate and grow until they reach their perfection, just as menstrual blood grows an embryo from a tiny seed into a great size—preserving the distinction of parts—through nourishment and the alteration of any medium into another, and of any quantity and form into another: these mediums and qualities existing in any alteration into forms from...

...male from the first different ones, until some being arises, in continuous quantity fused from various and discrete things, into a body living by soul and spirit. It happens no differently concerning the **metaphysical stone** <term>metaphysical stone: another name for the Philosopher's Stone, implying it is a spiritual or "beyond-physical" substance</term>, which is generated from a heaven possessing a "vegetable" or growing property. The stone transuses the likeness of this property into the **perfect medicine** and even beyond, just as a vegetative matrix <note>original: "matrix"; meaning the womb or life-giving source</note> does for the son whom she conceives and brings forth; the offspring also retains that property just like the parent. Likewise, the perfect medicine and more retains the property of its parents—namely, of heaven and the elements—by which it transfuses the likeness of its own perfection (such as its incorruptibility and its balance) into external substances and transmutes them into its own species. For this reason, it is called **Vegetable Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius vegetabilis"; in alchemy, "vegetable" refers to the power of life and growth, not just plants</note>, born from two substances, like a woman conceiving the seed of a male and possessing a different form and power than she had before the beginning of conception.

The **elements** in this art are considered to be the four apparent colors, and they are understood in four other ways: First, as they are drawn from "heaven" out of the raw matter. Second, insofar as the simple elements of heaven are separated from the coarser elements by the circle of **rotation** <term>rotation: a repetitive alchemical process, such as repeated distillation or circulation, intended to refine a substance</term>. Third, as they exist naturally in forms and are joined with heaven. Fourth, as they are separated from the form and heaven through alteration, mixture, dissolution, and generation as mediums, through the mastery of separating their qualities; and from the stated parts, only the "airy" part is taken and enriched through the artifice of rotation, and thus it is mixed with the forms into heaven. It must also be noted that the elements can be led out from the forms through heaven before they are joined, so that their "first matter" or heaven may be considered as approaching more closely to the most general classification of things, etc.

**Dissolution** is called the knowledge, or the metaphysical **coitus** <note>original: "coitus"; sexual union, used here as a metaphor for the chemical bonding of principles</note> of the male with the female, and of the female conceiving from the male that very thing which it ought to conceive. Let this be the beginning of "particular generation," where the effect of our metaphysical marriage is perceived by the senses, being the union of the twofold seed into an embryo.

**Alteration** is the conversion of one thing into another through likeness. This is considered in two ways, according to a twofold operation, insofar as it happens by itself. In the first way, it is considered as forms are altered into "heaven" and heaven is altered into forms. In the second way, let it be understood that the forms and heaven are so completely converted that they can be converted a second time into a "third number"—namely, into the **perfect medicine** and more.

These conversions or alterations are called "simple." Others are those which happen "by accident," as when from imperfect things, by **projection** <term>projection: the final stage of the Great Work, where the Medicine is cast onto base metal to transform it into gold or silver</term>, they become the perfect medicine through alteration or transmutation. **Mixture** is made from two colors, such as pale and azure, so that from them it may be known that forms and heaven are mixed in the **Great Work** <note>original: "opere majore"; the complete process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note> without any...

It details the stages of rotation, dissolution, and alteration necessary to refine the elements and achieve the final "Perfect Medicine."</summary>

### SUPERNATURALE.

...from another, just as from the beginning of the generation of man nothing else is mixed in with the man and woman or their seeds: and in this place the **marriage** <note>The "chemical wedding" or union of opposites required to create the Stone.</note> occurs between the forms and heaven. Another mixture also occurs, by which the air and fire of any of these, and the forms of heaven—through alteration, mixture, dissolution, generation, and the matter of heaven—are mixed with the forms, and so on.

**Digestion** is said to be the fostering of the conceived seed from the dregs <note>original: "sentine"; literally the bilge-water or dregs of a ship, referring here to the base fluid or residue from which the pure essence is refined</note>, by which means the **perfect medicine** arises—and even more than perfect. For it is necessary that the forms be digested in "heaven" for so long until the earlier medicine, which we mentioned above, is reached; and afterward, when it seems right to the practitioner, he can proceed even unto the second perfection. From this, best reader, you will be able to gather that there will be a double digestion: one, namely, by which the transition is made from the forms and heaven to the perfect medicine; the other, by which one must pass from this and heaven to the more perfect. For this reason, other means are necessary, not unlike the earlier ones—namely, mixture, alteration, dissolution, generation, and operation—except that something more imperfect arises from the earlier ones than from the later ones. And as soon as the **saffron color** <note>original: "croceus color"; a deep yellow or orange-red associated with the success of the "Solar" stage</note> appears through digestion, it denotes the forms; while **azure** <note>original: "azurinus"; a blue color associated with the "Heavenly" or Mercurial spirit</note> denotes our heaven, and those colors which are intermediate between these denote the medium of conjunction of heaven with form, connecting the former to the perfect medicine, or the latter to the most perfect.

**Generation** in this place is considered in various ways (but to provide its definition: it is the **manifestation of hidden forms** <note>A core alchemical belief that "generation" doesn't create something new from nothing, but brings out a potentiality already hidden within the matter</note>). First, insofar as it is the step generating the perfect medicine from heaven and forms; second, insofar as it generates the most perfect medicine from the perfect medicine and heaven. In another way, when it begins from dissolution to pass through alteration and digestion to the perfect medicine, it makes its limit there and reaches the end of the "lesser perfection"; or where, passing from here, it acquires the ultimate of the "greater perfection." By this latter reasoning, the **mastery of the greater perfection** <note>original: "magisterium"; the Great Work or the highest level of alchemical achievement</note> can be easily perceived, promoted by nature rather than by artifice—nevertheless, it is excited by artifice in the lesser perfection, where the artifice was more useful than nature. In the latter mastery, indeed, generation occurs no differently than a fetus in the womb or a bird in an egg. For this reason, it is also called the **philosophers' egg** <term>philosophers' egg: a sealed glass vessel (an athanor or alembic) intended to mimic the protective environment of a womb or eggshell</term> in its own way. This artifice can be understood no less than that which results from the mixture of matter with forms to create precious stones, such as **rubies, sapphires, and pearls** <note>original: "uniones"; large, high-quality pearls</note>, which are made in the womb of our philosophical heaven by means of generation, with the same virtues as those which, having been obtained from nature, are natural. From this it follows that this heaven is able to attract all virtues existing in stones, indeed by the virtue of unity, or its own simplicity, or (to say it better) by **magnetic virtue** <note>The idea that the alchemical substance acts like a magnet, drawing down celestial influences or extracting the "virtue" from other materials</note>. In this way, the distinguished practitioner can elicit celestial virtues from natural bodies—

As this color vanishes, the **red** arises, by which we are made certain that the members or parts of our Stone are gathered in the third number and perfection.

For after the appearance of this color, it is certain that our infant is completed in body and **vegetable power** <note>Refers to the power of growth and multiplication inherent in the Stone.</note>. From this time, the artisan must know the number of days during which our Stone was first led from the beginning of conception to the limit of the appearance of the red color; and without intermission, he must apply double that time, but a little more intensely. Once this is completed, that which was sought is acquired: namely, a **hard stone** wrapped in many superfluities, appearing just as a fetus does after a woman gives birth. The intermediate stages between the saffron and red colors are digestion, generation, and mixture, perceived by water, matter, form, and heaven. By their commingling, toward their end, the intermediate stages appear: water, matter, and form, without form and heaven. For if the form and heaven were still there, some parts would be very unwilling to be bound with others, nor would they be joined in the third number.

**Separation of virtues** is the extraction which occurs by the motion of fire, in this particular mastery, by which heat accidentally moves and excites form, heaven, and the elements through alteration, mixture, dissolution, generation, colors, digestion, separation, and operation toward a lesser or greater perfection. # SUPERNATURAL
### T 2
<meta>catchword: Less</meta>

...mediators, by separating themselves from others, enter into others; and through that operation of separation, a formal and also a material virtue is attracted from the forms and from **heaven** <note>original: "cælo"; the purified spirit or mercurial solvent used in the work</note> toward a lesser perfection, and from this toward a greater one. And in this way the form and the heaven—even the less perfect—change their simple forms into a greater or lesser perfection: the less perfect itself existing in a different form than the forms and heaven possess by themselves, and the greater perfect thing existing under a different form than when it was less perfect, or than the form and heaven were by themselves. Indeed, these perfections retain their own proper virtues—existing under a third form—within the **transforming venom** <note>original: "transformante veneno"; in alchemy, "venom" or "poison" often refers to a powerful corrosive or the "mercurial water" that dissolves the old form to allow for a new one</note>. If such an origin did not occur through the said separation, there would be neither alteration, nor generation, nor a progression of the lesser, but the work of nature would be destroyed in the **Philosopher's Stone** <term>lapis philosophicus: the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and conferring longevity</term>.

This medium is the indicator of the simple elements, existing actually in our heaven, with natural elements existing in forms, and [shows] that fire, air, water, and earth arise and are also separated from heaven into a mixture with the others that have been mentioned. And all these things are designated by colors.

**Potentiality** here is the same as alteration, by which degree it is understood that all other degrees and any media are present by potential in our first **Chaos** <note>original: "Chao"; the prima materia or the raw, unformed starting material of the work</note>; and secondly in the elements existing by potential in our matter. This potentiality, therefore, is nothing other than the act of our heaven, which we deal with more extensively in the "work of stone-making." Many know how to prepare stones, but not how to apply natural virtues to them, because they are ignorant of our **heaven**, in which, from which, through which, and with which the completion of stones and the increase of their perfection consists.

In this work, "Operation" is the name given to the excitation of the **four colors**, by which various modes of operations are designated. The **first color** <note>likely black, or nigredo</note> denotes that heaven has its action and operation upon the forms, or upon the less perfect and the form. The **second** denotes that external fire has an action upon heaven, forms, and the other elements, as well as upon natural and actual media, through movement toward lesser and greater perfection. The **third** denotes that the forms, or the less perfect, possess their action upon heaven, informing it so that it may arrive at lesser and greater perfection. The **fourth color** signifies the actions of operations which the **craftsman** <note>original: "artifex"; the alchemist</note> has over all that was said above: of fire through its administration as a cause, in the separation of heaven and the operation of forms, etc. It also signifies the actions of perfect things—both of the lesser and the greater—upon external substances through **projection** <note>original: "projectionem"; the final act of throwing the Stone upon a molten metal to transmute it</note>, according to their faculties toward the **red** or the **white** <note>referring to the two final stages of the Stone: the white stone for silver and the red stone for gold</note>, by which they were informed. This medium denotes that the rite and method of fabrication is done by fire, and by the mixture of matter with the forms and the philosophical heaven, along with the instruments suitable for the art.

The "less perfect" is called the **white stone** <note>original: "lapis albus"; the stage of the Great Work associated with silver and lunar perfection</note>, which is bounded by only three colors, as is evident to the eye: for it is composed of them. These colors, when driven into one, denote the perfection of the completed work—namely, of the **heaven** <note>original: "cœli"; in alchemy, the "heaven" refers to the purified, volatile spirit or the "quintessence" extracted from the matter</note>, the elements, alteration, mixing, dissolution, generation, color, digestion, separation, operation, and fire. By this medium, it can be recognized that the substance has proceeded from the heaven and from form through the power of gradual operations. Whoever reaches this goal will surpass all the wise men of the world in true wisdom and doctrine, and all physicians ignorant of this art in medicine. For he shall remove not only the infirmities and the **leprosy of metals** <term>leprosy of metals: the impurities, corrosion, or "sickness" of base metals like lead or copper that prevents them from being gold</term>, but also the "incurable" diseases (as they are called) of human bodies.

**Fermentation** is properly described in this place as the multiplication of a lesser perfection and its advancement to a greater one, using the means of mixing, dissolution, alteration, generation, colors, and digestion: by composing the heaven and the form, placing the "less perfect" into the mixture, and administering the regime of fire for as long as it takes to pass through all the aforementioned stages. This leads the generation and the colors into a greater perfection—far more powerful in quantity, quality, and virtue—toward the red and the white, and toward recovering the health of the human body. From these things, it is easily gathered that the less perfect passes into the greater through the aforementioned means and the actions of the forms, the heaven, the elements, fermentation, separation, operation, and fire through proper administration. Furthermore, the artist (whenever he wishes) ought to compose the less perfect only once, because it can be infinitely multiplied and led to the greater; afterwards, from that one, it proceeds into another infinitely, just as the human race continues its species—one always generating another as long as the world shall exist. A similar thing can be said of the **dough of flour** <note>original: "pasta farinæ"; a common alchemical analogy comparing the Stone to leaven or yeast that "infects" and transforms the whole mass</note>: for this produces another through successive fermentations. In this place, however, it should be noted that the less perfect can proceed into the greater and the infinite by means of the form and the heaven acting as ferments—which until now has been known to very few, even among excellent artists.

The **greater perfect** is the final perfection of the "greater stone," which consists of and is composed of four colors. Two of these colors denote that the four elements are within it with every perfection of virtue, and the conclusion of numbers into unity, as is expressly evident in the colors **green and red**.

The other colors, however, signify that the heaven and the form exist there, with all perfection and the simplicity of unity, through the **mastery** <term>magisterium: the specialized process or "Great Work" by which the Philosopher's Stone is created</term> of the four elements and the aforementioned mediums, etc.

From this final stage, it can be perceived that the "greater perfect" has the power to multiply its species in two ways, and of generating its own kind and things similar to itself: namely, in virtue through the aforementioned operations, and...

->### SUPERNATURAL<-

...and in the transmutation of external substances. It [the Greater Work] is far more perfect than the Lesser, both in its virtues and operations, as much in the transformation of metals as in the cure of infirmities deemed desperate by all; for this reason, it is not undeservedly called the **Greater Perfect** <note>original: "majus perfectum"; refers to the highest stage of alchemy, resulting in the Red Stone or elixir of life</note>.

Among all the degrees and mediums, some are **intellectual** <note>referring to concepts understood by the mind rather than seen by the eye</note>, such as **Chaos**, potency, operation, generation, and digestion. Some are **sensual** <note>perceptible by the senses</note>, such as wine and the **First Matter**, the body, form, elements, the "less" and "greater perfect," colors, fermentation, and separation, because they are perceived by the senses, such as the eyes. Others, however, are partly sensual and partly intellectual, like the **heaven** <note>original: "cœlum"; the purified volatile spirit</note> and all the mediums and degrees of the minor work. Furthermore, each of the aforementioned degrees or mediums retains its own property, differing by its own logic: of these properties, some belong to nature, and others to the perfection of the art. The mediums retaining the property of nature are wine and any mediums of the minor work, which behave like the **universal form** and the **first matter**, by reason of the property mentioned before. From these two arise all mediums and degrees by means of the **artifice** <note>the alchemist’s skill or the laboratory process</note>, just as the composite elements arise from the universal form and the first matter by the mediation of nature.

After discussing the degrees and major mediums, it will be worthwhile to bring some light to the minor ones as well, and to produce their definitions from the **Minor Work**—lest the practice seem to lack anything for those reading toward its understanding. In this context, **form** is the very same thing we spoke of in the Greater Work. However, its use here is different, because it is prepared in the formation: not toward a "less" or "greater perfect." It differs from the form of the **Stone**, because it receives its condition from the form, the heaven, elements, alteration, mixture, dissolution, generation, colors, digestion, fermentation, separation, and operation.

**Matter** in this work is considered in various ways. First, it is taken universally. Second, as the **Key of the Philosophers** <note>original: "clavis philosophorum"; a specific reagent or secret process that opens or dissolves matter</note>. Third, as oil. Fourth, as **sulfur**, by informing the oil of those informing [the substance], specifically in **inceration** <term>inceration: the process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a soft, waxy consistency</term>, by reason of which this Stone arises.

**Body** is taken here for the bodies of imperfect metals <note>such as lead, tin, or copper</note>, from which the **sulfur of nature** arises through the operation of the philosophical key. Through the form of the oils of those informing, it is prepared by the middle operations, such as solution and inceration, until the Stone which is sought is made.

The **philosophical key** in this place is considered no differently than the **heaven** itself in the Greater Work. Through this key must be performed **calcination** <note>original: "calcinatio"; reducing a metal to a powder using high heat</note>, dissolution, evacuation, multiplication, spirit, **exuberated quicksilver** <term>exuberated quicksilver: mercury that has been highly purified and "enlivened" through repeated distillations</term>, the sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, and inceration, by means of sublimation and fire, until the aforementioned sulfur is brought to the effect of the Stone.

<meta>This page continues the technical breakdown of alchemical processes, moving from the conceptual "mediators" of the previous page to the specific definitions of the operations—such as Calcination and Dissolution—required for the Lesser Work. It establishes a vocabulary for how the "bodies" (metals) are manipulated to extract their "spirit."</meta>

# THE ARTIFICE

<meta>catchword: is tinged</meta>

### CALCINATION
**Calcination** <note>The process of heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder or "calx."</note> is considered in various ways. First, when it is performed by common **Quicksilver** <term>Mercury: associated here with the "Mercury of the common people" used as a solvent</term>, under which **the Sun** <note>Gold</note> and **the Moon** <note>Silver</note> undergo change. Second, when a most powerful vinegar is made, by which a saffron-colored powder is drawn from **Mars** <note>Iron</note>. Third, when by means of sulfur and orpiment <note>arsenic trisulfide, a yellow pigment</note> as mediums, burnt copper is made from **Venus** <note>Copper</note>. Fourth indeed, <unclear>with</unclear> the **key of the philosophers**, and in this way all the metallic bodies are prepared for entering into **solution**, **evacuation**, and the other operations previously mentioned.

### DISSOLUTION
**Dissolution** <note>The liquefying or breaking down of a solid</note> is the hiding of the prior manifest form of the aforementioned bodies; it does not happen by itself, but by the mediation of the said "key," which is highly compatible with the bodies. We see this just as water is "corrupted" by fire through the medium of air, without which it is not raised into vapors. It differs from the **Greater Dissolution** in that by this [lesser] process, only the forms and the "lesser perfect" components of any of those metallic bodies are resolved.

### EVACUATION
**Evacuation** is nothing other than the extraction of the hidden **spirits** from their bodies, so that they may be formed into another of the "informing oils" <note>essential essences</note>; in this way, after **fermentation** and **inceration** <term>Inceration: the process of adding liquid to a dry substance to bring it to a waxy consistency</term>, they may pass into the **Stone**. That which is drawn from the aforesaid bodies by this operation is the matter from which our Stone must be led from potentiality into actuality by the means and operations already described.

### MULTIPLICATION
**Multiplication** is nothing else here than the repetition and continuation of the "evacuations." Through this operation, the **six bodies** <note>the traditional metals: Gold, Silver, Copper, Iron, Tin, and Lead</note> are provoked to nausea, and to vomiting the Stone from their very bowels.

### SPIRIT
**Spirit** is the quicksilver drawn from the six bodies, existing within the waters of the evacuations.

### EXUBERATED QUICKSILVER
**Exuberated quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum vivum exuberatum"; a refined, hyper-active form of mercury</note> is the spirit of the bodies, already separated by means of a completed evacuation.

### SULFUR OF NATURE
**Sulfur of nature** is the spirit of the bodies, exalted through **sublimation** <note>the process of turning a solid directly into vapor and back to solid to purify it</note> into a most excellent salt of four colors: namely, pale, green, black, and red. This last color denotes fire, and through it, the transition to the "Sulfur of Nature" which arises from the **exuberated quicksilver**. This indicates that it takes its origin from the spirit, and the spirit from the **multiplication** which proceeds from **evacuation**, and evacuation from **dissolution**, and dissolution from **calcination**, which indeed comes from all the bodies. Furthermore, this sulfur is the "son" born from the imperfect metals, and is ready to be dressed in white or purple garments <note>referring to the White or Red stages of the Great Work</note>. The "son" who is generated from the perfect metals differs from this one, being produced through the oil in which the forms of the imperfect "sons" are contained; their sulfur is of nature, unlike others whose sulfurs are dry and merely receptive to moisture.

### TINCTURES
**Tinctures** <note>The coloring agents or essences that transform the metal</note> are colors appearing in the work in different modes. First, green and saffron. Second, red and saffron, green and black. The first colors denote the tincture itself, by which the sulfur of nature... <note>original catchword: "tingi", indicating the next page begins with "is tinged"</note>

# SUPERNATURAL

<meta>catchword: ...should be tinged</meta>

...should be tinged <note>original: "tingi debet"</note>, and draw its origin from **the Sun** <note>Gold</note> and **the Moon** <note>Silver</note>, through the artifice of those operations which were mentioned above. Others, however, mean the **Sulphur** <term>Sulphur: In alchemy, this represents the active, masculine principle of "combustibility" and soul</term> of any imperfect bodies; they say these must induce colors so that from them may be made a **Stone** having and possessing the power of its "parents" from which it had its origin. If the two sulfurs are not joined together like brothers, being clothed in the said colors, that which is sought will not happen; nevertheless, three or more sulfurs can be joined together at once.

**Oil** is a form having a double color, namely green and yellow, by which it is indicated that it is produced from perfect bodies through suitable means.

**Inceration** <note>The process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency</note>, **Fermentation**, or rather **Information** <note>original: "informatio," used here in the sense of "giving form to"</note> is truly called the formation of the offspring of imperfect things to accept the condition of the Stone.

**Sublimation** <note>The process of heating a substance so it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again</note> is called "subtilization," which happens in two ways: namely, into a very fine powder and into a liquid. By this latter way, the spirits of the bodies are converted through intermediate multiplication into **exuberant quicksilver** <term>Exuberant Quicksilver: A "potentiated" or highly refined Mercury used in the Great Work</term>; by the former way, they are turned into the **Sulphur of Nature**. Sublimation is also considered in another way, as the matter which becomes closer to perfection, just as exuberant quicksilver is closer to the Stone than spirits, and as those natures of sulfur are closer to the Stone.

**The Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note> is the end and the perfection of all imperfect bodies and operations, in which they rest as if in fire and like **salamanders** <note>A mythical lizard believed to live in and endure fire without being consumed</note>. This is a "third thing" consisting of matter and form, above nature and yet by means of nature, then forged together by the industry of the craftsman.

**The Elements** are considered in two ways in this place: first as the fire acting externally; secondly, as an agent from without: like that which is drawn from perfect bodies into oil, etc.

->*On other differences of terms previously defined, and on divisions necessary to know.*<-

### CHAPTER VI.

Nature, in destroying <note>original: "corrumpens"</note> any individual thing, first **putrefies** <note>Rotting or breaking down, the first stage of transformation</note> it, afterwards separates the composite elements which are more closely joined in it, and then brings each of these to its highest simplicity, and finally to its **First Matter** <term>Materia Prima: The formless, primal substance from which all things are created</term>. When this is done, the **Wheel of Corruption** is complete, and from the First Matter, the **Wheel of Generation** takes its beginning, passing to the simple elements. Finally, through the mixing of these, composite elements arise, from which a material subject is made, according to its own species and form, under which the elements are drawn into the composition of the individual. The **metaphysical craftsman** <note>The alchemist, who works with the underlying principles of reality</note> must observe this process, so that where nature has finished, he himself, through the rotation of corruption...

# ARTIFICE

<meta>catchword: Subtili-</meta>

...[subtiliza]tion <note>original: "subtiliationem," referring to the process of making a substance refined or spiritualized</note> should begin with a backward step—that is, from the end, tending through the middle toward the beginning of the "wheel of corruption"—by employing the means of **calcination**, **dissolution**, **putrefaction**, **division**, **purification**, and so on. Next, one must come to the "wheel of generation," the means of which are **mixing**, **inceration** <term>Inceration: The process of softening a dry substance until it has the consistency of wax</term>, **decoction** <note>extended boiling or heating</note>, and others, which are the most excellently arranged instruments of the **Stone**. Once all these have been duly performed, the artisan shall possess that which he desired.

The **Form** of this work is considered in a threefold state: First, as it is the Primary Cause; second, as the artisan; third, as any other of the intermediate means.

**Matter** is also considered in just as many ways: First, as the subject from which our **Mercury** <term>Mercury: Not necessarily the common metal, but the "Spirit" or fluid principle of all things</term> is drawn; second, as the elements; third, as the **Sulphur of Nature** <term>Sulphur: The active, masculine, or combustible principle in alchemical theory</term>.

**Heaven** likewise has a triple consideration here: First, as the Greater Heaven <note>the macrocosm or cosmos</note>; second, as **Vegetable Mercury**; third, as the **Soul of the Metals**.

The **Elements** are considered in two ways in this place: First, simply; second, compositely.

**Power** or **Alteration** differs in as many ways as there are diverse means.

**Mixing** has a fourfold significance: First, of heaven with form; second, of air with water; third, of water with fire; fourth, of air with water and heaven.

**Dissolution** has only one consideration, which is between heaven and forms.

**Generation** has a double significance: First, by which the elements are generated; second, insofar as the Stone is generated from these elements and heaven.

**Colors** also have a double significance: the first in the evacuation of bodies and the rectification of the elements; the second in the generation of the Stone.

The **Less Perfect** <note>likely referring to "base" or imperfect metals</note> has only one consideration, as is evident from the senses.

**Fermentation** is threefold: the first from virtue <note>internal power</note>, the second from quantity, and the third from both together.

**Separation** also has a triple operation: the first is between the qualities of the elements; the second is their purification and fixation; and the third is of the Vegetable Mercury and the dregs <note>original: "faecum," the physical impurities or "dead" matter left behind</note>.

**Operation** has as many meanings as there are means of this Art.

The **More Perfect** <note>referring to gold or the completed Stone</note> has a single consideration like the less perfect, which is also evident to the senses.

The principles and means of **Philosophy** are found in all the principles and means of this Art, such as the motion of the sphere <note>the rotation of the heavens</note>, which must be considered as a Form containing all natural instincts and appetites.

**Vocabulary:** calcination, dissolution, putrefaction, division, purification, mixing, inceration, decoction, the stone, Mercury, sulphur of nature, elements, fermentation, separation.

The most subtle and powerful medium in the work is the **reiteration** <note>the process of repeating a cycle of distillation or refinement</note> of the **wheel of corruption** of metals, which is performed as follows.

With the **Forms** placed in **heaven** <note>original: "cælum"; in alchemy, this often refers to the upper part of the vessel or a state of extreme volatility</note>, unburied, dissolved, and emptied out through the practice of the "brief art" until one arrives at the **Sulphur of Nature** in metals, the wheel of corruption is then finished.

Reiteration occurs when the **sublimated earth** is placed in "heaven" and is dissolved therein by **putrefaction** and **division**. After the air, fire, and water have been emptied out, the artisan should once again reduce the earth to its purest sublimation. When this is finished, the **wheel of generation** follows with its own principles and mediums, until it is brought to its conclusion. This operation is more subtle than others; though it is longer, it is more perfect. By this path, that which is less perfect—which is the **unfermented stone**—is converted into that which is more perfect, the **fermented stone**, through the **separation** and **composition** of the elements, which exist in such a way. Nature in no way allows elements to be separated on their own: for in that way each would remain alone, possessing only a single quality, and would have no appetite for **generation** <note>the creation of new matter</note>, which is contrary to nature.

Indeed, the **separation of elements** is the predominance and victory of one over and above another, in a mixed rather than a divided way. For the color of **fire** is red; and because before one arrives at its sphere, one must pass through the sphere of **air**, a **yellow** <note>original: "citrinus"</note> color appears before the redness—clear and transparent. This results from the mixture of fire with air. Even before the sphere of air is reached, it is necessary to make the passage through the sphere of **water**: for this reason, the white and watery color appears splendid. But because **earth** is the center and the beginning from which the ascent must be made, while the stone is still in its sphere, the **black** color—which is proper to the earth—appears in it. Note therefore the separation and conjunction of these into one, namely fire. Likewise, if before the black, a red or white color should appear, or any other than what was said above, believe that the operation of the stone has been **destroyed**, due to the destruction of the mediums of conjunction.

The difference that is said to exist between the **elixir** and the **stone** also warrants notice, distinguished by "the raw and the cooked" <note>original: "per crudum & crudum & coctum"; the repetition of 'raw' suggests a distinction between degrees of unprocessed material</note>. For the **elixir** is a medicine composed of air, water, and earth only for the "white" work. A body dissolved into water, if it was red, reflects the color of the most excellent **carbuncle** <term>Carbuncle: A legendary gemstone said to glow in the dark, representing the highest perfection of the red Stone</term>, when it has been converted into a composite of the **soul of fire** and air, and into a composite of earth and fire. But if it was white, it will put forth a green color mixed with blackness.

Various **errors of the artisans** should also be noted. The first and most significant consists in this: that they do not know how to **imitate nature**. The second is that they think the end of the stone is its beginning, and they think they have finished when they have barely begun, as in the false opinion of the **red triangle** <term>Red Triangle: Likely a reference to a specific geometric symbol in alchemical theory representing the three principles or a specific stage of heating</term>. For the composition of the **Greater Stone** lasts two years for those who have never composed it before; but for the experienced, through a year...

# THE ART.

...whether continuous for three months. Some branches of the art are greater in scope, being completed in four or six months; if the artisan can find these, well and good; if not, let him lament the meager capacity of his own intellect, since they are described clearly enough in this little work. Now I see that we must come to the finer distinctions.

**Form** is twofold: namely, **simple** and **composite**. Simple form is absolute unity, the singularity of its own thing existing in itself and not with another. Composite form is the union of its four primordial chambers <note>likely referring to the four elements or the four stages of the work</note>.

**Matter** consists of the four elements: simply, as signified by the first form; or compositely, as denoted by the latter. **Vegetable menstruum** <term>Menstruum: In alchemy, this is not a biological term but refers to a powerful solvent capable of dissolving solid metals</term>, which is called "heaven" or the **philosophical key**, is the dissolving agent; the other part is that which is to be dissolved. The dissolving "celestial" agent is of a certain kind, while the other is not, being instead more corporeal <note>physical or dense</note>. The "celestial" is the **quintessence** <note>the "fifth essence" or purest extract</note> of wine or of tartar, from whose nature the dissolvable matter is brought into action. Otherwise, it is defined thus: the **Menstruum** is perfectly rectified "burning water" <note>original: "ardens aqua"; high-proof alcohol or ethanol</note>, by whose power any bodies are dissolved, putrefied, and purified; their elements are separated, and it is exalted into a "wonderful salt" and "earth" by the great attractive power it possesses. Whoever thinks there is another "water" is ignorant and foolish. The dissolvable menstruum is a "potential vapor" existing in any metallic body, joining **sulfur** and **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury</note>, without which it is by no means brought into action. Finally, it is defined thus: the **Menstruum** is the medium joining imperfect and perfect metals into the **Stone**. This dissolving menstruum is hot up to the second point of the fourth degree; therefore, its power must be increased with "hot" vegetables <note>In Galenic medicine and alchemy, "hot" refers to a substance's energetic temperament, not just its temperature</note> up to the final point of that degree, such as **wild celery**, **monkshood**, **oleander**, **cashew**, **black pepper**, **pellitory**, **spurge**, etc., without which it does not dissolve except over a long time.

Once this is completed, pour over the dregs an equal weight of **heaven** <note>original: "cæli"; referring to the "vegetable menstruum" or solvent defined on the previous page</note> as before, and let it stand in dung <note>original: "fimo"; horse dung was used as a natural, gentle heat source for digestion</note> for the same length of time as previously. Then, draw off the **air** through the ashes until it refuses to drip further. Afterward, let there be a repeated fusion of "heaven" over the **earth** <note>the solid residue or "feces"</note>, and after it has stood in the dung for an equal time, let it be distilled through the ashes again, until no more air comes out. Finally, pour the entire quantity of this air over the dregs remaining in the cucurbit <term>Cucurbit: The lower, gourd-shaped vessel of a distilling apparatus</term>—or those previously ground very finely upon a marble stone—and let **putrefaction** <note>the stage of decomposition or "blackening"</note> take place in a closed vessel for forty days in the dung-bath. Next, you shall separate the air from the fire by distillation in dung, whereby the fire will remain at the bottom and the air will ascend. But if this heat is not sufficient, you shall complete the work of separating the air from the fire using the slow heat of the ashes; let the fire be kept and set aside. Afterward, you shall pour the air back onto its own earth and return it to the dung to be digested for 15 days. Then, having removed the vessel, you shall distill the air and fire together through the ashes, and separate one from the other by means of dung or a water-bath, each being placed always with its own kind. You shall repeat these pourings, burials <note>original: "inhumationes"; the act of placing the vessel in the warm dung or earth</note>, and distillations so many times until no more fire wishes to exit the earth, and the earth is black or reddish. Only then place the lowest air to digest for eight days, and afterward distill as much as can ascend through that heat; pour this same substance back onto its dregs, and hide it away for a week for burial in the dung. Afterward, distill by dung, and return what has been distilled to the dregs; do this even until the seventh distillation with its burials, and afterward distill by dung. Return what has been distilled to the dregs, and do this likewise until the seventh distillation, repeating the pourings, burials, and distillations through their appointed days, as has been said. Thus far the **triangle** has been formed from air, heaven, and dung, in the center of which is the **soul of air**. Also, by the aforementioned operations in dung, you will be able to convert fire into the **soul of fire**, and form another triangle from heaven, dung, and fire. When all these things are finished, the **elemental wheel** is completed from the fixing and the overflowing of these elements—namely, of air and fire—through corruption, etc.

Finally, take the **earth**, and you shall empty it until it is deserted and converted into the **sulfur of nature**, and let a **triangle** be formed from earth, dung, and ashes, in the center of which shall stand the **soul of the earth**. Not before this is the **wheel of corruption** finished, the instruments of which are heaven, dung, the secret furnace, and the heat of the ashes, etc. Now it is proper to approach the **wheel of generation** as follows. For the composite made of fire and air, take four parts of fire to the sun, and mix with fifteen parts of air,

### THE CRAFT

...of the air; you shall place this back into **digestion** <note>a process of gentle heating to encourage chemical breakdown</note> for fifteen days, and afterward distill it by means of dung <note>original: "fimum"; horse dung was used as a natural, steady heat source</note>. You shall repeat this digestion and distillation as many times as necessary, until there remains at the bottom of the vessel a certain substance like a shining oil, a composite joined from air and fire, which is called **Slime** <note>original: "Limus"; here referring to a concentrated, oily essence rather than common mud</note>. By this same process, you shall convert fire and earth into their own composite so that a double **quadrangle** <note>a four-sided geometric figure representing a stable state of the four elements</note> may be formed. The first is made from fire, air, dung, and ashes, in the middle of which the composite of fire and air shall rejoice. The second is made from fire, dung, and also ashes, in the middle of which shall stand the composite of earth and fire.

Now, take a part of the composite of fire and air, to which you shall mix a sixth part of **heaven** <note>original: "cæli"; the "vegetable menstruum" or solvent prepared earlier</note>, and place it into digestion for thirty days. In this way, you will have formed a **triangle** from heaven, the composite of fire and air, and dung; in the middle of this, the **greater perfection** is found, transforming toward the **red** <note>the *Rubedo* or Red Work, indicating the final stage of the Philosopher's Stone</note>, drawing its birth and origin from heaven and the composite of fire, air, and dung. When you have done the same with the composite of earth and fire—joining to it one and a half parts of heaven—you will have a second triangle made of heaven, the composite of earth and fire, and dung. In its center shall stand the **lesser perfection**, transmuting toward the **white** <note>the *Albedo* or White Work, which produces a silver-making tincture</note>, and so forth.

However, if you do not wish to mix in the "heaven," in order to avoid such great labor, you may **cerate** <term>Ceration: The process of softening a hard, dry substance until it flows and melts like wax</term> the previously given composite elements for as long as it takes until they flow like wax. Place this cerated material into digestion for ten days, and once extracted, cerate it again as many times as needed, injecting it drop by drop, until you perceive in it an easy liquefaction. Place this matter into a **philosophical vessel** <note>a specially sealed glass flask, such as a "Pelican" or "Hermetic Vase"</note> that is very well sealed, and put it in a **secret furnace** for one hundred and fifty days or more, until you see the work completed by the signs described below. This process is the best in the **Greater Work** <note>the search for the Philosopher's Stone</note>, performed through the method of the Lesser Work. Take note that the ceration with fire and air can be done separately before they are reduced into one.

Thus the **Wheel of Generation** is finished, through which the good craftsman acquires what is desired, with the Lord's permission. From these two "slimes," various things can be made in the **metaphysical work** according to its breadth: first as in the royal practice, and in the craft of cerating the proper **foliated earth** <note>original: "terrae foliata"; a purified, crystalline earth</note> or the elements, by cerating first with air and fire, or with the said "slimes" made of air and fire. In this craft, the Wheel of Generation has its limit and end, the sign of which is the **red triangle**. 

Therefore, **corruption** is the beginning of the work, but **generation** is the end. By these operations, one quality is corrupted, and another is introduced through generation—just as by corrupting water, one generates earth, but by hiding this earth and making air and fire manifest, until the lesser and greater perfections arise through their own media. These media are the heats of the dung, the ashes, and the secret furnace, by which water is converted into earth, and this earth into air and fire. Earth is therefore the medium between water, fire, and air; and the dung, ashes, and secret furnace exist as the means through which...

SUPERNATURALE.

...fire and air are converted into the **soul of fire and air** <note>original: "animam ignis & aeris"; the essential life-force or vaporous essence of these elements</note>. Therefore, fire and air serve as the medium between the earth itself, the soul of fire, and the soul of air. Next, the **dung** <note>original: "fimus"; horse dung used to provide gentle, consistent heat</note>, the ashes, the **secret furnace**, and **heaven** <note>original: "cælum"; likely referring to the purified solvent or "vegetable menstruum" described on previous pages</note> are the medium through which the soul of fire and the soul of air are converted into the composite of fire and air, and into the composite of earth and fire. For this reason, heaven is the medium between the soul of fire, the soul of air, the composite of air and fire, and the composite of fire and earth. Likewise, dung, ashes, and the secret furnace are the medium through which the composite of fire and air, as well as the composite of earth and fire, are joined to the elements. Similarly, the composite of fire and air and the composite of fire and earth are the medium between the soul of fire, the soul of air, the less and more perfect, and so on.

### *Concerning the Particular Practice of the Stone from the Lesser Work.*

### CHAPTER VIII.

Cast the **metallic body** into the **philosophical key** <note>original: "clavem... philosophicam"; a specialized alchemical solvent designed to "unlock" the properties of metals</note> contained in its own vessel, and allow it to **digest** <note>a process of gentle heating to encourage chemical breakdown</note> for one week in the heat of the first degree or in dung. But before it is cast into the key, it must be reduced to a **calx** <note>original: "calcem"; the crumbly residue left after a metal is heated, similar to an oxide</note> so that the body may be better dissolved and evacuated by means of the key and the heat of the first degree from the **triangle** <note>a symbolic geometric arrangement of the alchemists representing the relationship between three substances or states</note> according to the natural order. 

Once the dissolution of the body is achieved, the vessel should be placed into **distillation**—already stirred by the aforementioned heat—and it will lose the "key" and be reduced to **earth**. On a marble stone, grind this earth thoroughly and let it resolve into water by itself. However, if the earth is too dry, sprinkle it with a little of the key; after three days, it will begin to resolve into a **composite water** containing the four elements. 

**Distill** this water through a **filter** <note>original: "filtrum"; often a piece of wool or cloth used for gravity filtration</note> and repeat the solution of whatever earth remains in the filter until the quantity of water seems sufficient to you. By this operation, the **triangle of evacuation** shall be completed; in its center is the earth, which must "drink up" its own water, as follows: 

Place the filtered water into the heat of the first degree to digest; it will cast out the key entirely and be converted into **small stones** <note>original: "lapillos"</note>. These, however, are not yet the **elixir**. By the aforementioned evacuation, another triangle is completed from the water, the heat of the first degree, and the key, in the middle of which the said stones exist. 

Grind these stones most finely and place their powder into **putrefaction** <note>the stage of the work where the matter breaks down and often turns black, symbolizing death before rebirth</note>. In this way, it will be converted into a metallic water or oil in which the elements reside. Divide their qualities as you have heard. Once these are divided, purify the earth or return the finest part through the necessary **sublimations** <note>heating a substance until it vapors and then solidifies again to purify it</note>. Finally, **imbibe** <note>to saturate or soak the solid matter with liquid</note> the earth with its elements: first with the celestial, then with the aerial water, and lastly with the igneous, according to the rules of the art. Let them be decocted into the **perfection** which you have heard. According to this process, the extreme principles and the mediums of this art are applied to whatever **metaphysical work** you desire.

<meta>This page transitions from the specific physical instructions of the "Lesser Work" in Chapter VIII to a theoretical discussion on the "Metaphysical Operations." It explores how the mind of the alchemist (the Intellect) interacts with the substances (Matter) and the animating forces (the Vegetable and Motive forms) to achieve transformation.</meta>

ARTIFICIUM.
<note>original: "Artificium"; The Craft or Artifice of the alchemical work.</note>

### *On the coherence of the metaphysical operations of both practices.*
<note>original: "utriusque practices"; refers to the two branches of alchemy: the "Particular" or "Lesser" work and the "Universal" or "Great" work.</note>

### Chapter IX.

The instruments of these works hold together in a wondrous way—that is to say, the intellectual media are joined to the sensory ones. Thus, the **form** <note>In alchemical philosophy, "form" is the internal organizing principle that gives a substance its specific identity, as opposed to its raw "matter."</note> which represents the person of the artist is an existing instrument by which nature generates our **particular egg** <note>original: "ovum"; the sealed vessel or the philosophical embryo containing the matter to be transformed.</note> out of the intellect. Although this form is to be distinguished from our form which we elsewhere call **heaven** <note>original: "cælum"; as noted on the previous page, this is the purified alchemical solvent or "mercury," not the literal sky.</note>, nevertheless, the former cannot persist without the latter in our craft, nor vice versa. For our form, "heaven," is the principle and sensory medium that generates, nourishes, and causes things to grow or vegetate; it moves the elements toward a particular generation just as the **greater heaven** <note>The macrocosm or the literal celestial sky.</note> moves the lower things of the world. By means of the forming "form"—which it acquires through the **vegetable form** <note>The life-force or growth principle within the chemical mixture.</note> and holds joined and bound to itself by an indissoluble knot—it causes the sought-after "particular" to multiply within external substances. So it is with many other things hidden in the process of the art, which are possible for the artist to know and to effect.

However, the form which is the **intellect of man** is the beginning, the middle, and the end in the preparations. This is denoted by a **saffron color** <note>original: "croceo colore"; a deep yellow-orange associated with gold, the sun, and the perfected soul.</note>, which indeed indicates that man is the "greater form" and the principal agent in this metaphysical work, superior even to the form of "heaven." Other forms are truly lesser than these, existing in states of greater or lesser perfection. The equal mixing of the **saffron color with the green** <note>Green represents the "Green Lion" or the raw, living energy of nature.</note> signifies that among all these forms, there must necessarily be a harmony—a hierarchy of "greater" and "lesser" without conflict, aiming toward the equality of the ultimate goal. For not one of these three forms can be absent without everything failing at once. Indeed, if "heaven" were lacking, the generation of the elements would fail, and there would follow a deprivation of both greater and lesser perfection. Therefore, the **intellective form** must be joined with the **vegetable form** and the **form of motion** through the intellect, so that one is conditioned by the presence of the other; and so on through the remaining degrees and media until the "more perfect" is reached.

The form called **motive** <note>The principle of change or transition from one state to another.</note> is a certain universal principle in the stages of this art, moving each thing through all the degrees to the next, until the end. Thus, the form of motion can be said to rouse all the stages in order until perfection is reached. **Form and matter** are substantial principles much greater than **accidental ones**; for the accidental ones are merely the changes seen in the work, such as colors, alteration, digestion, and so forth. The truth of this matter is demonstrated by the "lesser" and "greater" perfection, through the immensity of their transmuting power, rather than through these accidental stages. Nevertheless, the principles, the media, and the stated end are all equal because of the similarity of that same goal, toward which all things tend through a **wonderful chain** <note>original: "catenam admirabilem"; likely referring to the "Golden Chain of Homer," a concept where all levels of creation are linked from the divine down to the mineral.</note>.

SUPERNATURALE.

### *On the most excellent philosophical practice of the stone.*
<note>original: "lapidis"; The Philosopher's Stone.</note>

### CHAPTER X.

Take one of the forming bodies <note>These are the purified metals that provide the "seed" or "form" for the work.</note>, mixed with common mercury and common salt, and calcined. Let this silver <note>original: "Argentum"; here referring to the metallic essence or the mercury derived from the body.</note> be sublimated from it, or be recovered in "living water" <note>liquid mercury</note> as you know how, and let the salt be diluted with warm water. Afterward, divide the qualities of the elements, and to three pounds of our **heaven** <note>original: "cælo"; the alchemist's purified solvent or "Mercury of the Sages."</note>, add two ounces of the lesser form; then, for every half-pound of heaven, you shall take two and a half ounces of the greater form. From these you shall make a "marriage," placing the mixture in a vessel closed very tightly, and you shall cherish it with a continuous heat until, through dissolution, it passes into alteration and another color begins to arise—namely, a blackness, not entirely dark, but like that of a deep pomegranate. By this sign, you shall judge that the "form" and the "heaven" are passing through alteration, generation, and operation, and that a bond of love or a "fetter" has been made between the form converted into heaven, and the heaven into form.

Thereafter, by always continuing a tempered decoction <note>A slow boiling or heating process.</note>, and as the form and heaven begin to enter digestion and generation (which operations indeed last through their own colors until the least perfect state), that black color is mortified <note>original: "mortificatur"; the "death" of the old form, often called the *nigredo* stage.</note>, and by the continuation of the heat, a white color arises. When everything is under this color, it is a sign that the bones and nerves of our **child** <note>original: "infantis nostri"; the philosophical embryo or the Stone in development.</note> or infant are joined with the **third number** <note>Likely referring to the triad of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury reaching a specific proportion.</note>; nevertheless, this operation lasts until a saffron color appears. When this appears, it is a sign that the body of the infant has been formed and is complete with its organs, and is beginning to be prepared so that the **vegetable spirit** <note>original: "spiritus vegetabilis"; the life-force or animating principle that allows the Stone to "grow" or "multiply."</note> may enter into it. This operation will last until the saffron color vanishes in the preparation and a red color arises.

When this [redness] has finally arisen, you shall judge that the **vegetable soul** is within the body of the infant, and that the end of the termination of its body and soul is at hand. Then, finally, the craftsman must count the intervening days between the beginning and the end of the generation—which he can recognize by eye from the completion of the act of dissolution. For twice that amount of time, he must not cease in the least from administering the fire; and when the space of time is finished, he should allow it to cool. He will now find our **infant** in the manner of an egg; let him take it out, clean it, and place it in a clean glass vessel and back into the furnace of decoction, which is a **dry bath** <note>original: "balneum siccum"; a method of indirect heating, such as a sand bath.</note>. For six natural days, he shall administer fire successively in the same way as before, so that a hand can scarcely bear to hold the place where the vessel is positioned without injury. Extract it afterward, and preserve it most preciously until you have need of it. One part of this [Stone] by weight, projected upon two thousand parts, is powerful enough in external substances to multiply and generate a form similar to that from which it took its origin. Another secret of multiplication is held, namely this: take one pound of the said **menstruum** <note>The alchemical solvent.</note>...

...with two ounces of the said form—or two and a half, according to the aforementioned condition—and you shall imbue it with only one drachma <note>A small unit of weight; about 1/8 of an ounce.</note> of the **lesser perfect** <note>original: "perfecti minoris"; likely referring to the White Elixir or a less potent stage of the medicine.</note>. It must be noted, therefore, that the colors of these "infants" <note>original: "infantum"; a common alchemical metaphor for the Stone as it "grows" in the vessel.</note> are diverse: such as the red of the male and the greater perfect, and the white of the female and the lesser perfect. Clothed in this color, the infant is born from the mother’s womb. One weight of this, projected upon three thousand [parts] of matter, can multiply its own kind; and by a third repetition, it can be projected upon three hundred thousand. Of this Stone, as with the former "greater perfect," multiplication can also be made. 

It must be noted that in this **metaphysical-chemical** <note>original: "metaphysice chemico"; highlighting that alchemy was viewed as both a physical laboratory practice and a spiritual or theoretical science.</note> work, a certain or determined space of time cannot be assigned. For sometimes our infant is born sooner—specifically when the heat happens to be stronger than is balanced—and sometimes later, due to its reduction, as is seen in a human fetus. Colors are the best indicators of this art, by which it must also be ruled. Thus, when the metaphysical infant is in "dissolution" and entirely liquefied, and a black color begins to arise, you shall judge it to be in the "mixture" and to have passed through "alteration." And after the saffron color appears, you shall consider the body to be formed and complete in its limbs. But when the final color appears—namely red—know that the body is joined with the soul. Once this is perceived, the fire must be continued, as was said above, until the birth. Just as has been said here regarding the colors of the Red Infant, it must be understood no differently for the colors of the White Infant, according to its own qualities. By these signs, the practitioner can approach the metaphysical work without fear and complete it happily—with God’s favor, however, and not otherwise.
