->*Another way of practicing.*<-

Of any of those things which have been mentioned in the mixture of the "heaven," with the "heaven" of red or white wine, or of tartar drawn through the **mastery** <note>magisterium: the high-level laboratory process directed by the skill of the master alchemist.</note> of the separation of qualities from the elements, and placed with the "form" or "forms" according to the doctrine of the Greater Work—the vessel being blocked so that the "heaven" does not escape—let it be cooked with the continuous heat of a **bath** <term>balneum: a water bath (bain-marie) used to provide gentle, even heat.</term> without intermission for several days. Afterward, having opened the vessel, with the said "heaven" and "form," let some of the "air" of any of the mentioned things be placed for the second part of the "heaven," and let it be cooked for as many days as before. When these things are finished, having opened the vessel again, you shall place as much of the "heaven of fire" <note>cælo ignis: the most volatile and energetic portion of the substance, corresponding to the element of Fire.</note> of any of them as there was "heaven of wine." Having blocked the vessel again, let it be cooked with continuous heat for another fifteen days. Once the artifice of mixing is complete, you will see the mixed things **transmuted** into the less perfect state, through mediating colors, according to which the craftsman ought to govern the work, until it reaches the most perfect Greater Work, which is able to transmute and multiply its own species in external substances by three thousand times its own weight, etc.

### On the Universality of Philosophical Mercury.
### CHAPTER XIII.

Our Mercury may be found in any elemental thing; however, in some it is so remote that human life would fail before it could be separated from it. Some, knowing this secret—namely that Mercury is within everything—have attempted to extract it from stones, rye straw, flowers, and wood, but in vain; they reached the end of their lives rather than their intention. The first is that it actually converts everything placed upon it into the species under which it exists. This is an evident sign of an admirable **vegetable power** <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" refers to the power of growth, life, and multiplication, rather than just plants.</note>, by reason of which substances are transmuted into other forms. Let the craftsman therefore consider what he might be able to work when our **Mercury** has been stripped of its own form and shaped by another. 

There is also another equally evident operation: when the bodies of the **perfect metals** <note>Gold and silver.</note> are ground with that "form" upon a **porphyry stone** <note>A hard, purple-red stone used as a surface for grinding alchemical ingredients.</note>, both of these will be reduced into the form of an **amalgam** <term>Amalgamation: The process of combining mercury with another metal to form a soft or liquid alloy.</term>, from which the Mercury can be extracted through a cloth. Wherefore, in the "angle of concord," they are gathered together so that in our **heaven**, the perfect bodies are multiplied, and their Mercury is in no way able to resist being reduced into the appearance of an amalgam by another natural bond. These operations of our **heaven** could also be marked in other substances, which brie— <note>The text ends mid-word: "bre-" likely for "breviter" (briefly).</note>

# ARTIFICIUM

... [bre]vity <note>original: "vitatis," likely completing "brevitatis"</note>, we leave aside those things, because the things already said satisfy the understanding of them. The end of this entire mastery is this: that **our Mercury** <term>Our Mercury: The "Mercurius noster" or philosophical mercury, a purified spirit of matter distinct from common quicksilver.</term> must be placed in the celestial sphere; otherwise, the craftsman will work in error. It seems to be a marvel that **our Mercury**, situated in a super-celestial place, does not retain its color, weight, quantity, and quality, since all these are of its own nature. But the reason for this is that it is placed under another form than that in which it lay hidden as an individual substance.

This is also the method for extracting Mercury in this artifice: namely, that the best white or red wine is placed into a separation vessel, and from it is distilled **burning water** <term>Burning water: "Aqua ardens," an early alchemical term for high-proof alcohol or distilled spirits.</term>, as is customary. Afterward, let it be rectified to a greater subtlety four times, though three would suffice, lest the burning spirit exhale; therefore, those who rectify it seven times have erred. Let the sign of rectification be this: when sugar is placed within it, the whole is burned away together with the water, leaving nothing behind. This matter is the subject from which the **fifth essence** <term>Fifth Essence: The "Quintessence," the most refined and spiritualized extract of a substance.</term> is drawn, by means of the vessel called the **pelican** <term>Pelican: A circulatory distillation vessel with two arms that return condensed vapors to the body of the flask.</term>. By this operation, it will happen that, along a diametrical line, the superior part or fifth essence is separated from the inferior: namely, from the turbid dregs, etc.

Mercury can also be extracted from **tartar** <term>Tartar: "Tartarum," the hard crust of potassium bitartrate that forms in wine barrels.</term> by calcining it in a glassmaker's furnace for three natural days; but a large quantity of it should be used, for it is greatly diminished. Grind this burnt material upon a marble stone, and when left in a very cold and humid place, it will dissolve into water. This must be distilled through a filter sleeve and received in a glass vessel. You will be able to extract Mercury from it in two ways: the first as we said above regarding wine, the other through the artifice of separating the qualities from the elements, etc.

### CHAPTER XIV.

The spirits of the **imperfect bodies** <note>The "imperfect bodies" are the base metals (lead, tin, copper, iron), which alchemists sought to "perfect" into gold or silver.</note> are evacuated, or their **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> is made exuberant, or their primary matter is born fit to receive any form. A similar oil is made through the separation of the qualities of the four elements, etc.

**Saturn** <note>The alchemical name for Lead.</note> and **Jupiter** <note>The alchemical name for Tin.</note> are of one and the same nature when they are reduced to spirit; therefore, into spirit, the exuberant quicksilver...

Likewise, Jupiter has another unique condition in mixture with each of the aforementioned. Furthermore, another condition arises by mixing Saturn and Jupiter with Mars and Venus: or by mixing Jupiter or Saturn with either of those, or Venus and Jupiter with Saturn, or with Mars itself. By this reasoning, the conditions of the metals can be multiplied by mixing one or more with another. In however many ways the mixture is made, the condition of the Stone will vary accordingly.

Calcination, again, is equal to Solution, and Dissolution to Evacuation: the latter to Multiplication, which is equal to Spirit, etc., for the constitution of the subject, which is the stone. Likewise, the alembic communicates itself equally to all according to its function.

For this is what the definition of a "medium" requires: namely, that the stone be composed of the sulfur of nature and the quicksilver exuberated from imperfect things, along with the oil of the perfect ones. Thus, the stone is a medium participating in both natures, by reason of the harmony it has with the said imperfect things. # THE ARTIFICE

### Page 312

For those things that are imperfect, they are formed through all their parts and bound to a certain external form by an unbreakable bond and a vegetable property <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" refers to the power of growth and multiplication, similar to how a plant grows from a seed.</note> which they receive from the **philosophical key** <term>Philosophical Key: The secret agent or solvent—often a specialized form of Mercury—used to open the "doors" of solid metals to transform them.</term>. They are so shaped by that form that in their smallest part, there truly exists a tiny portion of that same form. In this way, they cast off their old, imperfect forms which were actively within them, so that they may receive the forms of perfect things which were only potentially within them, and thus be transmuted into perfected metallic bodies. 

The method of operating has been mentioned before: while we spoke of it being done with the **sulfur of nature** <term>Sulfur of Nature: The internal, active fire of a metal that drives its characteristics and color.</term> extracted only from **Saturn** <gloss>Lead</gloss> or **Jupiter** <gloss>Tin</gloss>, we now say that a mixture can be made with two, three, four, or all of them, according to the will of the operator, depending on what condition the craftsman desires for the stone. 

The method for eliciting **oil** from perfected bodies <note>In this context, "perfected bodies" refers to gold and silver.</note> has also been established; it is one and the same as for all others, achieved through **calcination**, **dissolution**, **evacuation**, **multiplication**, **spirit**, the **alembic** <gloss>a distilling apparatus</gloss>, **exuberated quicksilver**, **sulfur of nature**, **tincture**, **oil**, **inceration** <term>Inceration: The process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a soft, wax-like consistency.</term>, **sublimation**, and through **fire**. When you wish to join two together, place them into calcination by means of our philosophical key; afterwards into dissolution, and through the rest of the aforementioned steps up to and including sublimation. If they are perfected and made into sulfur of nature, place them into multiplication; and if the substance proves too hard, pour on a portion of **menstrual blood** <note>original: "sanguinis menstrualis" — An alchemical metaphor for a life-giving solvent or "mercurial water," not literal blood.</note> so that it may be converted into oil.

Note that the elements of metals drawn from them by **vegetable Mercury** <term>Vegetable Mercury: Mercury that has been "animated" so that it can cause other metals to grow or change, much like a plant.</term> are called their **First Matter** <term>First Matter: The raw, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made; the "blank slate" of the physical world.</term>, approaching most closely to their most general genus. It is also called their **Fifth Essence** <gloss>Quintessence</gloss> or even their **Heaven**. 

This matter, however, must be converted (if it is from perfected things) into the nature of forms, and into that other nature of imperfect things. This is called a **composed ferment** <term>Ferment: A substance—like yeast in bread—added to the alchemical mix to "leaven" it and direct the transformation toward gold or silver.</term>, which is made from the First Matter, the nature of the metals, and oil instilled drop by drop. Afterwards, by joining the Mercury with the said First Matter through **natural Mercury** via inceration (which is the middle step), a **philosophic gum** is created. 

A **simple ferment** is one to which nothing has been added, such as the elements or the evacuated metals existing by themselves or taken simply. It is a **composed ferment** when several are mixed together. One who is able to specifically convert the bodies of perfected and imperfect things into their First Matter will be able to possess both simple and composed ferments (without which the stone will be empty and void). 

Indeed, the **Earth** raised from metallic bodies into the sulfur of nature is called the **Salt of the Philosophers** or vegetable Mercury. It is the medium joining the extremes together toward one end—that is, the "heaven of the form," or the philosophical key for perfected bodies. This earth is also called **mercurialized elements**. That which is less perfect is the **Philosophic Stone** not yet fermented in power or in quantity; it is composed of fire and air, or of earth and fire.

->SUPERNATURAL<-

V 5

**Fermentation** is an operation denoting a double multiplication: specifically, of quantity and of power <note>original: *virtutis*</note>. When multiplication occurs in quantity, the power is diminished, and vice versa. There is also a third type where both power and quantity are increased simultaneously. The first is done with common **Mercury**; the second with the **Mercury of metals**; the third, indeed, with the **vegetable Mercury** or the **menstruum** <term>Menstruum: In alchemy, a universal solvent used to dissolve solid matter, named for its role in the "gestation" of the Stone.</term> of the philosophers, etc. Fermentation occurs to shorten the long duration of the work through form, the heavens, and Mercury as it is commonly understood.

**Evacuation** is the name given to the separation of the pure from the impure.

**Multiplication** is the returning <note>original: *reductio*</note> of the evacuated substance back upon its own "earth," so that the purity of the spirit may arise.

The **Spirit of bodies** is the substance which is evacuated from metallic bodies through solution by means of the **philosophical key**.

**Exuberated Quicksilver** <gloss>Mercury</gloss> is the spirit of bodies ascending together with the key and passing through the **alembic** <note>A distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube.</note>.

The **Sulfur of Nature** is the sublimated earth of the bodies, converted into **foliated earth** <term>Foliated Earth: A highly purified state of matter that appears layered or flaky, representing the "pure earth" ready for transformation.</term>, which is called the first and nearest matter of metals.

**Tincture** <note>The coloring or transmuting agent.</note> comes either from air and fire, or from earth and fire. **Oil** is the fixed element that allows for melting <note>original: *liquationem*</note> and fixation.

The **Stone** is the sprout or germ grown from the foliated earth and the fixed oil already sown within it.

The **Fire of the Stone** consists of the essential fire of the body and the co-essential fire of the **vegetable menstruum**. From these, a single fire is composed which transmutes all metals in an instant; it is aided by the aforementioned vegetable fire through its own power of growth. The elements of the bodies must be distilled with the menstruum many times for the **Great Stone**, until they are fixed and no trace of the menstruum remains visible with them. Thus, from the nature and properties of these things, a fire arises like a **bolt of lightning**, suddenly burning away the imperfections of any metal and inducing a new, perfect form.

### *On the abbreviation of the philosopher's stone.*

### CHAPTER XV.

The entire life of minerals consists in **two waters**. The first makes the Stone volatile without labor and without danger; the second fixes the Stone, and is itself fixed with it, though not without danger. This is because this second water is drawn from a certain "stinking" solvent <note>original: *menstruali quodam fœtente*</note>, composed of four things. No water stronger than this is found in the world; it is lethal, etc. There is a great danger that the spirits might escape during the washing process. This stone is produced in a much shorter time than other stones.

The **Animal Stone** <note>Alchemical "kingdoms" (animal, vegetable, mineral) refer to different methods or levels of the work rather than the literal ingredients.</note> is that which has almost no end because of the regulation of the elements; it contains greater knowledge than any other stone. The **Vegetable Stone**, although its preparation is quite long and of the highest condition, must nonetheless follow the path of the Animal Stone.

...regarding the ratification of elements and their rectification: and thus prepared, it is more effective than the animal [stone or spirit].

The **Fifth Essence** <note>original: *Essentia quinta*; commonly known as the Quintessence, the purest and most medicinal part of a substance</note> is the spirit within the mineral stone that has the power both to kill <note>original: *mortificativus*</note> and to bring to life.

In the animal kingdom, it sometimes exists as the supreme medicine for human bodies, especially if it is extracted from blood.

However, within the vegetable stone <term>Vegetable Stone: An alchemical substance derived from plants, believed to contain the concentrated life-force of growth and regeneration.</term>, the spirit of the fifth essence resides, along with the restoration of youth and the preservation of the human body from all decay.

### THE ABBREVIATION <note>A "Short Work" or accelerated method intended to achieve results faster than the traditional, lengthy alchemical "Great Work."</note>

Take 2 pounds of rectified **burning water** <note>original: *aquæ ardentis*; usually refers to high-proof distilled alcohol or a powerful solvent</note> and 1 ounce of ferment. Place them in a **pelican** <note>A circulatory distillation vessel with two side-arms that return to the base, named for the bird believed to nourish its young with its own blood.</note>, and leave it to digest for twenty or twenty-two days. The spirit of the fifth essence will be thickened by the ferment and converted into a stone. After it has congealed, dissolve it for one night in [warm] dung or a water bath, and congeal it again. Let this be done three times or more, until it no longer wishes to coagulate, but remains like an oil. With white ferment, it does not dissolve as quickly, but it coagulates faster. This medicine transforms things into no other state than that of its ferment, and no higher. If you ferment it with its own "earth," it will be a universal medicine, though not as effective as when used with one of the [specific] ferments. If you dissolve **gold** in the aforementioned water after its tenth distillation, and then allow the water to evaporate with gentle heat or fire, and finally place it in a damp spot, it will dissolve by itself over four days into **potable gold** <term>Potable Gold: *Aurum Potabile*, a legendary medicinal elixir made from dissolved gold, thought to grant longevity and cure all diseases.</term>, for the preservation of human health. And if you take **Mercury** that has been sublimated seven times with **vitriol** <note>Sulfate minerals used as strong acidic agents in alchemy.</note>, such that there is one part gold and seven parts of its silver <note>likely referring to the mercury/silver mixture used in the process</note>, and then sublimate it until the Mercury is "fixed," you will have a medicine that tints <note>alters the color and nature of metals</note> and penetrates, etc.

If one part of this dissolved gold is placed in a gentle fire by itself for eight days with a hundred parts of Mercury, this entire mixture will congeal into gold. This happens because of the spirit of the water, which, in the solution of the gold, becomes inseparably fixed with it. By this path, you can mix minerals with vegetable substances and make a medicine from them in this manner: Distill the vegetable stone until the distillation where it is entirely deprived of **phlegm** <note>the watery, tasteless, and inactive byproduct of distillation</note>—which usually happens by the fifth [distillation]. Then, take clear and good vitriol, grind it with an equal weight of the best **cinnabar** <note>Mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral used as a source of mercury and for its symbolic solar properties.</note>, and let it dry in the sun, then over coals, until all wateriness seems consumed. Finally, pour on the water, and distill it first with a gentle fire and then gradually increasing it, as is done with the sharp **water of the philosophers**. The spirit of the fifth essence of the vitriol, and of the cinnabar or **antimony** <note>A brittle, silvery-white metalloid used to purify gold and in various medicinal preparations.</note>—which primarily constitute the mineral stone—is then mixed with the spirit of the fifth essence of our blessed burning water. Some make these in the shape in which precious stones are usually cut, in this manner: they take an iron tool, cut and polished at one end just as they wish the stone to be; they dip this into oil, then into melted wax, and finally into cold water. When it is now wrapped in wax, they cut the wax all around so that the mold is freed from the iron. In this way, they prepare stones for themselves like cut gems. But I scarcely believe it possible for the matter to be done exactly this way. Therefore, I would advise that they be made in a round or semi-round shape in any manner, and afterwards cut like natural stones. 

Then, dig up the vials from the earth and take down the others from the air. Next, fill the lower part of your spherical vessel with the "earthy" mercurial water so that it fills half of it, and make the molds float upon it. Afterward, if you want a Mercurial, Solar, Lunar, Jovial, Saturnian, Venereal, or Martial stone, fill your wax molds a little less than full with the "heaven" of any of those said planets—that is, with its "aerial" water; however, do not fill them to the very top, lest the waters perhaps overflow. Finally, cover the spherical vessel with its upper part, and let it remain closed for several hours, until you see the waters in the molds have thickened somewhat. When this is observed, open the vessel and turn the molds over, so that the paste touches the fixative water. Leave it thus in the shade until it hardens into a stone.

But this process seems to pertain more to the **transmutatory art** than to medicine, because of the simultaneous infusion of "earth" with "heaven" <note>The author refers to the mixing of materials previously "tempered" by the ground and the sky.</note>. By which it happens that the stones made by this method are darker than those manufactured in that [other] way.

...are brought from their potential into act? Indeed, it is no wonder to those who consider the great alliance of the superior world to the inferior, and of the latter to the former. It is no different than if some limb in a human body were injured in a wife; the corresponding part in her husband's body—even if not actually injured—nevertheless perceives the pain in potential and through a certain natural compassion, born of natural love and the **divine marriage** <note>The "divine marriage" refers to the Hermetic concept of *As Above, So Below*, where the celestial and terrestrial realms are bonded like a couple.</note>. Likewise, if any limb in a man's body is touched, that touch immediately reaches the spirit, just as was said above concerning the heaven.

We see, therefore, that a similar marriage exists between the spirit and body of man as we have described between heaven and earth. Again, whatever movement occurs in heaven flows into man, or into the elements for his use. Therefore, it is not to be wondered at if stones not unlike precious gems can be made by art, by which the diseases of men can be cured, provided they were fashioned under favorable **astrological aspects** <note>original: *aspectibus felicibus*; the specific angular relationships between planets that alchemists believed influenced the success of a "work".</note> (as they say). How much more so when they have been dissolved into their own liquors and applied within the body; they will become the most powerful remedies.

# THE ART.

<meta>catchword: is, and</meta>

...soon from there a key is necessary, without which absolutely no access lies open to natural philosophy.

After we have entered, three chests appear to us. One, a vast treasure far more blessed than the others, for the medicine of the human body, is contained under the waters of the air and the heavens. In the other two are contained waters both aerial and earthly together, as much for immense riches—namely the transmutation of metals—as for the cure of diseases. In the third, indeed, similar waters are contained, but for the fabrication of precious stones. From these three fountains gush waves blessed for the world, by which wonders are performed in the nature of things. When the celestial waters, impregnated with mineral virtues, have been exposed to the air through the revolution of a whole circle <note>This likely refers to a full year or a complete astrological cycle of the heavens.</note>, they become more widely impregnated with celestial powers, through which they become fit for the resolution <note>original: "resolutionem," meaning the breaking down or dissolving of a substance into its primary parts.</note> of all things, even the most solid bodies.

Yet the lower waters—also celestial, but exposed to the belly of the earth—receive those same virtues at the same time, but by another medium, namely the earthly one, by which they acquire the power of coagulating <note>To "coagulate" in alchemy is to turn a liquid or spirit into a solid, material form.</note> all things and their own **quicksilver** <term>Quicksilver: Known in Latin as *argentum vivum*; the liquid metal mercury, which alchemists believed was the "mother" or base fluid of all other metals.</term>. Among various sulfurs, this one is the most excellent, just as the quicksilver we have set down exists as the most outstanding and philosophical kind.

Although other philosophical substances are found, they are not **sublimated** <note>Sublimation is a chemical process where a solid turns into vapor and back to solid, used here to mean "refined to the highest degree."</note> in such subtlety and purity. Therefore, these waters of the philosophers are the greatest among the rest: namely, one formal, celestial, and superior; the other material and inferior. Yet both are born from the same root, and they differ only through industry and application to the craft. This confirms what was preached to us by father **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the foundational texts of alchemy are attributed.</note>: "**That which is above is like that which is below**" <note>The most famous axiom of the *Emerald Tablet*, suggesting a correspondence between the heavens (macrocosm) and the earth or the individual (microcosm).</note>, to perform the miracles of the one thing.

Here we see the first restorer of this most excellent art placing two things contained under the likeness of unity, by which wondrous works are made from natural things through a supernatural **mastery** <term>Mastery: The *magisterium*, or the successful completion of a complex alchemical process to produce a transformative substance.</term>. The former he calls "superior," that is celestial, by which we can understand the celestial waters. The other he names "inferior," and this we can relate to the earthly waters, which he says are one and the same water. For they are of one and the same substance and do not differ in nature, but only in "accident"—that is, in their preparation. For through the medium of the air, the superior waters acquire a dissolving power, while through the medium of the earth, the inferior ones acquire a coagulating power; these actions are indeed "accidents" <note>In the philosophy of the time, an "accident" is a property (like color or state) that can change without changing the essential nature of the substance.</note> and not substances.

See how **Johannes Trithemius** <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German Benedictine abbot and polymath whose writings on cryptography and hidden knowledge deeply influenced later alchemists.</note>, the most excellent of natural philosophers, explains this saying of Hermes. He says: "The One <note>original: "Unarius."</note> is not a number, and from it every number arises." For before the celestial water we mentioned was divided into two parts, it was one—not divided into two vessels by separation, but truly divided by the introduction of different accidents, as you have heard. For this reason alone, the One became the Two <note>original: "binarius."</note>, the first of all numbers, as the same Trithemius says. -># SUPERNATURAL.<-

X

<meta>catchword: now to-</meta>

is, and is composed of accident <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, an "accident" is a property that a thing possesses (like color or temperature) which is not essential to its nature as a thing.</note>. Therefore it cannot be numbered, because before it there is no number. Let this be understood regarding unity, which **Hermes** explains in another way through a likeness, saying: *It is as it is*, etc. However, the **binary** <note>The number two, representing duality, division, or the separation of spirit and matter.</note> is denoted by Hermes through the "above" and the "below." Let the binary be rejected (says **Johannes Trithemius**) and the **ternary** <note>The number three, representing the synthesis of the two opposites into a new whole.</note> will be convertible back to unity. The same Hermes says this, but in other words, namely: *To perform the miracles of the one thing.* <note>original: "Ad perpetranda miracula rei unius." This is a famous line from the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus.</note> It must be especially noted in this place that unity is understood by both men in two ways. Any natural thing of all things is numbered in its species, but in any *particular* individual it is not numbered: unless it is considered as being composed of elements by nature, then it is numbered. Hermes numbers unity no differently through the "above" and "below," and Trithemius himself through the constitution of every number from the monad <note>The "monad" or "unario" refers to the primary unit or the number one.</note>. 

Later, both measure unity by a far different reasoning: one by the reduction of the "above" and "below" to the likeness established for a miracle; the other by the rejection of the binary, and its conversion into unity through the ternary. Certainly, by a wondrous reason, they both agree on the same opinion. Therefore, there is a **natural unity** divisible into the binary, or rather countable, and here through the ternary it is reducible to another unity, the **supernatural**, which second state is truly called "attained unity," beyond which it is permitted to proceed in no way at all. Trithemius speaks of it thus: 

> Therefore, every operation of wonders consisting within the limits of nature descends from unity through the binary into the ternary: yet it does not do so before it rises from the **quaternary** <note>The number four, often representing the four elements (Earth, Air, Fire, Water) or the completion of a cycle.</note> through the order of steps into simplicity: for if you wish to count four, you know that you must begin in no other way than from one, and you say: one, two, three, four; which, taken together, make **ten**.

This is the perfect consummation of every number, because then a return to one is made, and beyond the **denary** <note>The number ten, or the decade.</note> there is no simple number. Those who do not know the depths of this connection are amazed, wondering what principles we use in the operation of wonders, falsely thinking that we rely either on the help of demons or on some superstition against our Christian faith. We, however, do not wonder at those who judge us this way, because of their ignorance of the things we have set forth. Since, just as the most holy Scripture testifies concerning the internal knowledge of God—which no one understands except he who receives it—so no one can be imbued with or use these things unless he has received a singular light of understanding from divine gift, moving from nature into nature; and there must be in him, along with the light, fire; with the fire, wind; with the wind, power; with the power, knowledge; and with knowledge, the integrity of a sound mind. Thus far he has spoken.

From these things it is apparent that in the decade or the "second unity," attained perfection exists, by the progress from natural unity to supernatural unity: with the binary, however, being reduced to the ternary through the mediation of the quaternary, as was said above. I understand this opinion to serve our purpose in this way: Whosoever [would apply] that medicine now to—

# THE ARTIFICE

<meta>The previous page ended with "on," likely leading into "that admirable unity" or "that admirable art."</meta>

Anyone who wishes to attain that admirable thing and perform miracles must first reduce himself from the **binary** <note>The state of division or duality, specifically the separation between the physical body and the spiritual soul.</note> into the **ternary** <note>The number three, representing a state of spiritual completion or synthesis.</note> by way of the degrees of the **quaternary** <note>The number four, referring to the four physical elements: earth, water, air, and fire.</note>, before he presumes to do so in other natural things. For man is naturally one, and is not counted, but supernaturally he is counted as two: as in spirit and body, which constitute the **binary** within him. 

But because of the first corruption <note>A reference to the Fall of Man or "Original Sin" in Christian theology, which was believed to have disrupted the perfect harmony between body and soul.</note>, the body overcomes the spirit, with the result that the spirit is unable to produce anything wonderful. But if this is to be achieved in this life, the binary must be overcome by the ternary—that is, the body must be conformed to the nature of the spirit, and the spirit must be so joined to the body that it finds peace within it. Once this is done, the ternary is born and rejoices in a second and perfect unity: for from the two aforementioned parts, through their conjunction, a third thing is made. 

This conjunction, however, must be achieved through the degrees of the **quaternary**—that is, through the **transmutation** <term>Transmutation: The alchemical process of changing one substance into another; here, it refers to the spiritual refinement of the human elements.</term> of the elements from which the body is composed into a single and purest element, in this way: 

*   **First**, let water be made from the earth of your body: that is, from your stony and sluggish heart, let it become soft and vigilant toward the knowledge of God and yourself, so that the images of the spirit may be imprinted upon it, no differently than characters are pressed into wax by a seal. 
*   **Next**, from this water let air be made: that is, lift up your heart, now humbled, toward heaven to Him who created you, always tending toward the highest things like air, and knocking at the gates of prayer so that your intellect may be opened to understand the things of God. 
*   **Finally**, from this air let fire be made: that is, let the whole desire of your heart be converted into love (to which fire is compared because of its heat) for God and your neighbor here on earth, so that this flame is never extinguished. 

Thus it will happen through this likeness that your binary—that is, spirit and body—is perfectly joined into one ternary, through the quaternary and its degrees, as you have heard. 

Now you have, excellent reader, the manifestation of the **Key of speculative philosophy** <note>original: "Clavis philosophiae speculativae"</note>, published for you with a generous spirit, and for all students of hidden things; a key which is kept so hidden in the riddles of the ancients. In the likeness of this, it is necessary for you to fashion the key of chemical philosophy. Now what shall hinder you from being able to understand the enigmatic writings in this art? You need no longer falsely judge, as others do, that the practitioners of this art are necromancers <note>Sorcerers who communicate with the dead; alchemy was often unfairly associated with dark magic.</note>, even though they do wonderful things, but rather that they are magi and truly wise men. 

And so that you may see in how few words I have now explained to you those things which the ancient and modern magi have veiled in so many and various coverings, I will not be at all reluctant to add some things that **Trithemius** <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot, cryptographer, and occultist who influenced many later alchemists.</note>, the most sagacious of all modern writers on this subject, has written. You will see that in this art there is absolutely nothing of ghosts or superstition (as the ignorant falsely claim), nor anything that is contrary to the true religion of God. 

But I recall earlier in the title or inscription of this little book, I made mention of the ten degrees of speculative or attained philosophy, of which we have explained seven. It is right, therefore, that this...

# SUPERNATURALE

<note>original: "Supernaturale" — Concerning the supernatural or that which is above nature.</note>

...[it is pleasing] to add in this place, toward the end, a decade <note>A series of ten steps or levels.</note> of these things in this manner, namely:

**Study** generates **knowledge**. **Knowledge** gives birth to **love**. **Love** [produces] **likeness**. **Likeness** [produces] **frequency**, or **communion**, or **familiarity**. **Communion** [produces] **confidence**. **Confidence** [produces] **virtue**. **Virtue** [produces] **dignity**. **Dignity** [produces] **power**, and **power** effects a **Miracle**. The three steps which are numbered more than the preceding ones in this place depend on others, and are easily perceived by any initiated philosopher. Wherefore I would now make an end of our **attained philosophy** <note>original: "adepta philosophia" — a term for alchemy or the completed Hermetic science.</note>, were I not first reminded of the words of Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot, cryptographer, and occultist who influenced Agrippa and Paracelsus.</note> uttered concerning this art, which it seemed good to set down here.

Attained natural philosophy (he says), which once, resting upon the principles of nature, consisted in its pure simplicity, has been confused by so many lies and impurities and so many deceptions, that no one can discern or understand them unless he is most learned in both [the true and the false]. How many wandering men have I known in this art, otherwise most learned; none of whom, spending their time and substance on **alchemy**, failed to lose it: some lose their life along with their possessions; others, desiring to elicit medicine from it, gain nothing after long labors; others, searching into the secrets of wonderful effects, have been able to reach no experience; others, longing to predict future things, speak falsehoods instead of truths. These men, while they thrust in the windy opinions of their own heads, clumsily produce bad and false things from the good and true writings of experienced men which they do not understand.

Note three principles hidden in this **natural magic**, without the perfect knowledge of which, no effect follows the operator. 

The **first principle** consists in the **One**—not *from* which, but *through* which every power of natural wonders is brought into effect—of which we have spoken, because that which is pure, proceeding from the One, is neither compounded nor changed. To it, from the **ternary** and **quaternary**, a progress is made toward the **monad** <note>The Monad (from the Greek *monas*) represents the primary, indivisible unit or the Divine Source.</note>, so that the **denary** <note>The number ten, often seen in Pythagorean and Hermetic thought as the number of perfection or completion, as 1+2+3+4 = 10.</note> may be completed: for through it there is a return of number to the One, and simultaneously a descent into the four, and an ascent into the monad. 

It is impossible for the denary to be completed except through it: the monad is joyfully converted into the triad. All those who are ignorant of this principle after the principle of the monad gain nothing in the ternary, nor do they reach the sacred quaternary. For even if they possess all the books of the wise, and perfectly know the courses of the stars, their virtues, powers, operations, and properties, and fully understand their images, rings, seals, and every most secret thing: nevertheless, they can achieve no effect of wonders in their operations without the knowledge of this principle, from the beginning, in the beginning. Wherefore all those I have seen working in **Attained Natural Philosophy** have either achieved nothing, or have fallen through despair into vain, frivolous, and superstitious things after long and useless operations. The second principle, indeed, in order though not in worth <note>The Latin text cuts off at "dignitate," which matches the catchword for the next page.</note>

# ARTIFICIUM
<note>original: "Artificium" — The Artifice, or the skillful workmanship of the Great Work.</note>

...[in real]ity indeed, separated from the first, which being one makes the **ternary** <note>The number three, often representing the union of spirit, soul, and body.</note>, it is that which works wonders through the **binary** <note>The number two, representing duality, polarity, or the division of the primordial one.</note>. For in the one there is the one, and it is not the one; it is simple, and in the **quaternary** <note>The number four, representing the four elements (Earth, Air, Fire, Water) or the material world.</note> it is composed: when this is purified by fire in the sun, pure water comes forth, and having returned to its own simplicity, it will show the completion of hidden things to the worker. Here is the center of **attained natural philosophy** <note>original: "adeptæ philosophiæ naturalis" — The completed science of alchemy.</note>, whose circumference, united to itself, represents a circle—an immense order unto infinity. Its virtue is purified above all things and simple, yet smaller than all things, composed upon a grade above the quaternary. 

The Pythagorean quaternary number, supported by the ternary, if it observes order and grade, purified and pure in the one, can work the wonders and secrets of nature toward the binary in the ternary. This is the quaternary, in whose measure the ternary, joined to the binary in the one, performs all things which it does so miraculously. For the ternary number, reduced to unity through observation, contains all things in itself and can do what it wills. 

The third principle is not a principle by itself, but between it and the binary lies the end of all science and mystic art, and the infallible center of the middle. In no other thing is it easier to err than in this, since very few live on earth who understand its depths. It is a varied composite, rising and remaining fixed through the **septenary** <note>The number seven, associated with the seven planets and the stages of transformation.</note> multiplied eight times into the ternary. In it is the consummation of number, grade, and order: through this, all philosophers, true seekers of the secrets of nature, have attained miraculous effects. Through it, reduced to a simple element in the ternary, miraculous cures of infirmities and naturally of all sicknesses suddenly occur; and the work of the practitioner in attained natural and preternatural philosophy achieves its effect according to the arrangement of the quaternary. 

The prediction of the future is verified through it, and the suggestion of hidden things is perceived from nature through it alone. By this sole means, the secret of nature is opened to **Alchemists**, without which neither an understanding of the art is acquired, nor is the effect of the operation found. They err, believe me, they all err, who trust that they can work anything in the hidden sciences of nature without these three principles. Moreover, the greater cause of error is that the wise men of old, imbued with nature's secrets, either kept these things entirely silent or shrouded them in such great obscurity that they cannot truly be understood except by those like themselves. 

The philosophy of this instruction is secret and heavenly, in which if anyone truly desires to know and understand something, he must flee the crowds of men—it is a withdrawal—leave the world, and contemplate heaven not only with his eyes, but with his mind. The Spirit of God blows where it wills, illuminates whom it wills, and whom it overshadows with its divine power, it leads into all knowledge of truth. Let him who has received this give thanks to God, and strive to respond with the fruits of good works according to the strength received, and acknowledge that he has received it, and so he will find no reason for pride. But he to whom [it is given] to know these sublime...

# SUPERNATURAL
<note>original: "SUPERNATURALE"</note>

...if these thresholds <note>original: "limia," likely a transcription of "limina"</note> have not been granted to him, let him either recognize his own sloth, because he did not labor to know; or let him praise the mercy of the Creator, who willed for his own benefit that there be impediments so that he would not know; or, if he has not acquired it, let him confess that God was not a debtor to him for so great a gift, and let him not murmur. You are a friend; listen to a friend advising you, and you will understand the deed. As a victor over those close to you, tread upon the fire of envy, not the air of mortals; levity threatens danger through hatred of the immortal God. Flee the assembly of men caring for worldly things, but associate with those meditating on heavenly things. Your safety is in the swallows' nest, but there is danger in the dung of hens. <note>The swallow was often a symbol of the soul or heavenly aspirations in alchemical allegory, while the "dung of hens" refers to base, earthbound, or false materials.</note> You chase a sail caught by the wind; you will be worn out in the **septenary** <note>The number seven, often relating to the seven planets or the seven steps of the Great Work</note>, but through the **ternary** <note>The number three</note> you will rise again in unity, and you will find yourself happy. 

If you begin to approach your operations from the sun <note>In alchemy, the Sun represents both the metal Gold and the enlightened human spirit</note>, which nature seems to hide from you, so that you are converted from all things toward the true sun, which is God, through the study of knowledge—the mind having been purified from lower things—in the desire of the soul and the fervor of most holy love, it will show you something else. Because the art of divine love is long, but time is short <note>original: "ars longa, tempus vero breve," a play on the famous aphorism by Hippocrates</note>, and it is better to always love the Creator in truth than the creature. However, these principles are exceedingly difficult for the human intellect, and are accessible only to a man disposed by the stars, by art, by genius, and by a special condition of nature; without the perfect knowledge of these things, those working in the attained philosophy <term>attained philosophy: a term for alchemy or high magic where the practitioner has reached a level of mastery or "adeptship."</term> achieve nothing. This natural philosophy not only performs visible effects, but also wonderfully illuminates the intellect of the man skilled in it with the knowledge of divinity, and provides invisible fruits to the soul.

But we see its name is today hated and loathsome to men, so that they condemn all who study it with one voice, and think its every use is entirely adverse and contrary to the Christian religion. Yet if it were reduced back to its primary purity, it would become lovable again to all and most useful to Princes. But who is so fit, who is so learned and powerful, that he can undertake this work? It is not the business of a single day, nor the work of a poor man, nor of the unlearned: where both the deepest knowledge in almost every science is required, and wealth, so that the volumes of many authors can be gathered together. 

That this may indeed happen someday, may Almighty God, the Best and Greatest <note>original: "O.M." — "Optimus Maximus"</note>, grant. Meanwhile, let us not cease to gather little flowers from the Holy Scriptures according to our strength, from which it can be restored to us in full—and not from elsewhere, such as the opinions of men, which are a sink-hole of all evils. Having utterly cast these aside, let us turn ourselves to the fountain of truth and bid farewell to sloth; putting an end at last to this little work, let us enjoy the knowledge of truth through Jesus Christ.

<header>THE ARGUMENT</header>

### TREATISE
# ON THE PHYSICAL LIGHT OF NATURE TAKEN FROM GENESIS,
### ACCORDING TO THE WISDOM OF THEOPHRASTUS PARACELSUS.

->General Argument of the whole work.<-

It is surprising that the ancient natural philosophers <note>original: "Physicos"</note> did not consider the highest and chief secret of all natural philosophy <term>Natural philosophy: The study of the physical world and nature, which in the Renaissance included what we now call science, alchemy, and theology.</term>, founded in the single center of eternal immensity. Perhaps because, being intent on more obvious things, they passed over those that are deeply hidden, or rather, it was not granted to them to know God more clearly through His works. Indeed, in these latter times, Jesus Christ willed to reveal this to His own followers. Concerning which also Paracelsus, the first of all (as far as I know), writing in his *Book to the Athenians* <note>Referring to Paracelsus's *Philosophia ad Athenienses*, a work on the origins of the world.</note>, or writing to their disciples, teaches under a veil <note>original: "sub involucro," meaning allegorically or cryptically</note> that the **great mystery** <term>Great mystery: original Latin "mysterium magnum," a Paracelsian term for the primordial "womb" or unformed matter from which all things were created by the Word of God.</term> is uncreated and is the mother and **first matter** of all natural creatures. And because it deigned to unite itself at times, even with things that will eventually pass away into the universe, it exists also in a single created center. All things (he says) are to return into their first essence, yet not into their **first matter**, nor into the **great mystery**; but only into that which existed before it, namely good or evil—that is, into the likeness of the **Unary** <note>original: "Unarii," referring to Unity or the Monad, symbolizing God or perfection.</note>, or the **Binary** <note>original: "Binarii," referring to Duality or the number Two, symbolizing division, conflict, or the fall.</note>. Nor is this mystery ever to return to that state in which it was at the time of creation. This first principle is divided into the **three first natural principles** <note>In the Paracelsian system, these are the "Tria Prima": Sulphur (soul/flammability), Mercury (spirit/volatility), and Salt (body/solidity).</note>, the third of which is again divided into four <note>The four traditional elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth.</note>, while the other two nevertheless remain under the sacred triad. For one was divided by one into the **firmament** and the **element**, yet they remain under the marriage of union by the power of light, which vivifies their soul and body. But in these matters, he [Paracelsus] chose to be obscure on purpose...

Paracelsus did this—though not for everyone—for those whom he judged to be unworthy of such secrets <term>Secrets: original Latin "arcanis," referring to the hidden inner workings of nature or alchemical mysteries.</term>, and especially for those who are accustomed to despise such things. Perhaps he feared that if they ever understood these matters, they would abuse them. Meanwhile, he did not consider that those wandering along the "broad way" <note>A biblical reference to the path of destruction (Matthew 7:13), here implying those who follow false or superficial science.</note> ought to be led back to the true path according to God’s command. I, on the contrary, because I see that God is the key and the one who unlocks His secrets to the worthy, while closing them to the unworthy, did not hesitate any longer. I believe that those things which can benefit good men should be published as far as is permitted, and should not be suppressed on account of the wicked. For He to whom these secrets belong knows how to protect them from all who strive to profane them, and how to take them away whenever it shall seem right to Him. Furthermore, He said: *To him who has, it shall be given, and from him who has not, even what he has shall be taken away from him.* <note>Quoting Matthew 13:12.</note> Accordingly, it seemed timely to explain in very clear words those things which were handed down in riddles—not only by Paracelsus, but also by the most ancient authors and spagyric <term>Spagyric: A term coined by Paracelsus referring to alchemical medicine, specifically the process of separating and then recombining the essential components of a substance.</term> physicians. My hope is that, if it is ever possible, the mutual stains of hatred and the jealousies born from obscure traditions might cease. 

Nor did we judge it fair to use any other authorities to prove our foundations of Physics <note>original: "Physicæ," referring to natural philosophy or the study of the physical world.</note> except for Him who established nature itself, and who taught us through Moses that the Genesis of all things was founded "in the beginning." Therefore, we have undertaken to treat this same subject of Genesis only physically (as our vocation leads us), and not theologically, lest anyone think we are wandering outside our professional expertise. To theologians and pious men, therefore, we leave their interpretations entirely intact; indeed, we wish them in no way harmed by this work. Rather, we embrace the physical in a theological manner. Finally, so that it may be seen that many others—both the most ancient and also more recent spagyric professors of the "attained philosophy" <note>original: "adeptæ philosophiæ," referring to those who have mastered the secrets of alchemy or the Philosophers' Stone.</note>—were of the same opinion, I bring forward as witnesses Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure believed to be the author of the Hermetic Corpus, foundational to alchemy.</note> and Johannes Trithemius <note>A German Benedictine abbot and polymath (1462–1516) known for his work on cryptography and magic; he was a teacher to Paracelsus.</note>. Their writings are drawn directly from Genesis, and I have explained them according to the strength of my intellect, clearly and in various ways—now in a physical and spagyric way, and at other times explained morally. ### The Author’s Outcry to God.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'S' featuring a central cross within a circular frame, surrounded by floral and scrollwork ornamentation.</image-desc>

Summoning the highest goodness, immense wisdom, and eternal God, it is in no way possible for the human intellect—without the greatest consternation of mind—to consider even the smallest point of your inexhaustible wisdom. I remain silent indeed on how the tongue might express it with faltering speech, or how a trembling pen might write it, unless it be done by the command of your most sacred spirit, impressing that very wisdom into the hearts of men. This spirit never ceases to silently admonish and daily exhort them to the confession of truth in all things. 

Since, if this is to be attempted or achieved by anyone living on earth, it is necessary above all that they be illuminated by the light of your divine splendor, so that they may recognize the shadows of their own ignorance. They must candidly confess that they can be liberated from those shadows by no other means than your power. And if perhaps, by the persuasion of the **slanderer** <note>original: "calumniatoris," a common term for the Devil, who "accuses" or "slanders" humanity.</note>, a person seeks help from themselves, they will find themselves submerged in a deeper pit of captivity. For by themselves, they will never find any other means of liberation than the snare with which they entangled themselves from the beginning, when they turned away from the obedience they owed to you alone, their Creator.

Most evident examples of this disobedience are still placed before our eyes daily through the writings of the faithless. These works proceed from human wisdom—especially regarding the treatment of all faculties, arts, and sciences—in which they seek and teach nothing but paths deviating from the target of truth. This state of affairs arises from no other source than their own principles and foundations. They did not draw these, as was proper, from the true fountain of truth—the center of all sciences—but from the opposite and false center of lies: namely, **Duality** <term>Duality: original "Dualitate." In this context, it refers to the state of being separated from the Divine Unity, leading to error, conflict, and "binary" thinking that misses the singular truth of God.</term>. To resist these good men more fiercely, they have built up ramparts and bulwarks to better cover and protect the falsehood of their poorly founded principles. As it is...

# AN EXPLANATION OF THE FIRST TWO
### chapters of Genesis according to Natural Philosophy. <note>original: "juxta Physicam." In this context, "Physics" refers to Natural Philosophy—the study of the laws and nature of the physical universe as created by God.</note>

It requires no debate at all that the Scripture of God teaches us true Natural Philosophy from the mouth of Moses in the holy book of Genesis. For who will dare to deny that nature itself had its beginning at the creation of the World? Or who would affirm that nature exists anywhere other than in the heavens and in the elements? Every Christian will confess that the Prophet of God, Moses, speaks nothing at all from himself in this place, but has purely and sincerely reported to the people of Israel only those things which he had heard from the mouth of God. If anyone should perhaps doubt this, he should be judged as one to be deservedly driven out from the assembly of the faithful; for such a person should neither be listened to further, nor admitted to a pious and truly Christian conversation, unless he repents. 

Therefore, in teaching the people of Israel (who were chosen by God) at God’s command, Moses makes his beginning with Natural Philosophy through the narrative of the creation of the World and of nature’s first visible creature. He did this so that he might better and more easily draw his pupils—who were still new and unrefined—toward higher things (namely, toward the supernatural) through their admiration of such magnificent works of God, and lead them into the knowledge of their supreme Creator. 

Therefore, from the beginning he teaches them that before the most high God procreated man, His final creature, in His own image and likeness, He willed to create from nothing a dwelling place for him, and in it whatever would be necessary for his use. Nor did He wish that this world—which He had established as the first visible creature—be destitute of the image of His unity. He adorned this world, created in the most beautiful order and arranged by number, measure, and weight, with a certain wonderful craftsmanship. <note>The phrase "number, measure, and weight" refers to Wisdom 11:20, a Bible verse that was a cornerstone for early scientists who believed the universe was designed mathematically.</note> He decreed to use these three things as instruments, or as the first ideas and forms, in this work of His. 

From this, we conclude neither unwisely nor rashly that men ought to have drawn the principles of the foundations of their arts and sciences—especially medicine (which presented itself to man as a necessity immediately after the Fall) <note>Referring to the "Fall of Man" in Eden, after which humans became subject to disease and death, making medicine necessary.</note>—with the highest reverence and thanksgiving. This is especially true since we see that the supreme Creator used these means, even though He was in no way in need of them. For He, being the almighty God, could have created all things by His will alone. But in order to give examples to us men (who have no power of our own) so that we might have a standard against which to compare whatever we were to work at in this World, and so that we might recognize all our wisdom as having arisen from the fountain of wisdom, which is God, and not from elsewhere, and that we might give all thanks to Him—He decided to act in this way. Therefore, we shall teach that our principles of both Natural Philosophy and Medicine have arisen and been taken, as is just, from divine likenesses of this kind.

and this we shall endeavor to demonstrate with the strongest arguments—namely, from Holy Scripture—and with irrefutable examples, against which the infidels may rage as they will. We have also determined to declare their principles from the opposing side, so that both may be open to the whole world, and it may be free for judicious men to discern in the meantime between the true and false foundation. We are greatly consoled that we depend upon the fountain of truth and imitate Christian teachers in this, rather than infidels; furthermore, our enemies can bring nothing against us except the authorities of men, who are even rejected by God and entirely ignorant of the truth existing in God alone. Let there be shown to us one among the wise infidels, those ancient professors of the arts, or rather the teachers of their own inventions, who knew God in truth, or who was not a blasphemer against God and the Son of God (like that prince of medicine, Galen <note>Galen of Pergamon was a 2nd-century Greek physician whose works dominated Western medicine for over 1,000 years; here, the author attacks him for his pagan views.</note>) or an idolater, and led astray by a spirit of contradiction. 

Nevertheless, they want whatever they write and teach to be held as truth; led indeed by that reasoning which they do not even blush to put forward impudently. "In the treatment of arts," they say, "and of faculties <note>The "faculties" refer to the traditional branches of university study: Theology, Law, and Medicine.</note>, it is not a matter of the knowledge of God, but this belongs to Theology"—as if they would conclude that these arts are to be possessed and practiced without God. What blasphemy is this? From this it appears clearer than light that those who utter such things do nothing out of love for their neighbor, but only out of greed. Can there be a true physician and true medicine without their Creator? But let us dismiss men of that stripe who even think such things, and let us finally recall ourselves to the concept of our own mind. 

God is surely a pure and simple essence consisting through Himself, incomprehensible by any other, invisible, indefinable, and indivisible; He is prefigured for us through **Unity** <note>The number "One." In this philosophical system, Unity represents God's perfection and wholeness.</note>. This Unity, indeed, being devoid of multitude, does not admit contrariety <note>Opposition or conflict between two things.</note>, and consequently admits no weakness. The world, therefore, since it was created by God in the image and likeness of Unity, persists in that union, although ordered through numbers, as mention is made of them in Genesis. For these numbers would still retain the nature of union even under man’s disobedience and would produce no "multitude," until, seduced through the **Duality of the Binary** <note>original: "dualitatem Binarij." In Pythagorean and Neoplatonic thought, the "Binary" or number two represents the first departure from the unity of God, leading to division, conflict, and eventually decay.</note>, man had been plunged into the confusion of multitude, contrariety, and disobedience. Having stripped off the garment of perfection and the health of body and mind, wretched man contracted the stain of every vice, infirmity, and disease. Previously, he did not need any medicine, until he fell into this "disease"—the source of all types of diseases—deprived of all health. 

Since, therefore, the first origin of all diseases happens to man through his departure from Unity, it is necessary that all health consists in this Unity alone, and that it must be sought in it. Now let us see into what diseases he has fallen: namely, into confusion and the apprehension of both deaths <note>Likely referring to the "first death" (physical) and the "second death" (spiritual/eternal).</note>. Therefore, being ill-disposed in spirit and body,

Being thus affected, because he felt himself making an exit into both deaths <note>This refers to the dual theological concept of temporal death (the end of physical life) and eternal death (spiritual damnation).</note>, he feared the voice of the Lord and hid himself, not seeking a remedy. However, a double medicine was necessary for him to be saved: namely, the Mercy of God and bread. Under this latter one is contained the healing of the body, found within these words of correction and punishment brought forth by the Lord: *In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread.* This bread is to be understood not only as that by which the body is sustained for nourishment, but also as whatever is necessary for natural life. For a diseased and poorly healthy body, the medicine for its life is bread; if the body is deprived of this, no differently than if it lacked food, it becomes subject to death. Therefore, the Bread of Medicine (not that which is acquired through this art <note>The "art" here refers to the practice of medicine or pharmacy.</note>, but that which is necessary for recovering health) is to be sought nowhere else than in that place where it was lost to us—namely, the garden of unhappiness and unity, which we have undertaken to explain briefly, by means of Natural Philosophy <note>original: "Physice"</note> alone. 

Previously, we touched upon the fact that the world itself was created by God in the image and likeness of unity. Since by its wonderfully perfect roundness, its pure and mere simplicity without multiplicity—with which it was endowed from the beginning of its creation—it becomes openly known to us. For we see that a spherical body, no matter how great, when moved in every direction on a plane, rests only on a single tiny point. This point it has for its foundation, and like its hidden center, it makes it manifest everywhere upon the surface. So that from this, one could not wrongly conclude that every sphere is no larger than its center, since it reflects nothing other than that very thing; it is everywhere always like itself and enjoys the fellowship of unity. In that mystery lie hidden certain great secrets <note>original: "magnalia... arcana"</note>, both natural and supernatural, as well as much wisdom regarding the foundations of the arts and sciences. If the world, therefore, had remained in its union, there would have been no need for a doctor nor medicine. Thus, the end of all medicine is that the sick person be reduced to union, upon which we have founded the true principles of Natural Philosophy and Medicine. It remains that we carry out what was begun, with the help of the divine power, according to our strength.

Others wish it to denote order, as if it were said, "first of all." But these words, namely *in the beginning*, seem to be interpreted both for time and for order, outside every common mode and reason of speaking:

### PHYSICS

->336<-

Since Moses would have rather said *from the beginning* <note>original: "à principio"</note> in that sense of time, as some common interpretations also have it, or *among the first, at first* etc., they by no means seem to designate a place. For to wish to include God Himself within some place by the word of God is a sacrilege <note>original: "nefas," a term implying something forbidden by divine law</note>. Even before the creation of the world, no place could exist or be assigned. Indeed, the infinite amplitude of divine immensity has no boundaries; it follows that there is no "place" within the infinite, as place is defined by the circumscription of limits.

What, therefore, does Moses seem to mean by the "beginning"? Truly the same thing appears (spoken, however, under correction) as what Saint John in chapter 1, using a similar and not different phrase, expresses in the same sense; this one thing excepted: that his treatment is more Theological than this one, which seems to be primarily natural and **Physical**. Therefore, the Word of God—God—cannot be contained in any place, as was said above, but rather comprehends and encloses all things in Himself, so that He is excluded by nothing. 

Hence, if God was in the beginning of creation (which is piously to be believed), it is necessarily required that this "beginning" was not a place. Yet this beginning was *something* in which the eternal Word of God created heaven and earth. Saint John testifies that Moses spoke well and correctly, sounding the same as he did and with the same words. Otherwise, it could have been argued in this passage about improper phrasing or an error of the interpreters. It would be safest, therefore, not to understand it otherwise than as the words themselves sound, according to pure and sheer simplicity. 

The majority of interpreters assert that Moses adapts his speech to the weakness of the still-unrefined intellect of the Israelite people and the fledgling Church. We indeed concede this. But how it happened that he did not also instruct them plainly and simply about this "beginning," we do not see—unless perhaps because it was not fitting for the unworthy to be sharers of such a great mystery equally with others. It is to be believed, therefore, that Moses simply narrated all that he had heard from the Lord, and did not defraud his people: but if he attained anything through the intellect by a special gift of God, it is by no means doubtful that he also revealed to the teachers those things which are not openly written. 

Indeed, the sacred scriptures testify that distinguished minds existed at that time when Moses was teaching **Genesis** among the sons of Israel, who could have borne much greater things than the untaught people. But what he taught them privately, I leave to other men studious of such mysteries to judge concerning this matter. Which indeed would be very pleasing and delightful for me to hear along with the others who belong to this study. ### GENESIS.

...according to the small talent I have received from the Lord, for the sake of the community <note>original: "Reipub." abbreviated for "Republicae," here meaning the community of scholars</note> devoted to mysteries and secrets, to faithfully do everything I can. That teacher of ours, who can never be praised enough, **Paracelsus** <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), was a Swiss physician and alchemist who revolutionized science with his theories on nature and medicine</note>, also wrote previously at the very start of his *Philosophy to the Athenians* in nearly these words:

*There was one single beginning for all things that were created and are subject to corruption, in which all creatures were enclosed that the entire ethereal region holds: yet in such a way that there existed only one single matter for all, and not a separate one for each. This matter of all things is the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "mysterium magnum," a central Paracelsian concept referring to the primordial "mother" of all things</note>, something not perceptible, not of any essence or form, with no property, inclination, or the like; likewise without any color or elementary nature. As widely as the whole ethereal region extends, so vast was the sphere of the Great Mystery. This was the mother of the elements, stars, trees, creatures of flesh, and all other things sensible and insensible, and of all corruptible things. Each thing drew its origin from that mystery, not successively, but by a single creation only: substance, matter, form, essence, nature, and inclination were given by the Lord. The Great Mystery of the created had no likeness to anything, nor was it even "created" itself. It was nonetheless the **First Matter** <note>original: "materia prima," the formless state of perfect potentiality</note> from which all mortal and corruptible things arose. Therefore, this uncreated mystery was prepared by the highest **Craftsman** <note>original: "opifex," a term for God as the cosmic builder</note> God, so that there will never be anything like it, nor will it ever return to what it was. And even if all things are to return into their first essence, they will not return into the Great Mystery, nor into their first matter. For that which has been corrupted cannot be restored, nor is it restored, but it indeed returns into that very thing which existed before the Great Mystery. From that uncreated Great Mystery, many other special mysteries proceeded. Therefore, the founder of all things created the highest **Secret** <note>original: "arcanum"</note> and the highest good in this one uncreated thing all at once—not essentially nor qualitatively, but they were in it just as an invisible image is in some trunk of wood, before all the superfluous wood is removed: then finally, and not before, does it appear. The Great Mystery is to be judged no differently than that, in its separation, each of the fleshy and insensible things was brought back into its own form. Yet nothing of that which was cut away perished, nor was it cast aside, but everything was made into form and essence. Most admirable...*

Is it not known that two foundations are necessary in all man-made buildings: one consisting of the same matter from which they are made, and another upon which they rest, and without which they cannot endure? It is necessary, therefore, for these two to be joined together, even though they exist with different conditions and natures. Therefore, the principle of the world's creation is its foundation. Someone will perhaps ask: which of these should we establish as the principle? It has been answered more than enough by what has been said: namely, that both are joined to the other, so that they must either be one, or that which is built upon them must fall. Who can wonder enough that everything that can be called heavy and burdensome is carried by this one single point—by the power of the point alone without difficulty—and is firmly fixed, and is retained beyond all constancy, and sustained without any staggering?

Nothing is more like Divinity than a <term>center</term> <note>The author argues that because a geometric center point has no physical dimensions, it is the best metaphor for the nature of God.</note>. For because this center occupies no place due to its lack of quantity, it cannot be grasped, seen, or measured. # PHYSICS

Nevertheless, all things which do not fill a space because they lack corporeality—such as all spirits—can be comprehended through the **center**, because both are incomprehensible. Therefore, the words of creation, namely *in the beginning*, cannot be physically referred to a specific location, even if the "beginning" is related to the center.

Nor do I judge that the truly marvelous nature of the center should be passed over, regarding the formation of a sphere in Physics. For from that center, with equal lines flowing in every direction and touching one another, a solid spherical body arises; there are as many centers on the surface as there were lines flowing from the original center. It is clear from this that a sphere, no matter how huge, lacks a base and cannot rest on a flat surface unless it is held there. Therefore, we conclude without absurdity from these points that every sphere is born naturally and in a physical manner from its center, through the extended rays of its unmoving center reaching to a just surface—that is, one that is equally finished and determined. And although these things may seem quite crude <note>original: "rudia," meaning unrefined or basic</note> to you, as they have not been heard before, you should nevertheless consider them such that they provide more than enough contemplation and study for those endowed with a sharp mind throughout their entire lives; yet do not think they could attain even a thousandth part of the center’s nature. Indeed, whoever has a well-perceived knowledge of the nature of the center (as a certain most excellent man in attained philosophy <term>adepta Philosophia: a term used in alchemy and Hermeticism to refer to the highest level of natural and spiritual knowledge</term> says) could not be hidden in any way from anything natural in heaven or on earth. Therefore, as there is no end to the center, the infinite abyss of its virtues and secrets cannot be sufficiently described by any pen. For this reason, we must rest for a while from describing and treating it, until we have contemplated the other things concerning the creation of the world which we think are worthy of note in Physics. We will only add this: that a rough and unpolished image is proposed of the center, and of those things which can proceed from it, which we offer to be decorated by those who cultivate more refined ornament. It will be enough for us now if we have established some sort of path for those studious of the secrets of nature, by which the way to higher things may lie open. We are the doorkeepers; may you be the one, excellent reader, who penetrates more deeply into the hidden places, or the one whom He appoints, whose role it is to call each person to the duty and office of their life.

Creation is the work of God alone. For who else can summon matter out of no pre-existing material or substance? Certainly no angel or man. Furthermore, the excellence of any work is judged primarily by this: when the first and last things within it are seen to correspond to each other. The reason for this choice appears to us by a certain conjecture: because this element, compared to the others which are by nature fluid, mobile, and rare, is stable, firm, and solid, and more closely related to the center; and also it is more suitable and better known than the rest for bringing forth creatures necessary for human life and for supporting them.
