# PHILOSOPHY
<meta>catchword: Mixing</meta>

...from the seed into a large quantity, while maintaining the distinction of individual parts, through the nourishment and alterations of any medium into another quantity and form (these mediums and qualities existing in every alteration) into forms different from the first, until some being arises in a continuous quantity, forged from various and discrete parts into a single body, alive with soul and spirit. It happens no differently with the **spagyric fetus** <term>Spagyric fetus: A term for the alchemical product during its developmental stages, comparing the "growing" medicine to a biological embryo.</term>, which is generated from the **heaven** <note>original: "cœlo," referring here to the volatile, celestial spirit or the "Mercury of the Philosophers" that provides life to the matter</note> possessing a vegetative property; it pours the likeness of this property into the perfect and more-than-perfect medicine, just as a vegetative womb <note>original: "matrix"</note> does for the son it conceives and bears. It also retains that property just as its parent does. Likewise, the perfect and more-than-perfect medicine retain the property of their parents—namely, the heaven and the elements—and they pour this likeness of their perfection into external substances and transmute them into their own species. For this reason, **Vegetable Mercury** is said to be born from two substances, just as a woman conceiving the male seed takes on another form and a different virtue than she had before the beginning of conception. From the male seed, the elements in this art are considered to be the four appearing colors; likewise, they are considered in four other ways. First, as they are drawn from matter by the heaven. Second, as the simple elements of the heaven are separated from the coarser elements by the circle of rotation. In the third way, they exist naturally in forms and are joined with the heaven. In the fourth way, they are separated from the form and the heaven through the means of **alteration**, **mixing**, **dissolution**, and **generation**, by the mastery of the separation of their qualities; from these parts, only the airy portion is taken and augmented <note>original: "exuberatur," literally 'made to overflow' or enriched</note> through the artifice of rotation, and thus it is mixed with the forms in the heaven. It must be noted, therefore, that the elements can be drawn out of the forms through the heaven before the conjunction, so that their **First Matter** <term>First Matter: The "Materia Prima," the original, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made and to which they must be returned before transmutation.</term> or heaven, approaching more closely to the most general genus, may be obtained, etc.

**Dissolution** is the "knowledge" <note>original: "cognitio," often used euphemistically in Latin for sexual union</note> or the spagyric intercourse of the male with the female, the latter conceiving from the former all that it ought to conceive. Let this be the beginning of the particular generation, by which the effect of our spagyric marriage is perceived by the senses, and the union of the double seed into an embryo.

**Alteration** is the conversion of one thing into another through likeness. It is considered in two ways according to a double operation, insofar as it happens through itself. In the first way, forms are altered into the heaven, and the heaven into forms. In the latter way, it is understood that the forms and the heaven are so simply converted that they can be converted into a "third number"—namely, into the perfect and more-than-perfect medicine. These alterations or conversions are called **simple**. Others are found which occur by accident, as when a perfect medicine is made from imperfect things through projection, alteration, and transmutation.

### CHEMISTRY
#### Dd 3

**Mixing** <note>original: "Mixtio"</note> occurs from two colors, pale and azure, so that from them it may be known that the forms and the **heaven** <note>In alchemy, "heaven" (cœlum) often refers to the quintessence or the highly purified, volatile spirit that acts as a medium for the work.</note> are combined in the **greater work** <term>Greater Work: The *Magnum Opus*, or the full process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</term> without any other addition; just as in the generation of a human being, nothing else is added to the man, the woman, or their seeds. In this place, the marriage between the forms and the heaven occurs. Another mixing also takes place, in which air and fire—as mediums for the forms, the heaven, alteration, mixing, dissolution, and generation—are combined with the forms and the matter of the heaven.

**Digestion** <note>original: "Digeftio"</note> is the name given to the nourishment of the conceived seed by the seed, by which medium the **perfect medicine** <term>Perfect Medicine: A term for the Philosopher's Stone or the Elixir in its completed state, capable of healing metals or the human body.</term> and the more-than-perfect medicine arise. For it is necessary that the forms be digested in the heaven for so long until the "prior medicine" is reached, and thereafter, whenever it seems right to the craftsman, until the other, more perfect one is achieved.

From this it can be gathered that there is a twofold digestion: the prior, by which the transition is made from the forms and heaven to the perfect medicine; and the posterior, by which one must pass from this and the heaven to the more-than-perfect. Along this path, other necessary mediums are required, not unlike the prior ones—namely mixing, alteration, dissolution, generation, and operation—except that something more imperfect arises from the prior ones than from the posterior. But as soon as the saffron color <note>original: "croceus"</note> appears through digestion, it will denote the forms; but the azure color denotes our heaven; and the colors that are intermediate between these designate the medium of the conjunction of the heaven with the forms, connecting it to the perfect medicine, or those forms to the most perfect.

**Generation** is considered in various ways. Generally, it is the manifestation of hidden forms. In the first way, it is considered as the stage generating the perfect medicine from the heaven and the forms. In the second way, insofar as it generates the most perfect medicine from the perfect one and the heaven. In the third way, when it begins from dissolution through alteration and digestion to pass into the perfect medicine and reaches its limit there, attaining the end of the "lesser perfection"; or indeed when, passing from here, it acquires the final degree of the "greater perfection." In this latter case, it can easily be perceived that the **mastery** <note>original: "magifterium," referring to the refined skill or the completed alchemical process itself</note> of greater perfection is promoted by nature rather than by art; nonetheless, it is excited by art in the lesser perfection, in which art is more beneficial than nature. In the posterior mastery, generation occurs no differently than a fetus in a womb, or a bird in an egg: for which reason it is also called, in its own way, the **Philosophers' Egg** <term>Philosophers' Egg: The sealed glass vessel (hermetic seal) where the alchemical matter undergoes transformation, likened to a womb or an egg where life is incubated.</term>. This artifice can in no way be better understood than from the fact that it results from the mixing of matter with forms to produce precious stones—rubies, sapphires, and **pearls** <note>original: "uniones," a term for large, high-quality pearls</note>—which are in the womb of our philosophical heaven, through the mediation of generation with the same virtues that natural stones obtained from nature. From this it follows that this heaven can attract all the virtues existing in stones, by the power of unity or its own magnetic simplicity. In this way, you, the ingenious craftsman, will be able to [draw out] virtues from natural bodies...

# PHILOSOPHY

...to elicit the celestial virtues, and to enclose them within artificial virtues by the mediums of the operations of this art. For whatever is placed upon this **heaven** <note>original: "cœlo." In alchemy, the "heaven" refers to the quintessence or the highly purified, volatile spirit that acts as a container and medium for the transformation.</note> is dissolved; likewise, if things suited to the dissolved matter are added, that very thing which is desired will be made, even one thing from many. From that work indeed many things can be gathered which pertain to the work of composing precious stones, by the mixing of matter and form through waters, etc.

**Colors** <note>original: "Colores"</note> in this craft are visible changes, and the first of them is **black** <note>The stage of *Nigredo*, symbolizing death, putrefaction, and the stripping away of old forms.</note>: this indicates that the forms have lain with the heaven, and that the heaven has conceived an embryo in its womb. By this same color it is also demonstrated that the **dissolution** <term>Dissolution: The process of breaking down a solid substance into a liquid or primordial state.</term> has reached the limit of its perfection. Finally, as that blackness diminishes and **white** <note>The stage of *Albedo*, representing purification and the washing away of impurities.</note> gradually emerges, it is shown to us that nature, along with the heaven and the forms, is beginning the transition to a lesser perfection; and thereafter, with these and the heaven and form, to a greater one: at the end of which transition, **digestion** <note>original: "digeftio"</note> has its complete limit. 

But when [the white] begins to diminish through a greater excitation of the fire, and **saffron-yellow** <note>original: "croceus." This stage is often called *Citrinitas*, the yellowing that bridges the gap between white and red.</note> begins to arise, it is known that the parts and members are joined together in the **third number** <note>Likely referring to the chemical triad of Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt, or the union of Matter, Form, and Spirit.</note>, and are gathered into a continuous quantity, in such a way that the framework or binding of the members of our **infant** <note>The "infant" or "fetus" is a common alchemical metaphor for the developing Philosopher's Stone.</note> appears to our senses. For the seed is diffused through the whole substance of our **philosophical heaven**. Once this color has arisen, shortly afterward it seems to be gathered into a round shape not unlike the form of the moon, or enclosed by a circular line. 

As this color fades, **red** <note>The final stage, *Rubedo*, signifying the completed Stone and the height of its power.</note> arises, by which we are made more certain that the members or parts of our stone are gathered to perfection in the third number. Indeed, after the appearance of this color, it is certain that our infant is complete in body and in **vegetative power** <note>The basic level of life responsible for growth and nutrition in Aristotelian philosophy.</note>. From which time the craftsman must know the number of days within which our fetus was first led from the beginning of conception until the limit of the appearance of the red color, and without intermission apply a double length of time to it, but a little more vigorously. When this is complete, what was sought is acquired—namely, a hard stone wrapped in many superfluities, appearing not unlike a woman's fetus after birth. 

The mediums between the saffron and red colors are digestion, generation, and mixing, and those things which are perceived by the water, matter, form, and heaven; by their mingling, towards the end of those mediums, water, matter, and form appear without matter and heaven. For if the form and heaven were still in that place, some parts would by no means wish to be bound with the others, nor to be joined in the third number.

**Separation** <note>original: "Separatio"</note> is the extraction of virtues, which occurs by the motion of fire in this particular **mastery** <term>Mastery: Referring to the *Magisterium*, the specialized procedure or the secret knowledge of the alchemical art.</term>, by which heat the form, heaven, and elements are moved by accident and excited by alteration, mixing, generation, colors, digestion, separation, and operation toward a lesser or greater perfection. Because the stages and mediums, by separating themselves from others, enter into others, and through that operation of separation...

<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of alchemical transformation, moving from the appearance of colors to the underlying "virtues" or powers that drive these changes. It defines the specific roles of the alchemist (the "artist"), external heat, and the "philosophical heaven" in achieving the white and red stages of the Great Work.</meta>

# CHEMISTRY

...formal and material power <note>original: "virtus." In this context, it refers to the inherent active qualities or "soul" of a substance.</note> is drawn by this method from the forms and the **heaven** <note>original: "cœlo." In alchemy, the "heaven" refers to the quintessence or the highly purified, volatile spirit that acts as a medium for transformation.</note> toward a lesser perfection, and from there to a greater one. And in this way the forms, the heaven, or the "lesser perfect" change their simple forms into a greater or lesser perfection—existing within that which is less perfect—than the forms and the heaven possessed by themselves. When a greater perfection exists under another form, these perfections retain their own specific powers under a third form within the transforming **poison** <note>original: "veneno." Alchemists often used "poison" or "venom" to describe a potent, corrosive solvent or the transformative "mercury" that breaks down substances.</note>. If such an origin did not occur through this stated separation, there would be no alteration, nor generation, nor progression, but the work of nature would be destroyed in this **philosophical work**. This medium is the evidence of the simple elements actually existing in our heaven, along with the natural elements existing in their forms: likewise fire, air, water, and earth arise, and are also separated from the heaven into a mixture with the other things that have been mentioned; and all these things are indicated by **colors**. 

"Power" <note>original: "Potentia"</note> in this context is the same as alteration; and through this stage, all other stages and any mediums are understood to be present potentially in our **first chaos** <term>First Chaos: Also known as the *Materia Prima*, the raw, undifferentiated matter from which the philosopher's stone is made.</term>; and secondly, in the elements existing potentially in our matter. Therefore, this "power" is nothing other than the action of our heaven, which is discussed more extensively in the **work of stone-making** <note>original: "opere lapidifico"</note>, where it is said that many know how to prepare stones, but are ignorant of how to imbue them with natural virtues—of which, through which, and with which the completion of the stones and the increase of their perfection consists.

In this work, **Operation** is the excitation of **four colors** by which various modes of operations are designated. The **first color** denotes that the heaven has its action and operation upon the forms, or upon the "lesser perfect" and the form. The **second** indicates that external fire has an action upon the heaven, the forms, and the other elements, as well as the natural and actual mediums, through motion toward a lesser and greater perfection. The **third** shows that the forms or the "lesser perfect" have their own action upon the heaven, shaping it so that it may arrive at a lesser and greater perfection. The **fourth color** signifies the actions of the operations which the **artist** <note>The "artist" or "artifex" is the alchemist performing the work.</note> has over all those things mentioned above through the administration of fire—acting as the cause in the separation of the heaven and the operation of the forms. # PHILOSOPHY

...achieved. These colors, when reduced into a single one, signify the completion of the work and its perfection; namely, that of the **heaven** <note>original: "cœli." In this context, it refers to the "Philosophical Heaven," the purified celestial influence or volatile spirit within the chemical vessel.</note>, the elements, alteration, mixture, dissolution, generation, color, digestion, separation, operation, and through the means of fire. By this medium, it can be known that the substance has progressed from the heaven and **form** <note>original: "forma." The active, organizing principle that gives a substance its specific identity.</note> by the power of gradual operations. Whoever reaches this goal will far surpass all the world’s sages in doctrine and wisdom, as well as all physicians. For they will most easily cure not only the **leprosy of metals** <term>lepram metallorum: A metaphorical term for the impurities, corrosion, or "sickness" found in base metals like lead or iron that prevent them from being gold.</term>, but also all so-called incurable diseases of human bodies.

**Fermentation** <term>Fermentatio: In alchemy, this is the process of adding a "leaven" (the Stone) to a base substance to "ferment" it into a more perfect state, just as yeast transforms dough.</term> is properly called the multiplication of a lesser perfection and its advancement to a greater one; and this is done through the media of mixture, dissolution, alteration, generation, colors, and digestion, by composing the heaven, the form, and the "lesser perfect" into a mixture. This is administered through the **regimen of fire** <note>The specific, controlled sequence of heat levels required at different stages of the alchemical process.</note> for as long as it takes to pass through all the stated stages, and through generation and colors into a greater perfection—one far more powerful in quantity, quality, and virtue—leading toward the **red** and the **white** <note>The "White Work" (Albedo) produces silver, and the "Red Work" (Rubedo) produces gold and the universal medicine.</note> and toward the restoration of health for mankind. From these things, it is easily gathered that the "lesser perfect" passes into the "greater" by the aforementioned means: through the actions of the operations of the forms, the heaven, the elements, and by the fermentation, separation, operation, and fire through proper administration. Likewise, it is understood that the artist need only compose the "lesser perfect" once (unless he wishes otherwise), since it can be multiplied unto infinity and led to a greater state, and from that into another without end; no differently than the human race propagates its own species, with one always generating another as long as the age shall last. It seems not unlike flour, which is transmuted into infinite dough by its own ferment, becoming like the ferment itself. It should also be noted that the "lesser perfect" proceeds into the "greater" unto infinity, with form and heaven acting as the ferments—a fact which has been known to very few artists until now.

The **Greater Perfect** <note>original: "Perfectum majus." This refers to the final, most potent state of the Philosopher's Stone.</note> is the ultimate perfection in the Great Work. It is composed of and consists of four colors, two of which denote that the four elements exist within it with every perfection of virtue and the conclusion of number into unity, as appears in the colors green and red. The remaining colors signify that the heaven and form exist there with all perfection and the simplicity of unity, through the mastery of the four elements and the media which have been mentioned. From this final stage, it can be perceived that the "Greater Perfect" has the power of multiplying its species in two ways and of generating something similar to itself: namely, in **virtue** <note>Inherent power or medicinal potency.</note> through the aforementioned operations, and in external substance through **transmutation**. It is much more perfect than the "Lesser," since it exists for virtues and operations, both in the transmutation of metals and in the cure of even desperate diseases.

...since through sulfur and orpiment <note>original: "auripigmentum," a deep yellow-orange arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment and in alchemical recipes.</note>, burnt copper <note>original: "æs uftum." **Dissolution** is the hiding of the manifest form of the aforementioned bodies, not by itself, but by means of the said "key," which is very compatible with the bodies: just as we see water being corrupted by fire by means of the air, without which it is not raised into vapors. It differs from the "greater dissolution" in that in this case, only the form and the less perfect things are resolved; whereas in the other, any metallic bodies are.

**Evacuation** is nothing other than the extraction of the hidden spirits from their bodies, so that one or the other of the forms may be shaped into informing oils <note>These are "essential" oils or essences that give a substance its specific properties or "form."</note>, and in this way, through fermentation and inceration <note>The process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency.</note>, they may pass into the perfect work. **Multiplication** is nothing else than the iteration and continuation of evacuations. Through this operation, we provoke the six bodies <note>Refers to the six metals known besides gold (Silver, Copper, Iron, Tin, Lead, and Mercury).</note> to nausea, and to vomiting our offspring <note>Alchemical "offspring" or "fetus" refers to the emerging Philosophers' Stone or the refined essence being born from the base matter.</note> from their bowels.

**Spirit** is exuberant quicksilver <note>original: "argentum vivum exuberatum." This refers to mercury that has been highly refined or "animated" for alchemical work.</note>, and it is the spirit of the bodies already separated by complete evacuation.

**Sulfur of nature** is the spirit of the bodies exalted through sublimation <note>The process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again.</note> into a most excellent salt of four colors: namely pale, green, black, and red. **Tinctures** are the colors appearing in the work in various ways: first green and yellow; second red and yellow, green and black. **Oil** is a form having a double color, green and saffron, by which it is indicated that it is produced from perfect bodies through their appropriate media.

**Inceration** <note>The process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency, often to prepare it for "ingression" or fusion.</note> is a fermentation, or rather the "informing" <note>Giving a specific "form" or nature to raw matter.</note> of the offspring of imperfect things so that they may receive the condition of a perfect fetus <note>The "fetus" or "offspring" in alchemy refers to the developing Stone or perfected metal within the vessel.</note>.

**Sublimation** is a certain refinement which happens in two ways: into an impalpable powder, or into a liquid. The **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold and offering spiritual perfection.</note> is the end and the perfection of all imperfect bodies and operations, in which they remain permanent, just as salamanders rest in fire <note>In ancient and medieval folklore, the salamander was a creature believed to be born from and nourished by fire, symbolizing the Stone's ability to withstand the furnace.</note>. This is a "third thing," consisting of matter and a form that is above nature, yet forged through the mediation of nature and the industry of the craftsman.

**Elements** are considered in two ways in this place: in the first way, as an external active fire; in the second way, as an internal agent, like that which is drawn from perfect things into oil, and so on.

Now you have, best of readers, those things which contribute to **spagyric knowledge** <note>original: "cognitionem spagiricam." The third degree of meditative philosophy is called **philosophic love**, produced from knowledge; it is the union of secrets from one back into one through peace. Indeed, peace is the concord of parts within the whole through union. God loves union above all, because He is one, and whatever He ever created, He enclosed under union. From the one determined thing, made through one indefinite thing, all things proceed which are finite, and again each thing tends toward that one by natural instinct. If any should decline from this, they are judged by philosophers to be held under the **binary secret** <note>The "binary" or "dyad" represents division, duality, and the fall from original unity.</note>, and must be reduced back to union through the **ternary** <note>The number three, symbolizing the reconciliation of opposites into a new unity.</note>.

God created heaven and earth and all things in them, united together in a hidden way, but separate in a manifest way. And as we said before regarding **Genesis**, under the name of "earth" the elements are contained, which are embraced by heaven with such a love of covenant as one can rarely see among other creatures. ...there is a natural love <note>original: *amor naturalis*; a philosophical concept where substances are drawn together by inherent sympathy.</note> between the primary parts of inanimate things, as well as an enmity, just as there is in the three primary parts of man mentioned before. Therefore, it is your task to make peace between enemies, so that friends may come together as one. In all imperfect bodies that fall short of their ultimate perfection, enmity and friendship are simultaneously innate. If this enmity is removed by human ingenuity or industry, it is necessary to arrive at the ultimate perfection of union through **Art** <note>In this context, "Art" refers to Alchemy or Spagyrics—the intentional manipulation of nature.</note>.

You shall, therefore, separate the parts from each body by fire; cleanse the impure parts, and afterwards mix the pure with the pure. By first sublimating the heavier things with the lighter, it will come to pass that the fixed is rendered volatile, and the corporeal is made spiritual. In short, there is a philosophically natural love within the elements; embrace this through Art if you truly desire to be a **Physician** <note>original: *Physicus*; here meaning a "natural philosopher" or one who studies the laws of nature.</note> and not a neglector of nature—or rather, a destroyer of it.

Just as we have heard that concord is necessary in both supernatural and natural matters, in spagyric <term>Spagyrics: the alchemical process of separating and then recombining the constituents of a substance to reach a higher state of purity.</term> matters there is also a certain wonderful coherence to be observed among the mediating instruments, similar to the coherence between intellectual and sensory things. Although this must be distinguished from our form (which we otherwise call "Heaven"), nevertheless, one cannot persist without the other in the spagyric art.

For the form "Heaven" is the principle and the sensory medium that generates, nourishes, and causes growth or vegetation, moving the elements toward a specific generation—just as the greater heaven moves the lower things. From the forming form—which it acquires through the **vegetable form** and holds bound in an indissoluble knot—it causes the specific object sought to multiply within extrinsic substances. So it is with many other things hidden in the progress of the Art, which are possible for the craftsman to know and effect. 

However, the form which is man’s **intellect** is the beginning, middle, and end in all preparations: and this is denoted by the **saffron color** <note>original: *croceo colore*; yellow or gold, often symbolizing the Soul, the Sun, or the final stages of the alchemical Work.</note>. This indicates that man is the greater and principal form in the spagyric work, and a form more powerful than "Heaven" itself. The remaining forms are lesser than these and of lesser perfection. Likewise, the equalized mixture of saffron color with **green** <note>Green often represents "raw" nature or the "Green Lion," the solvent that dissolves matter.</note> indicates the existence of greater or lesser concord regarding the conflict within the equality of the ultimate goal. For one of these three forms cannot be absent without all of them failing at once. If "Heaven" were lacking, the generation of the elements would fail, and a loss of both lesser and greater perfection would follow.

Therefore, the intellectual form, the vegetable form, and the form of motion must be so joined by the intellect that each is conditioned by the other: and so it proceeds through the remaining levels and means until the greater perfection is reached. <meta>This page continues the technical application of the alchemical principles introduced previously. Having established that "Art" (Alchemy) is required to harmonize the natural love and enmity within matter, the author now describes the specific stages of motion—the "steps"—required to bring a substance to its final, perfected state. # PHILOSOPHY

...of this art, moving each one through all stages toward another, until the very last and the end of the work. Therefore, movement can be called the form of motion that excites all stages in order, until perfection is reached. But form and matter are substantial principles much greater than the accidental ones; for the latter are only changes in the work, such as colors, alteration, digestion <note>The process of slow heating to mature a substance.</note>, etc. The truth of this matter is demonstrated through the "more or less" perfect, by the immensity of their transforming power, rather than in accidental stages. Nonetheless, the beginning, middle, and end that were mentioned are equal because of the similarity of the same end toward which all things tend, as if by a wondrous chain. 

To have a greater understanding of what has been said, we must necessarily come to the universal practice of this art. Pour such a quantity of the **spagyric heaven** <note>original: *cœlum spagiricum*; likely referring to a high-quality distilled solvent, such as a "quintessence" or pure spirit of wine.</note> over either of the forms so that it stands four fingers-width above it. Keep this whole mixture placed in **dung** <note>original: *fimum*; animal manure was used as a source of gentle, constant "natural" heat for fermentation and digestion.</note> for six natural days, or until the form is converted into water. Afterward, having removed the vessel and placed it in **ashes** <note>original: *cineres*; an ash bath provided a higher, drier heat than dung.</note>, let that which has been dissolved be emptied out by distillation. 

Pour as much of the "heaven" as before onto the dregs, and keep them together in dung for a month and a half, or longer, in **putrefaction** <note>The alchemical stage of "death" and breakdown, often associated with the color black, necessary before a substance could be reborn.</note>; finally, let all the liquor be distilled in a secret furnace until it no longer drips. Next, distill in the ashes a water thicker than the previous one, which they call **air** <note>original: *aër*; here referring to a specific volatile state or "spirit" of the substance.</note>. Again, pour the same amount of "heaven" as before onto the nearly dry dregs, putrefied in dung for the same amount of time as before, and distill through ashes into "air" until it no longer wishes to drip. 

Afterward, let there be a repetition of pouring the "heaven" over the earth like rain, with a weight equal to that above, and for the same amount of time: after it has putrefied in dung, let it be distilled again through ashes until no more "air" comes out. Finally, pour the entire quantity of this "air" onto the dregs (or first grind them very well upon a marble stone), and let both the "air" and **fire** <note>original: *ignis*; the most subtle, hot, and active part of the substance.</note> be distilled together from the putrefied matter in the ashes within a closed vessel for forty days; meanwhile, care must be taken that the dregs do not turn red from too fierce a fire before the proper time. 

Then you shall separate the "air" from the "fire" by means of dung, and if the heat of a bath <note>original: *balneum*; a water bath or *bain-marie*.</note> is not enough, the slow heat of the ashes will supply it; keep both separately. Then pour the "air" back onto its own earth, and having digested it in dung for fifteen days, you shall distill the "air" and "fire" from there together, and separate them as above by the bath, storing each with its like. Repeat these pourings, **burials** <note>original: *inhumationes*; the act of placing the vessel in dung or earth to maintain heat.</note>, and distillations until no more "fire" comes forth from the earth, and the earth itself is black or reddish. 

Finally, from the "air" digested in a dung bath for eight days, distill by that same heat whatever can ascend: pour this distilled liquid back onto its dregs, digest as before and distill, pour back again, digest, distill, etc., repeating the same process seven times. Thus far the for-

# CHEMISTRY

...a triangle is formed from air, heaven, and dung, in the center of which is the **soul of air** <note>The "soul" (anima) refers to the extracted essence or volatile spirit of the element.</note>. Having also performed the preliminary operations in dung, you will be able to convert fire into the **soul of fire**, and form another triangle from heaven, dung, and fire. When all these things are finished, the elemental wheel is completed by fixation, and by the overflowing of air and fire through **corruption** <note>In alchemy, "corruption" is not a negative term; it refers to the breaking down of a substance's form so it can be reborn into a higher state.</note>. Afterward, once the earth has been evacuated until it is deserted and converted into the **sulfur of nature**, let a triangle be formed from earth, dung, and ashes, in the center of which will stand the soul of the earth. The wheel of corruption is not finished before this; its instruments are heaven, dung, the **secret furnace** <note>original: *furnus secretus*; a specialized alchemical furnace designed for precise heat control over long periods.</note>, the heat of ashes, and so on. Now, finally, one must proceed to the **wheel of generation**.

To make a compound of fire and air for the **Sun** <note>Sun/Sol refers to the production of Gold.</note>, take four parts of fire and mix them with fifteen parts of air; having been digested together for fifteen days, let them be distilled by means of dung. You shall repeat this digestion and distillation so many times until there remains at the bottom of the vessel a liquid like a shining oil, which is a compound of air and fire, and is called **slime** <note>original: *limus*; a technical term for the primordial, viscous matter that serves as the foundation for the Stone.</note>. By the same process, you will convert fire and earth into their own compound, so that a double triangle is now formed: the first from fire, air, dung, and ashes, in the middle of which the compound of fire and air will **rejoice** <note>original: *jubilabit*; a poetic alchemical term indicating the successful and "active" union of substances.</note>; the second from fire, earth, dung, and ashes, in the middle of which will stand the compound of earth and fire. 

Now finally, take one part of the compound of fire and air, to which you will mix a sixth part of **heaven** <note>likely referring to the pure solvent or "quintessence" mentioned on the previous page.</note>, and keep it in digestion for thirty days. In this manner, you will have formed a triangle from heaven, the compound of fire and air, and dung, in the center of which is found this **greater perfection** which transforms things into the **red** <note>The *Rubedo* or Red stage, representing the final perfection of the Philosopher's Stone for transmuting metals into gold.</note>, taking its rise and origin from heaven, the compound of fire and air, and from dung. When you have done this same thing with the compound of fire and earth, joining to it one and a half parts of heaven, you will have another triangle from heaven, the compound of earth and fire, and dung, in the center of which will stand the **lesser perfection**, transmuting things into the **white** <note>The *Albedo* or White stage, used for transmuting metals into silver.</note>, etc. 

If, however, you do not wish to mix in the heaven, so that you may avoid immense labor, you shall **cerate** <note>original: *cerabis*; to treat a substance until it becomes soft and pliable like wax.</note> the elements with the compounds previously given, until they flow like wax. Keep this cerated mass in digestion for ten days; afterward, once extracted, cerate it again as before, repeating this until, drop by drop, you perceive it has become easily liquefied. Keep this matter very well closed in a **philosophical vessel** <note>A specialized glass flask, such as a retort or a sealed "Pelican" vessel.</note> in the secret furnace for one hundred and fifty or more days, until you see the work completed by the signs described below. 

This process is the best in the **Greater Practice**, using the method of the **Lesser Work**. Note that the creation can also happen with fire and air separately before the creation, while they are not yet reduced into one. Thus far is completed the **wheel of generation**, through which the practitioner acquires the desired goal, God granting it. From these two "slimes," various things can be made in the **spagyric work** <note>Spagyrics involves the separation, purification, and recombination of plant or mineral components.</note>, according to its breadth, as in the first royal practice, and in the [practice] of ceration...

# PHILOSOPHIA

...by the skill of the proper **foliated earth** <note>original: *terra foliata*; the purified solid residue of the alchemical work, often described as "leafy" or flaky in texture.</note>, or of the elements, by first waxing it with air and fire, or with the aforementioned slimes made from air and fire: in which skill the wheel of generation reaches its final end, the sign of which in us is the **red triangle**. Therefore, the beginning of the work is **corruption** <note>The breakdown of a substance's previous form.</note> and the end is **generation**, by which operations one quality is destroyed and another is introduced through generation, just as by corrupting water and generating earth: then, by concealing this [earth] and manifesting fire and air, until the more and less perfect arise through their mediums, which are the heats of dung, of ashes, and of the **secret furnace**, by which water is converted into earth, and this into air and fire.

Earth is therefore the medium between water, fire, and air; and dung, ashes, and the secret furnace stand as the medium through which fire and air are converted into the **soul of fire** and the **soul of air** <note>The "soul" (anima) refers to the extracted essence or volatile spirit of the element.</note>. On account of this, fire and air are the medium between the earth itself, the soul of fire, and the soul of air. Next, dung, ashes, the secret furnace, and the **heavens** <note>original: *coelum*; in this context, it refers to the highest part of the distillation apparatus or a specific high-heat stage.</note> are the medium through which the soul of fire and the soul of air are converted into a compound of fire and air, and into a compound of earth and fire. By this reasoning, the heavens are the medium between the soul of fire, the soul of air, the compound of air and fire, and the compound of fire and earth. Likewise, dung, ashes, and the secret furnace are the medium through which the compound of fire and air, and the compound of earth and fire, are joined to the elements. Equally, the compound of fire and air, and the compound of fire and earth, are the medium between the soul of fire, the soul of air, and the lesser and greater perfection.

After having heard concerning the universal practice of the **greater spagyric work** <note>The "Great Work" (Magnum Opus) aimed at the creation of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, let us also come to a certain general practice of the **lesser work**. Once the dissolution of the body is completed, let the vessel be placed for distillation at the same heat; it will lose the key and be reduced to earth. Allow this earth, after being ground very well upon a marble stone, to be resolved into water by itself. Where the earth is certainly dry, let it be sprinkled with a small amount of the key, and after three days it will begin to resolve into a **composite water** containing the four elements. Distill this water through a filter, and whatever remains undissolved should be dissolved again as before and filtered, repeating this until a sufficient quantity of water is obtained. # CHEMICA

According to this process, the extreme and middle principles of this art are applied to whatever **spagyric work** <term>opus spagiricum: alchemical work involving the separation and recombination of purified essences</term> you desire.

Now that the third step of the **spagyric scale** <note>A metaphorical ladder or series of stages in alchemical practice, often linking physical laboratory work with spiritual growth.</note>—which is called **philosophical love** <note>original: *amor philosophicus*; likely referring to the attraction and union of chemical principles, or the devotion of the practitioner.</note>—is finished, we reach the fourth step of the meditative scale, which is called **frequency** <note>In the sense of "constancy" or "regularity."</note>, and the perseverance of the love conceived toward the truth. For there is no other approach to the virtues than through diligence. If the earth is not constantly cleared of the weeds <note>original: *lolio*; literally "tares" or "darnel," common weeds in grain fields.</note> it produces on its own, instead of sweet herbs and flowers, it will produce nothing for us but thistles and nettles. 

It is no different regarding the animal man or his **corporeal soul** <note>The aspect of the soul tied to bodily functions and worldly desires.</note>. For this reason, it was given to us as a colony <note>The author views the human body and soul as a territory that must be settled and governed by reason.</note>. Whatever grows in it beyond the divine planting already performed long ago must be uprooted. Nor can we tame it better than by first of all removing excess <note>original: *crapulam*; usually referring to the "hangover" or physical sickness resulting from over-indulgence.</note> itself, which brings on sleepiness and laziness. We shall also remove idleness, so that the most powerful root of vices may wither within us. Let nothing be granted to the body beyond necessity, for whatever is in excess will grow into a vice. 

If the soul neglects to correct its body, it will go ill for it because of that, since reason was given to the soul primarily to be turned to its own uses, which is the true **knowledge of God**. Therefore, the soul is to its body like a teacher; if he does not correct his student, he will be punished along with him without mercy. This discipline is not unlike the care of gardens, which must be maintained with a double effort: namely, first by eradicating the useless weeds growing over them, lest they suppress the growth of the good ones; likewise, by utterly casting out and excluding wicked thoughts, enmities, and other things of that kind from the soul, and by restraining the body from every evil work. 

Nor is it fitting for a teacher to teach one thing and do something else contrary to his own principles. What if he gives his student an occasion for sinning through his own example? Why then should he scold him? The body contemplates nothing, but the soul carries out the silent operations of the imagination, which the body then tries to execute in imitation of the pattern; for the conception belongs to the soul, but the execution to the body. Let us see, therefore, that we do not attribute more to the body than it is capable of. Although the body itself is more prone to executing the soul's wicked conceptions and delights in them more than in good ones: if we substitute these [good ones] in place of those cast-off [bad ones], it will be able to work nothing but good, or to desist from all evil. This is one method of conquering the body; hear the second...

Indeed, through familiarity, we are made similar in both will and character to that which we are familiar with, so that we even communicate with it in every action and desire. Likewise, in any art, through frequent use we are made ready, habituated with ease, and delighting in constancy. What does it profit one wishing to learn the art of baking <note>original: *pistoria martem* - likely a transcription error for *pistoriam artem*.</note> merely to have seen a baker working very often, unless he puts his own hand into the dough and repeats the work as many times as needed, until, having become a practiced and ready baker, he is able to teach others the art he professes? ### CHEMISTRY

->the mind,<-

surpassing the mind, body, and age of men, it is granted to only one among hundreds of myriads to conquer—that is, to reach the perfect goal of the art. Truly, some secrets of nature and certain mysteries can be uncovered with the greatest zeal and labor, which contribute to medical matters far more than any other things found outside said art. But in truth, to find that **universal medicine** <note>The *medicina universalis* or Philosopher's Stone, believed to cure all diseases and perfect all matter.</note> mentioned above has happened to very few—indeed, almost none so far—and then only as a miracle. It happens only to those who, by the grace of a merciful God, have first been able to restore themselves into a certain likeness of that which they desire: that is, those who have cleansed their bodies from impurity through the mind, and at last have removed all clouds of the mind and body alike.

I advise any investigators of this art to pray to God assiduously, to study, and to work; it cannot be otherwise than that they will achieve what they ask for in the name of Jesus from the **Giver of Lights** <note>A biblical title for God from James 1:17: "Every good gift... comes down from the Father of lights."</note>. But first, let them consider what it means to ask the Father in the Son: it is truly nothing else than to demand only that which is done for the glory of the Father and the Son. Many are accustomed to desire what seems useful to themselves, but they receive from God nothing except what is truly useful. God aids diligent and frequent efforts and despises the negligent. Thus, let us love the good so that we do not desire the evil.

It remains for us to pass on to <term>spagyric</term> <note>The alchemical practice of separating, purifying, and recombining materials to create medicines.</note> frequency in this manner: namely, that we ruminate upon those things said above. Therefore, when Nature breaks down any individual thing, she first putrefies it; afterwards, she separates the compound elements from it which are more closely joined within it; later, she brings each of these to its highest simplicity, and finally to its **first matter** <note>original: *materia prima*; the formless, primal substance from which all things are created.</note>. When this is done, the **wheel of corruption** is complete, and from the first matter, the **wheel of generation** takes its beginning, passing toward the simple elements. Finally, through the mixing of these, compound elements arise, from which the "elementated" subject is made according to its own species and form, under which the elements are drawn into the composition of the individual.

Therefore, the <term>spagyric</term> craftsman must observe this process, so that where Nature ends, he begins with a backward step through the rotation of corruption—that is, moving from the end through the middle toward the beginning of the wheel of corruption, employing the means which are <term>calcination</term> <note>The reduction of a substance to ash through high heat.</note>, <term>dissolution</term> <note>Dissolving a solid into liquid.</note>, <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The rotting of matter, seen by alchemists as the death of the old form preceding a new life.</note>, <term>division</term> <note>The separation of the pure from the impure.</note>, <term>purification</term>, etc. Next, one must come to the **wheel of generation**, whose means are <term>mixing</term>, <term>waxing</term> <note>original: *inceratio*; the process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a wax-like consistency.</note>, and <term>cooking</term> <note>original: *decoctio*; the application of steady heat to mature the substance.</note>, which, when best arranged, are the instruments of the "spagyric offspring." When these are performed in that manner, the craftsman will have what he desires.

The **Form** of this work is considered in three ways. First, as the First Cause; second, as the craftsman; third, as any other of the means.

The **Matter** is also considered in three ways: First, as the subject from which the <term>Mercury</term> <note>The transformative, volatile principle in alchemy.</note> of the art is drawn. Second, for the elements. Third, for the <term>sulfur</term> <note>The active, combustible principle or "soul" of the substance.</note> of nature.

### PHILOSOPHY

The **Sky** <note>original: *Cælum*; in an alchemical context, this usually refers to the volatile spirit or the upper part of the distilling apparatus where vapors collect.</note> also has a triple consideration: First, as the greater sky; Second, as **vegetable mercury** <term>Mercurius vegetabilis; a vital, spirit-like solvent believed to be extracted from organic matter</term>; Third, as the **soul of metals**.

**Elements** are considered in two ways in this place: First, simply; Second, in a composite manner.

**Power** or **alteration** differs in as many ways as there are different mediums.

**Mixture** has a fourfold meaning: First, the sky with form; Second, air with water; Third, water with fire; Fourth, air with water and the sky.

**Dissolution** has only one consideration, which is between the sky and forms.

**Generation** has a twofold meaning: The former by which the elements are generated; the latter by which the **spagyric offspring** <term>fœtus spagiricus; the term "spagyric" refers to the alchemical process of separating and recombining parts to create a perfected substance; the "offspring" is the resulting product.</term> is generated from these and the sky.

**Colors** also have a twofold meaning: The former in the evacuation of bodies and the rectification of elements; the latter in the generation of the spagyric offspring.

The **less perfect** has only one [consideration], as is clear from the senses.

**Fermentation** is triple: First, from virtue; second, from quantity; Third, from both together.

**Separation** also has a triple operation: First, between the qualities of the elements; Second, of their purification and fixation; Third, of the vegetable mercury and the **dregs** <note>original: *fæcum*; the solid waste or sediment remaining after a process.</note>.

**Operation** has as many meanings as there are mediums of this art.

The **more perfect** has a single one, like the less perfect, as is clear from the senses.

The principles and mediums of **Philosophy** are in all the principles and mediums of this art, such as the motion of the sphere, which is to be considered as a form containing all natural instincts and appetites.

The most subtle and powerful medium in the work is the **Reiteration of the wheel of the corruption of metals**, which occurs as follows: With the forms thus placed in the sky, inhumed, dissolved, and evacuated through the practice of the "brief art" <note>likely a reference to the *Ars Brevis*, a simplified or condensed method of alchemical practice</note> until one reaches the **sulfur of nature** in the metals, then the wheel of corruption is finished.

**Reiteration** occurs when the **sublimated earth** is placed into the sky and is dissolved therein by **putrefaction** <note>The intentional breaking down of matter through heat and moisture to allow for new life/form to emerge.</note> and division. After the air, fire, and water have been evacuated, let the craftsman again reduce the earth to its purest sublimation. When this is finished, the **wheel of generation** follows with its own principles and mediums until it is led to the end. This operation is more subtle than others; although it is longer, it is nonetheless more perfect. By this path, the less perfect—which is the unfermented offspring—is converted into the greater and fermented spagyric offspring through the [separation] <meta>catchword "rum se-" suggests the next word is *separationem* (separation).</meta>

### CHEMISTRY

->Ee 3<-
<meta>catchword: Resolution-</meta>

...their separation and composition, as described below. Nature in no way allows elements to be separated on their own, for in that way each would remain alone, possessing only a single quality, and would have no appetite for generation, which is contrary to nature.

The separation of elements, therefore, is the predominance and victory of one over and upon another, mixed in some specific way rather than being truly divided. Now, the color of fire is red; but before reaching its sphere, one passes through the sphere of air. Before redness appears, a clear and transparent lemon-yellow <note>original: *citrinus*</note> color manifests, because it consists of fire mixed with air. Furthermore, before arriving at the sphere of air, one must make a passage through the sphere of water; for this reason, the white color appears watery and brilliant. But because earth is the center and the principle from which the ascent must be made, while the **spagyric offspring** <term>fœtus spagiricus; the product of alchemical separation and recombination</term> is still in its sphere, the black color proper to the earth appears within it. Note, therefore, the separation of these elements and their subsequent conjunction back into one—that is, into fire.

Likewise, if before the black color has appeared, red or white or any other color appears, believe for certain that the operation of the offspring has been destroyed, due to the destruction of the intermediate stages. A difference is likewise to be noted between the **elixir** and the **stone**, regarding the raw and the cooked. For the elixir is a medicine composed of air, water, and earth—therefore leading only to the white <note>The "white work" or *albedo* is a major stage in alchemy, preceding the final red stage.</note> stage. If a body resolved into water is red, it reflects the color of the most excellent carbuncle <note>a deep red gemstone</note>, when it has been converted into a composite of the soul of fire and air, and into a composite of earth and fire. But if it is white, it will bring forth a green color mixed with blackness.

Various errors are also to be noted by craftsmen. The first and most significant consists in this: when they do not know how to imitate nature. The second is that they sometimes judge the beginning of the stone to be its end, and think they have finished where they have scarcely begun, as in the false opinion of the **red triangle** <note>likely an alchemical symbol or a specific stage in the geometric representation of the Great Work</note>. For the composition of the **greater stone** lasts two years for those who have never composed it before; however, for the experienced, it takes one year and three months. There are several branches in the breadth of the art which are completed in four or six months; if the craftsman can find these, it is well indeed; if not, let him deplore the smallness of his own intellect's capacity, since they are described clearly enough everywhere. Now we must come to the greater differences.

**Form** is twofold: simple and composite. **Simple** is absolute unity and the singularity of its own thing, consisting in itself and not with another. **Composite** is the union of its four primordial chambers.

**Matter** consists of the four elements: either simply, as signified by the first form; or compositely, as denoted by the second.

The **vegetable solvent** <term>Menstruum vegetabile; a vital, spirit-like solvent believed to be extracted from organic matter</term>, which is called the **sky** or the **philosophical key**, is of two kinds: one is resolving, while the other is referable <note>original: *referabile*; likely meaning a substance that can be brought back to its original state or related to a specific result</note>.

**Separation of elements**, **spagyric offspring**, **elixir**, **stone**, **red triangle**, **vegetable solvent**, **philosophical key**

# PHILOSOPHY

<page-num>438</page-num>

->Ee 3<-
<meta>catchword: Credi-</meta>

The **resolutive agent** <term>resolutivum; a substance used to dissolve or break down matter into its components</term> is something celestial; the other kind is not, but is instead more corporeal. The celestial one is the **fifth essence** <term>essentia quinta; the quintessence, the purest and most potent form of a substance</term>, or that of **tartar** <note>original: *tartari*; referring to the salts found in wine casks, highly valued in alchemy</note>, from whose nature its power to dissolve is brought into action. Alternatively, it is defined as follows: it is "burning water" <note>original: *ardens aqua*; typically referring to distilled alcohol or a potent acidic solvent</note> perfectly rectified, by whose power any bodies are dissolved, putrefied, and rendered purer; their elements are separated and exalted into a **miraculous salt** <note>original: *sal mirabile*</note> and earth, through the highly active power it possesses. Whoever thinks there is any other such water is ignorant and foolish. 

The **resolvable solvent** <term>menstruum; in alchemy, a solvent that can dissolve solids and extract their "essence"</term> is a potential vapor existing in any metallic body, joining sulfur and quicksilver <note>original: *argentum vivum*; mercury</note> together, without which nothing is brought into action. Finally, it is also defined thus: it is the medium joining imperfect and perfect metals into the **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone</note>. This resolutive solvent is "hot" up to the second point of the fourth degree; therefore, its power must be increased with "hot" plants <note>According to the humoral theory of the time, certain plants possessed an energetic "heat" regardless of their physical temperature</note> up to the final point of the same degree, such as wild celery, monkshood, oleander, cashew, black pepper, pellitory, euphorbium, and so on; without these, it only dissolves over a long period. 

Thus far we have spoken of the **fourth degree of the meditative scale**, namely: frequency, which works to create familiarity, likeness, and communion of the soul with the divine spirit. We have also spoken of the comparison made to it through diligence in the **spagyric work** <term>spagirico; the alchemical art of "separating and recombining" to achieve purity</term>, which brings forth readiness and an ease of habit with the greatest delight. 

Now, however, we come to the **fifth degree**, which is **Virtue**. Let us, therefore, hear of this. The virtue of things is the center and truth of each thing: this [truth] is efficacy known through experience; but that [virtue] is celestial influence. Whatever does not come from heaven cannot be called virtue, but is rather an image of it, and often a false one. 

In former times, those philosophers ignorant of God wished to depict the virtues, but they did so falsely because they did not understand His Son, in whom all the virtues of God are revealed. Their disciples are also accustomed to dividing virtues into Theological and Ethical parts, not considering that these latter qualities should in no way be called virtues unless they come from God. 

The courage of the Romans against their enemies was actually stubbornness; their magnanimity was pride; their prudence was fraud and deceit; their abstinence was an ambition for honors. And so it was with the rest: they were vices rather than virtues, because they were performed not for the glory of God, but for the glory of men and themselves. 

Christian philosophers of every profession hold only truth to be virtue, which they divide into **faith, hope, and charity**. In these three, and in them alone, does all truth consist, as well as every virtue; outside of them, there is nothing but falsehood. Now, **Faith** is the certainty of those things which are heard and not seen. For this reason, it was said by Paul that "faith comes from hearing," because that which is seen is not faith, but rather a certain knowledge demonstrated as if to the eye. In Holy Scripture, we have testimony of this from the Gospel:

"You have believed," says Christ, "because you have seen: Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed." <note>original: "Credidisti (inquit Christus) quia vidisti: Beati qui non viderunt & crediderunt." A reference to John 20:29.</note> Hope is the stimulus of faith toward the certainty of future truth, and it is a firm constancy. For unless one knows for certain that they will acquire what they pursue, their effort grows quite cold; but when they have confirmed their hope through faith—and vice versa—aided finally by constant practice and ingenuity, there is nothing they cannot achieve. Furthermore, in this context, it is certain that faith is proven through **charity** <term>charitas; in this sense, selfless love or active virtue</term>, just as faith can work for good or ill depending on whether it is moved by a good or evil impulse. Charity, therefore, is faith made absolute in action. Who else ought to judge true faith than the person in whom that faith resides? And does it not say that faith must be known by its works? 

Some people, understanding the matter well (in my opinion), have said that charity must begin with oneself. This can be interpreted in the following way: a Christian must first acquire a habit of this kind of virtue through the constant practice of love toward God and neighbor, before he is able to exercise it toward others in action. Learn then, O mind, to work true charity within your own body by restraining its vain appetites—which are sown in the soul by the evil one. In this way, your body will gradually become ready to join you in all good things. 

Not otherwise, in natural things, there is a certain truth hidden in their center, which is not seen by external eyes but is first perceived by the mind alone. Philosophers have gained experience of this and discovered its power to be such that it has performed certain miracles. Therefore, it is not to be wondered at that men have performed miracles through faith, since even mindless things are able to do the same through the power granted to them by God. 

The whole **Art** <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy, often called the Sacred Art.</note> consists chiefly in this: that the **spirit** <term>spiritus; the active, volatile essence of a substance</term> of things be liberated from its bodily chains, just as it was said of man above—that his mind ought to be made free from the body. The body of any thing is therefore a prison, in which the virtues of the "soul" of things are detained and hindered, preventing their natural spirits from freely impressing their powers and actions upon it. The spirit of such mindless things possesses an efficacy (according to the nature of the substance) similar to the power of undoubting faith in a human being. Thus, the virtue of men is true faith, and for all other things, their virtue is the truth of their efficacy. 

That every thing contains its own virtue and celestial influence—perceptible to the eyes only by its effect—is taught by the **lodestone** <note>original: *magnes lapis*; a naturally magnetized mineral</note>. In the stone, one does not see that magnetic or attractive force for iron, because the spirit is hidden within it and does not fall under the senses. Even **wine**, both the common kind and the "philosophical" kind <term>vinum philosophicum; a specialized alchemical solvent, often a highly rectified spirit or a metaphorical "mercury"</term>, has diverse virtues within it. These have come to light through the experience of the Art by **separation** <term>separatio; the process of isolating the different components or "elements" of a substance</term>. For its spirit heats and dries, but its body does the exact opposite, for it moistens and cools—as can be seen in "burning water" <note>original: *aqua ardens*; distilled alcohol</note> and vinegar. These faculties, belonging to one and the same natural compound, are entirely contrary because of separation; before that, they were not so diverse, because then [they were part] of a mixture through natural...

They share a union. Who but a madman would go so far as to deny that such virtues exist in all other natural bodies, to a greater or lesser degree? One cannot be a philosopher if they deny that bread, or grain, or any other thing possesses a spirit <note>original: "spiritum"; in this context, the active, volatile essence of a substance</note> no less effective than the spirit of wine—though perhaps not as abundant—provided the quantities and powers are equal. If, therefore, such a spirit can be separated from bread, wine, and other things by art, how much more does a far more subtle division occur naturally within a human being?

From these things alone can "philosophical transmutations" be understood. Do we not know that the purer substance of bread and wine is transmuted by nature into the flesh and blood of man? Thus, from an invisible vegetable form, it becomes a visible animal form. In this process, the **species** of things do not change, but their **forms** do. <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, "species" refers to the essential nature of a thing, while "form" refers to its outward organization or current state.</note> Who can still doubt that philosophical transmutations—achieved through both art and nature—can be performed in man far better than nature alone could manage with bread, wine, and the rest, without the aid of the chemist's hand? 

There are many other bodies in the nature of things that possess a greater natural virtue and celestial influence than wine or bread. From these, spirits can be separated and transmuted into human substance—flesh and blood—more excellently through art than through nature, though nature still acts as a co-operator. But why should I repeat so often things that are clearer than light to philosophers? If someone refuses to give credit to this, let him experiment; if he remains stubborn, let him be. No such person should be forced for his own benefit, only warned: if he holds it in contempt, he does so to his own loss, not the loss of the one who warned him.

Furthermore, let us apply what has been said to the <term>spagyric art</term> <note>The alchemical practice of separating substances into their primary components and then recombining them in a purified form.</note> regarding the attraction of virtues. In every elemental body, **Our Mercury** <term>Mercurius noster; the "philosophical mercury," a hidden essence or "first matter" sought by alchemists, not to be confused with the common liquid metal</term> is contained. In some, however, it is so remote that a person's life might end before it can be removed from them; in others, it is so near that its extraction is very easy. Some, not ignorant of this secret—namely, that Mercury exists in everything—have tried to extract it from stones, rye straw, flowers, and wood, but in vain. 

Others have extracted Mercury from substances closer at hand, such as celandine, rosemary flowers, mercurialis, and the white lily, and from their juices, using the mastery of the water-bath and the manure-pit. <note>original: "balnei fimique magisterium"; these were standard laboratory methods for providing steady, gentle heat over long periods.</note> This Mercury was not unlike common mercury in color, weight, quality, and quantity. Thinking they had found the greatest secret, they then <term>sublimated</term> <note>The process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then cools back into a solid, used for purification.</note> it with corrosives and corrupted its nature. Consequently, they failed to achieve the goal of their expectations because they were ignorant of the principles, means, and extremes by which the spagyric work is completed. 

But whoever takes the **Mercury of the Philosophers** (converted into such a species) or common mercury, and reduces it into water without any material additive—which can be done with the "phlegm of the medium" if one gives it its own "air" inside the vessel and distills it seven times—will possess the **light of pearls.** <note>original: "lumen perlarum"; likely a reference to a refined alchemical liquor or a specific state of the "philosopher's stone" characterized by a pearly luster.</note> For this is the nature of...

...heterogeneous part, which lacks the condition of the philosophical stone <note>original: "lapidis... philosophici"; the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and grant long life</note>. Therefore, the extraction of this kind of Mercury is not necessary for the transmutatory art. In certain individuals <note>In this context, "individua" refers to specific, distinct substances or entities in nature</note>, our Mercury has a somewhat free action, as it does in tartar <note>original: "tartaro"; the potassium bitartrate crystals found in wine barrels, highly valued by alchemists</note>; for it is clear from the operations of goldsmiths that when something of **Venus** <note>The alchemical name for copper</note> is in **Luna** <note>The alchemical name for silver</note>, and it is placed in white wine or in its "soul" <note>the distilled essence or spirit of the wine</note>, the power of the philosophical Mercury will bring the tincture of Luna to the surface. By this, the bond of its concordance with Luna is revealed. It is better when you extinguish ignited Venus in tartar dissolved by white wine; it will contract a whiteness, but it is not a permanent color because it lacks a fixed spiritual subject. Another experiment of it is also made where **Mars** <note>The alchemical name for iron</note> is frequently extinguished in the aforementioned solution; it will contract the softness of **Sol** <note>gold</note> and **Luna**. For Mars is dry, and very far removed from Mercury—more so than any other bodies—and all dryness has the character of a vacuum; for which reason the philosophical Mercury is easily received into it, by which it is also brought to that softness.

However, the form of the **Philosophical Heaven** <term>Philosophical Heaven: A term for a highly refined, quintessential state of matter that acts as a universal solvent or medium for change</term> is another individual in which two free operations are discerned. The first is that by which it truly converts everything placed within it into the species under which it itself exists. This is an evident sign of an admirable vegetative power, by reason of which substances are transmuted into other forms. Therefore, let the craftsman consider what this Mercury, stripped of its own form and shaped by another, is able to work. And there is indeed another equally evident operation: that the bodies of perfect metals <note>Gold and silver</note> may be ground upon a porphyry stone with that form, and both of these will be reduced into the form of an **amalgamation**, from which Mercury will be extracted over the course of a year. Because the Mercury existing here in Sol and Luna is moved toward that which is contained by that form, and vice versa. Hence, in the "angle of concordance," they are gathered together so that in the Philosophical Heaven, the perfect bodies are multiplied, and the Mercury of those bodies can in no way resist being reduced into the appearance of an amalgam through another natural bond. These operations of the Philosophical Heavens could also be recorded in other individuals, which we leave aside for the sake of brevity, and because they can be understood from what has already been said. The end of this entire mastery <note>original: "magisterij"; the "Great Work" or "Magisterium" of alchemy</note> is that the Philosophical Mercury be placed in the celestial sphere; otherwise, the craftsman will work in error and in vain. It seems marvelous that this Mercury, situated in a "super-celestial" place, does not retain color, weight, quality, and quantity, since all these are of its own nature; the reason for this is because it has been placed under a different form than when it lay hidden within a specific substance.

Afterward, let it be rectified <note>purified by repeated distillation</note> four times for greater subtlety, though only three will be enough, lest the burning spirit exhale; therefore, those who rectify seven times have erred. # PHILOSOPHY (CHEMISTRY)

<page-num>442</page-num>

...cation <note>original: "cationis," likely the conclusion of "rectificationis"; the process of refining a substance by repeated distillation</note>. Let this be the indication: when sugar is added along with water, it is entirely burned away, leaving nothing behind. This material is the subject from which the **quintessence** <note>original: "essentia quinta"; the "fifth essence," the purest and most potent medicinal or alchemical core of a substance</note> is drawn through a **pelican vessel** <note>original: "vas pellicanicum"; a specialized alchemical flask with two curved side-arms that circulate vapors back into the base, resembling a pelican feeding its young from its own breast</note>. By this operation, it will happen that the upper part, or quintessence, is separated from the lower part—namely, from the turbid dregs—along a diametrical line.

Mercury can also be extracted from **tartar** <note>original: "tartaro"; the potassium bitartrate crusts found in wine barrels, used as a key reagent in alchemy</note> by **calcining** <note>heating a substance to a high temperature to reduce it to a powder</note> it in a glassmaker's furnace for three days. A large quantity must be used, however, because it diminishes significantly in the process. Once burnt, it should be ground upon a marble stone; while on that stone, if kept in a cold and humid place, it will dissolve into water. This water is then to be distilled through a filter sleeve and received in a glass vessel. Mercury can be extracted from this in two ways: the first is as we described regarding wine; the second is through the art of separating the qualities from the elements. From Mercury handled in this manner, the "greatest work" can be performed, as described below.

The **heaven** <note>original: "caelum"; the most volatile, spiritual, or refined portion of a substance</note> of any individual substance, together with the "heaven" of red or white wine and of tartar, is extracted through the mastery of separating qualities from the elements. This is placed with either form according to the teaching of the **greater work** <note>the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note>. The vessel must be blocked so that the "heaven" does not escape, and then cooked without intermission in the steady heat of a bath for several days. Afterward, when the vessel is opened, a portion of the "air" of any of the aforementioned substances should be added as the second part of the "heaven," and it should be cooked for as many days as before. When these steps are finished, the vessel is opened again and the "heaven of fire" of any of these substances is added—in an amount equal to the "heaven of wine" used previously. With the vessel blocked again, let them be cooked with steady heat for another fifteen days. Once this art of mixing is complete, you will see the mixture transmuted into less perfect colors; the artisan must guide the work by these mediating colors until reaching the most perfect "greater work." This final substance, through the power acquired by **spagyric** <note>original: "spagiricum"; alchemical techniques involving the separation and recombination of parts</note> work, can transmute and change the appearance of external substances three thousand times its own weight.

The individual substances used for mixing are rosemary flowers, new honey, **mercury-herb** <note>original: "mercurialis"; likely the plant *Mercurialis annua*</note>, **celandine** <note>original: "chelidonia"</note>, red lily, human blood, and so on. Furthermore, because dignity is acquired through virtue before the initiate is received into power, we judge it right to add here those things which can make a practitioner worthy to labor toward these greater things.

Accordingly, we shall bring forth the **spagyric offspring** <note>the resulting alchemical product</note> from three kinds of individual substances, through a shortened work.

The entire path of minerals consists in two waters: the first makes the **stone** volatile without labor and without danger; the latter fixes the stone and is itself fixed with it, though with danger. This is because this water is drawn from a certain foul-smelling **menstruum** <note>original: "menstruali... foetenti"; in alchemy, a solvent capable of dissolving solids, often described with biological metaphors</note> composed of four things. No water stronger than this is found in the world; it is mortal, etc. It is produced in a shorter time than other stones.

Yet the **animal work** <note>alchemy involving biological materials</note> hardly has an end due to the difficulty of regulating the elements, and there is greater science required in it than in any other stone.
