### CHEMISTRY

<page-num>443</page-num>

->**CHEMISTRY.**<-

<meta>catchword: post</meta>

The **vegetable stone** <note>original: "Lapis vegetabilis"; one of the three divisions of the Philosopher’s Stone, alongside the mineral and animal stones</note>, although its preparation is quite tedious, is nevertheless of the highest composition. It must nonetheless follow the **animal stone** <note>original: "animalem... lapidem"; a stone derived from organic matter like blood or hair</note> with respect to the stabilization and **rectification** <note>purification through repeated distillation</note> of the elements: prepared in this manner, it is more effective than the animal stone.

The **quintessence** <note>original: "Essentia quinta"; the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance</note> of the spirit in the mineral stone is both life-destroying and life-giving.

In the animal stone, the highest medicine for human bodies sometimes exists, especially when it has been extracted from blood.

In the vegetable stone, however, the spirit of the quintessence is the restoration of youth and the most powerful preservation of the human body from all corruption.

Therefore, into two pounds of **rectified burning water** <note>original: "ardentis aquæ rectificatæ"; likely high-proof distilled alcohol</note>, cast one ounce of **ferment** <note>a substance used to "ripen" or transform the mixture</note>; let it digest by the artifice of the **pelican vessel** <note>a specialized flask that allows vapors to circulate and drip back down, named for its shape</note> for a space of twenty or twenty-two days, and in this way, it will be converted into a stone. After **congealing** <note>solidifying</note>, let it be dissolved again in a **dung-bed** <note>original: "fimo"; using the gentle, steady heat of decomposing manure</note> or a water bath, and then congealed again. Let this be done a third time or more often until it can no longer be coagulated, but remains liquid like an oil. With white ferment, it is not dissolved as quickly, but it coagulates faster. This medicine transmutes in no other way than according to its ferment, and no higher.

If you ferment it with its own earth, it will be a **universal medicine** <note>a "panacea" or cure-all</note>, yet not as effective as with one of the other ferments. If you dissolve gold in the aforementioned water after a tenth distillation, and afterwards allow the water to evaporate with a gentle heat or fire, and keep the matter in a humid place, it will dissolve of its own accord within four days into **potable gold** <note>original: "aurum potulentum"; a legendary liquid form of gold believed to grant longevity</note>, for the preservation of human health. Likewise, if with this you take **Mercury** seven times sublimated with **vitriol** <note>original: "vitriolo"; a sulfate mineral, often copper or iron sulfate</note>, such that there is one part gold to seven parts of this "silver," and you sublimate it just as many times until the Mercury is **fixed** <note>rendered solid or non-volatile by heat</note>, you will have a staining and penetrating medicine. Again, if one part of this dissolved gold is placed by itself over a gentle fire for eight days with one hundred parts of Mercury, this entire mixture will be congealed into gold. This proceeds from the part of the spirit of the water which, in the dissolution of the gold, is fixed to it in an inseparable bond. In this way, minerals can be mixed with vegetables, and a medicine made from them in this manner:

From equal parts of the best transparent vitriol and the most excellent **cinnabar** <note>original: "cinabaris"; mercury sulfide, a bright red mineral</note> ground together and dried in the sun, and afterwards over a gentle fire so that all watery moisture seems consumed, let water be poured on and distilled first with a gentle fire and then gradually increased, as is usually done in the **sharp water of the philosophers** <note>original: "aqua philosophorum acuta"; a powerful solvent or acid</note>. The spirit of the quintessence of vitriol and cinnabar, or of **antimony** <note>a brittle, silvery-white metalloid used in medicines and alloys</note>, which primarily constitute the mineral stone, is mixed with the spirit of the quintessence of the philosophers’ "burning and blessed" water, which spirit is the **soul of the vegetable stone**. # PHILOSOPHIA

<page-num>444</page-num>

->**PHILOSOPHY**<-

<meta>catchword: to us</meta>

...after the fifth **distillation** <note>the process of purifying a liquid by heating it into vapor and then condensing it back into liquid</note>) with that specific mixture of the fresh materials mentioned before, which must be perfectly dry before they are cast in. After the tenth distillation, let **gold** <note>original: "aurum"</note> of the weight mentioned above be placed into the **vegetable stone** <note>original: "lapide vegetabili"</note> by itself; then, in the **philosophers' furnace** <note>a specialized oven designed to maintain steady, prolonged heat</note>, the entire **fixation** <note>the process by which a volatile substance is rendered stable and resistant to fire</note> will be completed in the space of ten days. This same fixation would scarcely be completed in twenty-five days in the vegetable stone alone, because one spirit thickens the other. This is a most excellent work for the **transmutatory art** <note>the practice of changing base metals into silver or gold</note>, but not for medicine. Once the fixation is done, proceed to the **solution** <note>the process of dissolving a solid into a liquid state</note> in a **water bath** <note>original: "balneo"; a vessel of hot water used to heat substances gently</note> by itself, as was said regarding the vegetable stone alone. It should be noted that this stone made from mixtures does not dissolve as quickly as the vegetable stone alone, yet it dissolves faster than the **mineral stone** <note>original: "lapis mineralis"</note> alone: it therefore holds a middle ground for solution, as it is completed in nine days. It is necessary to repeat these solutions and **congealings** <note>original: "congelationes"; the process of thickening or solidifying</note> quite often, so that the medicine may penetrate better.

Likewise, from the **philosophers' lead** <note>original: "plumbeo philosophorum"; usually refers to antimony or a purified lead used as a starting material in alchemy</note> is extracted an **oil of golden color**. If you use this oil to dissolve the mineral stone, the mixed stone, or even the animal stone after the first fixation for three or four days (or times), you will be spared the labor of many solutions and congealings—provided you know well and rightly how to separate it from the watery parts and have worked according to the method of mixing set down previously. In thirty days, you will be able to complete the stone. This oil is not necessary for the vegetable stone by itself, since solutions occur quickly in that. However, if **sublimation** <note>the process where a solid turns into vapor and then back to solid, used for purification</note> were to take place there, the stone could be expanded.

Having also completed the fifth degree of the **meditative scale** <note>original: "scalae meditativae"; a spiritual or intellectual ladder used by the author to organize stages of enlightenment</note>, which is the **virtue of truth** <note>original: "virtus veritatis"</note> dignifying the soul toward the sixth degree, it will now be seasonable to treat of **power** <note>original: "potentia"</note>.

Furthermore, **power** is the constancy of the virtue received from the Lord God. There is no reason for any person to think they can have even the slightest spark of virtue from anywhere other than from God. If, on the contrary, someone seeks it from themselves or from any source other than the one we have named, they will obtain vice instead of virtue, to their own ruin. Thus the faithless **Gentiles** <note>non-Christians, specifically the Greeks and Romans of antiquity</note> were once accustomed to hunt for virtues through **heroic works** (as they call them) for no other reason than to leave behind a fame of themselves for their posterity and families after death. In this, they miserably placed their **highest good** <note>original: "summum bonum"</note> and all their happiness. But what became of them, the outcome of such "memorable" deeds has clearly taught us. For their kingdom, because it was founded upon sand and not upon the **rock** <note>original: "petram"; a common Christian metaphor for Christ or divine truth, contrasting with the "sand" of worldly ambition</note>, necessarily collapsed. Indeed, no greater trace of that ruin remains than that their foolishness is made plain to those who came after. One must not follow the footsteps of men, but of truth and the rock upon which all things are stable. Just as pure gold in the fire becomes purer and purer, and shines most gloriously for a very long time without loss, in no different a way do the confirmed professors of truth rejoice most greatly in every **martyrdom**. Likewise, in no other way than we said above, from the frequency of **meditative love** comes familiarity, likeness, and communion with the Divine Spirit.

### CHEMISTRY

<page-num>445</page-num>

<meta>catchword: with</meta>

...[is] granted to us by divine favor; through the careful observation of truth and virtue in both words and deeds, the constancy of virtues is infused from heaven to provide **power**. Similarly, in **Spagyrics** <note>the alchemical art of separating and then recombining the components of plants or minerals to create more potent medicines</note>, although virtues are extracted from inanimate natural bodies through this art, they will not be fit for the performance of miracles unless they are further led to their extreme power. But the more they are purified and refined, the closer they approach the first **celestial influence** <note>the idea that earthly substances receive their "life force" or "spirit" from the stars and planets</note> they possess, having been made more similar to it; and consequently, they penetrate and operate more effectively, so that what they achieve in the cure of any infirmity should be regarded as a miracle.

But now we must see what the power of natural things lacking sense is, such as minerals and other things of that kind. The "sons" of **imperfect bodies** <note>metals like lead, tin, or iron, which were believed to be "sick" or unfinished versions of gold</note> are their evacuated spirits, or their **exuberant quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum exuberatum"; a highly active form of mercury believed to be the "seed" of metals</note>, or primary matter naturally suited to receive any form. There is, however, a difference between these spirits and others evacuated from perfect bodies: for the latter exist formally <note>pertaining to the "form" or soul of the metal</note>, while the former are material. Likewise, both imperfect and perfect things can be converted into **oil**, and in this way, the preparation of form and matter occurs. Necessarily, the **sulfur of nature** <note>original: "sulphur naturæ"; the active, combustible principle in alchemy</note> of perfect things must be converted into oil, but not that of others, because it must be informed by the oil of the perfect bodies—unless, perhaps, one wishes to reduce everything to oil so the work may become more clear. This kind of oil is made through the separation of qualities in the elements.

**Saturn** <note>Lead</note> and **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note> are therefore of one and the same nature when they are reduced into spirit, exuberant quicksilver, sulfur of nature, **tincture** <note>a substance capable of imbuing another with its properties, especially color and stability</note>, oil, or the **stone**, these being present in both beyond number. Likewise, while they and all other things retain their ancient, individual nature, they also possess another nature in their simple virtue, multiplied through the way of generation and procession into spirit, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, and the stone. And this can be said more properly of the **stone** than of others, because its substance is multiplied from their unities, which indeed have a single virtue drawn from all of these. For every metal has an ultimate unity which it did not have before it was converted into the stone. This unity is extended by the multiplication of the extreme principles, just as in the said substances an argument for their form and the multiplication of virtues is made. In this manner, the doctrine of the **Lesser Work** <note>original: "minoris operis"; the preliminary stage of alchemy, often aiming for the "White Stone" capable of making silver</note> ends and concludes.

**Calcination** <note>reducing a metal to powder by heat</note>, **dissolution** <note>dissolving a solid</note>, evacuation, multiplication, spirit, the **alembic** <note>a distillation apparatus</note>, exuberant quicksilver, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, **inceration** <note>softening a substance to a wax-like consistency</note>, **sublimation** <note>heating a solid until it turns into vapor and then back to solid</note>, and the stone have one condition in **Saturn** <note>Lead</note>, another in **Mars** <note>Iron</note>, and another in **Venus** <note>Copper</note>, and so on for the rest. Also, Saturn has one condition in any of these, another with **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note>, another with **Mars**, another with the **Sun** <note>Gold</note>, and another with **Venus**...

<page-num>446</page-num>

with one of these, **Jupiter** <note>the alchemical name for Tin</note> and **Saturn** <note>Lead</note>, or **Venus** <note>Copper</note> and Jupiter with Saturn, or even with **Mars** <note>Iron</note> himself. By this method, the conditions of the metals can be multiplied by mixing one or more with another. In however many ways the mixture is made, the condition of the **stone** <note>the Philosophers' Stone, the goal of the alchemical work</note> will be varied accordingly.

**Calcination** <note>reduction to a powder by heat</note>, in turn, is equal to **solution** <note>dissolving a solid into a liquid</note>, and dissolution to **evacuation** <note>the removal of impurities or specific components</note>; this is equal to **multiplication** <note>increasing the potency or quantity of the alchemical agent</note>, and that to the **spirit**, etc., for the constitution of the subject, which is the stone. Likewise, the **alembic** <note>a distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube</note> communicates itself equally to all things according to its function.

The **sulfur of nature** <note>original: "sulphur naturae"; the active, combustible principle of a substance</note> is greater than **exuberant quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum exuberatum"; a highly purified mercury believed to be the "living" seed of metals</note>, and both are greater than the **spirit**.

The **Lesser Work** <note>original: "Opus minus"; the preliminary stage of alchemy or the creation of a lesser elixir</note> can by no means be accomplished without the sulfur of nature when drawn from **imperfect bodies** <note>base metals like lead or tin</note>, because there would be a lack of a "medium" <note>a middle or bridging substance</note> possessing their nature; in the absence of this medium, the perfect bodies could not transmute the imperfect ones into their own species. For this is what the definition of a "medium" requires: namely, that the stone be composed of the **sulfur of nature** and the **quicksilver** drawn from imperfect bodies, along with the **oil of perfect bodies** <note>the refined essence of gold or silver</note>. In this way, the stone is a medium participating in both natures <note>the base and the noble</note>, by reason of the harmony it has with the imperfect ones. This harmony gives the stone entry into every part of the imperfect metal, so that in its smallest particle <note>original: "minima pars"; refers to the concept of atoms or the smallest possible unit of matter</note> there exists the smallest part of the stone. Through its subtlety, the stone penetrates these existing parts. And because the matter of the stone, which was extracted from the imperfect bodies, is formed in all its parts and bound to a certain external form by an indissoluble bond—and by the vegetable property <note>the power of growth or life</note> which it receives from the **philosophical key**—it is so informed by that form that in its smallest part, the smallest part of that same form truly and really exists. In this way, the imperfect metals lay aside their old forms which were present in them in "act," so that they may receive the forms of the perfect metals, which were present in them in "potentiality," and thus be transmuted into perfect metallic bodies.

Elsewhere, the mode of operating with the sulfur of nature of **Saturn** or **Jupiter** has been described; but now we say that a mixture can be made with two, three, four, or all of them according to the will of the operator, so that the craftsman may choose the condition he wishes them to have. The method of eliciting **oil** from the perfect bodies is also placed in another location; the method for one is the same as for all the others through **calcination**, **dissolution**, **evacuation**, **multiplication**, **spirit**, the **alembic**, **exuberant quicksilver**, **sulfur of nature**, **tincture**, **oil**, **inceration** <note>the process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency</note>, **sublimation**, and through **fire**.

When you wish to join two things together, you should place them into calcination by means of the **philosophical key**, and afterwards into dissolution, and through the rest of the aforementioned steps up to and including sublimation. If, however, they are already perfected and made into the **sulfur of nature**, place them into multiplication; likewise, if the matter is too hard, pour on some portion of **menstrual blood** <note>original: "sanguinis menstrualis"; an alchemical term for a specific solvent or the "mercurial water" used to dissolve and nourish the "embryo" of the stone, not literal blood</note> so that it may be converted into oil.

# CHEMISTRY

<page-num>447</page-num>

It should also be noted that the elements of metals, when drawn from them by means of **vegetable Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium vegetabilem"; in alchemy, this refers to a life-giving or "growing" solvent rather than a plant-based one</note>, are called their **prime matter** <note>original: "materia prima"; the fundamental, formless substance from which all things are made</note>, which most closely approaches their most general type; it is also called their **fifth essence** <note>original: "essentiam quintam"; the quintessence, the purest and most concentrated spiritual force</note> or even their **heaven**.

This matter indeed must be converted (if it belongs to the "perfect" metals <note>Gold and Silver</note>) into the nature of "forms," and the matter of other "imperfect" metals must be converted into that same nature. The resulting mixture is called a **ferment** <note>original: "fermentum"; an agent that triggers transformation, like yeast in dough</note>, because it is made from prime matter, the nature of metals, and oil added drop by drop. Afterward, through **philosophical Mercury** and the process of **inceration** <note>original: "inceratione"; the process of softening a dry substance with liquid until it reaches a wax-like consistency</note>—which is the medium that joins Mercury with the aforementioned prime matter—the **philosophical gum** is produced in this way.

A **simple ferment** is one to which nothing else has been added, such as the elements themselves, or "evacuated" metals <note>metals stripped of impurities</note> existing by themselves and taken in their simple form.

A **composite** ferment is when several things are mixed together. He who is unable to convert the bodies of both perfect and imperfect metals specifically into their own prime matter will be able to possess neither a simple nor a composite ferment; without these, the **stone** <note>the Philosophers' Stone</note> will be useless and empty.

Indeed, the **earth** that is raised from metallic bodies into **sulfur** is called the "salt of nature" by the philosophers, or "vegetable Mercury," or the "medium" that joins all extremes to a single end—that is, it joins "heaven" with "form," or the **philosophical key** <note>original: "clavem philosophicam"; a specific reagent or method used to "unlock" or dissolve a substance</note> with the perfect bodies. This earth is also called **Mercuriated elements**.

The **less perfect** stone is the philosophers' stone that has not been fermented in power or in quantity; it is composed of fire and air, or of earth and fire.

**Fermentation** is an operation signifying a double multiplication—namely, of quantity and of power. When multiplication occurs in quantity, the power is diminished, and vice versa. There is also another multiplication of both power and quantity together: the first with common Mercury; the second with the Mercury of metals; the third with vegetable Mercury, or the **philosophers' menstruum** <note>original: "menstruo philosophorum"; here "menstruum" refers to a powerful solvent used in dissolution, not the biological process</note>, etc.

Fermentation is performed to shorten a long period of time, using form, heaven, and Mercury as it is commonly understood.

**Evacuation** is the name given to the separation of the pure from the impure.

**Multiplication** is the reduction of an evacuated thing back onto its own earth, so that a "spirit of purity" may arise.

The **spirit of bodies** is the substance that is evacuated from bodies through solution by means of the philosophical key.

**Exuberant quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum vivum exuberatum"; a highly refined, "living" form of mercury</note> is the spirit of bodies that ascends together with the "key" and passes through the **alembic** <note>a distillation apparatus</note>.

The **sulfur of nature** is the sublimated earth of bodies, converted into "foliated earth" <note>original: "terram foliatam"; a flaky or crystalline state of matter</note>, which is called the first and nearest matter of metals.

# PHILOSOPHY

<page-num>448</page-num>

A **Tincture** <note>original: "Tinctura"; a potent substance capable of changing the color or quality of metals</note> is composed of air and fire, or of earth and fire.

**Oil** is a fixed element that facilitates melting and fixation <note>original: "fixationem"; the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat</note>.

The **Stone** is "foliated earth" <note>original: "terra foliata"; a purified, crystalline residue that has been distilled until it appears leafy or layered</note>, in which the fixed oil is the sown seed or sprout.

The **fire of the stone** consists of the essential fire of the body and the co-essential fire of the **vegetable menstruum** <note>original: "menstrui vegetabilis"; a life-giving alchemical solvent</note>; from these, a single fire is composed which transmutes all metals in a moment, aided by the aforementioned fire through its own vegetative power.

The elements of the bodies must be distilled so many times with the solvent itself, toward the great philosophical and **spagyric** <note>original: "spagiricum"; the alchemical art of separating and then recombining the pure parts of a substance</note> offspring, until they are fixed, and none of the solvent appears actually present with them. In this way, from the condition and property of these things, a fire like a flash of lightning arises, suddenly consuming any imperfect metals and inducing another, perfect form in them.

These things pertain to the power of the sixth step of the **meditative scale** applied to the spagyric art; it remains for us to climb to the seventh and final step, in which the "miracle"—as mentioned above regarding the stability of the most fixed stone—is founded. This is, therefore, the **miracle of constancy** <note>or "steadfastness"</note> effected through the power of truth. To explain this, we can only use the examples of others who attained such great happiness as to reach the goal and finish-line of this most expert philosophy.

This shone forth first in the blessed **Stephen the Protomartyr** <note>the first Christian martyr, stoned to death in Jerusalem</note>, who, while being overwhelmed by stones for his most constant profession of the truth, served as an example that his soul suffered nothing, as he saw the heavens opened and prayed for those slaughtering him. The same also happened to those **three youths** <note>Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego from the Book of Daniel</note> cast into the furnace of burning fire; while they professed the truth with a truly constant mind, the evidence that they suffered no pain was that they sang a hymn and praises to God, the Truth, in the midst of the flames, rejoicing with a cheerful spirit.

We read that this has happened not only to Christian sages, but also to pagan philosophers, such as a certain **Anaxarchus** <note>a Greek philosopher of the 4th century BCE</note>, a follower of Democritus. He was subjected to this martyrdom by a certain emperor and tyrant of Cyprus named **Nicocreon**, also because of his profession of the truth. While he was being crushed in a stone mortar with an iron pestle, he said: "Pound, tyrant, pound this little body of Anaxarchus, for you do not pound Anaxarchus himself." Since this greatly vexed the tyrant—so that the philosopher might no longer speak the truth, which the tyrant could not bear to hear—he ordered the executioner to cut out his tongue. But Anaxarchus bit it off with his own teeth and spat it into the open mouth of the tyrant before his body was pounded into a pulp. O, admirable constancy of men, terrified by no martyrdoms, but rather enduring death with the highest joy for the love of truth, conquering the tyranny of the world.

In no different a way, in the spagyric offspring, after it has reached the spagyric miracle...

Hear now the generation of this substance: After one of the forming bodies has been mixed and **calcined** <note>reduced to powder by heat</note> with common **Mercury** and common salt, let the silver be sublimated from that compound, or let the "water" receive the "wine" <note>likely referring to the extraction of a spirit or *aqua vitae*</note>, and let the salt be thoroughly washed away from the body with hot water.

Afterward, let the qualities of the elements be divided, and to three pounds of the **philosophical heaven** <term>cælum philosophicum; a highly purified, volatile solvent or spirituous substance</term>, add two ounces of the "lesser form." Then, for two and a half ounces of the "greater form," you shall take half a pound of the "heaven," and from these make a "marriage" <note>an alchemical union or "conjunction" of substances</note> for mixing in a vessel that is very well-sealed. Thereafter, with the tempered **decoction** <term>decoctio; a process of boiling or heating to extract essences</term> always continued, and as the form and the heaven begin to enter digestion and generation (operations which last until the substance is less than perfect), that black color is "mortified" <note>the *nigredo* or "death" phase where the matter decomposes to be reborn</note>, and through the persistence of the heat, a white color arises.

When all parts are under this color, let it be a sign that the bones and nerves of the **philosophical fetus** <term>fœtus philosophicus; the developing alchemical Stone or "Great Work"</term> are joined with the "third number"; yet this operation lasts until a saffron <note>yellow</note> color appears. When this appears, it will be a sign that the body of such a fetus is formed and complete with its organs, and is beginning to be prepared so that the **vegetable spirit** <term>spiritus vegetabilis; the life-giving, growing force in alchemy</term> may enter into it. This operation will last until, during the preparation, the saffron color vanishes and a red color arises.

When the red at last arises, you shall judge that the "vegetable soul" is within the body of the fetus, and that the end of the completion of its body and soul is at hand. Then finally the craftsman must count the intervening days between the beginning and end of generation, which he can also know by sight from the completed end of the act of dissolution; and for twice that amount of time continuously, he must by no means cease the administration of fire. When this space of time is finished, let it be allowed to cool.

Now the fetus will be found in the manner of an egg; having been extracted and cleaned, it should be placed in a clean glass vessel and contained again in the furnace of decoction—which is a **dry bath** <term>balneum siccum; a method of heating a vessel using sand or ash rather than water</term>—for six natural days, administering fire successively in the same manner as before, so that a hand can scarcely be held in that heat without injury. Let it be extracted afterward and kept most carefully. One part by weight of this, "projected" <note>the act of casting the Stone onto base metals to transform them</note> upon two thousand parts of external substances, is powerful enough to generate a form similar to that from which it took its origin. Namely, to one pound of the said **solvent** <term>menstruum; a liquid used to dissolve or extract substances</term>, add two or two and a half ounces of the "form," according to the aforementioned condition, and only a drachm of the "lesser perfect" substance. It should be noted, therefore, that the colors of these **offspring** <note>original: "fœtuum"; the text treats the growing alchemical Stone as a developing embryo or fetus</note> are diverse: the male or "greater perfect" is red, while the female or "lesser perfect" is white. The colors appear as follows: first, green mixed with redness; second, yellow, also mixed with a brilliant redness, which indicates the union of the parts with their whole; third, a white and shining color, which is a sign of the completion of the "offspring's" body; and fourth, a snowy white mixed with a honey-like color, which signifies the entry of the soul into its body. 

Once imbued with this color, the "fetus" is born from the mother's womb. One part of its weight is able to **multiply** <term>multiplicatio; the process of increasing the power and quantity of the alchemical agent</term> three thousand parts of matter into its own kind; by the third repetition, it can multiply over three hundred thousand. The multiplication of this final substance, just like the earlier "greater perfect" substance, can also be performed. It must be further noted that in the **spagyric work** <term>spagirico; the alchemical art of "separating and recombining" to achieve purity</term>, there is no precise or fixed time. Sometimes the fetus is born sooner when the heat happens to be more intense than required; sometimes it is born later due to a reduction of heat, just as is seen in a human pregnancy.

Colors are the best indicators of this craft, by which it must also be guided. When the spagyric fetus is in dissolution and completely liquefied, a black color begins to arise; from this, you shall judge it to be in the state of mixing and that it has passed through "alteration." After the yellow color appears, you shall consider the body to be formed and complete in its members. When the final color appears—namely red—judge that the body has been joined with the soul. Once this is completed, the fire must be continued, as has been said; the same must be understood regarding the colors of the White work according to their qualities. Having well recognized and noted these signs with the greatest diligence and careful attention, the artisan may approach the spagyric work with a cheerful spirit and without fear, and—God willing—bring it to completion. Now that the **Great Work** <term>opus majus; the most significant alchemical process to create the Philosopher's Stone</term> has been dispatched, let us turn to the **Lesser Work** <term>opus minus; a secondary or preparatory process, often involving the purification of specific metals</term>.

To the **calx** <term>calci; a powder produced by the roasting or "calcination" of a metal</term> of any body placed in a long-necked philosophical vessel, pour enough juice of the **philosophical key** <term>clavis philosophica; a specialized solvent believed to "unlock" the properties of metals</term> so that it stands four fingers above it. Afterward, let it boil over moderately hot ashes for one natural day, and then in warm dung or a **bath** <term>balneove; a water bath or *balneum Mariae*, used for gentle, even heating</term> so that it may be better digested, and the matter separated into its subtle parts—namely, the pure from the impure.

When the term of this separation is finished, let the vessel be removed. From it, by a gentle tilting so as not to disturb the dregs, pour all (or slightly less) of the liquid into another vessel, which is to be kept closed, and

# CHYMISTRY

<page-num>451</page-num>

<header>CHYMISTRY.</header>

<sig>Ff 2</sig>

Once the evacuation has been performed, you shall pour on another **key** <term>clavis; a specific alchemical solvent or catalyst used to "unlock" the matter</term> similar to the first, so that it stands above the matter as was said before: let it boil and place it in **dung** <term>fimus; decomposing manure used by alchemists as a reliable source of gentle, steady heat</term>, as before. You shall repeat these operations as many times as necessary until the **body** <note>The solid material or "earth" of the work</note> is evacuated of its **spirits** <note>The volatile or gaseous components</note>. If you run out of the "key," you shall distill all the waters of the evacuations through an **alembic** <term>alembicum; a classic distillation apparatus with a cooling cap</term> over a slow fire or the heat of a water-bath, until you have two parts of the evacuation. You shall pour this amount of water over the matter, as said above; this process is to be continued until the earth is entirely empty. You shall test it in this way: first, place a little of this earth, dried in the sun, upon a red-hot plate; if it gives off smoke, the said operations must be repeated until it shows none. Keep the waters of the evacuations stored in a moist and warm place.

Once this test is successful, you shall place the matter in a **cucurbit** <term>cucurbita; a gourd-shaped chemical flask</term> and, having placed the **helm** <note>The "galea" or cap of the still</note> on top, you shall dry it by distillation. Weigh the dried earth, and pour over it three times its weight of the best-rectified "key," as you know how to do; and from the cucurbit, covered with its **beaked helm** <note>original: "galea rostrata"; a still-head with a long downward-pointing spout</note> and with the joints very well sealed, you shall distill it over a very slow fire until it is dried again as before. Let it be moistened again with a similar "key" and distilled as before, with each of the distillations being collected together in a closed vial. These distillations are to be repeated as many times as necessary until the earth is reduced to a most subtle powder, barely feelable between the fingers. Afterward, distill all the waters of the evacuations through an alembic and a **sea-bath** <term>balneum maris; a water-bath (bain-marie) used for uniform heating</term> until the matter appears at the bottom of the vessel like melted wax or like honey. While the bath is cooling, pour back onto the matter the water you had drawn off by distillation, so that it stands four fingers above it, and let it be placed for **digestion** <term>digestio; a process of slow heating to mature the substance</term> in dung or in a bath for a natural day, with the vessel closed. Finally, distill through the alembic as before, and when the vessel is cooled, return the drawn-off water once again to the matter; digest, distill, return, and diligently continue these repeated operations of this process until you perceive that the entire matter has ascended upward along with the water. 

This volatile matter is called **virgin’s milk** <note>original: "lac virginis"; a poetic term for the white, purified liquid resulting from this refinement</note> by the philosophers, and **exuberated quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum exuberatum; mercury that has been rendered highly active and refined</term>. Finally, take the aforementioned most subtle powder of the earth and moisten it with half its weight of the water mentioned above, and let it be digested by the heat of dung for eight days. When these are finished, distill the water from the earth over a slow fire through the alembic as before. Having noted its weight again, the water now received should be poured back over it, supplementing it (if it is lacking or diminished) with the previously "exuberated" water to reach half the weight as above. All these operations—such as the moistenings, digestions, **calcinations** <term>calcinatio; heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to powder</term>, or **congealings**—are to be repeated until the earth has "drunk" half of its own moisture. You will know it has drunk enough when a tiny bit of it, placed upon a red-hot plate, entirely flies off into the air, leaving nothing behind on the plate: but if it does not...

...state is reached, the process must be repeated until it is accomplished. Once this is perceived, let it be **sublimated** <note>The process of turning a solid into vapor and back to solid to purify it</note> through ashes in a vial, first with moderate heat, and finally with the heat increased gradually and successively until the whole ascends to the sides of the vessel. Thus, the matter will be exalted into a **miraculous salt** <term>sal admirabile; a purified, crystalline state often associated with the final stages of the Great Work</term>, which the philosophers call the **stone** and the **sulfur of nature**. This salt must be "waxed" with the **oil of the perfect** <note>The liquified essence of gold or silver</note> until it flows as easily as wax. In this way, you will possess the perfected **Medicine**, one part of which will most excellently transmute one hundred parts by weight of tin (if it be the **salt of Jupiter** <term>sal Jovis; alchemical term for tin</term>) or fifty parts of lead (if it was projected from **Saturn** <term>Saturnus; alchemical term for lead</term>) into a perfect body, more perfect than any produced by nature. For the **oil of the perfect** <note>original: "oleum perfectorum"; the essence of noble metals</note> has a fixative power over all salts extracted from imperfect metals.

Therefore, take one ounce of the filings or leaves of the perfect metals, which have been **calcined** <note>Reduced to powder by heat</note> as stated elsewhere, from which the moisture or **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum; the "living" or philosophical spirit of mercury</term> may be extracted by the juice of the **philosophic key** <term>clavis; the specific solvent used throughout these instructions</term> through the artifice of liquefaction or evacuation. All the liquefactions from the evacuations should be distilled by a **water-bath** <term>balneum; a vessel of water used to provide gentle, indirect heat</term> from an **alembic** <term>alembicum; a distillation apparatus</term>, until a viscous matter remains at the bottom, like liquid and skimmed honey. Once the vessel has cooled, pour enough of the **philosophic key** over this matter so that it stands four fingers above it, and let it be kept in **digestion** <term>digestio; the process of slow, steady heating to mature a substance</term> in dung or a water-bath for one full natural day. Once the vessel is cooled, that which has been dissolved is to be poured out by a gentle tilting.

Afterwards, let the vessel with its alembic, just as it is covered, be placed in the water-bath to dry the matter with a slow fire. Make that water and as much of the fresh **key** as before float over it: then expose it to digestion for a similar day, and once the digestion is done, pour off the dissolved part. This process is to be repeated until the entire matter is converted into a clear water. 

Next, place this water in digestion for eight days, after which you shall extract the qualities of the **elements**. First, by a most gentle bath-fire, receive as much of the **water** as can ascend with that heat. When the distillation stops and the vessel has cooled, pour all the liquor already distilled back onto its **dregs** <note>original: "fæces"; the solid residue remaining after distillation</note>, and let it be kept in digestion in a closed vessel in dung or a water-bath for several days.

Afterward, through ashes and a fire of sawdust governed by **registers** <term>registra; sliding plates or vents used to control the airflow and temperature of a furnace</term>, distill all the **oil** that can ascend with that heat. Distill this distillate again by the heat of a water-bath; that which ascends, they call **water**, but that which remains at the bottom, they call **air**. Pour the distilled water back onto the dregs once more, and when they have stood in digestion for seven days, let them be distilled by a **naked fire** <note>A direct flame against the glass, rather than using a bath</note> or in sand with a slow heat at first, until all the water has passed through the alembic. Afterwards, the heat being gradually increased to the **fourth degree** <note>The highest intensity of heat in alchemical practice</note>, let all the liquor be driven upward until the matter at the bottom is thoroughly dried and, when ground upon a marble slab, becomes an impalpable **alcohol** <term>alcool; in this era, this term referred to an extremely fine, subtle powder, not a liquid</term>, or powder. Distill the liquor in a water-bath to separate the **water** from the **oil**, which they call **fire**.

Having indeed completed this evacuation, add to the weight of the aforementioned powder half its weight of the aforementioned **quicksilver** <term>argentum vivum; mercury</term> by soaking it, and place it in a closed vessel to **digest** <note>A process of slow heating to encourage chemical change</note> in dung or a water bath for eight days. When the time for this digestion is finished, complete each step as has been stated elsewhere regarding other reductions; noting this diligently: that every substance should have its own proper quicksilver. Once the **sublimation** <note>The process of vaporizing a solid and collecting the deposit</note> is complete, that which has been sublimated—found both on the sides of the vessel and at its top—should be kept in a closed vessel in the digestion of warm dung or a **sea-bath** <term>balneum maris; a double-boiler or bain-marie</term> for eight days. When these are completed, if the material is not yet dissolved, let it remain longer until it is resolved into a clear water, which is called the **ointment** <note>original: "unguentum"</note> and **oil of the philosophers**. If perhaps it proves too difficult to dissolve, add a little of the salt already known to you, which has been dissolved and congealed twice or thrice; this is our **heaven** <note>original: "cœlum"; likely a reference to a highly purified spirit or "mercury of the philosophers"</note> and the **philosophical key** <term>clavis philosophica</term> rectified four times, and it will dissolve perfectly. Do this very thing in all your dissolutions.

Finally, you shall **wax** <term>inceratio; the process of softening a dry substance into a wax-like state by adding liquid</term> some portion of the salt of any metal, heated in a crucible over ashes, by infusing it drop by drop with the oils already mentioned, until it is reduced to the thickness of cold honey. When the material is removed from the fire, let a small piece be brought near the flame of a burning candle; if it melts very easily, it is well; if not, repeat the waxings until the material flows before the **Mercury** <note>The volatile part of the substance</note> escapes. You may also perform this waxing with the **fifth essence** <term>essentia quinta; quintessence</term> of the perfect metals, in the manner described above. These oils are incombustible.

Thus far we have spoken of the steps of the **meditative scale of philosophy** <note>A conceptual ladder linking chemical work to spiritual growth</note>, which I shall not find burdensome to review briefly.

Just as there are seven philosophical degrees through which an entrance to sublime things lies open to the mind, there are also seven principal **spagyric operations** <term>spagiricæ; alchemical processes involving separation and recombination</term> through which the artist can arrive at that most excellent secret of universal medicine. Indeed, **spagyric putrefaction** <note>The breakdown of matter through rot or fermentation</note> is compared to the study of philosophers. For just as philosophers are prepared for knowledge through study, so natural things are prepared for dissolution through putrefaction; to which **philosophical knowledge** is compared. For just as doubts are resolved through the knowledge of philosophers, in no different a way are metallic bodies opened through spagyric dissolution for the extraction of their spirits. Just as a frequency of studies arises from a meditative love, and from there a familiarity with wisdom, a likeness to truth, and a communion with virtue, so too from the frequent repetition of **congealing** <note>The solidification of a liquid</note> after dissolution—one always following the other—the parts of natural bodies acquire a likeness to purity through the persistence of said operations, in order to communicate with the spagyric union. Just as the wits of those philosophizing are sharpened by the frequency of studies, the parts of natural bodies are also refined by spagyric washings. In the same way that they are united through virtue...

<header>PHILOSOPHY</header>

With the truth of the philosopher, through **spagyric** <term>spagyric; the alchemical art of separating components and recombining them in a purified state</term> mixture and composition, the elements are composed into their smallest parts. Through power, philosophical virtues are stabilized and confirmed with dignity; through alchemical **fixation** <note>The process of making a volatile or "spiritual" substance stable and resistant to the heat of fire</note>, spirits are also fixed in their bodies so that they no longer flee from the fire. Just as if by a miracle, attained philosophy makes its virtue and truth manifest to men, so do spagyric medicines reveal their perfection through **projection** <note>The final stage of the Great Work, where the alchemical "Stone" or medicine is cast upon a substance to transform or heal it</note>. 

Here, in brief, you have everything that true philosophy shares in common with the spagyric art in its operations. I see nothing lacking here for you, seekers of secrets, regarding what makes for a long life, except for that which we once recounted concerning the **Tree of Long Life**. Nor will I be reluctant to add this, which encompasses much of what preceded it in brevity; thus, what seems obscure to you in one place shall be made more clearly manifest in another. In the following section, by contrast, I intend to place another tree where I have proposed to treat several matters regarding a "short life." Therefore, let us approach the matter cheerfully.

With the highest reverence and veneration, the adept philosophers of old worshipped the **Triad in unity** <note>A reference to the concept of the Trinity mirrored in the natural world</note>. This included those who were partly ignorant of Christ, or who saw Him only through a faint ray appearing from afar through shadows (among whose number that man **Anaxarchus** <note>Anaxarchus of Abdera, a Greek philosopher who traveled with Alexander the Great</note> seems to have been), as well as our own philosophers, who, being illuminated from up close, embrace and profess Christ. 

For indeed, that **Trinity** which we worship and confess with the highest honor in the Divinity places a specimen and figure of itself before the eyes of those who search out the most hidden secrets of nature, appearing in every naturally produced thing created by that same Divinity. In the human body, first, there are three things required for the preservation of its health and the protection of a long life: namely, the **Sun**, **Jupiter**, and the **Moon**, in a physical-spagyric sense. 

Let the **Tree of Long Life** therefore be planted from these three; let its root and more solid parts be **Jupiter**, through whose trunk and branches the lunar liquor passes and ascends to the **Sun**. These three planets, in a most beautiful order, rejoicing in a long life, represent the soul and the mind in the human body, just as the four imperfections represent the body below them. 

From this, it happened that the ancient philosophers who had attained true philosophical knowledge, when they wished to pray for happiness for a friend, hoped for a triple and quadruple blessedness for them: that is, health of soul and body, using these words: **"May God grant a sound mind in a sound body"** <note>original: "mens sana in corpore sano," a famous phrase from the Roman poet Juvenal</note>. 

Lest this most ancient and beautiful sentiment pass by unresolved, let us first explain the health of the mind. To achieve this, the mind requires three faculties above all: **Reason**, which belongs to the Sun; **Intellect**, which belongs to the Moon; and **Memory**, which is the faculty of Jupiter. To these, the three most powerful spagyric grades are not unsuitably compared, leading to the highest attainment and the summit of the scale: namely, the virtue of Jupiter, the power of the Moon, [and the Sun's...]

<sig>Ff 4</sig>

And the miracle of the Sun. The most learned experts in natural things once said that the Sun begets the Sun, and therefore it is the father of all things (after God, however), and the Moon is the mother, the Air (which is dedicated to Jupiter) is the womb, and the Earth is the nurse, as we have said above more than enough. <note>This is a direct reference to the "Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus," a foundational alchemical text that describes the relationship between the microcosm of man and the macrocosm of the universe.</note> Nothing can be more certain than that the Sun, which circles the entire globe in the space of twenty-four hours, flows natural life into all things produced by nature. Therefore, the Sun exists in all things by power and virtue through the life of "Sun-begotten-by-Sun." <note>original: "Solem à Sole genitam"</note> Furthermore, just as that same Sun sends its influences to the lower realms through the Moon, in no different a way does that solar and vital fire of things infuse its animal virtues—which it received from the higher Sun—into all the members of its body through its own Moon; that is, through water or liquor, or if you prefer, the blood, which we said above is the fuel and nourishment of the fire. Jupiter, however, or the Air (which was previously called the Wind), holds the middle ground between the Sun (or Fire) and the Moon (Water); without this middle ground, life cannot persist, no more than extremes can exist without their mediating links.

->*We have heard what the nurse and the breasts of nature are.*<-

Behold, that which the ancients veiled in so many riddles, and sang of most secretively in innumerable volumes of both prose and verse, I now offer to you as a revealed gift, in brief and very open words for your sake, best of readers. I desire nothing from you in return, except that you do not disparage what you are ignorant of in the future, nor detract from it any further. Rather, love and cherish this art with all your effort, and cultivate it no differently than yourself; you will gather a huge profit from it. Once you have attained this, first give immortal thanks to God, and then turn and bestow what you have gathered from it for the use and love of your neighbor. If you do this, God the Best and Greatest will bless your labors, and you will encourage the professors of this art to detect more and more every day, for you and for honest men, those things which have remained hidden until now. Furthermore, oh you who desire to lead a long and healthy life, it is fitting to take care of your Sun and Moon through the **temperament** <term>temperatura; the balanced state of the bodily "humors" or qualities</term> of Jupiter. It has been said abundantly above what the Sun is in man, what the Moon is, and what Jupiter is. But lest I be said to have failed anyone through laziness, I will explain more clearly. The balance of food and drink, even when themselves tempered, can do much for the conservation of a healthy and long life. Yet, a **temperament** <note>In this context, a "temperament" is a mixture of qualities</note> or proportion cannot be made in one thing alone. It must be considered, therefore, that there must be at least two things which admit to a balance, and a third thing which is this balanced state. Accordingly, we assert that two qualities exist in our Jupiter: namely, the **natural heat** <term>caliditas naturalis; the internal fire that drives metabolism and life</term> of fire, and the **radical moisture** <term>humiditas radicalis; the essential fluid or "oil" that sustains the vital fire</term> of water. These must be made quite equal, as if balanced on a scale hung at right angles on both sides; otherwise, a healthy or long life can by no means follow. Some prescribe various methods of this temperament, both for defending it and for acquiring and preserving it...

# PHILOSOPHY

<page-num>456</page-num>

<header>PHILOSOPHY</header>

...not [only] physicians, and especially Marsilio Ficino in his *Three Books on Life*, but also many others whose writings can be read. <note>Marsilio Ficino (1433–1499) was a central figure of the Italian Renaissance whose work *De vita libri tres* combined Neoplatonism, medicine, and astrology.</note> They all agree primarily on this: that they should harmonize Jupiter—both in temperate food and drink used moderately, as well as in other movements and actions of life. <note>In medical astrology, Jupiter represents the "Air" element and the principle of balance, growth, and health. To "harmonize Jupiter" means to maintain a state of healthy equilibrium.</note> It would be superfluous to list them all; I will only add that it is a vast and most painstaking labor to always observe Jupiter in foods and other things. Therefore, if by chance the proportion becomes unequal through excess or deficiency of one of the parts—since it is not within human power to know nature's proportions perfectly—I would not advise anyone to proceed by supplementing a deficiency or subtracting an excess (as has been the custom until now). Instead, one should leave this duty and office to nature, to whom it belongs.

However, if someone should suffer a blockage of the stomach due to an excess of food or drink, and had weakened the digestive powers of the natural fire, I would advise rather that he abstain from drink and food for a time, until wise nature herself desires more. For she is her own best and principal physician. If this should happen more slowly than is right, he should use very little at first to sustain the vital fire, especially those things which in their temperament most resemble Jupiter. Meanwhile, it will be helpful to gently loosen the obstruction of the intestines, as with an enema or similar means.

On the other hand, for one who has kindled the vital fire through excessive exercise or some other way, I would advise that, having observed a certain rest, he eat and drink moderately for nourishment those things which have a mostly Jovian nature; lest for lack of food, the fire—which is by nature devouring—consume its own radical moisture, upon which it feeds and is nourished in the absence of other external nourishment. <note>original: "radicale suum humidum." The "radical moisture" was thought to be the innate "oil" or fuel of the body; its depletion by the "vital fire" was the primary cause of aging and death in Renaissance medicine.</note> Whoever follows these two methods, which are very easy for anyone to observe, will easily maintain health for a long life without any medicine that causes nausea to the stomach.

Furthermore, philosophically and in the spagyric manner <note>original: "spagirico modo." Spagyric refers to alchemical medicine, which involves separating a substance into its components, purifying them, and recombining them to create a more potent remedy.</note>, any of the said parts that are in excess or deficiency—such as Mars, Venus, Mercury, or Saturn—can be corrected, either individually or together, through transmutation alone. For philosophical spagyric medicines do not act through quantity, but only through quality. Hence, if the solar virtue in a man fails and has lapsed into a Martian imperfection <note>In this context, a "Martian imperfection" refers to an over-hot or inflammatory state, which is corrected by "Solar" medicine—representing balanced vitality—through the principle of resonance.</note>, it must be restored by a solar medicine drawn from some other body: through sympathy, indeed, and not antipathy. Since nature seeks nature and rejoices most in being transmuted into its own likeness.

These are the things that needed to be said about the tree of long life, so that what preceded might become somewhat clearer. Furthermore, "long life" for us is incorrupt nature—not as it was before the Fall, but as it is after being restored. # ON THE DARKNESS AGAINST
### NATURE, AND SHORT LIFE.

->*“Now the serpent was more subtle than any of the animals of the earth,”*<-

In the previous treatise, we spoke of nature in its integrity and as it is restored to a long life; now, however, let us bring forth some observations concerning nature corrupted after the Fall and degenerated into a short life, and simultaneously address those things which appear to contribute to its restoration and healing. Since a disease was introduced into nature by the serpent and a lethal wound was inflicted, a remedy must be sought. A medieval and Renaissance medical concept referring to the innate "oil" or fluid that fuels the body's "vital lamp" or heat.</note>.

For we have previously stated that the life of the world is the **light of nature** and **celestial sulfur**, whose underlying substance is the ethereal moisture of the firmament and heat, much like the sun and the moon. In the same way, we must consider in the **spagyric art** <note>The alchemical practice of separating and recombining the components of natural substances to create medicines.</note> that the life of all natural things is their light, which shines without hindrance within its own firmament. 

However, this light is prevented from shining freely and clearly by the darkness of its own elements. This happens when those elements, with a certain violence and against the course of nature, penetrate the "firmament" of things—especially within the human body—and mix themselves into the light, causing it to become clouded. We have learned from the matters discussed above that it has been provided by divine order that, in the future, darkness should no longer be mixed with the light of nature. For this purpose, a "firmament" was placed in between to ward off the darkness of the "lower waters" and keep them within their proper boundaries. 

We are warned to act in no different a way regarding the **minor world** <note>the *microcosm*, or the human body, which was believed to reflect the structure of the entire universe.</note>. We must take care that what the order of nature forbids does not happen within the body itself. Above all, its firmament must be restored so that the darkness of its elements is restrained in its proper place and forced to remain there. Thus, if the elements have perhaps at some point been mixed with their own light, they may be driven out once a division has been made, separating the corrupt waters from the incorrupt superior ones. 

But by what means this can be achieved, we have clearly enough declared in the preceding pages. What is to stop us from clearly understanding that this means of division and governance must be strengthened? It must be restored by something similar to itself—namely, by taking an incorrupt medium that has been separated from a natural body most fit and suitable for the task, once the impure elements have been cast away entirely along with their darkness. 

This is not to say that those [impure parts] are entirely useless, but rather that they are less fit to be consumed for internal use unless they are very highly prepared in combination with other things. For external use, however, once they have been thoroughly purged of their own darkness, they are the most suitable remedies for surgeons above all others. This ensures the natural order of **similarity** is preserved, which teaches everywhere that **likes should be applied to likes** <note>original: *similia similibus*. This is a core principle of Paracelsian medicine—treating a disease with a substance that shares its nature.</note>: such as bodily things to bodily things, and to the more sensory parts on the outside; likewise, vital things should be applied to the external and more vital parts. 

Therefore, if the disease of life is a gradual destruction caused by the corruption of the elements, who would not judge that **life alone** is needed to retain life? We should not use those things which, because they admit corruption so easily, are equally able to take life away—as the elements themselves do. Therefore, once these have been divided through separation, that which is pure and free from all corruption will be able to exercise its powers freely. It will act without hindrance upon whatever body it has been introduced into.

...[God] makes this light common to those whom he has judged worthy of the **secrets of nature** <note>original: "arcana suæ filiæ naturæ"</note>. Men of sincere character and good will, who are at peace with themselves and all others in God, have been illustrated by a supernatural light. Through their contemplations, they have attained the light of nature in this manner:

First, they considered the order and progress of the divine workmanship from the **account of Moses** <note>The creation story in the book of Genesis.</note>. Eventually, aided by the inspiration of the Divine Spirit—which assists all the pious efforts of men—they devoted themselves entirely to imitating His work, as much as was possible, for the benefit of the human race. They did this only after first directing many prayers to God, so that, having received a worthy testimony that they were not offending the Divine Majesty in this matter, they might proceed more happily to the honor and glory of Him to whom alone the highest praise is due.

Therefore, from the storehouse of nature—specifically from whatever substance seemed most excellent for completing the sought-after work—they divided the **lower waters** from the **upper waters**. They used this light everywhere as the most excellent, pure, and simple remedy for all things that can be found under heaven. It possessed such great virtue that all the imbalances in the human body were restored to their proper temperament by it, so that it was seen and regarded as a miracle by everyone. And why should this be a surprise? The power of the heavens and the firmament, as has been stated often above, is naturally implanted in things from the beginning of their generation, when they received their specific form—even if that power remains dormant under a universal state.

Furthermore, they gathered the lower waters remaining from this division into one place through what they call **distillation** <note>original: "stillatio"</note>, so that the "dry land" appeared. Beneath all of these lies the darkness, which they also removed through separation in this manner:

...that we should succumb to these frivolous arguments. Let us immediately add what follows, which will utterly cast them down from their vain hope. The **natural Binary** arose from God through the division of the higher from the lower in **Genesis** <note>referring to the second day of creation when God divided the waters</note>; it is held within the bond of Unity and produces the Ternary, since it is suited to return into Unity. But the **Binary against nature** is that which is most hostile not only to nature, but first to God; it long ago attempted to destroy all things that were created. This is the **root of all diseases and of death**, since it is held by no bond; rather, it is the first divorce, busily seeking to loosen the connection of peace and concord, not only in supernatural things but also in the natural creatures of Almighty God, the founder of all, as is clear in what follows.

# BRIEF SUMMARY
<page-num>463</page-num>

...just as in the **triad** <note>original: *ternario*; the number three, often symbolizing the Trinity</note> he saw the image of the **unary** <note>original: *unarij*; the Monad or the number one, representing God</note>, he lured himself into the most wretched condition of the **binary** <note>original: *binarii*; the number two, which the author associates with division and the fall</note>. Indeed, this binary was made a devil and a slanderer <note>original: *calumniator*</note> from an angel by his own doing, by a single thought: namely, that he might make himself a monarch, or an equal, or even superior to God. But no sooner was this crime of high treason against Divine Majesty <note>original: *crimen læsæ divinæ Majestatis*</note> conceived by him, than the binary was cast down from heaven; together with his accomplices, he fell out of the light and into the outer darkness, and he was given the punishment of perpetual death without an end to his torment.

To better explain this matter, let us bring forth the analogy of a **compass** <note>original: *circini*</note>: one foot is compared to the center, as the foundation of a building; the other foot, however, is compared to the circumference, the outlines and the boundary of the entire machine. Therefore, when the fallen angel tried to imitate God, the supreme creator, in the production of the universe, consider that he fashioned a compass for himself in his perverse mind. But in truth, he was forced to build upon another center, because two centers cannot agree in one **monarchy** <note>original: *monarchia*; a single rule or sovereignty</note>, nor can two circumferences. For this reason, he is rightly called "binary," because he attempted to lead the unity and the center of truth toward a multitude of numbers. Having assumed a center of falsehood, he drew a circumference halfway; when he had reached that point, the foot of the circumference was fixed upon another center, and through an intersection with the first, he sketched another middle circumference—concluding nothing, but displaying an interrupted figure of falsehood. From this arose the image of the brutal beast and the crooked, double serpent, raising four horns against heaven and creeping against the monarchy of truth. Once this crime was perpetrated—the root of all evils and vices—that kingdom fell, divided against itself, along with its prince Lucifer and his legions of fellow soldiers.

Therefore, we should not wonder why God, in the creation of the world on the second day of **Genesis**, did not say (as He did on the other five days) these words: *He saw that it was good*. This was because of the origin of that number, from which the multitude took the beginning of confusion, division, and controversy through the binary against God and nature. We do not assert by this (as we said above) that "two" is always to be condemned, provided that they remain in union, just as "two in one flesh"; but as often as they are divided into a **bition** <term>original: *bitionem*; a play on the Latin *unio* (union) and *bitio* (a going-twice), meaning a false doubling of unity</term>—that is, whenever they wish to effect a "twice-union" against the nature of monarchy—they are to be rejected along with the binary, together with their fourfold offspring of single-combat <note>original: *monomachiæ*</note>, or rather the quaternary, or the varying "four-horn" generated from the double-variant.

Whenever, therefore, two or more observe peace in the truth of unity, we say that the **doublet** <note>original: *duernionem*; a positive pairing or coupling</note> is well-constituted, and it is not a **duality** <note>original: *dualitatem*; here implying division</note>. We must not judge "bition" or "twice-union" in the same way, because there should not be, nor can there be, two unions, but only one—just as there is only one God, and neither more nor fewer. Furthermore, we do not wish to interpret the **ternary** <note>original: *ternarium*; the number three</note> as merely a three, because it is the offspring and the fruit of the unary...

...of the **unary** <note>original: *unarij*; the Monad or the number one, representing God’s indivisible unity</note>, which never varied from unity, as the **binary** <note>original: *binarius*; the number two, representing division</note> did. So that we may finally bring our minds back to the things we set out to say: it has been heard quite recently that that divided binary **duel** <note>original: *monomachiam*; literally "single combat," here referring to the struggle of dualism</note> has raised up **four horns** <note>The author is likely equating the "four humors" of traditional medicine with the horns of a beast or devil</note>, brought forth by the birth of the binary. By this very act, they would surpass the devil twofold, for he had only tried—though in vain—to separate and tear unity into two parts.

It is clear from their example: whereas God willed to create and bring forth a single humor, they have determined to persuade the unwary and the mentally unsound that there are **four humors** <term>four humors: the traditional medical theory that health is governed by four fluids: blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile</term>. It is a wonder why there must be four humors rather than four drynesses, four heats, and as many coldnesses; likewise four earths, four fires, four waters, and four airs, and from there four worlds. This is a marvelous and absurd confusion, by which those wretches—infidels ignorant of all truth—would strive to pull us Christians, the followers of the truth, into their insanity, if they could. 

Did they not see that wherever they turned, they could find nothing but restlessness of spirit (as even most of them have confessed), and nothing certain, true, or stable? Of such people the Apostle says: *always studying, and never arriving at the knowledge of the truth* <note>A reference to 2 Timothy 3:7</note>, because they perceive nothing unified in their studies, but see everything as contrary to the truth. The greatest proof is the maxim of their medicine, by which they teach that **"Contraries are cured by contraries"** <note>original: *Contraria contrariis esse curanda*; the fundamental principle of Galenic medicine</note>. What else is this but to admit that they are born of the false binary, which is the root of all opposition? Why do they even think that the Devil, the father of contraries, would act against himself? 

It is the Devil who introduced opposition into nature. For what reason do these Doctors think the devil has become such a friend to nature that he would finally wish to remove from it what he instead strives with the greatest zeal to increase by his own nature? Is he just as stupid as those who teach such things? For the wisdom of the serpent is established for evil, and not for good, so that even if he *could* wish to benefit man, he would never be able to. Since Almighty God does not want men to be cured through the devil, but through the truth and power which He Himself established for this purpose in natural things, brought toward union—that is, toward medicine. 

Therefore, these are lying doctrines of men, which teach that war is driven out by war, and fire is extinguished by fire, and the devil is repelled by the devil. For these things even seem to fight against the opinion of the infidels, because they are not contraries, but entirely similar. A clever person will say that this is the opinion of the **spagyrists** <term>spagyrists: alchemists, specifically followers of Paracelsus, who believed in "like cures like" (similia similibus curentur)</term>: that **"likes are cured by likes."** Do you understand the matter in such a way that you do not see the difference between healing and expulsion? Diseases are not healed, but rather the *subjects* of diseases are healed, which by their own nature were healthy before the disease struck. If, therefore, they ought to be healed, it is necessary that they become like the healthy state. If, however, [the disease] must be expelled...

# LIFE

...previously [it was shown] that there cannot be multiple centers in a single **monarchy** <note>The author uses "monarchy" to describe a state of perfect, unified health in the human body and soul.</note>, unless they are made one under a union, nor can a single space be enclosed by multiple circumferences. These things regarding medicine against spiritual illnesses: now one must come to that bodily and physical medicine, so that its **quaternary** <note>original: *quaternarius*; the number four, representing the material world and the four elements.</note> with its **ternary** <note>original: *ternario*; the number three, representing the divine or spiritual union.</note>, through the bond of union, may both meet together in a **septenary** <note>original: *septenario*; the number seven, representing a complete and perfect state of being.</note>. 

For the quaternary is ascribed as the **binary of matter** <note>The "binary" (two) represents division; here, the author suggests matter is inherently divided or unstable.</note>, because of the four elements which exhibit the whole matter of nature, just as heaven provides the same with all form and action upon said matter. Disease, therefore, is an impression of evil, through the act of a **false center** into the body, disposed to a suffering similar to that action. Conversely, medicine is the repression of evil, through the act of the true center and the universe into the body, by which it is disposed to a state capable of receiving such an act. 

Since, therefore, all disease proceeds from a single root, likewise all medicine has its progress from a single root. It is as if from the binary of confusion and discord—the origin of "multitude"—that disease broke into the monarchy of both mind and body; for this reason, all medicine is from the **unary** <note>original: *unario*; the state of oneness or unity.</note> of simplicity. What, I ask, can the "One" generate of itself other than only the ternary of union? This ternary is receptive of every temperament and simplicity, into which no "multitude" falls, and therefore no contrariety. 

Again, what foolishness it was to place the quaternary as the foundation of the medicine of the infidels <note>Likely referring to traditional Galenic physicians who relied on the four humors/elements.</note>, since it is the offspring of the binary? Let the infidels show us how there can be multiple natural principles of things. Meanwhile, we shall return to the restoration of the shattered monarchy. 

Therefore, the highest virtue and immense goodness of the invisible and indivisible center is of such efficacy that it draws to itself everything that is conformed to it in simplicity and roundness. By this it happened that man—who was created in a similar image from the beginning, though he did not remain in it of old—nevertheless, when he wishes to recover lost health of body and mind, let him study to know and understand the center exactly, and commit himself entirely to it. Then the center will be liberated from all imperfections and diseases, so that he is restored to the state of the prior monarchy, with the "four horns" removed and deleted, both mental and physical. 

So that we may better understand these four horns of the binary, it was said very recently that the devil raised these into heaven when falling and being cast down from it, and also that he afterwards attempted to fix them into the human mind: namely, **ambition, brutality, calumny, and separation** <note>original: *divortium*; literally "divorce," but used here to mean the internal separation of the soul's components.</note>. Frustrated, however, in his hope regarding the portion of calumny (which he was unable to fix into Adam), he only lethally intruded three, with the names merely changed: namely, **mental ambition** into the heat of bodily diseases; **brutality** into the boiling of the body's liquids; and **separation** into the dissolution of the temperament of the preceding parts. He would have liked to lead calumny into the complete wasting away of these, but it was not permitted to him—
