# BRIEF [ACCOUNT]

...nevertheless, to turn nature away from its own temperament. For nature never admitted any other temperament except in these three: in the **natural heat**, which is the organ of life; in the **radical moisture**, which is its nourishment; and in the **light of nature**, which provides a balanced and long life to both. Paracelsus, enlightened by the supernatural light of nature, learned by experience that he possessed these things in this manner. Accordingly, he called the natural heat **sulfur** and the light of the bodily nature; he called the radical moisture the **Mercury** of the body's life; and he called the body itself the **balsam** of bodily life, and a bright, translucent **salt**. 

However, when these things are polluted by the **binary** <note>original: *binarium*; in this context, the number two signifies division, discord, and the fall from a state of healthy unity.</note>, as we have said, he called them by these names when they introduced diseases through that binary distraction from their own temperament, which was called the "horn of divorce" <note>original: *cornu divortij*; a metaphor for the separation of the vital principles that should remain joined.</note>. Specifically: the natural heat, receding from its temperament, becomes a sulfur that is either burning or scorched, consuming and devouring all else, as is most evident from the diseases it produces. Likewise, the radical moisture, deviating from the temperament of union, becomes a Mercury that is congealed or sublimated. Similarly, the balsam of life, when it does not persist in its natural state, he called **resolved salt** <note>original: *sal resolutum*; salt that has lost its protective, solidifying property and has become "dissolved" or unstable.</note>. 

The causes of the dissolution of these temperaments and the diseases arising from them must be discussed elsewhere. Therefore, if one must grant a place to the four horns of the binary—according to the opinion of the unfaithful <note>The author likely refers to traditional Galenic or Aristotelian physicians who attribute all pathology to the four elements rather than these deeper alchemical principles.</note>—there is nowhere for them to go except into the elements. Yet, in the higher, ethereal parts of nature, there is no place for them, as is also clearly enough evident from the previous treatise. 

Therefore, let us lift up our torn monarchy of the **ternary** <note>original: *ternarius*; the triad of Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt which constitutes the "monarchy" or unified health of the human being.</note>—which has been pulled apart into the form of an **Omega** <note>The Greek letter $\Omega$, here symbolizing the end of life or a broken circle.</note> marking the end of life—by deleting its three "horns." Let us restore it on both sides into the figure of the **Alpha** <note>The Greek letter $A$, symbolizing the beginning and the restoration of life.</note> of the beginning of a restored long life, in place of a perpetual one. To do this, let us turn ourselves toward Him who said: **"I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end"** <note>original: *Ego sum alpha & omega, principium & finis*; a quote from the Book of Revelation.</note>. He Himself will teach us to walk by another way—both in supernatural and natural matters—than through the labyrinth of the unfaithful, so that we may drive all diseases away from us. 

For He Himself has no beginning, nor an end; therefore, He wished us to understand these words as a teaching for us alone, and concerning all things which He created and made for our sake. He intended for us to recognize in Him alone the beginning and end of the health and happiness of our life, tending first to His glory and then to our salvation. Furthermore, although the monarchy has been restored to us through Christ to the beginning of its prior state, lest we should ever be unmindful of so great a benefit, the torn semi-circumference of the **apple** <note>A reference to the bite taken from the forbidden fruit in Eden, which "tore" the perfect circle of human immortality.</note> is still perceived to intersect our monarchy. It carries out its "single-combat" <note>original: *monomachiam*; a spiritual and physical struggle.</note> against us, both in the soul and in the body, as long as we dwell in this falling state. This is evident from the mark of the **Alpha**, in which an arc intersects the circle, just as a semicircle intersects a whole one. 

The medicine for the **ternary** of the soul or mind, therefore, is the **uncreated unity** given from the uncreated center of truth; but the medicine of the body is the **created unity**, born from the center of the created universe.

# LIFE

<meta>catchword: led</meta>

**Unity**, however, in no way requires medicine, because it is health itself. **Duality**, on the other hand, is disease, which can by no means grasp medicine, since it was condemned to eternal death in the "binary of falsehood" <note>original: *binario falsi*; refers to the state of division or separation from God and nature's wholeness</note> without mercy. Truly, only the **Ternary** <note>original: *ternarius*; the number three, representing the three Paracelsian principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> is that into which medicine falls through the **Unary**, because it was deemed worthy of grace through Him who alone is one and merciful. 

Therefore, we do not see why the infidels <note>the author refers to traditional Galenic physicians as "infidels" for rejecting the spiritual/alchemical unity of nature</note> attribute medicine to the **Quaternary** (the number four); for it is condemned together with its root, the binary, from which it was generated with the same condition and nature as its parents. Indeed, good fruit is never produced from a bad tree. Therefore, let them continue to build their edifice upon the sand and protect it with a roof—nevertheless exposed to the winds and the lightning of Jupiter—while we build upon solid rock. 

In brief, this is our foundation in medicine: Just as the health of a long life was given to us by God through **Unity**, it is through that same unity, and never otherwise, that it must be recovered. In the same way, every disease of a short life has its origin through **Duality** alone. 

Furthermore, I remember that I previously planted the tree of the health of long life in the **Ternary**; it remains for us to examine that which was once planted by the natural binary, and was supplanted by the "binary of falsehood" with these sophistical words: *You shall by no means* (by no means, he said) *die* <note>original: *Nequaquam moriemini*; a reference to the Serpent's lie to Eve in Genesis 3:4, which the author links to the origin of division and death</note>, and what follows. 

Because of the four imperfections in the planets in the sky, they wish for four elements to correspond in our body: as to Saturn, Mercury, Venus, and Mars, they correspond to earth, water, air, and fire, from which the body is forged—and it is infirm because of the imperfection of its parts. Therefore, let a tree be planted from these elements, whose root is ascribed to Saturn, through which that various Mercury and Venus provide the trunk and ascending branches, the leaves, and the flowers, while Mars provides the fruit. 

Here a great disagreement occurs between the <term>spagyrists</term> <note>alchemical physicians who use the art of "separation and recombination" to create medicines</note> and the infidel physicians. It seemed right to place this here so that the latter might see the opinion of the former; let them examine it accurately enough and visit it from every side to see if they find any authority from the light of nature that can weaken it, and render **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>the legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the foundation of alchemy and hermetic philosophy is attributed</note> along with his followers a disciple of **Hippocrates** and **Galen**; if not, let the latter become disciples of Hermes. 

There is no reason why either of the two parties should bring forward their own writers as authority for their doctrine; otherwise, the dispute will remain forever undecided. Let them establish **Nature** alone as the author and judge of medicine, and let them fight among themselves using authorities derived from her light. 

Meanwhile, I shall attempt to describe the opinions of both one side and the other, as far as I am able, starting from the aforementioned "supplanting"—introduced to the elements and the heavens alike through the binary of falsehood and through the word "you shall by no means die." The opinion of the infidel physicians is that four humors exist in the human body, which they call black and yellow bile, blood, and phlegm, from which they constitute their physical body. ### BRIEF.

...led by reason, because they see water floating on top of human blood drawn from a vein or another place, which they call phlegm <note>original: *pituitam*; traditionally one of the four humors, associated with cold and moisture</note>: they also judged from this, and from the mixture of yellow and black colors, that the four elements consist of four humors, and that the human body is made from these. Yet, in truth, God separated the elements from a single humor—that of the "lower waters"—not into four peculiar humors, but into a single one, and the remaining three elements are far different and entirely foreign in form from that humor. What wonder is it? Since they follow only manifest nature, they are utterly ignorant of the occult <note>the hidden or internal spiritual forces</note>: they cannot judge anything except superficially. 

Truly, the matter does not stand in these hidden things as they have thought. Have they been able to perceive that the body and the blood are two different bodies? The first is that which is nourished and was produced from seed; the latter is that which nourishes, coming from external food and drink. Therefore, their judgment concerns the nourishing and external body, but not that which is the subject of accidents and susceptible to diseases. Consequently, they treat the food and drink converted into blood and excrement, rather than the disordered natural body and its accidental or waste-related ailments. 

If they should say there is no difference between the seed <note>original: *sperma*</note> and the blood, claiming that the former is generated from the excess of the latter: we deny what they assert, namely that blood—as it remains in the veins or elsewhere—is the origin of the seed. From that, an absurdity would follow: namely, that the human body is generated only from liquids, and not also from the other more solid members, and that the whole generated body would be bloody, not fleshy or bony, etc. On the contrary, we certainly admit that blood is transmuted by nature into the nourishment of the individual members of the body, but then it is no longer blood, nor does it have the form of blood; rather, it is abundant nourishment transformed into flesh and bone before it can take the form of seed. Likewise, it is not formed from some waste, but is separated from the most potent and most necessary substance of the individual members of the body; otherwise, the fetus would not be complete in all its members. Therefore, human blood is not the primary nor the proximate matter of the seed (even if it is the most remote), but this seed is a gathered chaos <note>original: *chaos*; here meaning a primal, undifferentiated substance containing the potential for all parts of the body</note> of all members, parts, and faculties into one intense center, for the extension of its own form. 

Again, the purest blood—separated from the other three mentioned humors of both biles and choler <note>original: *bilis & choleræ*; referring to yellow and black bile</note>—contains within itself elements purer and more sincere than those which appear on the surface of the blood. But thus far the tree of the elements has been uprooted by the binary of falsehood <note>original: *falsi binario*; the state of division or separation from natural unity</note>, which is restored in this way: Its Root is Saturnian <note>associated with the planet Saturn; representing stability, lead, and the solid parts of the body</note> and all the more solid parts. All the sap which rises through the root into the trunk, branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits, is Mercurial <note>associated with the planet Mercury; representing the fluid, vital spirit</note>. The heat and fire which, sucking up such sap, draws it forth, is partly Martial <note>associated with Mars; signifying sharp or digestive heat</note>, and partly Venereal <note>associated with Venus; signifying the heat of generation and attraction</note>. # THE DUEL OF THE SOUL
<meta>catchword: food</meta>

Venus cannot be separated from Mars any more than air can be separated from fire, because there is an indissoluble marriage between those two. For no air is void of fire, and no fire can exercise its powers without air. Wherefore both should be held as one and the same natural sulfur <term>sulfur: in alchemy, the active, solar, or masculine principle of a substance</term>. From these three things mentioned <note>Saturn, Mercury, and the Mars-Venus union</note>, the true spagyrists <term>spagyrist: a physician-alchemist who "separates and recombines" substances to create medicine</term> have most consistently taught that all diseases are imprinted upon the physical body (which they said belongs to the seed and not to food), through three most general types; they even assigned specific species to each type. Just as a root in the earth, and the branches above the earth, are spread through the trunk into various extremities, so too does a physical and infirm Saturn <note>original: *Saturnus physicus*; associated with lead and the element of earth</note> imprint his various diseases into the "earth" of the human body—that is, into all its more solid parts. Likewise, an infirm Mercury pours his diseases through the trunk and all the branches into the human liquor <note>the fluids or "living waters" of the body</note>. And an unhealthy Mars, together with his physical Venus, sets the human fire ablaze with various flames. This is the work, this is the labor <note>A classic reference to Virgil's *Aeneid*: *Hoc opus, hic labor est*</note> to assign to each of these three types their peculiar species, so that conversely, the "tree of infirmity" of a short life might be transmuted into the "tree of health" of a long life, of which we spoke above.

...they have converted into the Jupiter of charity. The prior companion of these men, **Mars**, had directed **Saturn** toward this: that they should seek dominion over others, but none over themselves. Now, however, through the help of **Jupiter** whom they have recently possessed, let them strive to rule and restrain their vain, ambitious, and proud appetites. In this way, they will transmute **Mars**—who was imperious toward others—into their own dominant **Sun** <note>The Sun often represents the light of reason, the heart, or the vital spirit in this period's philosophy.</note>, the reformer of their wicked life.

**Venus** had also persuaded those men to seek riches for the fulfillment of all their carnal appetites. Now, on the contrary, let them constantly pursue the love of chastity and integrity, and thus they will change their lustful **Venus** into the most modest and chaste **Moon**. 

If you do not understand this well enough, I will explain it more broadly. As soon as you feel the pockets of greedy **Mercury** stimulating your imagination, recall the voluntary poverty of **Christ**. Against the vengeance and tyranny of **Mars**, oppose the patience of **Christ**. Against the lust of **Venus**, oppose the purity of the temple of God, which your heart ought to be. More briefly: against all these things, be mindful of death and resurrection.

A reference to Matthew 4:10.</note> and immediately return to good meditations. In this persistent battle, thus conquer evil with good—that is, drive away temptation with prayer. The most powerful weapons with which one must fight in this duel are prayer, through which we acquire strength and power against our enemy.

For example, if someone has **Jupiter** as their second leader, their pursuit will be directed toward piety, charity, and holiness—provided that the first companion favors that inclination. Furthermore, a pursuit ruled by **Mars** as leader, with the **Sun** as the first companion, seeks a kingdom through war. If **Jupiter** follows that leader, it leads to piety; if **Venus**, to lust; if **Mercury**, to greed and the expansion of wealth and riches; if the **Moon**, to the preservation of peace. 

The pursuit of the **Sun**, with **Jupiter** as the first companion, seeks a kingdom for the glory of God. If with **Mars**, it leads to cruelty and tyranny; if with **Venus**, to pleasures; if with **Mercury**, to the accumulation of wealth; if with **Moon**, to the tranquility of the fatherland. ...with **Jupiter** as a companion, the individual is directed toward an honorable marriage in the observance of holiness. Yet the pursuit of **Mercury** himself, when **Jupiter** is the primary companion, signifies honest trade or lawful arts practiced without deceit. If his companion is **Mars**, it signifies robberies and plunderings; if the **Sun**, dominion; if **Venus**, debauchery; if the **Moon**, integrity. 

Truly, the pursuit of the **Moon**, with **Jupiter** as the primary companion, signifies health of conscience; with **Mars**, it signifies stubbornness; if with the **Sun**, wisdom; with **Venus**, chastity; with **Mercury**, the preservation of things acquired. The remaining second and third companions, and so on, are to be judged in this same way. 

Anyone will be able to recognize these leaders and companions within themselves in this manner, even if they have not learned to do so by any other method. Let them consider what first and most powerfully comes to mind, and what pursuit or desire sticks most tenaciously. If they find it is a desire to be enriched, they already have an indication of the inclination of **Saturn** toward **Mercury**. Second, if the desire is that they might live at leisure and free, they have the inclination of **Mars**, who "desires to reap where he did not sow" <note>original: "metere cupit ubi non fævit" — likely a variation of the biblical phrase regarding reaping where one did not sow, indicating an entitled or predatory nature</note>, to command and not to obey. Third, if it should be that they might live in luxury, they have the inclination of **Venus**. 

Nor should one lose heart if some good companions have followed these. For instance, if through a fourth thought they were moved to pity for a ruined or needy brother, they already have the inclination of **Jupiter**, which they can substitute in the place of **Mercury**. If, from a fifth pursuit, a desire for serving God more diligently in the future than before comes to mind, they have the inclination of the **Sun** to be substituted in the place of **Mars**. Sixth, if the thought was that they should abstain from vanities, they have the inclination of the **Moon**, which they can exchange for **Venus**.

But these things are presented to mockers in a way that appears simple, so that they may laugh more at the "insanity" if they wish; while hearing, they do not understand. 

For indeed, that serpent has closed the ears and blinded the eyes of the mind with darkness, lest his followers see their own nakedness and, confessing it at some point along with **Adam**, come to their senses. So that they may do this, it is necessary that we uncover the serpent’s cunning in deception as much as we can. 

The prophet **Moses** says: *But the serpent was more cunning than all the animals of the earth which the Lord God had made, who said to the woman, "Why did God command you that you should not eat from every tree of Paradise?"*

# THE DUEL OF THE SOUL
<meta>catchword: lean)</meta>

...to be held by the woman, he decided that this long cloak was necessary, under which each part of his wickedness—from head to foot, that is, from the beginning to the end of the deceptions he had devised—might lie hidden and covered. Furthermore, seeing that this kind of animal is most ready to penetrate through any cracks or fissures, he believed that by this very means, by slithering, he could gradually make his entrance into a mind that was still whole and conscious of no evil. Therefore, cloaked in this manner and attacking her simplicity, he addresses her with captious and lying questions from his own brand of sophistry: *Why did God command that you not eat from every tree?* <note>original: "Quare præcepit Deus omne lignum." A reference to Genesis 3:1, where the Serpent begins his deception by misrepresenting God's command.</note>

Behold how shrewdly the "Father of Sophists" <term>Sophists: originally a class of teachers in ancient Greece, the term became a pejorative for those who use clever but fallacious and deceptive reasoning.</term> proposes a fallacy. Through a lying question, he attempts to draw even the poor woman toward a lie, testing if he might somehow make a small crack in that still-whole kingdom of the soul, and through it, creep inside—which is exactly what he did. Thus, the poorly cautious woman—who more wisely would have remained silent or said, "be gone far from here"—responds to the devil's lie (concerning "every tree") by adding a doubled lie of her own: *lest we touch it,* she said, *and lest perhaps we die.* <note>The author notes that Eve altered God's words in Genesis 3:3; God had not explicitly forbidden "touching" the tree, nor was the death "perhaps" or a mere possibility.</note> 

Now, God had not said "you shall not eat of every tree"; on the contrary, He said, *Eat from every tree of paradise.* But that worthless Sophist tried to lure her toward a lie with the bait of a lie. Furthermore, the Lord God had not forbidden them from touching the tree, nor did He leave them any occasion for doubting their death if they should eat; rather, He asserted it quite affirmatively, saying, *You shall surely die,* <note>original: "morte moriemini" (literally: "by death you shall die"). A Hebrew idiom indicating the absolute certainty of the outcome.</note> as if to say "you shall die," or rather, "you shall most certainly die." 

Once he had gained entry through the lies brought forth on both sides, the worthless blasphemer repeated his lie and simultaneously accused God of lying: *By no means,* he said, *shall you die.* It was as if he were saying, "the matter is not as God has persuaded you." The villain added this to confirm his false and sophisticated argument: *For God knows that on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like Gods, knowing good and evil.* 

First, he accuses God of envy, so that he might make the woman an enemy to God in this regard, as if God envied them the happiness of possessing divinity. Second, he tries to persuade the woman to look at the fruit with her fleshly eyes, so that she might be lured toward appetite by this sight; likewise, he speaks as if God were "bewitching" their eyes so that they would not see the happiness within the fruit, in order to make them more and more disobedient to God. Third, he concludes that they must not obey, but rather should make a trial of the outcome. 

In no different way has the doctrine of "unfaithful wise men" been accustomed to deceptively cheat the minds of men until now. First of all, such a person gains authority for himself with a certain cloaked display, with the adornment of his garments stretched out into the long form of a serpent and presenting a "serpentine wisdom." Then, he uses the elegance of interspersed speech—now in Latin, soon in Greek, then in Hebrew, Chaldean, or Arabic—even though some of these men barely know their own mother tongue.

...to be seen) with little words, so that by this variety the ears of men might be fascinated; drawn into admiration of such a variegated speech, they might believe that much wisdom is hidden under his long, flowing cloak. <note>original: "sub talari veste." Literally a garment reaching the ankles, symbolizing a scholarly or religious authority that masks the "serpent" within.</note> In this same way, the Pharisees once hid their own serpent under a similar mantle when they approached Christ; no differently than that "serpentine binary" <note>The "binary" or the number two was often associated in mystical thought with the first departure from Divine Unity, and thus with division, doubt, and the devil.</note> approached Eve, they began with sophistical questions, testing if they might find some entrance to ensnare him with their cleverness. They hoped he might not easily extricate himself and would instead be dragged into some error, providing them an occasion for mockery and a pretext to remove him from their midst.

Truly, if the doctrine of these unfaithful ones had proceeded from the Word of God, or could be proved as having been taken from there, we would embrace it without any resistance. But that miserable serpent of the binary will sooner return to being an angel of light than that shall happen.

# THE DUEL OF THE SOUL

->...of the devil,<-

that we may consider more broadly the craftiness of the arch-sophist <term>Arch-sophist: A master of "sophistry," the use of clever but false arguments intended to deceive.</term>, which he used in deceiving Eve. That sharp-tongued supplanter did not wish to use his first "horn" <note>original: "cornu." In logic, the "horns of a dilemma" are the points of an argument used to trap an opponent.</note> at the start, nor the same argument by which he himself had fallen; he reserved that for the end (just as sophists sometimes perversely put later points before earlier ones, so that they may more securely deceive the mind through confusion). Indeed, through ambition, he had transformed himself from an angel of light into an angel of darkness. 

Instead, he used the other "horn" from the opposite side of the semi-circle—specifically, a slander directed first against God. He lied with deliberate effort. He knew the truth of the matter, yet he asks a question—not because God had forbidden every tree, but he either feigns ignorance or, more likely, frames his question through a lie so that he might incite the woman <note>The Latin "muliercula" is a diminutive, suggesting she was viewed as vulnerable or simple in the face of the devil's complex logic.</note> into giving a lying response herself. This is evident from the first words of Eve’s answer: *We eat of the fruit of the trees, etc.* <note>Genesis 3:2</note>—as if she were saying, "The matter is not as you ask, but in this way." Behold, as soon as she entered into conversation with the devil, she was infected by the slander of the lie against God; wounded by that "horn," she brought forth a double lie. 

For what else is slander but a lie joined with a quibble, and vice versa? Someone might say: "You said before that the 'monarchy' <term>Monarchy: Here, the "Monarchy of Truth" refers to an undivided, sovereign state of divine reality and integrity.</term> was only torn on one side, because the slanderer could not force the human into slander; why do you now bring forth a different view?" I bring forth nothing but what I said before: that Adam was never reduced to slander. Rather, he confessed the pure and sheer truth to his Lord, saying: *I heard your voice and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid myself;* and likewise, *the woman whom you gave me as a companion, she gave to me, and I ate.* <note>Genesis 3:10-12</note> Where was he lying? Not at all, for it happened exactly as he spoke. 

Therefore, on his part, the monarchy of truth was not torn but remained coherent; but on Eve’s part, the way was opened through which the serpent crept. For he knew that he could not gain an entrance through the **Ternary** <note>The number three (Ternary) was traditionally associated with spiritual perfection and the Trinity; here it represents Adam's original integrity.</note> of Adam while the **Unary** <note>The number one (Unary) represents Unity and God.</note> was protecting that Ternary. He therefore attempted to enter through the **Binary** <note>The number two (Binary) was viewed by mystical philosophers as the first departure from Unity, and thus the number of division, doubt, and conflict.</note> of Eve, so that he might achieve his goal through the likeness of the first number of multitude and confusion—for "like is more easily attracted by like" than by the unlike. 

Again, it will be asked: since Eve was created perfect, how could she be seduced? For it is foreign to all perfection to fall. We shall respond with another question about a similar case; once that is answered exactly, we shall respond even more clearly than now. How did it happen that the angel of light, who was created far more perfect in an even more incorruptible heaven, fell when he had no occasion and no one persuading him? 

Therefore, we must be especially careful, O brothers, against **false imaginations**, lest they persuade us of things that are outside the monarchy of truth. For this reason, these certain examples from Holy Scripture were to be proposed to you, so that you might be armed and become more vigilant and cautious in repelling the snares of the devil.

which you now perceive better than before through your imaginations and thoughts. Through these, he strives to creep in like a thief and a robber into your inner kingdom <note>original: "monarchiam," literally "monarchy," referring here to the self-sovereignty or the ruling part of the soul.</note> of truth and simplicity, so that he might tear it apart by enticing you to answer him, or by causing you to dwell on them even for a short time. Now at last he uses his first horn, which he knew and experienced in himself to be the most effective temptation of all, by which he had fallen into the crime of high treason against Divine Majesty. For he was not satisfied with that happiness which God had deemed him worthy of—namely, the sight of Him and the enjoyment of His glory and the highest good—but he even wanted to be God. We do not disdain this name; for we would rather enter the new Jerusalem with our leader Christ, sitting upon a young donkey, than be led to eternal punishments upon the most adorned mules.

We have said before that the world was created in order, and that this consists of three things: namely, number, measure, and weight <note>original: "numero, mensura, & pondere." This is a reference to the Wisdom of Solomon 11:20: "But thou hast arranged all things by measure and number and weight."</note>: which God wished to use as instruments for our instruction. Therefore, beginning from numbers, we say that all numbers are consummated in the ternary <note>The number three.</note>, and in it is the most absolute end of all numbers. For when the ternary is reflected into itself, through generation it produces the nonary <note>The number nine (3x3).</note>, beyond which it is not permitted to progress in numbers; rather, one must return to unity <note>The number one.</note>, through which the second unity of the second order of numbers arises <note>Meaning that after 9, we reach 10, which starts a new cycle of tens (10, 20, 30, etc.).</note>. This same thing is accustomed to happen in the accumulation of the first three numbers, 2, 3, and 4, which also provide the same absolute completion. From this, it can be seen how the ternary is the most excellent of all numbers.

On the contrary, let us examine the imperfection of the binary <note>The number two.</note>. The binary, by its own reproduction through generation, produces the quaternary <note>The number four.</note>, which is certainly distant from the completion of numbers. Although some wish for that completion to be in the quaternary—since they say that by the accumulation of the first four numbers, the denary <note>The number ten (1+2+3+4=10).</note> is made—the contrary is sufficiently clear; for the denary is surpassed by the quaternary, as is evident from the aggregation of the first numbers, 2, 3, 4, and 5 <note>Adding 2+3+4+5 equals 14, surpassing 10.</note>. For the "unary" <note>The number one, or Unity.</note> is not a number, nor is it to be counted among them; and if those committing a wrong act do it in this way—1, 2, 3, 4—so that they may forge the denary, we nevertheless deny that the denary is the completion of numbers through generation; for in this way, that offspring surpasses the denary by twice the quaternary <note>The author is arguing that the number one is the source of number, not a number itself.</note>. 

And although by progressing beyond the denary a return to unity is made, it must not be thought for that reason that unity puts on this multitude or composition because it is found in a series of composites. For in that place, it exists for the reduction of composite things into simplicity and purity, just as it exists in the denary like a center in a circle; however, in the "vigenary" <note>The number twenty.</note> it is not so, but the binary is the center of the vigenary for the sake of fabricating the "single-combat" <note>original: "monomachia."</note> placed above. Indeed, in the "centenary" <note>The number one hundred.</note> and "millenary" <note>The number one thousand.</note> and those similar to them, unity again presents itself as the center. These things are especially to be noted, because they are highly necessary for <term>spagyrics</term> <note>Spagyrics is an alchemical term for the production of herbal medicines through the process of separation and recombination, often linked to the "art of Hermes."</note>.

We do not deny that the quaternary can rest in the ternary, toward the constitution of the philosophical hebdomad <note>A grouping of seven (3+4=7), often representing the seven classical planets or the seven stages of alchemical transformation.</note>, of which we made ample mention above; and yet, not before it strips off the nature of its parent, the binary, making a passage through the ternary to the simplicity of unity, and thereafter to the attained philosophy. ...and we will listen with a cheerful mind; meanwhile, however, we shall proceed to our purpose. Therefore, our <term>ternary</term> <note>The number three.</note>, which we are now discussing, is threefold: namely, natural, artificial, and supernatural. Again, the natural is either simple or composite; the artificial is "decomposed" <note>separated into its parts</note> or moral; or it is supernatural, which latter most often follows the artificial and sometimes precedes it. 

The simple ternary does not allow for composition, because it is pure and separated from the composite. The composite ternary receives the <term>quaternary</term> <note>The number four.</note>, yet does not mix well with it except by the removal of its own <term>binary</term> <note>The number two.</note>; once this binary is overcome, it becomes the <term>septenary</term> <note>The number seven.</note>. The decomposed ternary is made by the <term>spagyric art</term> <note>Alchemical techniques of separating and recombining substances to reach a purer state.</note> through the total separation of the binary from the septenary, bringing them into union. The moral ternary is formed through the "scale of meditative philosophy" previously set down. The supernatural ternary, however, is a gift of God, and rests in the union of the mind. The hinge of this whole mystery turns upon the casting away of the binary: then finally the ternary, joined to the quaternary, causes the latter to rest in the former through the septenary. When the ternary is restored to this, one arrives at a likeness of unity in the revolution of the <term>denary</term> <note>The number ten.</note>, which lurks under the form of a center—as we have said—in natural things as much as in any others, and in the supernatural.

Enough has been said so far regarding the order of the world through numbers; let us now come to the order of measure. Just recently we said that in numbers the <term>unary</term> <note>The number one; the point of origin.</note> is the center of the ternary and its offspring—namely the <term>nonary</term> <note>The number nine.</note>—just as a point is in a circle. Therefore, the fountain and origin of the first measure is the center; for if a point flows from it in a straight line until it rests, a straight line is made. If this line is carried around the previously mentioned "flowing point" while the center remains unmoved until it returns to its place, a circle is made: an image of the triad in unity, or <term>monarchy</term> <note>original: "monarchiæ." Here used to mean a single, unified divine rule.</note>. 

This same straight line measures the circle precisely into a perfect hexagon, which, by skipping every other angle, delineates the figure of a ternary, and from that perfection proceeds an equilateral <term>triangle</term> <note>original: "trigonum."</note>. Furthermore, it should be noted that the center is the unary (one) and the circle is its ternary (three); whatever is inserted between the center and the enclosed monarchy must be considered as a binary (two), whether it be another circle, or a triangle, or any other figure.

I said recently that the dark angel <note>Lucifer/Satan.</note> had fashioned for himself a pair of compasses, one foot of which was revolving ambition, while the other was slander. When he tried to fix slander in place, he circled for so long until he reached a "half-three" <note>original: "semiternariam."</note> figure; then finally ambition turned into slander, and slander became ambition. ...he vigorously took up this instrument again, trying to see if he could somehow build a monarchy better than the first. Therefore, taking his beginning from the aforementioned intersection <note>Latin: *interfectione*. In geometry, this refers to the point where lines meet, but the author also plays on the word's meaning of "slaughter" or "destruction."</note>, he approached the matter with intersections. He fixed both feet of the compass: one in brutality and the other in separation. While he was circling with brutality until he had drawn a little more than a third of the circle's outline, the foot of separation moved from its place; with a growing slipperiness, it deceived its craftsman and yielded the center. Thus it happened that the foot of brutality, being recalled to its place from which it had first proceeded by that wicked craftsman, took the place of the center, while the foot of separation made a circuit similar to the first through the first intersection of the first book of Euclid <note>A reference to Euclid's *Elements*, Book 1, Proposition 1, which describes how to describe an equilateral triangle upon a given finite straight line by intersecting two circles.</note>. When the wicked craftsman saw that he had now been deceived twice and had accomplished nothing more than before, the "roaring lion" <note>A common biblical reference to the devil from 1 Peter 5:8.</note>, seeking in his wrath a <term>ternary</term> <note>A set of three; here representing the divine or perfect order.</note> to devour, circled around by repeating those mentioned intersections. Thus it happened that through three intersections he fixed three points, and six in total—four through intersections and the remaining two at the divided ends—along with eight serpents. Yet the most wicked corrupter of all crafts was able to bring none of these either to a square surface or to a solid cube. For his entire structure lacked any center, without which nothing can ever be perfect, solid, or stable in the whole nature of things. We conclude, therefore, that the devil exists only incidentally, lacking a center—that is, lacking the Word of God, **without whom nothing was made that was made.** <note>original: *fine quo factum eft nihil quod factum eft*. A quote from the Gospel of John 1:3.</note> For God alone can make something from nothing, and the best from the weak, and likewise all that is from that which is not; and He does this through His Word alone, which is the supernatural center of all power and of the truth of all things in all. 

Through the corruption of his own ternary (under which the angel had been created from the beginning), that figure called the <term>quaternary</term> <note>The number four, associated here with material corruption or a falling away from the divine three.</note> attempted to tear apart and divide the monarchy of the human ternary with these four intersections and eight serpents (intersected two by two) into so many and such horrid, irreparable parts due to the lack of a center. Yet he was unable to achieve this, because he was not permitted to delete the small residue of the center of truth remaining in Adam, despite the introduction of calumny and lies into which he had drawn Eve. Therefore, the almighty and merciful God, taking pity on the distressed misery and calamitous state of Adam and Eve together, decreed that He would erase this introduced mark of perdition—which was cut apart and clung together only by a tiny point—and restore them to His own whole monarchy. This was done by restoring this tiny point into a center, which is the true character and the safest mark of our salvation situated in the Word of God.

### THE DUEL OF THE SOUL

Therefore, it will be necessary to place a center for the **single combat** <note>original: *monomachia*. This refers to the spiritual struggle or the geometric tension within the diagram.</note> in this manner, namely: From each of the intersections looking at each other from across the diameter, always skipping two as you go around, let three diagonal lines be drawn; in the point where they intersect, the true center that is sought is found. 

So that I may now clearly demonstrate to you the image of the reduction of the **ternary** <note>The number three.</note> to the simplicity of **unity** <note>The number one, representing God.</note>, through the casting aside of the **binary** <note>The number two, which often represents division or duality.</note>, and also by what means the **quaternary** <note>The number four.</note> can rest within the ternary through conjunction, and become a participant in union along with it, take note: 

From each point to each intersection, draw straight lines; in this way you will have a quaternary of equilateral triangles: one of which is enclosed by the other three, but none of them has life or a center except the middle one, because in a monarchy there cannot be many centers, nor more lives than one. Do you see now the quaternary concluded within the ternary, yet not yet resting in the true **philosophical week** <note>original: *hebdomas philosophica*. A mystical reference to the number seven, signifying completion or the Sabbath rest.</note>, about which I have recently spoken twice? 

Therefore, so that it may be reduced along with the ternary to the simplicity of unity, the ternary must be completely cast aside in this very way: From the center of the whole ternary to any of the three points of the great triangle, let a straight line be drawn. This line is mentally understood to be revolved from its outer end, while staying fixed at the other end in the center. Then, whatever points and lines exist are to be abolished and deleted by that revolution, until the line returns to where it began its motion. 

Now no binary of the circle will appear in the monarchy, no ternary, and no quaternary either; but here the quaternary now rests in the ternary, it lies hidden, and together with it rejoices under unity—though it is not visible to external eyes, but only to the eyes of the mind. Only the remaining line of the semi-diameter is seen, which is what remains of the **apple** <note>A reference to the forbidden fruit and the Fall of Man.</note>; because of this, we must fight manfully and not weakly every day against the single combat of the crafty serpent while we remain in this falling state. We must do this lest, forgetting the transgression of both our first parents, we fall back into that very same sin. 

Behold, best of readers, you now have the idea of the monarchy of the **triad** <note>The Trinity.</note> in unity, depicted for you and placed before your eyes by me. From this—by penetrating with the edge of your mind deeper than the letter or the picture displays—you will know whatever pertains to <term>spagyric</term> <note>The alchemical process of separating and recombining elements to reach a higher state of purity.</note> and perfected philosophy, aided however by those things which I have recently revealed to you in this little work. 

It will not be my fault if you do not fare well in this matter, provided that you do not begrudge yourself the happiness of understanding these **secrets** <note>original: *arcana*.</note> through laziness and sluggishness. These secrets are necessary above all others in this life; because through admiration of the great works of God, they lead us as if by the hand to His true knowledge. Indeed, they draw us into His love, in which also the highest good of Christians lies hidden—and is open only to those believing in God through the Word, the center of truth, His Son, in whom and through whom all things are. To Him alone, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be praise, honor, and glory forever.

It remains in order that we balance this one through weights.

We said before that the order of creation consists of numbers, measure, and weight <note>This refers to a famous biblical passage from the Wisdom of Solomon 11:20: "But thou hast arranged all things by measure and number and weight."</note>. The two preceding ones <note>Number and measure.</note> we completed through the **unary** <term>the number one</term> and the **ternary** <term>the number three</term> alone, without the aid of others. Now, let us also weigh the weights to infinity through these same numbers, which can be done better or more aptly by no others. With only two weights—the first of one pound and the second of three—the weighing proceeds into infinite weights. Just as one is balanced by these, two weights—this one and one—weigh three, or three pounds. This weight once, and one once, makes four; three once, and one twice, makes five; three twice makes six; three twice and one once, makes seven; three twice and one twice, makes eight; three thrice makes nine; thrice three and one once, makes ten; thrice three and one twice, makes eleven; three four times makes twelve; and so on into many thousands of thousands.

But if anyone wishes to do this with lighter effort, let him fashion for himself three other odd weights from the **quinary** <note>the number five</note>, the **septenary** <note>the number seven</note>, and the **novenary** <note>the number nine</note>; or let him add weighted matter to the increase of weighted matter as often as it seems expedient. Indeed, however, **spagyric** <term>alchemical; the art of separating and recombining substances</term> weights remain in unity, nor do they have progress toward increase except through unity, like the progress of a single center toward its first monarchy and circumference—namely, the **decade** <note>the number ten</note>; and from the same center to the second unity, one hundred; to the third, one thousand; to the fourth, ten thousand; to the fifth, one hundred thousand; to the sixth, a million; to the seventh, ten million, and so on to infinity.

This progression of order is not so much spagyric as it is natural, and most hidden in the center of nature, yet brought into the light and manifested through the spagyric art, or led from its potential into actual existence. These are the things which ought to have been said in this place concerning numerical weights, both artificial and natural, through the unary, ternary, and denary <note>The numbers one, three, and ten.</note>. However, let us see what that **binary** <note>the number two</note>, with its **quaternary** <note>the number four</note>, is able to provide in artificial weights. With a weight of two pounds and another of four pounds, there is no way the unary nor the ternary—in short, no odd weight—can be balanced, but only even ones. In natural things, however, they exercise their tyranny, dragging all parts of nature through divisions <note>original: *sectiones*</note> out of just proportion and monarchy.

Dissolve the **mercury of the philosophers** <term>a specialized alchemical starting material, not common quicksilver</term> itself into its vegetable **quintessence** <term>the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual core of a substance</term>. Divide this into four parts: let one part be a quarter, and the other be three-quarters. From the three-quarters, take one and a half portions, and from the first quarter-part take a half portion; together these make up half of the whole. In this manner, three-eighths will remain to be buried in the earth, and one-eighth is to be exposed to the air along with the other things that will be mentioned later.

In a certain portion of the remaining half-part, dissolve a portion of **the moon** <note>original: "lunæ"; refers to silver</note>. Once dissolved, clarify it through a filter and save it, discarding the dregs as useless. Dissolve all the remaining **planets** <note>In alchemy, the planets refer to the seven metals: Saturn (lead), Jupiter (tin), Mars (iron), the Sun (gold), Venus (copper), Mercury (quicksilver), and the Moon (silver).</note> in a suitable portion of the **mercurial water** <note>original: "aquæ Mercurialis"</note> for each, and do exactly as was done with the moon.

The other phial, which contains the dregs, you should bury entirely in the earth under the open sky, except for the very tip of the neck which should stick out slightly. You shall do the same thing separately for each of the other planets. 

In two other phials, enclose the saved mercurial water and seal them as before: in the one to be placed in the air, let there be the "eighth" part mentioned earlier; in the other, which is to be buried in the earth, let there be the "three-eighths." By this work, you will have completed the **philosophical solution**; now you may proceed to the **coagulation** <term>the process of turning a liquid back into a solid</term>.

When a year has passed, have glass artisans blow a double vessel for you in the shape of a very round sphere divided through the middle. The upper vessel should be fitted to the lower one so that it can be removed and replaced whenever necessary. Once this is done, make empty wax molds for yourself, shaped like little vessels or boats, which are capable of being filled with liquid and floating upon water. 

The method for making such molds is this: Have an oblong iron tool, filed and polished at one end into the shape you wish the stone to take. Let this be dipped in oil, then submerged at that end into melted wax, and then into cold water. Once the wax coating is cut around, it is freed from the iron, and you will have the molds you desire. 
*Alternatively:* See to it that stones shaped in any round or rough form are cut or polished with a rotating wheel, just like natural ones. 

Finally, take the phials out of the earth and take down the others from the air. Then, fill the lower part of your spherical vessel with the "earthy" mercurial water so that it fills half of it, and set the wax molds to float upon it. Afterward, if you wish to have a **Saturnian, Jovial, Martial, Solar, Venereal, Mercurial, or Lunar stone** <note>These are artificial gems corresponding to the seven metals/planets: lead, tin, iron, gold, copper, mercury, and silver.</note>, fill the wax molds slightly less than full with the "heaven" of any of the said planets—that is, the aerial water—but do not fill them to the very top, lest the liquid overflow. Then, finally, [cover] the lower spherical vessel with its upper part...

Ancient sages knew how to cure nearly every illness without resorting to superstition, simply by using stones and metals engraved under specific **planetary alignments** <note>original: "tempore constellationum"</note> and worn around the neck. Where, I ask, does this power come from? It arises partly from the material itself, partly from the symbols and images carved into it, and most significantly from the virtues formally infused by the heavens into matter that has been properly prepared. These celestial influences flow more abundantly through precisely observed astrological alignments, guided by the right applications that bring these latent powers into physical effect.

This is not surprising to those who understand the unbreakable bond between the **superior world** <term>the Macrocosm, or the heavens and celestial spheres</term> and the **inferior world** <term>the Microcosm, or the earthly realm</term>—a relationship like an indissoluble natural marriage. Indeed, nothing can be moved by human art down here without a corresponding movement in the heavens above. Conversely, whatever occurs in the heavens is imprinted upon earthly things—the more carefully the material is prepared, the more powerfully and firmly the impression takes hold. However, one must note that like only acts upon like; natural properties do not affect things that are fundamentally different.

For example, if a husband injures a part of his body, the corresponding part of his wife’s body is also affected—if not physically, then potentially—through a kind of natural sympathy. Because of their divine (rather than merely human) bond, she feels the injury whether she is present or absent, provided the marriage is true and pure. Learned philosophers explain this by pointing to the **triad** <note>original: "triadis"; likely referring to the alchemical Trinity of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>, which forms a dense and unbreakable union with its counterpart. If this is true in specific cases, how much more so must it be in nature as a whole? The universe itself is a divine marriage of the upper and lower worlds, ordained by God so that nothing exists in one that does not have a mirror in the other.

Since the **lesser world** <term>the Microcosm, or Man</term>—consisting of body and vital spirit—was created in the likeness of the **greater world** <term>the Macrocosm, or the Universe</term>, and since the rational soul was made in the **image of God** <note>original: "imago Dei"</note>, whatever exists in the vast universe must also exist within man. To deny this would be to deny that man was made in God's image, which contradicts the Holy Scriptures.

Just as the motions of the heavens never cease, the **vital spirit** <term>the subtle substance that carries life and sensation throughout the body</term> of a human does not stop its work even when the body is resting or asleep. In fact, it often works more precisely while we sleep than while we are awake. This is why, as soon as any part of the body is touched, that sensation reaches the spirit instantly. Who could doubt this? If it were not so, we would feel nothing, for all sensation, life, and action come from the spirit, not the physical body. Conversely, when the spirit is saddened or afflicted, the body inevitably suffers or becomes sluggish. We see the same kind of "marriage" between a person's spirit and body as we do between the heavens and the earth. Furthermore, every movement in the heavens flows into man, or into the things created for his use. Therefore, it is no wonder that stones can be created through art...

...stones not unlike precious gems, which heal men and protect them from diseases when they have been manufactured under (as they say) favorable astrological aspects. How much more powerful as remedies will they be when they are dissolved into their own liquid forms and taken internally into the body! Indeed, every celestial virtue was created by God for this purpose: to imprint a long and healthy life upon man through its influences, whenever an unnatural vice—arising from the **binary serpent** <note>original: "serpente binario." In alchemical philosophy, this refers to the dualistic corruption of nature or the "fallen" state of matter that leads to decay and disease.</note>—has crept into the **monarchy** <term>the "monarchy" refers to the sovereign balance and health of the human body</term> of his being. Take some part of the **minor perfection** <note>A specific stage or substance in the alchemical process mentioned previously.</note> from a small gourd-shaped vessel <term>a "cucurbit," used for distillation</term> and distill it over ashes <term>an "ash bath" used to provide steady, indirect heat</term> with a very gentle fire of the first degree, until it can no longer drip at that heat. After removing and closing the receiving vessel, attach another, seal the joints perfectly with **lute** <term>a clay or paste used to make airtight seals in lab equipment</term>, and distill it with a stronger fire until all the liquid can rise at this heat.

Take this second liquid, place it in a fresh vessel, and distill it in a water bath a third time, pouring the distilled liquid back onto its own dregs <note>original: "faeces"</note> with each distillation. These dregs, having become viscous, are eventually dissolved by such pourings. However, on the third turn, let it be distilled in ashes. Place this final distillate in another fresh vessel and distill it in a water bath four times, removing the dregs each time and setting them aside separately. Continue the final distillation until the liquid becomes perfectly clear and shining with the luster of **pearls** <note>original: "unionum," referring to large, high-quality "union" pearls</note>. Here is its use:

Take oriental pearls or other beautiful ones of any size, place them in a very clean glass vessel, and pour a little of this last distilled water over them so that it floats slightly above them. Close the vessel tightly so it does not "breathe" <note>meaning to prevent any evaporation or air exchange</note>. After three hours, you will see the pearls dissolved into a very white paste. On the surface, a remarkably clear water will remain; pour this off by very gentle tilting into another small vessel without any disturbance. Leave the paste in the same glass where it was, and place it in a water bath in a closed vessel for three days; then, finally, take it out.

Next, order a goldsmith to make a silver mold, gilded with gold inside the cavity—like those used to form spherical pellets—of whatever size you wish the pearl to be. At the opening of each hollow part of the mold, let a very fine gold wire be fitted across the diameter so that it marks the middle of each part, and can be pushed forward or pulled back. Afterward, let each hollow part of the mold be filled with the pearl paste using a gold spatula. Join the parts with the wire extended, and move the wire back and forth so that the pearls are perforated <note>This allows the reconstituted pearls to be strung later</note>. Once the mold is opened, remove them with the greatest care and place them in a wide golden vessel without touching them with your hands, covered...

### THE STRUCTURE OF GEMS.

By the same process, carbuncles <note>original: "carbunculi." In pre-modern mineralogy, this term referred to any red gemstone that appeared to glow like a hot coal, usually garnets or rubies.</note> and many rubies, or even a single one of such a size as the craftsman wishes, can be made, provided the perfect **Red Mercury** <term>Mercurius rubeus; a highly refined alchemical substance used in the "Red Work" to create the Philosopher's Stone or "Great Elixir"</term> has been dissolved only once. Furthermore, celestial waters <note>This likely refers to dew or rainwater collected under specific astrological conditions.</note> impregnated with mineral virtues, when they are exposed to the air through the revolution of a full circle <note>Refers to a full year, or a complete cycle of the zodiacal heavens.</note>, are more broadly and fruitfully impregnated with celestial powers and virtues. Through these, they become fit and suitable for the resolution <term>dissolution or breaking down</term> of all things, even the most solid bodies. Yet the lower celestial [waters], even when exposed to the "womb of the earth," receive the same virtues at the same time, but through another medium—namely the earthly one—by which they acquire the power of coagulating all things, and their own **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum," literally "living silver."</note>. 

Among all sulfurs, this one is the most excellent, just as the quicksilver which we have taught is superior to the rest and more philosophical: although there are many other philosophical sulfurs and likewise quicksilvers, they are not sublimated to such a high degree of subtlety and virtue. Therefore, these waters of the philosophers are the most excellent among all others; one is formal, celestial, and superior, while the other is material and inferior. Yet both are born from one and the same root, and they differ only through industry and application to this **spagyric** <term>the alchemical art of separating, purifying, and recombining natural substances to produce potent medicines</term> craft, so that what was taught above through Hermes might be confirmed: *That which is below is like that which is above, and vice versa.* <note>original: "Quod est inferius, est sicut id quod est superius, & econtra." This is the core axiom of the Emerald Tablet of Hermes Trismegistus, expressing the correspondence between the microcosm (man/alchemy) and the macrocosm (the universe).</note> 

Therefore, let no one in the future (as has been common until now) complain about the obscurity of the Stone and the "Stones of the Philosophers." I have already brought them forth from the darker realms—clear enough, transparent, translucent, and illustrious—and have illustrated and restored them to their own light for you, ingenious readers. In this way, the last might correspond to the first, and vice versa: namely, the artificial and spagyric light to the **Light of Nature**, which gave the name to this little work and to our newly born offspring. 

May Almighty God grant that it may be useful and salutary to all readers whom He knows to be worthy, for His own glory—to whom alone I bring the light I have received, and not to the schools of Athens <note>A reference to classical academic or purely theoretical philosophy, which the author contrasts with practical, divinely-inspired alchemical experience.</note> nor to any others. But may He keep the unworthy from the reading of these things, because they are not of the same kind of ferment; truly, for the worthy the entrance to the inner sanctuary <note>original: "adyta," the innermost, most sacred part of a temple.</note> lies open, but for the unworthy it is hidden.

->THE END.<-

# A COLLECTION
# OF PARACELSIAN CHEMISTRY
## ON THE TRANSMUTATIONS
### OF METALS.
->Preface to the reader.<-

Every operation requires its own proper order, without which nothing beautiful or praiseworthy is accomplished that can bring any utility to mankind. What, I ask, can be more ruinous in this life than confusion? Do we not know that this confusion has destroyed the world from the beginning? Its traces are still placed before our eyes to the great misfortune of many, so that one can see nothing that is not corrupted everywhere among the nations. Therefore, confusion must be utterly rejected and avoided by every good man, and especially by a Christian, mostly because it proceeds from the enemy of God and men. 

Or do we think that God, the Greatest and Best <note>original: "Deum Opt. Max." (Deo Optimo Maximo), a common Renaissance title for God meaning "to God, the Best and Greatest," originally used for Jupiter but adopted by Christian writers.</note>, wished to maintain order in establishing the fabric of this world for no reason? He proposed this order to us, without a doubt, to be meditated upon, not merely observed with the eyes. If it were properly understood how much utility and how much doctrine could be obtained from this, we would wish for no other books, nor any other Doctors prior to Him, who alone bears witness to the truth in our hearts. 

Here you teach us in peace—He who is the author of peace—to seek order above all else; for if order is preserved, all things will be peaceful and tranquil at the same time. On the contrary, when order is violated, discord through confusion is soon at our doors. This is why our Lord **Jesus Christ**, so often impressing peace upon His disciples, also left it as a testament when He departed from them, and for us in union. "My peace," He says, "I give to you; my peace I leave with you." <note>original: "Pacem meam do vobis, pacem meam relinquo vobis." A quotation from the Gospel of John 14:27.</note> What else do these most sacred words mean than if we were to hear: "Be united in me, just as I and my father are one"? Indeed, we could be united in no other way than through peace, which consists in the observation <note>The Latin text ends on "observatione" (observation/keeping).</note>

...observation of the divine. Therefore, in all works, whether spiritual or temporal, order must be maintained as the most powerful root of peace and all concord, so that all human actions and any exercises whatever may look toward this. Accordingly, when Paracelsus was about to treat the highest and chief <term>arcanum</term> <note>original: "arcanum"; a secret or hidden vital power within a substance</note> of medicine—concerning the transmutation of natural things to the ultimate degree of perfection—he wished first of all to indicate what order must be maintained. 

Because this order is indeed not exactly preserved, very many are led astray in the artifice of transmutation; these people afterwards cast the blame for their own error upon the art itself. They falsely accuse the art, along with its authors, of falsehood—as if it could be pleasant for writers to spend so much labor just to mock other men. Whoever either thinks or utters such things, even if they ascribe great wisdom to themselves, speak in the manner of idiots. Nature herself clearly refutes this class of men in all things. 

But who considers her order, or contemplates it in any way? Even among those who profess <term>Physics</term> <note>original: "Physicam"; in this context, it refers to Natural Philosophy or the study of the natural world, not the modern specialized science</note> (to say nothing of others for now), who, I ask, searches her deep mysteries? Although her works are manifest and apparent, who would deny the transmutation of things? For whatever nature works, she effects according to the order prescribed for her by the divine, without variation. If she is sometimes hindered by an external accident, so that she is less able to observe this order, that which is produced departs from nature and becomes a monster. 

This is not nature’s error, but that of the hindrance. Who hindered it, you will ask? The author of confusion <note>a reference to the Devil</note>, through his ministers, has always striven for this from the beginning, and will not cease until the end. Therefore, this art is not to be learned from men or writers so much as from Nature herself, whom we see daily transmuting her composite elements into another decomposed form, yet not into another matter. Furthermore, this is common to all things and elements: they do not differ among themselves except in the species of their form. Let an example of this be the empty, sterile, and void earth, which, placed only under the open sky, by watering through rain and solar rays alone, produces—without any other seed—its own...

# To the Reader.

...mind. <note>original: "mentis"; this completes the final sentence of the previous page regarding the "order prescribed by the divine mind."</note> Nature produces herbs, little animals, and even minerals. Who, I ask, does not see that this is a natural transformation <note>original: "transmutationem"</note> of forms, and not of matter? We are taught by this very example: if forms are separated from the elements of natural things, those elements become fit to receive any form whatsoever. For the matter of the elements is one and the same; it does not merely accept one form or another, but all forms within the three-fold kingdom <note>original: "triplici genere"; referring to the three categories: animal, vegetable, and mineral</note> of products. Nor is it necessary to ask whether the elements of vegetables, once stripped of their forms, are able to receive a mineral form; is the matter not clear in itself? Furthermore, when the elements of corpses return to the earth, they become the elements of vegetables and other things, and so it goes for the rest. Since, therefore, the element of one category can become the element of another, how much more can the element of one species become the element of another species within that same category? For forms do not arise from the elements, but from the firmament. <note>original: "firmamento"; in Paracelsian thought, the 'firmament' refers to the heavens or stars, which were believed to bestow the specific 'form' or 'blueprint' onto material things, while elements provided only the physical 'body.'</note>

Accordingly, no sane person who sees forms being separated from elements will be able to deny the transformation of things. Let the experiment be wood consumed by fire and turned into ashes; its vegetable form departs into the breezes. If this form were captured by a <term>spagyric</term> <note>original: "spagiricum"; the alchemical art of "separating and recombining" substances to reach a higher state of purity</note> vessel so that it does not fly away, and were poured back again into its own ashes, and if they were purified together into a mucilaginous substance and committed again to the earth, they would return to their original form. This is something that the ashes could not have accomplished by themselves, as the author states in his book *On the Resuscitation of Things*. <note>original: "libro de resuscitatione rerum"; a reference to a specific treatise by Paracelsus concerning the chemical "rebirth" of plants from their ashes (palingenesis).</note>

He who is unwilling to believe this should try the experiment himself and keep to the prescribed order; otherwise, it will not succeed because of the confusion, whereas without such confusion it would have succeeded perfectly. Thus, just as a thing's own form can be separated from its elements and return to them again, if these elements were instead imbued with the form of another species (though still within the same category), what would stop them from taking on that new form? For elements produce no form of their own; they only produce that which is in the seed. In the same way, the earth does not produce the form of any specific element, but rather it produces grain from grain, and a tree from a fruit's stone. Therefore, the first and chief business of this work consists in this: that the separation of forms from their elements be performed rightly, according to the <term>spagyric</term> order borrowed from nature.

# PREFACE

...mind. <note>original: "mentis"; this word completes the phrase from the previous page: "the order prescribed by the divine mind."</note> The <term>spagyric: alchemical chemists, specifically those following Paracelsus who used chemical methods to separate and recombine substances</term> philosophers did not dream this up in the manner of the Greeks; instead, taught by nature alone, they use glass vessels as "organs." In these, they cook their material with fire, just as the stomach macerates food into <term>chyle: the milky fluid produced in the stomach during digestion</term> by cooking it with natural heat, refining, dissolving, and putrefying it before separation. 

In the same way, the Art <note>The "Art" refers to the practice of alchemy or chemistry</note> sublimates its material through calcination, dissolves it, and putrefies it before separating it through distillation. Afterward, it segregates the pure from the impure—specifically, the <term>firmamental: relating to the celestial influence, essence, or "form" of a thing as opposed to its raw physical matter</term> parts from the elements—and again separates both of these from their own excessive impurities. 

Nature herself teaches this: she divides her putrefied chyle into two parts, presenting one as the purer part to the liver to be cooked again, while relegating the other as the impurer part to the intestines for ejection. From the liver, another separation occurs: one part serves to nourish the elements of the body, while the other serves to nourish and cherish the vital and firmamental parts, for the sake of retaining the spirit of life in its <term>radical moisture: the fundamental life-sustaining fluid or "oil" believed to exist in all living beings</term>.

In this step, the controversy between the Greeks <note>referring to the classical medical tradition of Galen and Aristotle</note> and the spagyricists is clearly seen. The Greeks insist that the separation in the liver produces only the <term>four humors: the traditional bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which were thought to determine health and temperament</term>, which they attribute to the elements. Thus, they make no mention or distinction of the "firmament" of things, as if life were derived solely from the elements; they pass down a confused doctrine about these things without any distinction. 

On the contrary, the spagyricists teach that elements are nourished only by things similar to them, and life by vital things. Indeed, no physician <note>original: "physicus"</note> can doubt that the natural life of things is owed to the firmament (after God) and not to the elements. Likewise, corporeal things are nourished by bodies, and spiritual bodies by spirits; or to be better understood, material things by material ones, just as formal <note>meaning "of the form" or essence</note> things are nourished by formal bodies. We say this so that we are not accused by the clever of proposing "forms" without "matter," or vice versa. 

For we say that the elements have received their own form and life from the firmament, but that these elements alone can generate nothing without other peculiar firmamental influences <note>original: "influxus"; the "flowing in" of celestial power or astrological energy</note>, no more than a woman can without a man. Furthermore, in the creation, God gave life to all things through light; but for propagation, He gave to each a seed in which the form...

From this, it follows that the compressed force and the confluence of virtues achieve their most intense action and most vehement power in their expansion. Therefore, the further these influences are distant from the center, the more diluted and loose they are found to be, possessing lesser strength and virtue—as can be seen in the case of vegetables.*

*For this reason, experience following meditation has taught that in metals and minerals, which are closer to the center, there exist the most excellent and abundant virtues of all. Therefore, the philosophers preferred these above all other things, seeking to extract from them a certain <term>universal medicine: a "panacea" or "elixir" capable of curing all diseases by restoring perfect balance</term> in its most unified and tempered form, by which individual things might finally be brought to union and a true <term>temperament: the balanced state of the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry)</term>. Indeed, nothing is ever more balanced, more general, or more widely applicable than union; nothing is more abundantly extended than the central physical essence.
