...though he may perform demonstrations involving many preparations, the philosophers do not intend for the matter of their Stone to proceed primarily from any mineral intermediaries, even if they do call their stone "mineral." Taking the opportunity from this name, the <term>Sophists</term> <note>In alchemical texts, "Sophists" refers to false alchemists or "puffers" who followed the letter of the texts without understanding the true spiritual or natural philosophy.</note> have persecuted **Mercury** <note>The element quicksilver.</note> itself with various tortures—some with sublimations, others with coagulations, precipitations, or mercurial <term>aqua fortes</term> <note>Nitric acid or other "strong waters" used to dissolve metals.</note>, and so on. All these are erroneous paths to be avoided, along with the other preparations of minerals used by the Sophists, such as the purifications and "fixations" of spirits and metals. 

Furthermore, the numerous preparations of the Stone—indeed, almost all those described concerning minerals in this manner, such as those by <term>Geber</term> <note>A legendary figure, likely based on the 8th-century Persian polymath Jabir ibn Hayyan, though many works attributed to him were written by a 13th-century European "Pseudo-Geber."</note>, **Albert** surnamed **the Great**, and their like—are merely <note>original: "sophistricæ purgationes"</note> sophistical purifications. Their cementations, sublimations, distillations, rectifications, circulations, putrefactions, conjunctions, solutions, ascensions, coagulations, calcinations, and waxings are utterly useless—whether they are performed in a tripod, a reverberatory furnace, an <term>athanor</term> <note>A self-feeding furnace designed to maintain a constant heat over long periods.</note>, a melting pot, an acid-bath, or using dung, ash, or sand, or within a <term>cucurbit</term> <note>A gourd-shaped chemical vessel.</note>, a <term>pelican</term> <note>A circulatory vessel with two "arms" that feed condensed vapors back into the body.</note>, a retort, a vial, a fixing-vessel, and other things of that kind.

The same judgment must be made regarding the sublimations of **Mercury** through mineral spirits to produce the "white" or the "red," using vitriol, <term>saltpeter</term> <note>Potassium nitrate.</note> or some other salt, alum, <term>crocus of Mars</term> <note>Iron oxide, used as a pigment or polishing agent.</note>, etc. **John of Rupescissa** <note>A 14th-century Franciscan chemist and prophet who wrote extensively on the "quintessence."</note> tells false tales about all of these in his treatise on the white and red <term>Philosopher's Stone</term>; these are all dreams made up alongside others, miserably leading astray good and simple men. One must also flee those specific sophistical works of Geber, such as the sevenfold sublimations or "mortifications," as well as the "revivifications" of Mercury with preparations made through "salt of urine" or the "sepulcher"—each of these is entirely false regarding the Stone. 

Certain others have attempted to "fix" Mercury with the sulfurs of minerals and metals, but they were greatly deceived. Nevertheless, I have seen Mercury brought into a metallic body through fixations of this sort by this art; it feigned and represented good **silver** in all respects and through all tests, yet when put to the test of the <term>cupel</term> <note>A shallow, porous dish used in assaying to separate precious metals from base metals like lead.</note>, its falsity was exposed for what it was. 

Some of the Sophists have tried to squeeze out a "fixed oil" from this Mercury (sublimated seven times and dissolved as many times) by means of *aqua fortes*, by which they might bring any imperfect metals to perfection; but they were forced to abandon this work as fruitless. Others have purified **vitriol** seven times through calcination, solution, and coagulation, adding two parts of **sal ammoniac** and sublimating it so it would dissolve into a "white water." To this, they added a third part of "living" Mercury, so that the water would coagulate. They then sublimated the Mercury away from the said vitriol and sal ammoniac so many times that it turned into a hard stone. They claimed that this, conceived from vitriol, was the **Red Sulfur of the Philosophers**, the solution of which...

->### OF METALS ###<-

...they proceeded with [distillations] and coagulations, but in the final act of **projection** <note>The final stage of the alchemical process where the Stone is cast upon a base metal to transform it.</note>, nothing was achieved. Others coagulated **Mercury** <note>quicksilver</note> using alum water, turning it into a hard mass resembling alum, which they then fruitlessly attempted to "fix" <note>term: fixation; to make a volatile substance stable when exposed to fire</note> using sharp waters <note>strong acids</note>. The Sophists <note>false alchemists or "puffers"</note> claim many methods for fixing Mercury, yet they labor in vain because nothing permanent or perfect is found within it. Therefore, they pointlessly add minerals to it through their deceptive processes; by all these means, the Mercury is only roused to greater "malice" <note>instability or reactivity</note>, becoming more and more "alive" [volatile] and impure rather than perfect. Therefore, the matter of the philosophers is not to be sought from this, as it is something imperfect. Even if it could be brought to perfection, it would be extremely difficult—even impossible—through the methods of the Sophists, since there is nothing within it that can be forced or awakened into perfection.

Some took **arsenic** that had been sublimated several times and dissolved and coagulated many times in oil of tartar; they pretended to fix it so that they might turn copper into silver. This effort produced nothing but a certain "sophistical whitening" <note>original: "sophisticam dealbationem"; a surface treatment that makes a metal look like silver without changing its internal nature</note>. Indeed, this substance can by no means be fixed unless the "coloring spirit" within it is properly understood—a point on which nearly all philosophers have "slept," <note>failed to notice</note> trying in vain to produce something good from arsenic. Therefore, let those who are ignorant of this spirit have no hope of fixing it or of attributing any power to it by which the perfection of transmutation might be acquired.

For this reason, I make it known to all who spend their labor on this: the "whitening" mentioned above is drawn from a false foundation. By this deception, copper is only whitened on the surface and not otherwise changed. The Sophists even took **Venus** <note>the metal copper</note> disguised and painted in this way and mixed it with twice its weight of **Luna** <note>the metal silver</note>; they then sold this mixture to goldsmiths and mint-masters. Ultimately, they transformed themselves into counterfeiters—not only those who sold it, but even those who bought it.

Some of the Sophists took red arsenic instead of white, and this likewise vanished into a false art. For in whatever way it is prepared, it exhibits nothing but a superficial whiteness. Others went further to common **sulfur**; while it was still yellow, they boiled it in vinegar, lye, or very sharp urine for a day and night until it emerged white. Afterward, they "raised" <note>sublimated</note> it from common lime and lime made from eggshells; they boiled and sublimated it many times. Nonetheless, it remained combustible, even though it was white. With this, they tried in vain to fix raw Mercury into gold. However, a most beautiful **cinnabar** <note>mercury sulfide, used as a red pigment</note> resulted from this, the best I have ever seen. Thinking they could fix this through "cementing" and "fixation" with oil of sulfur, it held some outward appearance of success, but the outcome was far from what was actually desired.

Others reduced common sulfur into the form of a "liver" <note>original: "hepatis"; likely referring to "liver of sulfur," a potassium sulfide mixture</note> by adding linseed oil, oil of bricks, or olive oil, boiling it in vinegar, and afterwards [spreading it] upon a marble st- <insert>one</insert> <note>The Latin catchword "pidem" completes "lapidem," meaning stone.</note>

...pouring out the stone. They distilled this same substance into a lemon-colored oil <note>original: "oleum citrinum"</note> at first with a slow fire, but they learned to their own cost that they achieved none of what they hoped for—namely, that they had by no means turned **silver** <note>original: "lunam"</note> into gold. One must also beware of "sophistic" <note>deceptive or fraudulent</note> oils of vitriol and antimony, as well as the oils of perfect and imperfect metals, even those of gold and silver. For although the operation of these substances is most powerful in the nature of things, nevertheless their true process is known to very few even to this day. Likewise, flee the sophistic tinctures derived from marcasites and **crocus of Mars** <note>term: crocus Martis; a red oxide of iron used as a pigment or alchemical reagent</note>, and from that deception called "part with part," the fixing of silver, and similar trifles. For even if they show some superficial appearance of truth (indeed, this fixing of silver requires little labor or industry), nevertheless such a progression of preparation is void and invalid.

Let us now hear what the true matter of the **philosopher’s stone** is. Paracelsus says that philosophers have labored greatly in the art of ferments and fermentations, which seems the most important among others. Concerning this, some have even made a vow to God and the philosophers that they would never reveal the secret of this matter except through similarities and parables. However, Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary figure credited with founding the alchemical tradition</note>, in the seventh book of his treatises, reveals the ferments most clearly, saying that they consist of nothing but their own "paste." He explains further that the ferment whitens the composition, prevents burning <note>original: "adustionem"</note>, and completely delays the flow of the **tincture** <note>the "soul" or coloring power of the Stone</note>, strengthens bodies, and increases their union. He also says it is the key and the end of the work, concluding that the ferment is nothing other than "paste"—just as the Sun <note>gold</note> is nothing but Sun, and the Moon <note>silver</note> is nothing but Moon. Others claim the ferment is the **soul**, which cannot affect anything unless it is properly and thoroughly prepared by the **magistery** <note>term: magisterium; the master-work or the completed process of creating the Stone</note>. Some zealots of this art have sought their ferments in various primary and intermediate minerals, but they found they had run in vain. For the substance which is sought is the same as that from which it must be drawn. Therefore, it must be noted that such fermentations succeed

### On the preparation of spagyric matter in general.
#### CHAPTER VIII.

Nature first requires of the craftsman that the **philosophical Adam** <note>original: "philosophicus Adam"; a symbolic term for the "Prime Matter" or the first state of the material before transformation</note> be brought into a **Mercurial substance**, and finally be born as the eastern solar and lunar stone. Furthermore, it must be noted that those common preparations of **Geber**, **Albertus Magnus**, **Thomas Aquinas**, **Rupescissa**, **Polydorus**, and their like, are nothing other than certain "particular" solutions and calcinations <note>term: calcination; the process of heating a substance to high temperatures to achieve decomposition or oxidation</note> that pertain not at all to our **Universal**, which indeed requires only the most secret fire of the philosophers. Therefore, let fire and **azoth** <note>term: azoth; the universal solvent or essential agent of transformation in alchemy</note> be sufficient for you. 

You must understand that when the philosophers mention certain preparations, such as **putrefaction**, **distillation**, **sublimation**, **ceration** <note>term: ceration; the process of softening a hard substance to a wax-like state</note>, **fixation**, and so on, nature herself performs all these operations within the aforementioned matter in their "Universal" work—not the laborer—within the philosophical vessel alone, using a "similar" fire and not a common one. For the **White** and the **Red** <note>referring to the White Tincture (for silver) and Red Tincture (for gold)</note> spring from a single root without any intermediary. It is dissolved by itself and coupled by itself; it turns white and red, and becomes saffron-yellow and black by its own power; it marries itself and conceives within itself. It must therefore be boiled, roasted, and melted: it ascends and descends, and indeed all these operations are one, performed by fire alone. 

Nevertheless, some philosophers have dissolved the **body of the sun** <note>gold; original: "corpus solis"</note> through a highly graded **essence of wine** <note>distilled alcohol; original: "essentiam vini"</note> and made it volatile so that it might ascend through the **alembic** <note>term: alembic; a type of distilling apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube</note>, thinking this to be the true "volatile matter" of the philosophers, though it is not. Although it is a secret not to be despised—to bring a perfect metallic body into a volatile and spiritual substance—nonetheless they err in the "separation of the elements." 

The process of the monks—namely **Lully**, **Richard the Englishman**, **Rupescissa**, and others—is erroneous. For they believed they could separate gold by this path into a subtle spiritual and elemental power, and afterwards couple both back into one through circulation and **rectification** <note>the process of purifying a liquid by repeated distillation</note>, but in vain. For even if one element were separated from another in some way, nevertheless anything separated in this manner can be separated into something else again; these parts afterwards can by no means come together into one by **pelican** <note>term: pelican; a specialized circulatory distillation vessel with two side-arms feeding back into the body</note> circulation or distillation, but they always remain a certain volatile matter and **potable gold** <note>original: "aurum potabile"; gold in a liquid, drinkable form, often sought as a universal medicine</note>, as they call it. The reason why they could not reach their goal is this: because nature by no means wishes to be pulled apart in this way, nor separated by human disjunctions, such as through earthly glass and instruments. She alone knows her own operations and the weights of the elements, whose separations, rectifications, and couplings she executes without the aid of any worker.

is a matter of manual craft, provided that the material is contained in a secret fire and a hidden vessel. Therefore, the separation of the elements is impossible for a human; even if it seems to occur, it is not truly so. This is true regardless of what is said of **Raymond Lull** <note>original: "Raymundo Lullio"; a famous 13th-century polymath and alchemist</note> and his noble golden **Angelic** <note>original: "Angelico suo nobili aureo"; refers to the "Rose Noble" or "Angel" gold coins Lull was legendary for supposedly creating through alchemy for the King of England</note>, which he is falsely thought to have manufactured. For nature itself possesses its own internal separator, which again joins together what it separates without human help. Nature knows best of all the proportion of each element, whereas man does not—no matter what erroneous writers might fable in their frivolous and false recipes regarding this "volatile gold" of theirs. 

This is the opinion of the philosophers: that when they have placed their material in the most secret fire, it is cherished on all sides by this **philosophical heat** <note>a steady, gentle heat compared to the warmth of a brooding hen</note> so that, beginning to pass through corruption, it turns black. They say this operation is **putrefaction** <term>putrefaction; the stage where the matter decomposes and "dies" to be reborn</term>, and they call this blackness the **raven’s head** <note>original: "caput corvi"; a traditional alchemical term for the black stage, or *nigredo*</note>. They call the rising and falling of this matter their **distillation**, **ascent**, and **descent**. They say that its drying out is **coagulation**, while its whitening is **calcination**. And because the material becomes fluid and soft through continued heat, they make mention of **ceration** <term>ceration; from "cera" (wax), the process of softening a substance until it has a waxy consistency</term>. Furthermore, when it ceases to rise and remains liquid at the bottom, they call this **fixation**. In this manner, therefore, the names of the philosophical operations are to be understood, and not otherwise. Having thus explained the instruments and the material with its **ferments** <note>the "yeast" or catalysts that trigger the transformation</note>, we must now come in order to the weights, without which our work is in vain.

### *On the proportion of the matter and form of the spagyric stone.*

## CHAPTER IX.

The formal part of our "offspring" is the **Mercury of the philosophers** and the spirit or tincture of the sun; the other part, the "living" part, is the material. Accordingly, the composition of this most sacred **Adamic stone** <note>original: "lapidis Adamici"; referring to the "Red Earth" or the primordial matter of man</note> is made from the **Adamic Mercury** of the wise, joined with their woman, **Eve**, through marriage and the union of one Mercury with the other into a third. Thus, there is a single matter of the philosophers consisting of a spiritual, a corporal, and an animal Mercury. The **corporal Mercury** is the subject of the tinctures, while the spiritual and animal provide the means of joining them. 

However, in the joining of these, a due proportion must be observed; for if more of one is taken than the other, either the seed cast into the field will be suffocated—so that it cannot live long enough to be perfected by the fire united with the Mercury of the philosophers—or, on the contrary, if there is too little, it cannot be dissolved at all, which will result in it being dried up and yielding no fruit. Therefore, listen to how much of each should be taken, lest the entire work be destroyed through ignorance of its proportion. Let one part of the seed be taken to two parts of the earth, or three to four, and you will not err; rather, the work will be led to its desired end by this portion, provided that

In these things, the elemental weight consists. But the artificial weight is most hidden, since it is contained within the **magical art of weightings**. Between the spirit, the soul, and the body (say the philosophers), weight stands as the ruler of the work: for the soul especially desires **sulfur** <note>in alchemy, sulfur represents the active, combustible, and masculine principle of matter</note>, and necessarily observes it by reason of weight. Understand it in this manner: Our matter is united with a fixed red sulfur, to which a third part of the governance is committed, until the final degree, so that it may perfect the operation of the **stone** <note>the Philosopher's Stone</note> infinitely, and persist with it along with its fire, and a weight equal to the matter itself, in all things and through all things, without any variation of any degree of transmutation. Therefore, after the matter has been prepared and mixed in its proportional weight, it must be sealed perfectly in the **vessel of the philosophers** <note>the hermetically sealed glass flask or "philosopher's egg"</note> with its own seal, and committed to the secret fire, in which the **philosophical Sun** <note>original: "Sol philosophicus"; a metaphor for the perfection of the work or the gold-producing principle</note> will rise and ascend, and will illuminate all things that await its light and have desired it with great hope. But because these things cannot be rightly understood unless one has a perfect knowledge of the spiritual **tinctures** <term>tincture; a potent substance or "spirit" capable of transforming and coloring base metals into gold or silver</term> in metals, we must also discuss these.

Copper <note>original: "cuprum"; often associated with the planet Venus in alchemy</note>, when melted in fire or glowing white-hot, is not as easily consumed by fire or evaporated as the metals that follow it, nor is it as quickly corrupted by air or moisture as Iron <note>original: "Mars"</note>; for Copper persists more "fixedly" <term>fixed; resistant to the transformative power of fire</term> in the flame. Conversely, it shatters any other metals with which it is mixed—even the bodies of the "perfect" metals <note>Gold and Silver</note>—so that they will no longer endure the hammer and cease to be workable until they are freed from it. It acts no differently in the human body: if it is taken for some disease for which it was not naturally destined by its degree, it brings about contractions of the limbs. For this reason, a physician should first learn well which diseases the spirits and **tinctures** <term>tincture; a potent medicinal extract or the spiritual essence of a substance</term> of the "imperfect" metals <note>metals other than Gold or Silver</note> are suited for, before he experiments at the risk of his patients. Thus it happens that the physician is forced to do what he can and what he has learned—namely, to work with plants and animals. Yet these are surpassed and left far behind by minerals, even when the minerals are prepared with a "clumsy Minerva" <note>original: "rudi Minerva"; a Latin idiom meaning a lack of skill or sophistication</note>.

The **Martial Tincture** <note>the medicinal essence of Iron</note> consists of a thick and combustible mixture of elements, but compared to the other imperfect metals, it has a harder and less workable substance; it is barely even meltable, and is easily corrupted by air and water, by which it is consumed through rust or corrosion, and most easily by fire. Nevertheless, it surpasses all other metals in hardness and dryness, and it destroys or breaks the continuity of other metals in a mixture, the perfect no less than the imperfect. In the same way, it twists the limbs of the human body when it is applied to a disease other than what is appropriate. But when this spirit is taken for external ulcers, for which it is indeed suited, it heals them from the root, removing every cause of contagion equal to its own degree, though not those superior to it. It does not lack, therefore, powers and virtues granted to it by God and nature in its own special property.

### *On the specific preparations of the matter of the stone, and*
### *first through Electrum.*
## CHAPTER XI.

Nothing in the nature of things lacks its own form; for indeed, everything that exists is generated, multiplied, and destroyed within its own concordance <note>original: "concordantia"; referring to the internal harmony or specific proportion of qualities that allow a substance to exist</note>. It reveals its own beginning, from which it is perceived by the senses that the very thing which must be done at the start is also what will exist in the end. Whatever is interrupted seems to be something like an imperfection which nature, by accident, urges toward generation.

Since, however, these accidents <note>in philosophy, "accidents" are non-essential properties—like color or shape—that can change without altering the core essence of a thing</note> can be removed through Vulcan <note>the Roman god of fire, used here to represent the alchemical furnace or the art of transformative heat</note> so that they have no effect, nature can be corrected to that extent, as happens in the case of this Stone. For if you wish to manufacture this Stone from the true matter (which you have easily learned from the preceding instructions), it will be necessary above all to remove the superfluities <note>excess or waste material</note>, so that it may be formed, multiplied, and increased in its own concordance. Nature has indeed left the Stone imperfect, since she herself forms only its matter, and not the Stone itself; from this matter, that which is later achieved through the Stone after its preparation can by no means occur, because accidents hinder the matter. Therefore, without preparation, the matter is—in respect to the Stone—nothing but a semi-perfect thing, not consisting in any concordance that could be called perfect, or suitable for the health of the human body.

For example, take the Microcosm <note>the "Little World," a term for a human being seen as a reflection of the entire universe</note>: here, through its creator, only the man was fashioned, not a complete work, since he does not endure in his concordance, but is only a medium until the womanly mate <note>original: "virago femina"; referring to the biblical creation of Eve from Adam</note>, similar to himself and fashioned from him, arrives; then finally they achieve a whole and complete work. Both are earth, and two earths constitute one whole man who can be increased and grown, this being achieved by the formed concordance.

In the same way, the Philosophers' Stone (which must restore man no less than the metals themselves), when purged of superfluous accidents and liberated, and placed in its own concordance, performs certain miracles in all infirmities. Otherwise, any labor undertaken in the philosophical work of the balsam and the perpetual stone outside of this concordance is in vain. Therefore, so that it may come to its concordance, it must be reduced to the First Matter <note>original: "primam materiam"; the primordial, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made</note>, so that the male may be able to act upon the female, and its manifest part be hidden, and its hidden part become manifest <note>making the "hidden visible" is a core alchemical goal, where the inner spirit is brought to the surface</note>, so that the seed of both—namely, of the male and the female—enclosed in its concordance, and made more than perfect by means of Vulcan, and exalted to its highest degree, [possesses] qualified virtues...

<page-num>526</page-num>
<header>## ON TRANSMUTATION</header>

...all these things together, with a tempered and clarified essence, might be able to exert themselves upon the human body, as well as upon metals, by expelling impurities through the pulse, and by arranging what is good in the human blood in its proper place through touch, and by preserving it. In this way, the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: "The Little World," a term for the human being who reflects the entire structure and forces of the greater universe (the Macrocosm)</term> existing in the limbo of the earth and formed from it, may be radically and truly brought to health and preserved therein by this medicine, as if by its own likeness. So great a mystery of nature and greatest secret ought not to be hidden from any physician, at least one born from **astral medicine** <note>Medicine that considers the influence of the heavens and the "internal stars" of the human body</note>.

So that we may more clearly reveal the matter and preparation of such an admirable medicine to the "sons of doctrine": let it be known that one thing was given and produced by nature, in which—as if in an ark—the numbers 2, 3, and 4 are mystically enclosed and lie hidden. The powers and virtues of this thing, after preparation, have the most abundant power to drive all diseases and infections from the Microcosm. It is truly a defense for youth against old age, and for old age against untimely death, which we also call a **balsam** <note>In Paracelsian terms, a "balsam" is an internal preservative fluid that prevents decay in the body</note>. Therefore, it is first necessary to know in which subject nature has placed these numbers. You will find its virtues most extensively described in my *Archidoxis* (he says), in the book on renovation and restoration. Furthermore, I will now clearly demonstrate the matter to my astral disciples, along with the preparation of the entire work. He who has ears to hear and mental eyes to see, let him hear and see what Paracelsus teaches, before he judges unfairly with the rest.

Let the immature mineral **Electrum** <note>original: "Electrum minerale immaturum"; likely a complex ore or a combination of the seven planetary metals in their "raw" state</note> be placed in its sphere <note>the glass vessel</note>, so that dross and superfluities may be washed away, and let it be highly purified by means of **antimony** <note>original: "stibium"; frequently used as a purifying agent to "eat" the impurities of other metals</note> according to chemical use and custom, lest you suffer loss due to its impurity. Afterward, let it be dissolved in the **stomach of the ostrich** <note>original: "stomachus struthionis"; a colorful alchemical metaphor for a powerful corrosive acid or solvent, named because the ostrich was famously believed to be able to digest iron</note> born in the earth, strengthened by the sharpness of the **eagle** <note>original: "aquila"; a standard alchemical term for Sal Ammoniac (ammonium chloride), used to make acids more volatile</note>.

Once the Electrum has been absorbed and has acquired yellow flowers, or takes the form of sunflower flowers from the solution, do not forget to bring this very thing to a certain spiritual and transparent essence, which has the appearance of **white vitriol**. Then, finally, add half the weight that the bodily Electrum had before preparation, from the **extended eagle** <note>likely a reference to a sublimated form of the salt</note>, and from there, let it be drawn off frequently by the "stomach of the ostrich"; this is done so that the spiritual Electrum may emerge more and more. But when the "stomach of the ostrich" becomes weaker in its operation, it must be renewed and strengthened again by drawing it off at each turn. Finally, when it has again lost its sharpness, let a **tartarized quintessence** <note>A highly refined spirit derived from wine or vinegar salts</note> be added, so that it stands four fingers above the matter, and let it be deprived of its redness, which should rise up at the same time. This must be repeated until it becomes sufficiently white of itself (which indeed appears more and more to the eyes as it submits to sublimation). When this sign is perceived, let it be sublimated, and the Electrum [is turned] into the whiteness of the **sublimated eagle**...

He emphasizes its power to purify the human body (the Microcosm) and its role as a "balsam" against aging and disease.</summary>

<page-num>527</page-num>
<header>OF METALS.</header>

...it will be turned into filings, and with little and light labor brought to that point and transmuted: which indeed we seek for the use of our medicine. By this very means you will be able to proceed against many ailments which do not yield to common medicines at all. You will also be able to turn it into water, or into oil, or into a red powder, for all diseases for which you wish or need to apply it. In medicine, no greater foundation can be found than that which lies hidden in **electrum** <term>Electrum: In Paracelsian alchemy, this is not just the ancient gold-silver alloy, but a "magical" alloy of all seven planetary metals (Gold, Silver, Iron, Copper, Mercury, Tin, and Lead)</term>. I confess, however, and he says <note>original: "inquit" — Paracelsus often refers to himself in the third person or cites his own authority</note> that in other minerals the greatest secrets are similarly hidden, but they are subject to greater and more extensive labor, the use of which is turned into abuse by unskilled artists, whose hands destroy more in this medicine than they build.

Wherefore it is not to be praised that every chemist takes up the office and duty of a physician, of which he is ignorant and for which he is unfit. Rightly should those rash, imaginary, and presumptuous doctors of that sort be punished, who think themselves chemists and physicians after only a single reading, and rush into these arts through the window and not through the door. I do not want the blame to be cast on me because of my writing, nor do I recognize all those as disciples who proclaim themselves to be mine, or read my writings, but only those who both understand me and follow the truth; others I pronounce to be willful deceivers and vagabond men, who snatch the bread from the mouths of true disciples, harming everyone under my name, because they care for no art that is certain and true.

But let us return to the task. To finally bring the broken electrum to the desired end, take as much of its volatile part as previously rendered as the artist wishes to complete, and shut it in a **philosophical egg** <term>Philosophical Egg: A round, long-necked glass vessel used in alchemy, hermetically sealed to represent a closed system or "womb" for transformation</term> hermetically sealed, so that it cannot breathe out in any way. Let this be placed in an **athanor** <term>Athanor: A specialized alchemical furnace designed to provide steady, even heat over many weeks or months</term>, until it dissolves by itself gradually on the surface, and then finally an island is seen in the middle of this sea, which gradually decreasing turns into **blackness** <term>Nigredo: The first major stage of the alchemical process, representing the "death" or "putrefaction" of the matter</term> like shoemaker’s ink <note>original: "atramenti sutorij" — a common term for vitriol or copperas used in black dyes</note>. 

This is the bird flying at night without wings, which the first dew of heaven, by continued decoction, converts through upward ascent and downward descent into the **head of the crow** <term>Caput Corvi: A symbol of the final, deepest stage of the blackening process</term>, and finally into the **peacock's tail** <term>Cauda Pavonis: A stage where the matter in the flask begins to shimmer with many iridescent colors</term>, and afterwards it acquires the whitest swan-like feathers, and at last the highest redness, a sign of its fiery nature. Through this "fire" it drives the accidents of all diseases out of the human body, and restores limbs deadened by cold or paralyzed. This kind of preparation is made (according to the opinion of all philosophers) in only a single vessel, a single furnace, and a single continuous vaporous fire. When all these things are finished, the medicine is made and perfected as if celestial; it can be made "more than perfect" through its own flesh and its own blood, and through its own internal and hidden fire brought into the manifest, by which likewise metal...

<header>ON TRANSMUTATION</header>
<meta>catchword: to be covered for the pious</meta>

...the filth [of bodies] is washed away, and their hidden things are made manifest. This perfect medicine can do all these things: it penetrates all bodies, draws out their corruptions, and at the same time introduces health as if in a moment, such that it finds no equal in this world. Therefore, O Physician, practice yourself in this; through it you will acquire for yourself the highest praise and honor. Through this, you will emerge as a true physician, indeed compelled by it toward brotherly charity, because no mortal can understand or attain this divine secret without the will of God. Likewise, its infinite power works a knowledge of the ineffable God in those who cultivate it, especially in those who use it frequently, taken every month or at the new moons; for it removes the obstacles to the light of the intellect, so that all things hidden in the deepest recesses become clear to the purified mind.

Furthermore, it is necessary to know that no solution of **electrum** <note>original: "electri"</note> is made unless it first traverses the circle of the seven spheres three times most perfectly <note>The "seven spheres" refer to the seven planetary metals: Gold, Silver, Mercury, Copper, Iron, Tin, and Lead. Traversing them "three times" suggests a repetitive distillation or purification cycle</note>; for that number is appropriate to it. Therefore, observe your preparation diligently, which is the principal cause of the solution; once it is glorified and made spiritual (as you have heard), by applying the <term>tartarized secret of electrum</term> <note>original: "electro tartarisatum arcanum" — a preparation involving tartar, or potassium bitartrate, used as a powerful solvent</note>, the superfluities introduced through the preparation may be thoroughly washed away. This is done so that you do not work in vain. The <term>secret of tartar</term> <note>original: "arcanum tartari"</note> is similarly to be removed, so that your matter alone, pure and moved in a circle according to the prescribed order of the art, may be easily turned by itself into <term>philosophical water</term> (which they call **viscous**) by the vapor of the fire within the <term>philosophical egg</term> <note>A round, long-necked glass flask used for "digesting" alchemical substances over steady heat</note>. Likewise, it should coagulate by itself with the manifestation of all colors, and finally be adorned with the highest redness <note>The "rubedo" or reddening was the final stage of the Great Work, signifying perfection</note>. It is forbidden to write more about this most hidden secret of the philosophers; wherefore, what is appropriate must deservedly be left to the power of God, whose peculiar gift it is—not granted to everyone, nor entering the understanding of any person, however sharp.

It is also right that we add its use. The dose or weight of administration of this medicine ought to be so small that it scarcely represents an atom, in wine or another cordial broth; for if even a slightly larger quantity than is proper is applied, the celestial power lying hidden within it (and as if compressed into a center) works too strongly. God, the Best and Greatest <note>original: "D. O. M." — Deo Optimo Maximo</note>, wished this mystery of nature, which is above nature, to be known to some men for His own glory. To Him alone be praise, honor, and perennial glory forever. In conclusion, **Paracelsus** says:

> Behold, friend reader, you have in brief the whole foundation and origin of the secret and divine medicine, which can only happen to those preordained by God. It will be your task to imitate with understanding what I have prescribed to you at the beginning. Do not shirk the labors; let not the black coals terrify you, nor the laborious diligence with industry necessary in this place; but you must set it before your mind, with constant speculations and meditative prayers intervening, that even the most hidden things...

This marriage represents the union of opposites—the fixed and the volatile—necessary to create the Philosopher's Stone.</meta>

<header>OF METALS.</header>

...to be covered for pious minds, nor will this labor return to you without most abundant fruit.

So that I may bring some light to those reading these writings of **Paracelsus** <note>The famous Swiss physician and alchemist (1493–1541) who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine</note>, it seemed fit to add something that might open the **electrum** <note>original: "electrum"; here referring to a specific alchemical alloy or "super-metal," not just amber or a gold-silver mix</note> lying hidden in its hard bark. Everyone knows that metallic or mineral electrum is a mixture of two or more such bodies. Therefore, we must first seek out an immature mineral of this kind—that is, one compacted by nature—which contains several things, as if it were composed by art from various elements, such as **brass** <note>original: "lato"; likely latten or brass, common copper alloys</note> or bell-metal, and the like. But see what will be said below regarding **cinnabar** <note>original: "cinabari"; mercury sulfide, the common ore of mercury</note>. Truly, so that these things may become clearer, I wished to collect for you in order those things which are related rather than distant; hence, let us now subjoin that **spagyric marriage** <note>original: "spagiricum matrimonium"; the chemical union of opposing substances, symbolically described as a wedding</note> which we touched upon briefly above when discussing the spirits and tinctures of metals.

### *On the marriage of the spagyric or philosophical stone.*
### CHAPTER XII.

Let the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <note>A symbolic, purified form of mercury, representing the "soul" or "spirit" of the matter, not the common liquid metal</note> be brought into corporeal Mercury, just as seed is brought into its living field; that is, let the **Mercury of the Sun** <note>Often referring to the essence or "soul" of gold</note> be cast into the philosophical earth for the generation of **tinctures** <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" is a potent substance capable of transmuting metals or healing the body</note>. The living field will dissolve the **Mercury of the Wise** <note>original: "Mercurium sapientum"</note>, conceiving its powers within itself, and that [Mercury] will kill that living thing—namely, the living corporeal spirit—and from this a constant and inviolable marriage will be made through and in the fire itself. For philosophical Mercury (that is, of the Sun) is compared to the corporeal spirit of Mercury in their conjunction, just as a husband is to his wife, since both are from one and the same root or origin. Although the "body of the sun" remains fixed in the fire, and the "metallic woman" is not fixed, nonetheless the former is compared to the latter just as seed is to a field or the earth.

Whatever is sown must be harvested—as barley from barley, wheat from wheat, and so on with the rest. Likewise in the art, if gold is sown, this too shall be harvested; if silver, the same; if copper, the same, and so forth. Therefore, tinctures arise from the metals, each in its own degree, through the action of the Mercury of the Wise and not by **quicksilver** <note>original: "Mercurio vivo"; common liquid mercury</note>; yet common mercury serves as the augmentation, producing fruit as the earth does from seed. After you have enclosed the matter in its vessel, let it be placed in a **natural heat** <note>original: "calorem naturalem"; a gentle, steady heat, often compared to the warmth of a brooding hen or the sun</note>, so that the external heat does not overcome the internal; otherwise, no union will follow. For excessive heat scatters and burns the matter, so that nothing is generated from it. Consider the airy part of the world, midway between heaven and earth; without it, all creatures would be burned by the heat of the Sun and the other stars and would produce nothing. Therefore, let there be an **ethereal medium** <note>A buffer or temperate environment</note> between the fire and the matter, lest the work be destroyed. Conversely, if the living fire is more sluggish than is proper, the spirit of the matter will rest, doing nothing to its moisture other than causing its sudden drying and fixation.

<meta>catchword: coagulatio (thickening/congealing)</meta>

For indeed, the metallic spirits are dead and at rest, so that they can do or perform nothing unless they are roused to life by **living fire** <note>original: "vivum ignem"; the constant, carefully regulated heat of the alchemical furnace</note>. In the "great world" <note>the macrocosm or outer nature</note>, it appears not dissimilar: seeds cast into the earth lie there as if dead, so that they are by no means able to grow by themselves unless they receive life and motion from the Sun. Therefore, let the craftsman see to it in this place that he maintains a middle path in the government of his fire; otherwise, he will never be able to become a master of his wish. Once the matter is moved by the proper heat, it soon begins to turn black; and as the dryness subsequently works upon the moisture, the **philosophical garden** <note>original: "hortus philosophicus"; a metaphorical term for the chemical reactions occurring within the sealed vessel</note> begins to bloom in the **egg** <note>the "philosopher's egg," a round, long-necked glass flask</note> with diverse and various colors in the manner of a **peacock's tail** <note>original: "caudæ pavonis"; a famous stage in alchemy where a rainbow of colors appears on the surface of the matter, signaling the transition to the next phase</note>, such as the worker may never have happened to see in his life. 

Sometimes there will appear inside the glass a coating of gold, which is indeed a sign of the action of the husband’s seed upon the seed of the wife—that is, of the **sulfur** sperm in the **Mercury’s** menstruum <term>menstruum</term> <note>derived from the word for "monthly," this refers to a solvent or base liquid that dissolves and nourishes the "seed" of the metal</note>—and of the mutual alteration and mixing of one into the other. Afterwards, as the moisture gradually fails through successive drying, these kinds of flowers and colors pass into a sprouting whiteness, until it reaches the degree ordained for it by nature. 

Meanwhile, it must be noted that the work should not be rushed, as many do, desiring this "offspring" to be born in the space of one year or nine months, like a grain of corn or a human in a mother’s womb. Gold and silver are not born as quickly as those. Indeed, the more excellent and perfect a thing of nature is, the more time is needed for it to be born; for that which is made quickly seems to perish quickly, such as grass, man, and similar things, for which reason their life is short. It is not so with gold and silver, which are more compact by nature and made of more constant things than flesh or blood; therefore, they offer a long life to men more than other things, and even preserve their health against corruptions, just as they do for common **Mercury**.

When the whiteness is at its highest degree, the vessel can be opened and the **white stone** <note>the "Little Work" or *albedo* stage, capable of transmuting base metals into silver</note> taken out, of which this shall be the trial of perfection: if a small piece placed upon a glowing plate of **Venus** <note>In alchemy, Venus is the symbol for copper</note> gives off no smoke, it is well; otherwise, it must be digested longer until you learn the point of birth and **fixation** <note>original: "fixionis"; the state where a substance becomes solid and stable under heat, no longer evaporating</note>. You shall do the same when you have progressed to the **red stone** <note>the final goal or *rubedo*, capable of transmuting metals into gold</note>. 

This is the **leaven of multiplication** <note>the process of increasing the power or quantity of the Stone</note> with common Mercury, not otherwise than was said before regarding **Philosophical Mercury**, under the same weight, place, and equal moderation. This shall be done so that one part may perfectly tint a hundred parts further than before; and this, being repeated more often, will provide as great a supply of the matter as you wish, so that one part might bring a thousand parts of Mercury to the best **Moon** <note>original: "lunam"; the alchemical term for silver</note>. For a greater declaration of this work, **Paracelsus** breaks out more widely into these words, saying: "So that you may understand better, I say, let the highly purified Mercury of the Philosophers be dissolved by its spouse, namely the bodily spirit or living Mercury. The woman shall dissolve her husband, and the husband likewise his wife..."

...will coagulate and fix. For that mutual love which is seen between spouses is the same as that between the **Mercury of the philosophers** <note>A purified, "living" form of mercury used as a primary ingredient, distinct from common quicksilver</note> and the **earth of the metals**. For nature seeks nature similar to itself <note>original: "Natura siquidem naturam appetit sibi similem"; a foundational axiom of alchemy</note>. In terms of their physical body they do not differ, except in their powers and properties. For the "metallic man" is fixed in the fire, while the "metallic woman" is volatile <note>In alchemical allegory, "fixed" substances resist fire, while "volatile" ones evaporate or sublimate</note>. If a living man be mixed with a living woman, a generation results therefrom; however, this does not happen from a dead man with a living woman. For this reason, let [the woman] be united with a living [man]; then at last the woman dissolves the man, and he tinges the woman and makes her fruitful. 

Let both be placed at last into a glass vessel sealed with the tightest seal <note>original: "strictissimo sigillo"; referring to the airtight "Hermetic seal" made by melting the glass neck of the flask</note>, lest the woman should exhale any breath; otherwise, this work will be in vain. Place them finally into the "marriage bed" and the **bath of Mary** <term>balneum maris|A water bath used to provide gentle, consistent heat (the origin of the modern "bain-marie")</term>. When they have become sufficiently warm within it under a well-moderated heat, in the first stage the woman will be clothed in a black color. This is the sign of conception and the first key to unlocking the ark of this divine MYSTERY. 

As this very light heat is continued, that blackness will be gradually consumed by another succeeding color, just as one worm is consumed by another. Then others will follow, as many and as varied as are seen in a **peacock's tail** <note>original: "pavonis cauda"; a famous stage in the alchemical process where a rainbow of colors appears on the matter</note>, with the dryness itself working this upon the moisture. Let the heat of the fire be continued until that multicolored second "worm" is devoured by a third, or by the **white eagle** having swan-like feathers <note>The "White Eagle" represents the stage of purification where the matter turns a brilliant, shimmering white</note>, and the matter of **Luna** <note>The Moon, representing Silver</note> is made altogether white like snow, and the glass has reached its perfect degree. 

The newborn Queen thus addresses the world:

> I am the Queen most worthy of praise above all others, most filled with powers and virtues, who transforms **Venus** <note>Copper</note>, **Mars** <note>Iron</note>, **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note>, **Saturn** <note>Lead</note>, and **Mercury** into the most constant Moon <note>pure Silver</note>; and not only that, but I also free suffering humans from various infirmities and diseases, such as from all fevers, the falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note>, leprosy, the venereal disease, and other mineral corruptions.

After the fire is increased, the royal woman emerges as a most powerful king, with the whiteness gradually ending in a yellow or saffron color, and thereafter into the most ruddy splendor of a ruby. Now the **Eastern King** is born, ruling over all the princes of the whole world, whom he also addresses with these words:

> I am the **sulfur of nature**, King of Kings, Prince of princes, and Lord of lords, surpassing all with most perfect power, conquering and subjecting, overcome by none, nor compelled. I possess an invincible kingdom, by which I transform the Moon, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and the Mercury of the common people into the best gold—better than Hungarian gold <note>In the Renaissance, gold from Hungarian mines was considered the standard for highest purity</note>—and I confirm and stabilize them against the torments of all trials <note>meaning the gold will pass the tests of the furnace and acid without losing weight</note>. Nor do I only drive away the diseases of metals, but also those of men, which presumptuous physicians have hitherto thought incurable, such as **gout** <note>original: "podagra"</note>, dropsy, leprosy, the falling sickness, and all others that come against nature. Furthermore, I grant good memory, sound judgment and understanding, and long life to those who [use] my [remedy]...

they use a constant protection with food and drink: likewise, I exalt him who refreshes me with food and drink that are agreeable to me into the highest honors, infinite wealth and riches, and I make him powerful. Indeed, through me the entire world is governed. Whosoever shall have attained me shall possess all things with me; for he who possesses this gold of mine achieves every desire. Dissolve this in its own moisture; when placed in the marriage bed <note>A metaphorical term for the flask where the "male" and "female" principles are united</note>, it will complete its fermentation operations far more quickly than before, and will convert the dough into its own substance, and into the treasure of the philosophers, most precious beyond all other worldly things.

->*Concerning another process for the stone, by Paracelsus.*<-

### CHAPTER XIII.

The philosophical ways are various, all tending toward one and the same goal and stone, as is evident from the preceding and following pages. For this reason, this art is described in various ways by the author. Let us therefore hear what he teaches in another place concerning this stone. "The nature of minerals," he says, "produced one admirable genus in the bowels of the earth, and that is twofold; it is found in various places in Europe. The best that was offered to my hands and proven by experiment is a star <term>astrum|In Paracelsian thought, an 'astrum' is the celestial or 'star-like' vital power contained within a physical substance</term> from the beginning of the sphere of the sun; the other consists in the southern star in its first flowering; it is the viscous substance <note>original: "viscus"; a sticky or slimy matter</note> of the earth brought into the light by its own star. In its first coagulation it is adorned with redness, and in it are included all the flowers and colors of minerals, about which much is found among the philosophers. This pertains to the moist and cold nature, to which it was adapted by a certain comparison. 

But the perfect knowledge of it, when compared to experience, has remained hidden until now from many—indeed almost all—philosophers, as many as have hitherto shot their arrows at the target; striving in vain, they have turned very far aside from the true and complete goal. They have thought that **Mercury** and **sulfur** are the mother and father of all metals, but indeed they did not remember the third <note>original: "tertij non meminerunt"; referring to Salt, which Paracelsus added to Mercury and Sulfur to form his 'Tria Prima' or three primary principles of all matter</note>. Nay, what is more, none of them has yet been able to take into his hands the fishing net which is suited to the 'true water,' the mother of metals; this water, once separated by the spagyric art <term>artificio spagirico|The alchemical process of separating a substance into its components and then recombining them in a purified state</term>, makes its fish manifest, which neither the Galenic fishing <note>A reference to the traditional medical teachings of Galen, which Paracelsus sought to overthrow</note> nor the torn net of Avicenna <note>Avicenna (Ibn Sina) was a famous Persian philosopher and physician whose works were foundational to medieval alchemy and medicine</note> were ever able to catch. If I were obliged to demonstrate to modern physicians even the name alone of the conjunction, solution, and coagulation which nature itself has revealed and demonstrated in this, its creation, from the beginning of the world, a year would fail me, and all the paper, however much there might be, would be insufficient to instruct them—

...stated. It is dissolved in its own liquor, not yet mature, just as a pear is hidden within its tree. The concealer of the pear is the tree; when the stars and nature come together in it, it puts forth green branches, and afterward in March makes its atoms, foliage, and flowers visible, making progress toward the production of fruit—the pears—which finally emerge in autumn. In a not dissimilar way, one must judge the minerals in the bowels of the earth, which are pushed into the light by the stars: this very thing is the chief consideration for the alchemist gasping after the treasure of nature. I shall now reveal the method of this craftsmanship from the beginning, middle, and end, together with its water, sulfur, and balsam. By the solution of these three, and their subsequent conjunction into one, the entire business of the work is completed in this manner.

Let **cinnabar** <note>original: "minera cinabaris"; cinnabar is the bright red ore of mercury (mercuric sulfide), highly prized by alchemists.</note> ore be taken and washed with **celestial water** <note>Usually refers to pure rainwater or dew collected under specific astrological conditions.</note> for three hours; finally, let it be strained and dissolved in **aqua regia** <note>A powerful "royal water" acid made here from vitriol (sulfates), saltpeter (potassium nitrate), and common salt.</note> made from vitriol, saltpeter, and common salt. Let it be drawn off through an **alembic** <note>A distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels and a tube.</note>, then poured back on, and let it be cared for by **cohobating** <note>The process of repeatedly distilling a liquid off from the solid residue it was just poured over to concentrate the "essence."</note>, so that the pure may be separated from the impure which remains below. Let it putrefy in **horse dung** <note>A common alchemical method for providing a steady, gentle, and "living" heat for fermentation.</note> for a month, and afterward let the elements be separated so that, when they have revealed their signs, they may be distilled by an alembic with a fire of the first degree. By this, water and air ascend first, and finally fire, and this through the remaining degrees of heat which can be discerned by an experienced operator. At the bottom of the vessel the "earth" remains, in which lies hidden all that has been sought by many, yet found by very few. This earth, enclosed in a **reverberatory furnace**, you shall artificially **calcinate** <note>Heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder.</note>, proceeding from the first to the fifth degree of heat, each degree for the space of five hours. This is done so that you may have a **volatile salt**, as subtle as *alcohol* <note>In this context, "alcohol" refers to an extremely fine, purified powder rather than a liquid.</note>, and a constant "star" of fire and earth, which you shall separate by the elements of water and air which you saved before.

Finally, place it in the digestion of a **water bath** <note>original: "balnei maris"; a bain-marie used for gentle heating.</note> for eight hours, and you will see that which has been unknown to many alchemists until now and least considered. Separate it skillfully according to your experience and in the spagyric way; the earth itself will be rendered wonderfully white, from which the **tincture** <note>The concentrated spiritual or medicinal essence of the substance.</note> will have been extracted. Next, join the element of fire with the alcoholized salt of the earth through digestion and the craftsmanship of the **Pelican** <note>A "Pelican" is a specialized alchemical flask with two side-arms that feed back into the body, allowing for continuous circulation and "distillation of the spirit."</note>; this substance will still put down another sediment, which you shall separate from the pure. Then at last, take the "Pelicanized Lion" which was found at the beginning. When you see its tincture and the element of fire above the water, air, and earth, separate it with a separating funnel and strain this "Sun" by inclination; for it is **Potable Gold** <note>original: "aurum potabile"; a legendary medicinal liquid gold believed to cure all diseases and grant longevity.</note>. Let it be drenched with the sweet alcohol of wine and drawn off until no more of the sharpness of the aqua regia is perceived. Separate this **Oil of the Sun**, and place it in a retort with a **Hermetic seal** <note>An airtight seal made by melting the glass of the vessel's neck.</note>...

By this artifice, the tincture of **Gold** <note>original: "Solis"; literally "of the Sun," the alchemical name for gold.</note> is perfected in its degree. And when it has arrived at perfection, you will see the sign of the elements: separate one from the other, since the red appears to the eye as separated from the white. You shall separate this from the white; for it is a red tincture so powerful that it stains all white bodies red, or red ones white, which is quite marvelous. Continue this work of yours, and do not lose heart on account of excessive labor. Rectify it <note>To purify a liquid by repeated distillation.</note> so many times until you see the **true and bright Green Lion** <note>original: "viridem leonem"; a symbolic name for a powerful mineral acid or the vital force within matter, often associated with vitriol.</note>, heavy, which tinges matter into **perfect gold**. Do not desist (I say) from the work I have mentioned, until you have the signs and see the lion and the treasure that is not perishable. May it be well with him who finds it and knows how to apply it to the tincture.

This is the **true balsam of the celestial stars**, which allows no body to pass into decay, and leaves no leprosy, gout, or dropsy unexpelled, by the administration of a single grain, if it be fermented with the **sulfur of Gold** <note>original: "sulphure solis".</note>. The nature of the water and everything I have written will teach and reveal all. Take therefore as much of the mineral liquor as you wish, two parts of the salt of the red earth, and one part of the sulfur of Gold. Let them be dissolved and coagulated in a **pelican** <note>A specialized alchemical flask with two side-arms that loop back into the body, allowing for continuous circulation and distillation.</note>, and that for a third time. In this way you shall have the **tincture of the alchemists**, whose weight is by no means to be described in this place, but is reserved for its own place.

Whoever possesses one ounce of the **Star of Gold** <note>original: "Solis astri"; the spiritual essence or quintessential power of gold.</note> and projects it over several ounces of gold, will tinge his own body. If he has the **Star of Mercury**, he will similarly tinge the whole body of common mercury. If he has the <term>Star of Venus</term> <note>The essence of Copper.</note>, in a similar manner he will tinge the entire body of copper into the best gold, and into the highest and constant perfection: thus one must judge concerning the remaining stars of the metals, such as those of **Saturn** <note>Lead.</note>, **Mars** <note>Iron.</note>, etc. From these also, by the same reasoning, tinctures are drawn, which are not to be described here, because they are contained in the books *On the Nature of Things* and the *Archidoxes* <note>Two of Paracelsus's most famous works on medicine and chemistry.</note>. 

With these few words, I wish for the **first being** <note>original: "ens"; the fundamental essence or vital principle.</note> of metals and minerals of the earth, together with the tincture of the alchemists, to be sufficiently and abundantly declared to true alchemists. Nor is there any reason why any of the operators should be deterred by the span of nine months, but let him proceed without weariness under <term>spagyric</term> guidance, by which in forty alchemical days he will be able to fix, extract, exalt, purify, ferment, and coagulate the <term>philosophers' stone</term> <note>original: "lapidem alchemistarum"; the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals and providing an elixir of life.</note>, to the honor of God, to whom be praise, honor, and glory.

The explanation of the Cabalists <note>Followers of Kabbalah, a form of Jewish mysticism that alchemists like Paracelsus adapted into a "Christian Cabala" to explain the secrets of creation and nature.</note> holds, under the name of the **Phoenix**, that there is a **volatile eagle** whose feathers fly without wind and lift the body of the phoenix into its nest. In this nest, it is nourished by the element of fire; its chicks pluck out their mother’s eyes with their beaks, and a whiteness is produced in its own separate sphere. In this whiteness consists the life of its heart and the balsam of its intestines. According to the Cabalistic sense, sulfur is interpreted as **cinnabar** <note>A bright red mineral consisting of mercury sulfide, the primary ore of mercury.</note>, about which Paracelsus has spoken above. Very recently, when treating **electrum** <note>In alchemy, electrum often refers to a highly potent alloy of the seven primary metals, believed to have magical or medicinal properties.</note>, I referred the reader to cinnabar and not without cause, for they have the greatest affinity. What else is cinnabar but a composition or mixture of two minerals: sulfur and **quicksilver** <note>original: "argenti vivi"; mercury.</note>? What also is electrum, but a mixture of two or more substances, whether minerals or metals? Why then should the **Sulfur of Gold** <note>original: "Solis"; literally "of the Sun," the alchemical name for gold.</note>, when joined by artifice with the **philosophical Mercury of Silver** <note>original: "lunæ"; literally "of the Moon," the alchemical name for silver.</note>, not be considered electrum or cinnabar? Whether it is made by nature or by chemistry, the component parts do not differ. But this will be clearer in what follows.

#### *On the fourth Paracelsian process for the [philosopher's] stone.*

### CHAPTER XIV.

Before we speak of the **physical tincture**, it will be worthwhile first of all to know what its subject is; for this has always been hidden until now. The matter of the tincture is, therefore, a certain thing (provided you understand me according to the **spagyric** <note>The "spagyric art" is the Paracelsian method of preparing medicine by separating a substance into its core elements—sulfur, mercury, and salt—and recombining them in a purified state.</note> sense) which indeed passes from three into one essence by the chemical art, or is able to remain as such. Indeed, to declare it by its name according to ancient use and custom, it has been called the **Red Lion** by many, but known by very few. This, by the aid of nature as well as art, can be transmuted into the **White Eagle**, so that from one, two are made, which shine for the spagyrist with a brilliance greater than gold; when kept as one, they shine even more. Now, if you do not understand the accustomed speech of the Cabalists and the ancient Astronomers, you have by no means been called by God to the spagyric art, nor chosen by nature—indeed, you are not fit even to open your mouth in this art. Therefore, the matter of the tincture is the **greatest pearl** and most precious treasure, and the noblest thing of all that can befall the meditations of men through the manifestation of the Most High Creator. This is the **Lily of Alchemy** and of Medicine, which the philosophers have sought so accurately, but on account of a lack of complete knowledge and its perfect preparation, they have not yet been able to lead it to the most absolute end. Through their investigations and experiences, only the beginning of the tincture has been given to us; nevertheless, the true foundation, which it behooves my disciples to imitate, was left to me, so that no one should mix their own **masks** <note>original: "larvas"; referring to false appearances, deceptions, or the errors of "pseudo-alchemists."</note> with our inventions. I (says Paracelsus) shall deservedly correct the spagyrists after my long experiences, and separate the false and erroneous from the true...

I will indeed separate [these things], since through my very extensive investigations I have discovered how I might justly criticize and change such similar things. If, however, I had found the experiments of the ancients to be superior to my own, I would by no means have undertaken such great labors, which I have gladly endured for the sake, benefit, and honor of all honest alchemists. Since, therefore, the subject of the tincture has been sufficiently explained—so that it could and should scarcely be done more faithfully or truly between two brothers—I shall proceed to its preparation, and beyond the experiences of the first age, I will add my own discoveries.

The ancient spagyrists <note>original: "spagiri"; practitioners of spagyric medicine/alchemy, which focuses on separating a substance into its components and then recombining them in a purified form.</note> putrefied the **lili** <note>original: "lili"; in Paracelsian alchemy, this term often refers to the "matter of the stone" or a specific starting material, sometimes associated with antimony or a "blessed" matter.</note> for one philosophical month; afterwards, they distilled the moist spirits from it until the dry parts were finally raised. They soaked the **caput mortuum** <note>original: "caput mortuum"; literally "dead head," the useless solid residue remaining after distillation or sublimation.</note> with the moist spirits and repeatedly drew it off through distillation, until the dry parts were lifted up completely. Next, they united the extracted humors and dry spirits together using a **pelican** <note>original: "pellicanum"; a specialized circulatory distillation vessel with two "arms" that feed condensed liquid back into the main body, resembling a pelican pecking its breast.</note> three or four times, until the whole of the *lili* settled at the bottom as a dry substance. 

Although the first experiment gave this process before fixation, our predecessors nevertheless frequently achieved their desired goal perfectly through it. However, they would have had a shorter way to reach the treasure of the **Red Lion** <note>original: "rubei leonis"; a symbolic name for the final, perfected stage of the alchemical work, often representing the "tincture" that turns base metals into gold.</note> if they had learned the harmony of **Astronomy** with **Alchemy**, which I demonstrated in the *Apocalypse of Hermes*. Since indeed every day (as **Christ** says for the consolation of the faithful) has its own essence, there was immense and heavy labor for the spagyrists before my time; now, by the help of the flowing **Holy Spirit**, this labor will be eased in this last age by my theory and practice. 

Since the first age gave the first experience of the tincture, two spagyrists made it from one simple substance. But because this discovery perished in the middle age, their successors later happened upon two simple names of this kind through diligent searching, and they named it with a single word, namely **lili**, the subject of the tincture. Finally, the imitators of nature putrefied this matter in its own time, just like a seed in the earth, since before this "corruption" or decay nothing can be born from it, nor can any secret power break forth. Afterwards, they drew the moist spirits from the matter until, finally, by the violence of the fire, the dry parts were likewise raised and sublimated. In this way—no differently than a farmer following the seasons of the year—they reached maturity. 

At last, after their spring was finished, summer came forth, at which time they incorporated those fruits and dry spirits, and brought the mastery of the tincture to such a point that it reached the harvest and achieved its extreme maturity. The ancient spagyrists would not have needed such long labor and tedious repetition if they had learned the work from my school; they would have achieved their goal far more quickly and with less expense. "Therefore I say to you," says **Paracelsus**, "take only the **rose-colored blood** from the lion, and the **glue** from the eagle; after you have joined them together, coagulate them according to the ancient process."

You will possess the tincture of the philosophers <note>original: "Tincturam habebitis philosophorum"</note>, which countless many have sought but very few have found. Thus, the Alchemist compounds certain simple substances, which he "corrupts" <note>In alchemy, "corruption" refers to the breaking down or putrefaction of a substance so it can be reborn in a higher form.</note> according to the rules of the art, and from there prepares another thing, continuing until it becomes one: this accomplishes more than nature itself could do on its own. So that you may understand me rightly and properly, you should seek your **lion** in the East and the **eagle** toward the South for this work we have undertaken. You will find no better instruments than those produced by Hungary and Istria. But if you desire to derive it from unity through duality in trinity, with an equal transformation of each part, you must direct your journey toward the South; thus in Cyprus you will achieve your wish, though this is a matter I should speak of very little.

Many secrets <note>original: "arcana"</note> regarding transmutations are found, though known to few; and although they may be revealed to someone by the Lord God, a rumor does not immediately break out alongside the art. Rather, the Almighty gives the understanding of how to hide these and other things until the arrival of **Elias the Artist** <note>original: "Heliæ Artistæ"; a prophetic figure in Paracelsian alchemy expected to reveal all hidden knowledge at the end of the world.</note>, at which time nothing will be so hidden that it shall not be revealed. For we see that in the **sulphur of Jupiter** <note>original: "sulphure Jovis"; likely referring to a specific preparation of tin or a related mineral compound.</note> there is a very great tincture of gems, which indeed brings them to a higher state than nature itself is able; but enough on these matters, let us finally return to the medicinal <note>original: "physicam"</note> tincture.

Lastly, the ancient spagyrists "pelicanated" <note>original: "pellicanatum"; to circulate a substance in a pelican, a specialized glass vessel with two "arms" that return condensed vapors to the base.</note> the **lili**, fixing their matter with a certain regulated increase of fire until, after the disappearance of all colors, it took on a redness like blood, and with it the condition of the **salamander** <note>A mythical lizard believed to live in fire; in alchemy, this signifies a substance that has become "fire-proof" or stable at high temperatures.</note>. Their process was indeed correct, and it is right and proper for everyone seeking this **pearl** <note>original: "margaritā"; a common metaphor for the Philosopher's Stone.</note> to proceed in the same way. It would be very difficult for me to explain this more clearly to you; however, once you have learned in the school of Alchemists to observe the grades of fire and to change the vessels, then at last you will see—as soon as your *lili* has been heated in the **philosophical egg** <note>original: "ovo philosophico"; a sealed, oval glass vessel used for long-term chemical digestion.</note>—that it appears in wonderful demonstrations. It becomes blacker than a crow, then in time whiter than a swan, and finally, passing through yellowness, it becomes redder than any blood.

Since we have this "treasure of the Egyptians" in our hands, we should turn it to our benefit, and that through a double mastery: the first for the restoration of health in the human body, the second for the transmutation of metals. To use it for this [second] purpose, one weight of it must be projected <note>original: "projiciendum"; projection is the final step where the tincture is thrown onto molten base metal to transform it.</note> over a thousand weights of molten **gold** <note>original: "solis"; literally "the sun," the alchemical name for gold.</note>; only then will the Medicine be prepared to remove the **leprosy of metals** <note>The "sickness" or impurities that make a metal "base" (like lead or copper) rather than "noble" (gold).</note>. Likewise, some of the physicians in Egypt lived one hundred and fifty years by means of this tincture. The lives of others were even longer through this medium, as is clear from histories. Thus, the tincture of the physicians is a kind of universal medicine, which consumes all diseases just as fire consumes all wood. Its dose is very small, but its operation is most powerful. Through it (says Paracelsus), I have cured leprosy, dropsy,
