[These remedies] are given; likewise for the **French disease** <note>original: "morbum Gallicum"; a common historical term for syphilis</note>: it is effective for the **relaxation of the limbs** <note>possibly referring to paralysis or loss of motor control</note>: it wipes away **scrofula** <term>strumas: a swelling of the lymph nodes, often associated with tuberculosis</term> when smeared on: it is administered to **Epileptics** in a decoction of Betony and Peony: and for **those with a cough**, it is given with nettle seed and hyssop cooked in wine. It treats **fissures of the lips** and other parts, **cold diseases** caused by cold or putrefied humors, or those in which there is an abundance of gas, **red pustules of the face** and other infections: against the **French scabies** <note>syphilitic skin rashes</note> in the French disease, it is given with water of fumitory and flowers of Broom. Likewise, it thoroughly heals **"blind" hemorrhoids** <note>internal or non-bleeding piles</note> and their pain. 

It also draws **Mercury** <term>Hydrargyrum: quicksilver, often used as a toxic treatment for syphilis at the time</term> out of the body in **moist diseases** when smeared on immediately after a bath. It heals the **iliac passion** <term>a painful and potentially fatal blockage of the intestines</term> by smearing. Likewise, it treats **skin eruptions** <term>impetigines</term>, any **incurable diseases**, **freckles**, **lichens** <note>skin scaling or localized rashes</note>, **morphew** <term>morpheam: a skin condition involving localized discoloration</term>, **measles**, **cracks in the hands** and **the itch** <note>scabies</note>, **hardness of the breasts**, **swelling**, **ulceration**, **cancer**, and the **bites of poisonous animals**; it matures [the wound] by soaking a certain woolen cloth and placing it upon the area; it cleanses and softens **knots** <note>lumps or joint swellings</note>, **stiffness of the nerves** <note>tendons or muscles</note> and any injury; it matures and cleanses **broken or calloused bones** when a certain soaked woolen cloth is applied; it cures **paralysis**, **whitlows** <term>panaritium: a painful infection of the fingertip</term>, **putrid fevers**, and **daily**, **tertian**, and **quartan fevers** <note>fevers that recur every day, every third day, or every fourth day</note>. 

In the case of a **daily fever**, it is given with wine and a decoction of rosemary or mint shortly before the paroxysm <note>the peak or onset of the fever fit</note>; in a **tertian fever**, with a decoction of centaury in wine; and in a **quartan fever**, with bugloss water. Likewise, it treats the **plague** and **pestilential fever** with pimpernel water or its salt, and also with a decoction of radish in wine to which a little **theriac** <note>a famous "universal" herbal antidote</note> or **Mithridatium** <note>a complex ancient antidote against poisons</note> has been added; and **cold gout** <term>Podagram</term> by placing a certain soaked woolen cloth over it: likewise, with **ground-pine** <note>original: "Chamepytide"</note> it drives away **lice**, generates pus [to drain a wound], breaks open **abscesses** <term>apostemata</term> that have been brought to maturity, and warms **chilled feet**. 

In summary, **oil of sulfur** is so effective that it allows neither a living nor a dead body to pass into putrefaction, but preserves them so intact that no celestial influence, nor corruption proceeding from the elements, nor even any defect brought on from birth can harm it.

-> A D D I T I O N. <-

**Take** <note>original: "℞", the symbol for recipe</note> as much as you wish of **flowers of sulfur** <note>a powdered form of sulfur</note> sublimated three times; put them in a glass vessel and pour over them enough **spirit of turpentine** to dissolve the flowers of sulfur: place it over a very gentle heat, and after this you will see the sulfur and spirit of turpentine turn [red] like blood; then pour over it the best **spirit of wine** <term>ethanol</term> to a height of three fingers' width and leave it until the spirit of wine is tinted; pour that out, add more spirit of wine, and do as before until it is no longer tinted; and distill it in a [water] bath so that it is separated from the redness of the sulfur; remove the glass, attach another receiver, increase the fire, and then the **essence of sulfur** will come out like red blood: a noble medicine without any of the stench that common chemists usually produce in their preparations. Spirit...

For Turpentine, do thus: ℞ <note>Take</note>. Turpentine, as much as you wish, pour a sufficient amount of clear water over it in an earthen or copper vessel, and set it to distill. ### ON VITRIOLATED SULFUR

You will recognize **vitriolated sulfur** <term>Sulphur vitriolatum: a preparation where sulfur is treated with vitriol (sulfates) to alter its properties</term> when a disease must be cured by **anodynes** <term>pain-relieving medicines</term>; it then accomplishes this without any danger. This same Sulfur is "fixed" by its nature and possesses its own sweetness; indeed, if chickens swallow it, they will sleep for a time without harm, and afterward they are revived. This Sulfur settles all **passions** <note>disturbances or physical sufferings of the body</note> without danger, binds all pains and all **colic passions** <note>severe abdominal pains</note>, and this medicine ought to precede all preventive measures.

#### ADDITION

℞ <note>Take</note>. **Vitriol** <term>a historical term for sulfate minerals, often iron or copper sulfate</term>, dissolve it in water, and bring it to a boil. Place iron plates into it, and you will find them burdened with a red powder; scrape this off. Do this for as long as it takes to extract all the Sulfur. You shall then **circulate** <term>reflux or repeatedly distill</term> this with the best **spirit of wine** <note>distilled alcohol or ethanol</note>. Leave behind that which is black, and save that which is very red: it works most powerfully both internally and externally.

### ON SALT AND THE POWERS OF SALT

Salt is a certain very strong remedy, and according to the proverb, it is the most excellent seasoning of all seasonings. Indeed, the common power of all salt is to warm, to dry, to thin, to dissolve, to disperse, to cleanse, to bind, and to consume any superfluous **humors** <note>the bodily fluids that, when unbalanced, were thought to cause disease</note>.

However, salt that is drier is more suitable for salting; therefore, its power is also to turn away the loathing caused by poisonous humors, to prevent nausea, to incite and excite an appetite for all foods, and to consume corruption. The same is provided by preserved olives, lemons, caper flowers and fruits; likewise by grapes, apples, pears, figs, and turnips. Furthermore, the power of salt is to protect the meat of fish as well as of other animals which we eat from putrefaction—lest they happen to spoil even in the stomach or lest "cheese" <note>curdled or undigested masses</note> be formed there—and it most conveniently defends them. It also guards any wine from mucus and sourness, and clarifies them more quickly, while also reducing their harshness so they have less power to inebriate. Likewise, it makes softened skins looser and more capacious by washing, and by its sharpness, it corrects and improves the thickness of leathers, strengthens the flavor, and makes it better. Item: it makes sterile, marshy, and swampy fields fertile; it specifically heals the olive tree on the sea shore, as well as Radish, Beet, Rue, and Cumin, so that they are much sweeter and much more fertile—

...according to the testimony of Pliny. In cattle, herds, beasts of burden, and for livestock returning to pasture, [salt] corrects a loss of appetite when they taste it by licking, and it greatly provokes a craving for food and drink. This results in much more abundant milk, which in turn provides a much more pleasant cheese. Likewise, according to the testimony of Plutarch, it is most convenient for making livestock pregnant and for removing excessive fat that is harmful to them. On the advice of Aristotle, it induces mating in sheep if they lick it before and after; it also heals various diseases in cattle, herds, and beasts of burden. 

Likewise, it can purify muddy water through a certain addition, just as Elisha did by the word of God in the fourth book of Kings, chapter 2 <note>In modern Bibles, this is 2 Kings 2:21</note>. It resists the bites of wild beasts; when crushed in a linen cloth and soaked in vinegar—so that the area is tightly bound—it opposes the bites of crocodiles. When drunk with honey and vinegar, it counteracts the bites of the centipede. When smeared on with vinegar, it treats the bites of hornets or wasps; with vinegar or a fourth part of oil, it treats scorpion stings; and with oregano, pitch, wax, or honey, it treats the bites of serpents. When drunk with honeyed vinegar, it resists [poisoning by] mushrooms and ingested opium. 

The power of this same salt, through a certain addition, is to partially remove the pestilential malice of burning coals. When smeared on and applied with vinegar or hyssop, the power of salt resists <term>sacred fire</term> <note>original: "igni sacro"; a historical term for inflammatory skin conditions such as Erysipelas or shingles</note> and creeping ulcers. When applied with oil or chewed, its power prevents the blisters of those burned by fire from breaking out. When mixed with other medicines of similar capacity, it soothes itching. 

Likewise, it corrects leprosy, boils, lichen-like rashes, and <term>psora</term> <note>scaly or itchy skin conditions</note> when combined with raisins (with the seeds removed), beef tallow, and leaven or even bread itself. Likewise, it treats cancerous growths by application with "wild grapes" <note>likely *Bryonia alba* or *Taminia*</note>. When the same salt is crushed with barley flour and applied on a linen cloth moistened with wine, it heals <term>phagedenas</term> <note>original: "phagedænas"; rapidly spreading or "eating" ulcers</note> of the sores. 

The power of this salt, when mixed with soot, is to drive away the warts of our children through rubbing. The power of this salt, by dipping a linen cloth [into a solution], is to cure the growing or putrefying ulcers of many people. Likewise, when applied with spider webs, it commonly heals lighter wounds. When applied with honey and flour, it treats dislocations. By adding it to a <term>cleansing unguent</term> <note>original: "Smegmati"; a soapy or detergent preparation for the skin</note>, it extends and smooths the skin. 

Thus Galen sprinkled the body of a newborn infant with a modest amount of salt, so that its skin might be rendered thicker and more solid, and thus less vulnerable to external injuries. The power of this same salt, when mixed into medicines, creates a radiance in the skin of the face, and it is also useful for <term>bruises</term> <note>original: "sugillationes"; dark spots or discolorations under the skin</note> of the face. It disperses boils when used with raisins or swine fat, as well as with honey. The power of this salt, when added to medicines according to the opinion of the ancients, preserves those who are drunk from intoxication when they are anointed with oil. 

Likewise, it represses growths in the eyes. It consumes <term>pterygia</term> <note>original: "Pterygia"; triangular fleshy growths on the white of the eye</note> and removes other exuberant growths of flesh; therefore, its addition to eye-washes and plasters is very useful. For eyes bloodshot from a blow or bruised, its power—when combined with an equal weight of myrrh and honey, or with hyssop and warm water...

...is proven by applying it as a fomentation. The power of this same salt, when ground on small whetstones together with milk, is to counteract <term>suffusions of the eyes</term> <note>original: "suffusionibus oculorum"; likely referring to cataracts or corneal clouding</note>. Likewise, the power of salt applied with vinegar is to soothe earaches. Also, it is useful for spreading on a piece of linen for weeping ulcers of the mouth. Likewise, it is beneficial for gums distressed by moisture when rubbed upon them. The power of this same salt when rubbed—namely, when crushed—is to cure roughness of the tongue.

The power of this same salt, if held every morning on an empty stomach under the tongue until it liquefies, is to preserve the teeth from rot and corrosion; when rubbed on the teeth, it consumes internal moisture. Their pains are mitigated with a fomentation of vinegar and a certain liniment of resin, and it removes the numbness of the teeth. The power of this same salt, moistened with boiling water, is to warm the neck and contracted nerves when placed in bags, according to *Galen*. 

Likewise, salt relieves <term>angina</term> <note>In this historical context, "angina" refers generally to any inflammation of the throat or "quinsy" rather than a heart condition</note> when a liniment is made from <term>honeyed vinegar</term> <note>original: "aceto mulso"; oxymel</note> and oil. Likewise, the power of toasted salt with honey is beneficial for the tonsils and the <term>uvula</term> <note>original: "uvaeque"</note>. Likewise, by licking it, it dispels a chronic cough; the power of <term>Rock Salt</term> <note>original: "salis Gemmæ"; literally "gem salt," referring to pure, crystalline rock salt</note> is especially effective for this. 

Likewise, the power of common salt mixed in wine is even to soften the bowels. Furthermore, in a drink of wine, it expels intestinal worms and larvae; through the admixture of other things, it purges thick and sluggish humors, "glassy" phlegm, and melancholy. The power of this same salt, when drunk or applied glowing hot in bags, is to relieve <term>colic</term> <note>original: "colum"</note> and griping pains. 

Likewise, according to the assertions of *Hippocrates* and *Galen*, salt with millet—applied as a type of dry fomentation—soothes pains of the <term>hypochondrium</term> <note>the upper abdomen</note> arising from thick and viscous humors. Likewise, salt applied with millet in a small vessel warms those who have been scorched, as *Aretius* believes. Likewise, with the rubbing of vinegar and oil, it induces sweat by the fire for those suffering from the <term>royal disease</term> <note>original: "morbo regio"; a historical name for jaundice</note>, and it cures perceptible itching. 

Likewise, when anointed with oil, it heals those with <term>dropsy</term> <note>original: "hydropicos"; an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</note>. Likewise, the power of ground salt in water or oil, rubbed in the sun or near a fire until it reaches a certain viscosity, is beneficial to those suffering from *Leucophlegmatia or anasarca* <note>types of systemic swelling or edema</note>. Likewise, it mitigates kidney pains through a certain moist fomentation. 

Likewise, with oregano and leaven (and also butter, as pleases *Avicenna*), it ripens tumors of the testes. The power of this same salt, when drunk or applied glowing hot in bags, is to mitigate pains of the hips, and with the grinding of flour, honey, and oil, it relieves those with <term>gout</term> <note>original: "podagricos"</note>. However, with a very fine rubbing of oil and a morning massage after the gouty pains have subsided, it preserves one from such affections. Likewise, it removes corns on the feet and <term>chilblains</term> <note>original: "perniones"; sores caused by cold</note>. 

Likewise, it aids those who are exhausted when used as a liniment with oil. *Pliny* says that when rubbed on, it corrects the heat and burning of fevers. Likewise, the power of salt dissolved in water and taken daily preserves one from the plague, as the inhabitants of the kingdom of *Mellis* <note>The Mali Empire in West Africa, often referred to as "Melli" in early modern Latin texts</note> do. 

The power of salt, however, is not only to preserve the flesh of animals and vegetables for a long time, but also to test and smelt the veins of metals by a certain addition; for it liquefies easily, and therefore has a certain peculiar faculty in melting.

### THE VIRTUES OF THE OIL OF COMMON SALT

<margin>Salt excites thirst, but its oil restrains it.</margin>
A single drop of this, in which gold has been dissolved, or from which <term>potable gold</term> <note>original: "aurum potabile"; a legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold dissolved in a liquid, believed to grant longevity</note> has been made, overcomes all ailments that can even be imagined, even those closest or neighboring to death. A single drop of this oil and of <term>vitriol</term> <note>original: "vitrioli"; a group of sulfate minerals, here likely referring to sulfuric acid</note> made through <term>dew water</term> <note>original: "aquam roris"; water collected from dew, considered highly pure in alchemy</note>, taken with <term>water of life</term> <note>original: "aqua vitæ"; concentrated alcohol or spirits</note>, has sustained and caused one already in the death-agony to rise again. Furthermore, whatever is smeared with this oil that is putrid by nature—as happens in wounds or other pains—it erodes and consumes in a single hour. In contrast, all salt protects the putrid so that it is not consumed, and it is acrid. Next, salt excites thirst, but the oil drives it away; witnesses to this fact are several <term>dropsical</term> <note>original: "hydropici"; people suffering from edema or fluid retention</note> patients who, having taken it, lacked thirst for nine or often ten days. Finally, as far as the taste is concerned, the oil is not as acidic as salt, but greatly resembles the sweetness of honey or the juice of wild apples. 

Used outwardly or externally, the oil of salt mixed with oil of Turpentine, wax, chamomile, <term>mullein</term> <note>original: "verbasci"</note>, and similar things, remarkably soothes <term>gouty pains</term> <note>original: "dolores podagricos"</note>, dissipates <term>tophi</term> <note>original: "tophos"; chalky deposits of uric acid in the joints</note>, restores convulsed limbs if they are rubbed with it, heals abscesses, and cures <term>ruptures</term> <note>original: "ramices"; likely referring to hernias</note>. It is given by mouth drop by drop, especially that which is purple or lemon-colored, and is provided through dew water for dissolving gold and for curing infinite diseases. The equivalent of three drops taken from water of life every week renews a person and consumes <term>intercutaneous water</term> <note>original: "aquam intercutem"; edema or fluid under the skin</note>. It disperses the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: "morbum comitialem"; epilepsy</note>, drives away fevers, and heals <term>jaundice</term> <note>original: "Arquatum"; literally the "arched" or "rainbow" disease, a common historical term for jaundice</note>. The same is effective for ulcers that are called <term>malignant</term> <note>original: "cacoëthe"; from the Greek for "bad habit," referring to stubborn or cancerous-type ulcers</note>, <term>phagedenic</term> <note>original: "phagedenas"; rapidly spreading or "eating" sores</note> ulcers of the genitals, <term>nomas</term> <note>original: "nomas"; gangrenous mouth or genital sores</note>, and discharging ears; it removes dullness of the eyes, scars, and <term>white spots</term> <note>original: "albugines"; white opacities on the cornea</note>.

### ON THE BROTH OF COMMON SALT

<term>Salt broth</term> <note>original: "Brodium salis"; a concentrated brine or salt solution</note> is effective against dysentery when given in an enema. Likewise, it is used against <term>herpes</term> <note>original: "herpetes"; in this context, any creeping or spreading skin eruption</note> and <term>creeping ulcers</term> <note>original: "serpigines ulcerum"</note>, tumors of the breasts, sciatica, and for the <term>afterbirth</term> <note>original: "secundinam"</note>. When milk curdles in the breasts, it reduces it by fomentation; it also prevents milk from curdling in the breasts when linen cloths are moistened with it and applied warm. Let whoever has worms in their belly drink salt broth. One who has a bruising of blood from blows is cured by a sponge moistened in salt broth, applied several times a day as a warm or lukewarm fomentation for the clotted blood. This same fomentation promotes any part toward health. 

When drunk and gargled, it expels <term>leeches</term> <note>original: "sanguifugas"</note> if someone had accidentally swallowed them, but it must be drunk slowly in distinct portions and at different times. Likewise, when scattered, it kills fleas living in rooms and chambers. Likewise, when used as a fomentation, it keeps a <term>slipping eye</term> <note>original: "monoculum labentem"; likely referring to a protruding eye or a drooping eyelid</note> in place so that it does not slip further; it preserves and protects against worms and moths.

What is there (I ask) in this subject that is not worthy of admiration? Consider the union of prepared salt with its <term>incombustible agent</term> <note>original: "agente incombustibili"; a substance in alchemy that performs a chemical transformation without being consumed by fire</note>, which does not cease from its action until it is reduced into a better form. Likewise, consider the fusible salt which by itself penetrates and converts its entire body into the <term>Green Lion</term> <note>original: "Leonem viridem"; a famous alchemical symbol representing a potent solvent or a specific state of vitriol or lead during the "Great Work"</note> and into a permanent oil. I shall report elsewhere more details regarding this same subject and its spirit which dissolves all bodies. To this I will add only one thing: ℞ <note>The symbol for "Recipe" or "Take"</note> the <term>bark of the Sea</term> <note>original: "corticem Maris"; likely referring to the salt crust or a specific marine mineral</note> and no other; let it be purified and placed in a glass with our vinegar. Bury it for 15 days in the <term>warmth of the fermenter</term> <note>original: "ventre præliantis"; literally "the belly of the battler," referring to the gentle, digestive heat of a furnace or manure heap used for alchemical maturation</note>. Distill <margin>This is to reduce the whole of the salt into oil.</margin> the oil, and repeat the process until it becomes the Green Lion. With this secret remedy, you will radically remove <term>gout</term> <note>original: "podagram"; a painful form of inflammatory arthritis</note>; it is safely applied both internally and externally. — B. à PORTU <note>Likely referring to Bernard G. ## ON THE BROTH OF SALT FROM OLIVES.

For anyone whose gums in the mouth have become loose, the <term>broth of saltiness</term> <note>original: "brodium salsuginis"; the brine or pickling liquid</note> in which olives are preserved, if held often in the mouth, constricts the rinsed gums and throat once more. Likewise, it drives away dandruff if washed frequently, and extinguishes <term>impetigo</term>, <term>lichens</term> <note>original: "lichenas"; here referring to skin eruptions or scaling skin conditions</note>, burns, and the <term>holy fire</term> <note>original: "ignem sacrum"; a historical term for skin inflammations such as erysipelas or shingles</note>. Against worms in the ears, figs boiled with salt broth and pounded into the form of a plaster are effective when applied. Against pustules: ℞ salt broth, mix it with wine vinegar and gargle; afterward, wash the mouth with that wine, then with honey or <term>hydromel</term> <note>original: "hydromelle"; a mixture of honey and water, similar to mead</note>, and finally with water. For frostbitten limbs and soles of the feet, wash with salt broth; afterward, cook lentils with salt broth, mix them together with bread crusts or crumbs and a sufficient amount of rose oil to make a plaster to be applied. If one eats raw coriander, let them drink a fresh egg well shaken in a vial with salt broth while warm; this removes the poison. Likewise, it reduces the pains caused by <term>excessive milk</term> <note>original: "superfluo lacte"; likely referring to breast engorgement in nursing mothers</note> in this way: let lentils be boiled very well in salt broth; use this broth to foment the breasts, then pound and grind the lentils and apply them twice a day as a plaster. Salt broth from olives also heals pustules, and after <term>gangrene</term> has been removed and the mouth rinsed frequently with the same broth, it cures rot of the mouth. By rinsing the mouth and swollen gums, it consumes fleshy growths.

Likewise, it stops wounds that are dripping with blood. If a <term>hernia</term> <note>original: "ramice"</note> or a bladder stone has been removed, pour in oxalma immediately. Use oxalma when a <term>rupture of the eye</term> <note>original: "monoculo"; literally "one-eyed," but here likely referring to an ocular injury where the eye has protruded or been damaged</note> occurs. Also use it against rotting wounds. ## ON SAL AMMONIAC.

The <term>broth of sal ammoniac</term> <note>original: "Salis armoniaci brodium"; an aqueous solution of ammonium chloride, used here as a medicinal liquid</note> when swallowed heals dysentery and <term>griping pains</term> <note>original: "tormina"; acute, twisting abdominal pain</note> caused by a cold nature; it purges through warm application, relaxes the bowels when drunk, but when used in <term>clysters</term> <note>original: "clysteribus"; an enema</note> it binds them. When swallowed frequently by those with <term>dropsy</term> <note>original: "hydropicis"; swelling caused by excess fluid</note> and those burdened by <term>cold phlegm</term> <note>original: "frigida pituita"; in humoral medicine, phlegm was considered a cold, moist humor that caused sluggishness when in excess</note>, it not only purges the phlegm and water but also consumes them. The same water, drunk and gargled, brings out leeches and all kinds of worms from the throat and mouth, having killed them. The same gargle raises the <term>uvula</term> <note>the fleshy lobe at the back of the throat</note> and reduces it when it is swollen. It also kills <term>impetigo</term> <note>a contagious skin infection</note>, and heals <term>whitlows</term> <note>original: "panaritium"; a painful infection of the fingertip</note> by washing and rubbing; it treats ulcers and decay of the mouth by gargling. It treats stones of the kidneys and bladder by drinking, paralysis caused by cold, <term>erysipelas</term> <note>original: "Erisypelas"; a bacterial skin infection</note>, gout, and spasms. It strengthens all limbs and the nerves from which gout arises. It cleanses the <term>womb</term> <note>original: "Matricem"</note> and soothes pains caused by coldness, as well as swelling of the private parts arising from cold and moisture, and swelling of the whole body and feet; likewise, it relieves headache.

### ADDITION.

<margin>The sublimation of sal ammoniac.</margin>
Sublimate <term>sal ammoniac</term> <note>ammonium chloride</note> once with common salt, and twice by itself. After it has been כך sublimated, if this sal ammoniac is thrown upon a non-fusible metal, it makes it flow like wax—I mean the matter sublimated with it. — <term>B. à PORTU</term> <note>Giambattista della Porta (c. 1535–1615), a famous Italian polymath and alchemist who wrote "Magia Naturalis"</note>.

<margin>What must be observed in the taking of Niter.</margin>
It must be observed, however, how it is used according to each person's <term>complexion</term> <note>original: "complexione"; the specific balance of humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—that determined an individual’s physical and mental nature</note> or nature. For one who has a cold <term>stomach</term> <note>original: "ventriculum"</note>, it should be taken in warm or lukewarm wine with any suitable ingredients. This powder must be kept in a warm and dry place, not in a damp one, so that it remains in its full strength. Whoever is infested with a great internal burning during a time of <term>plague</term> <note>original: "pestis"</note>, or by a certain burning fever, should drink this powder mixed with sugar and good spring water, or with rose sugar, syrup, julap, and lettuce or other similar distilled waters, such as parsley or its juice, in the morning and evening or at night. He who is infested by the plague or otherwise by excessive heat should place a certain linen cloth, moistened in the said powder and mixed with vinegar and lukewarm houseleek juice, over the pulses and both sides of the heart, the neck, and also the pulses of the feet; in this way, it also stays certain burning swellings. This is the best foundation for extinguishing heat.

Those who are vexed by <term>colic</term> <note>original: "colica passione"</note> or <term>griping pains</term> <note>original: "torminibus"; sharp, cramping abdominal pains</note>, where sand and especially a <term>stone</term> <note>original: "calculus"</note> are present and dominant: they should take one <term>drachm</term> <note>a unit of weight, about 3.9 grams</note> each of this powder and well-ground cumin, and three ounces of <term>fat</term> <note>original: "adipis"; likely lard or suet</note> in a <term>sextarius</term> <note>about a pint</note> of <term>beer</term> <note>original: "cerevisiæ"</note>. ## PREPARATION OF BLACK SALT
### *against pleurisy.*

Take 5 <term>pounds</term><note>abbreviated as "lb"</note> of Salt of Niter, 1 pound of crude <term>Tartar</term><note>the potassium bitartrate crust left in wine barrels, used as a chemical reagent</note>: let them be distilled through a sixth <term>alembic</term><note>a type of still used for distillation</note>: the dose is 1 <term>scruple</term><note>represented by the symbol ℈; a unit of weight equal to 1/24th of an ounce</note> up to 1 and a half scruples; it should be administered in good spring water or the best wine, in the morning, around noon, in the evening, and around midnight; for it must be administered frequently so that the urine may be purged. **Addition.** Take 2 <term>ounces</term><note>represented by the symbol ℥</note> of this, 5 scruples of <term>Aqua Regis</term><note>literally "Royal Water," a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids known for its ability to dissolve gold</note>, 5 ounces of dried spirit of wine <note>original: "Alcool vini exiccati"</note>: let a mixture be made, the dose is from 5 scruples to 1 ounce. **For cavernous ulcers, a preparation of the same.** Take 5 pounds of niter-alum, 2 pounds of spring water: let them be distilled into a water. **Addition:** Take 5 pounds each of plantain water, <term>celandine</term><note>a herb in the poppy family used in folk medicine</note>, and oak leaves; 1 scruple is given in warm wine for pleurisy.

## THE COMPOSITION OF THE TRAVELERS' SALT, WHICH
### *strengthens the stomach, aids digestion, and preserves from putrefaction.*

<margin>So that no one vomits at sea.</margin>
Take 1 ounce each of salt of niter, <term>sal fulsi</term><note>likely a variant of "sal fusile" or cast salt</note>, and <term>salt gem</term><note>rock salt or halite</note>. Take 1 scruple each of <term>galangal</term><note>a root similar to ginger</note>, <term>mace</term><note>the reddish outer covering of the nutmeg seed</note>, and <term>cubebs</term><note>a species of pepper</note>: make a powder: the dose is 4 grains, in the morning on an empty stomach. Whosoever shall have used this salt while sailing upon the sea shall not vomit.

***

### THE PREPARATION OF THE
### *Travelers' Salt.*

Take 3 ounces of this salt and 5 pounds of dried spirit of wine: let the <term>Alkali salt</term><note>a basic salt extracted from plant ashes or minerals</note> be extracted; take 2 ounces of this, 1 measure of the liquor of juniper berries: reduce it into a compound: the dose is one grain in the best wine; nothing else should be added, otherwise it loses the virtue of the salt. This is its preparation in addition, which <term>Hermes</term><note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> held in the highest esteem for the conservation of a long life.

If the patient is of a moist temperament, let it be given with plantain water or <term>shepherd’s purse</term><note>original: "bursæ pastoris," a common herb used to stop bleeding</note> along with a little <term>diarrhodon</term><note>a traditional Greco-Roman medicinal powder made primarily of roses</note>. Against <term>knotted joints</term><note>likely referring to gouty tophei or arthritic swellings</note>, drink it with <term>Malmsey wine</term><note>original: "vino malvatico," a sweet, potent Mediterranean wine</note>, though it is often more effective during bathing or when applied with a cloth on the affected area. It heals <term>dropsy</term><note>edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</note> when its water is taken continuously, and it benefits paralyzed or weakened limbs if it is rubbed on with <term>ox gall</term><note>the bile of an ox, used historically in topical ointments</note>. It expels <term>stones</term><note>kidney or bladder stones</note> and opens blockages when taken with radish water and <term>sea-holly</term><note>original: "tribuli marini," the sea thistle</note>. A small amount of it drunk with a tiny quantity of roses restores lost speech.

It is suitable for a painful stomach when taken with good wine, Malmsey, or <term>wormwood water</term><note>original: "aqua absynthij"</note>; however, nothing should be eaten for three or four hours after, and nothing should be drunk before sleep. It is also used for difficulty in urination and for fevers during the plague, when five ounces of "cold" <term>diamargariton</term><note>a cordial powder made from crushed pearls, believed to have cooling properties</note> are added to <term>sorrel water</term><note>original: "aqua acetosæ"</note>. For one feeling a certain "cold" illness, give five or six drops in good wine or <term>brandy</term><note>original: "aqua ardenti," literally "burning water"</note> on an empty stomach at the break of dawn, and let him take food four hours later. Against fever, it should be continued with five ounces of rose water at dawn. A small amount of the same with Malmsey wine, continued for five or eight days, frees one from internal obstructions. It cures the "bad itch" <note>likely scabies or severe eczema</note> if drunk with <term>fumitory water</term><note>original: "aqua fumariæ"</note> and <term>preserved myrobalans</term><note>dried plum-like fruits from India used as a purgative</note>. It restores a person when taken with endive water. 

For one suffering from <term>catarrh</term><note>excessive mucus or "runny nose"</note>, let him dip a feather coated in the oil and touch the <term>uvula</term><note>the fleshy hangings at the back of the throat</note> with it, immediately withdrawing it while the patient’s head is tilted; much water will flow from the head, and at the last, a little blood, which is a sign of health.

## EXCELLENT OIL OF VITRIOL.
### *A SUPPLEMENT.*

Turn the vitriol red and make it boil in white wine until it reaches dryness. Afterward, grind it and place it in a <term>retort</term><note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note> and distill it over a slow fire. First, a clear water will come out. Then, swap the receiver and seal the joints of the vessels well; apply a very strong fire until nothing more distills. A red oil, like blood, will be distilled; it must be distilled with its <term>phlegm</term><note>the watery byproduct of distillation</note> until they become one. 

Then take an equal amount of the best <term>spirit of wine</term><note>highly distilled alcohol</note>, mix them together, and let them <term>digest</term><note>sit under gentle heat</note> in a <term>circulatory pelican</term><note>a specialized distillation flask with two side-arms that return the condensed liquid to the base, named for its resemblance to a pelican pecking its breast</note>; when it gives the sign, it is finished. Take one pound of this "circulated" liquid, the odor of which will be most fragrant. Let it digest in a sealed vessel. Give this liquor for every sickness, especially for epilepsy and apoplexy, alongside other appropriate remedies. Also for colic, continuous fever, and other desperate illnesses.

## ON ANTIMONY AND ITS POWERS.

Many doctors of medicine believe that <term>Antimony</term> <note>a metallic-looking mineral (stibnite) often used in chemical medicine as a powerful emetic and purge</note> is a poison. If it is indeed a poison, then <term>Dioscorides</term> <note>a famous Greek physician of the 1st century AD</note> did wrong when he used it in eye salves; and <term>Arnold of Villanova</term> <note>a medieval physician and alchemist</note> and <term>Nicolaus Myrepsus</term> <note>author of a 13th-century medical compendium</note> did wrong when they used it in castor-based preparations as an antidote against vertigo, paralysis, and apoplexy. Furthermore, Antonius Schneberg, in his catalog of simple medicines for the plague, teaches wrongly that it can be safely taken in small quantities when prepared in the chemical manner; and <term>Mattioli</term> <note>Pietro Andrea Mattioli, a renowned 16th-century botanist and physician</note> praises it wrongly; and the Bolognese doctors also act wrongly when they use it for <term>melancholic diseases</term> <note>conditions believed to be caused by an excess of black bile, ranging from depression to digestive issues</note>. Yet it is certain that these men were prudent, learned, and experienced in the art of healing, and they would never use anything recklessly.

<margin>Praise for the flowers of antimony.</margin>
Mattioli says that it opposes the poison of the plague; likewise, it drives away tertian, quartan, and daily fevers <note>recurring fevers often associated with malaria</note>, and it benefits those suffering from stomach and intestinal distress, for it purges the stomach of corrupt humors. Therefore, it is a health-giving medicine according to the authority of Georg Gallus of Schneeberg, the doctors of Bologna, Dioscorides, and Myrepsus. The reason is that it expels poisons. What is more excellent than the <term>flowers of antimony</term> <note>the white powder formed when antimony is heated and its vapors condense</note>? What is sweeter than its oil? What is more successful, praiseworthy, and useful than its extracted essence? The use of these is far preferable to those poisonous and crude medicines like <term>scammony</term>, <term>spurge</term>, <term>colocynth</term>, <term>turbith</term>, and <term>agaric</term> <note>all traditional, harsh herbal laxatives</note>. For this is a purgation through the bowels that cleanses a person, uprooting diseases more deeply than any other secrets, removing every impurity from the human body, and cleansing it of all ailments.

<margin>To reveal secrets to the ignorant and unskilled is to increase their audacity.</margin>
<term>Paracelsus</term> <note>the 16th-century Swiss physician who pioneered chemical medicine</note> says that if you discover this medicine—or rather, this <term>arcanum</term> <note>a powerful, secret medical mystery</note>—do not give it to any unskilled person. No one can fully list the powers hidden within it against all ailments. However, it is necessary that such preparations be made chemically, which is something those doctors do not know. When the plague comes, they flee like the <term>Levites</term> <note>a reference to the priest and Levite in the Parable of the Good Samaritan who ignored the suffering traveler</note> mentioned by Christ in the New Testament; they stand back and slander me and other good men who pass by. Truly, in this province and other places, I have cured many for whom the doctors, after holding a consultation, had despaired: namely, those suffering from <term>apoplexy</term> <note>stroke</note>, intestinal distress, plague infection, <term>epilepsy</term>, and those bent over by stiffening of the joints. Likewise, those who for four years had knobby knees and other knobby limbs, even ulcerated legs and many other defects; and furthermore, those who were wounded and pierced through; also the insane, even those who had been mad for nearly three years.

<margin>The administration of prepared antimony.</margin>
The dose of antimony is as follows: truly, at the beginning of an attack of the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>epilepsy</note>, give nine grains; after the paroxysm...

## PARACELSUS ON THE USE OF ANTIMONY.

Its tincture is used by pouring five ounces of this tincture into a barrel of fresh wine—about twenty measures—during the month of September or October. It should be allowed to <term>digest</term> <note>a process of slow maturation or steeping</note> and purify along with the wine. The patient should drink from this wine for three, four, or more weeks, completely omitting all other drinks. Meanwhile, any ulcers should be protected in passing with common <term>plasters</term> <note>medicated bandages or dressings</note>, for the tincture works sufficiently from the inside to heal the external parts.

### ADDITION.

I had intended to write an entire treatise on Antimony, but other business calls me away; however, I will briefly add some operations here.

Take Antimony and grind it; put it in a large new pot and place it upon well-lit coals. Allow it to stand there until it melts. Then take <term>salt of nitre</term> <note>original: salem nitri; potassium nitrate or saltpeter</note> and <term>crude tartar</term> <note>original: tartari crudi; the potassium bitartrate crusts found in wine barrels</note>, four ounces of each. Reduce these to a powder, mix them well, and sift them. Throw this over half a pound of fused and well-liquefied Antimony, adding it little by little and stirring with a stick. When you see it melted like water, throw it into a large quantity of common hot water and let it sit there for 24 hours. Afterward, strain it through a filter and add hot water again so that all saltiness is removed; thus, a deep red antimony will remain at the bottom. Then pour distilled vinegar over it and stir. Leave it for several days in <term>putrefaction</term> <note>here meaning a period of soaking or maceration at a gentle, steady heat</note>, filter it, and distill it three times in a <term>balneum</term> <note>a water bath or "bain-marie," used to provide gentle, indirect heat</note>, returning the vinegar to the top each time. In the bottom, you will find an oil like sweet butter. Take this essence of Antimony and place it in four times its volume of distilled vinegar. Place the closed <term>flask</term> <note>original: bociam</note> in dung <note>a standard alchemical technique where the heat of fermenting manure provided a constant, low temperature</note> for 40 days. Extract and distill it by water bath; the dissolved Antimony will remain at the bottom in the form of oil as the vinegar recedes. This oil cures cataracts of the eyes, leprosy, cancer, the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: caducum; a historical term for epilepsy</note>, and achieves much in <term>Chemical matters</term> <note>original: Chemicis; referring here to the art of alchemy and early chemistry</note>.

Through a longer circulation, it becomes a sweet and most excellent medicine to be applied both internally and externally.

## REGULUS OF ANTIMONY.
<note>In alchemy, a "regulus" is the metallic form of a mineral, purged of its "dross" or impurities. Antimony was often called the "little king" because it could purify gold.</note>

### ADDITION.

Take Antimony, <term>salt of nitre</term><note>original: salis nitri; potassium nitrate or saltpeter</note>, and <term>crude tartar</term><note>original: tartari crudi; the potassium bitartrate crusts from wine barrels</note> in equal parts as you desire. Pulverize them together, place them in a large pot among coals, and apply a slow fire around it so that the fire ignites within. Beware the force of those fumes. Stir it with a stick, and when it is well-fused, pour it into a vessel that has a pointed bottom. The dross will remain on top, but the Regulus will be at the bottom, like a metal. From this regulus, many and diverse things are made, both in medicine and in Alchemy.

If you take two parts of the Regulus and one of Mercury, and cook them with two parts of our <term>oil of vitriol</term><note>sulfuric acid</note> until it takes on the color of a lily, they produce wonders, provided you extract a tincture from them using <term>spirit of wine</term><note>highly distilled alcohol or ethanol</note>.

Likewise concerning Antimony: if crude Antimony is ground upon a marble slab with distilled vinegar, and then placed to <term>digest</term><note>the process of slow heating to encourage chemical change</note> in a well-sealed glass vessel for twenty days or more in horse dung, let it be taken out when the time is up, filtered, and the liquid drawn off by distillation. Circulate what remains with the best spirit of wine, and you will have a most deep-red tincture. I do not describe its powers here, but leave them to the <term>sons of the art</term><note>a traditional term for initiated alchemists</note>.

## THE QUINTESSENCE OF THE MARCASITE OF SATURN.
<note>Marcasite of Saturn likely refers to a lead-based mineral (as Saturn is the alchemical symbol for lead) or perhaps bismuth.</note>

### ADDITION.

This is the noblest and sweetest matter of all things that have existed; it surpasses all others by its nature (I except <term>potable gold</term><note>aurum potabile; a legendary liquid medicine made of gold</note>), though it is itself surpassed by the quintessence of our Stone, which we call the "Philosopher’s Stone" not unearnedly, but truly by its own name.

Take, therefore, the mineral mentioned above, which should be sharp, long, and glowing within; let it be crushed and sifted until it becomes an impalpable powder. Let this be soaked in the best strong wine for thirty days, and let the vessel be very well sealed. Note, however, that for every 1 pound <note>original: ℔ j.</note> of the aforesaid mineral, two measures of wine should be taken. These should be placed in the sun or in a similar heat. Afterward, let them be distilled—slowly at first, then more strongly—until the water coming forth begins to turn red. 

Then let another receiver be put in place; keep the water and allow it to settle for a long enough time in a well-closed vessel. Then, within a space of nine or ten days, something black will settle at the bottom of the glass. Take the water that was floating on top, and for every 5 ounces <note>original: ℥ v.</note> of it, take 1.5 ounces <note>original: ℥ j. ß.</note> of the root of <term>cardopacium</term><note>the Carline thistle, also known as the white chameleon</note> cut into small pieces. Let these be distilled together again. 

The other water, which is also red, requires a strong fire in the distillation so that the lid of the vessel glows white-hot; then you will see a red oil above the water, which must be separated from it. In this same way, oil of juniper is made. Both of these should be kept separately. And thus these three waters are extracted from the Marcasite of Saturn, which...

# ON MEDICINES.

contains in itself the <term>fifth essence</term><note>original: quintam essentiam; the most purified and potent form of a substance in alchemy</note>. In order for this to be extracted, the process proceeds in this way: while these three species of waters settle for a space of 30 days, you will find something earthy in the bottom of the glass, just as was done before regarding the first water. Then let the waters be strained; let the clear be separated from the turbid, the pure retained, and the others rejected. Afterward, let them be distilled in ashes at only the <term>first degree of fire</term><note>the lowest level of heat, roughly equivalent to the warmth of a brooding hen or a summer day</note> for thirty days, until the matter is coagulated and becomes a hard stone, in color similar to a pomegranate.

Let the stone be crushed and dissolved in distilled vinegar, and afterward let them be distilled. This water which comes forth in the glass should be placed over ashes at the <term>second degree of fire</term><note>a moderate heat, like a hot sand bath</note>; then you will find a red stone similar to a spinel, and this is the fifth essence of our antimony. It has not been found until now how useful this is for the human race: it heals all leprosies, all fistulas, scurvy, and finally all incurable diseases of that kind. It consumes all films and clouds over the eyes. It has a sweet flavor, not bitter, nor does it have a sharp hardness or thickness; it resembles nothing other than the color of red wine. It is a singular comfort for those with <term>dropsy</term><note>edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</note>, for it quickly consumes the dropsy if the sick person takes the quantity of a single pea of this medicine in violet water. It also heals paralysis, apoplexy, and the <term>falling sickness</term><note>original: morbum comitialem; epilepsy</note>, if it is taken with three drops of <term>potable gold</term><note>original: auri potabilis; a legendary alchemical liquid containing gold, believed to be a universal cure</note>. Lest this stone perish, it ought to be preserved in dry places and in millet seed; for if it is placed in damp places, it is corrupted within the space of four months.

## BALSAM OF ANTIMONY.

### ADDITION.

Take one part of Antimony pulverized into a <term>fine powder</term><note>original: Alcool; in early chemistry, this referred to a powder ground so fine it was impalpable, not just liquid alcohol</note>, and four parts of <term>turpentine solvent</term><note>original: menstrui Therebinthinati</note>. Mix them well, put them into a glass having a long neck, and let them be <term>digested</term><note>heated gently over a long period</note> at the second degree of fire for as long as it takes until they acquire a red color, which will happen shortly. Pour it off; pour in another new solvent. You should do this until the whole has been dissolved. Drive off the solvent by a gentle fire. What remains is like a gum, and it is extremely useful for wounds and ulcers. But if you wish to force it through a <term>retort</term><note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note>, you will have a Balsam; you may do the same with glass. I leave this to the experience of the Chemists. — **B. à PORTU**<note>likely Bernard Gilles Penot (c. 1519–1617), a famous Paracelsian physician and alchemist</note>.

### *ON OIL OF BRICKS.*
<note>Oil of Bricks (*Oleum laterinum*) was a common chemical preparation made by soaking heated bricks in olive oil and then distilling them. It was prized for its ability to "penetrate" the body.</note>

Oil of bricks is suitable for all "cold" diseases; it is hot, penetrating, and <term>resolutive</term><note>capable of dissolving or dispersing "humors" or swellings</note>. It softens hard things and disperses swellings; it helps those suffering from <term>epilepsy</term><note>original: epilepsiam</note>, vertigo, forgetfulness, paralysis, spasms, and pain in the back and knees. ### *THE QUINTESSENCE OF PEARLS is extracted in this way.*
<note>The "Quintessence" or "Fifth Essence" was considered by alchemists to be the purest, most potent medicinal core of a substance, stripped of its "gross" or physical impurities.</note>

#### ADDITION.

Pulverize the pearls and wash them in warm white wine. Then, dissolve them in the best distilled vinegar in the sun in a glass vessel very well sealed. However, the vinegar should be renewed every three days; the poured-off liquid should be carefully saved. Once all the pearls are dissolved, join the liquids and distill the vinegar; then solve it again with new vinegar as before, and distill as before, and something of the pearls will always rise. Retine and carefully guard this; you shall repeat this until nothing of the pearls remains for you.

<term>℞</term><note>Take</note>. Afterward, take all that has been distilled and add <term>half an ounce</term><note>original: ℥ ß; an ounce and a half-symbol</note> of the best camphor for every one measure of pearls. For this reduces the noble essence of the pearls so that nothing remains behind, but the entire substance of the pearls transcends through the <term>alembic</term><note>a chemical apparatus used for distilling</note>. For it has a wonderful power of <term>volatilizing</term><note>turning a solid or liquid into a vapor to be moved during distillation</note>, so to speak, the body of the pearls. Repeat the distillation once more. <term>℞</term>. Take this last distillate and place it in a heat that is not too strong but gentle; allow the vinegar to evaporate in a glass with a sufficiently wide mouth until only a twentieth part of the pearls remains. Place this in a clean glass with an alembic and distill it by itself with a slow fire. Collect only the first water that comes out; and when the drops turn yellow, apply another receiving vessel and strengthen the fire. You will see a yellowish, somewhat thick matter transcend, like honey. This is the true essence of pearls, a distinguished ornament of life.

## ON THE JEW-STONE AND THE POWERS of its salt.

## ON CRYSTAL AND ITS POWERS.

Oil of Crystals, taken as a drink in a dose of half an ounce <note>original: ℥ ß.; approximately 15 grams</note>, is a singular remedy for wearing down, crushing, and expelling stones of the kidneys and bladder, and for promoting the flow of urine. The salt of Crystals draws out the stone and, with certain additions, increases a woman's breast milk.

## ON CORALS AND THE POWER OF CORALS.

The quintessence or tincture of corals pulls out all internal ailments by the root and restores the body, by a certain heavenly power, to a temperate habit and an absolute and exquisite moderation. For it entirely removes any "comitial" disease <term>epilepsy</term> <note>original: morbum comitialem; so named because the Roman "comitia" or assemblies were dismissed if a participant had a seizure</note> or the "falling sickness" in adults and those of advanced age, within five weeks.

**Paracelsus**: Take 1 ounce of Tincture of Corals; if it is always given before the <term>paroxysm</term> <note>the sudden onset or "fit" of a disease</note>, and before the disease seizes the patient (if the onset can be perceived). Likewise, it restrains the flux of the bowels [diarrhea] arising from any cause, in children as well as adults, even if the disease has reached the very end. It also cleanses ulcers and the blood, and when applied in any manner, it restrains blood flowing from any part. It also stops the <term>menses</term> <note>original: menstrua & flores; "flowers" was a common historical term for menstruation</note> and any uterine discharges or open cases, bringing them back to a proper natural temperament; nor does it ever permit any recurring evil to remain in the rest of the body, as happens from the use of almost all other medicines. It also cures melancholy and insanity, and resists all poisons. The preparation is such: Take 2 ounces of ground corals and 1 pound of lovage water.

### ON THE PREPARATION.

Take: one ounce of coral, one ounce of myrtle oil, fifteen ounces of frankincense, and two ounces of molten salt. Mix and calcine <note>burn to ash or powder through high heat</note> by the fourth degree of reverberation <note>the highest level of heat in a furnace, where flames are reflected back onto the substance</note> for 12 hours or longer; afterwards, wash it with plantain water. The quintessence <term>quintessence: the most concentrated and pure form of a substance, believed to contain its essential medicinal power</term> of coral is made thus: Take: two ounces of coral, three ounces of ash from Roman cumin and kidney beans, and prepared alum to the weight of everything else. Mix and digest with five pounds of dried alcohol of wine for 2 or 3 days, then dry it out, and it will be entirely saffron-colored. The dose is five [units].

Simply crushed corals ward off storms <note>a common early modern belief held that coral could protect ships and homes from lightning and tempests</note>. Likewise, after a long time, they restrict urine and the bowels, as well as the menstruation of women, even without any preparation; however, prepared corals work more quickly and without danger. They are given in a soft-boiled egg in a dose of one scruple.

### USE OF THE TINCTURE.

For its administration, let half an ounce of coral tincture be mixed with ten ounces of chicory water or germander <note>original: chamedrios/gamandreæ; herbs often used for digestive and liver health</note> water. A portion of this mixture—one or two ounces—should be given to the patient to drink in the morning and evening, five hours before lunch or five hours after dinner, for six or seven successive days. Let the patient eat lighter foods, and let their drink be distilled water from fumitory <note>original: fumo terræ; literally "smoke of the earth"</note>, chicory, or similar plants, though these should be used only moderately.

### ADDITION.

Dissolve corals in radical vinegar <term>radical vinegar: a highly concentrated, potent vinegar used as a powerful chemical solvent</term>, let them stand in digestion for a month until the vinegar is tinted. Pour it off and add more until it is tinted further. Filter, evaporate, wash, dry, and circulate with spirit of wine [alcohol]. Then distill it and place it over marble; a marvelous and sweet liquor will be produced. Give 6 to 8 drops in a suitable liquid. Give thanks to God.

## ON PHILOSOPHICAL GOLD AND
->*its powers.*<-

<margin>The active power is present in every tincture.</margin>
Now we shall treat philosophical gold. All the philosophers <note>here referring to alchemists and natural philosophers</note> say that our gold is not that of the common people, but is "philosophical." For, with God the Best and Greatest giving and helping, it heals the human body without any danger or harm. I speak here not of a mere chemical imitation, but of true and natural gold, which has been prepared without any corrosive substances or poisonous waters. To such gold, great virtues must be attributed: for it is an elixir of life and drives away every contagious disease.

It is called "potable gold" <term>potable gold: *aurum potabile*; a liquid form of gold believed to be a universal medicine</term> whenever it has been reduced into a drinkable substance along with other spirits or liquids; its dose is one scruple <note>approximately 1.3 grams</note> at a time. It is "Oil of Gold" when a golden oil has been produced from its own substance alone without adding other oils; its dose should not exceed the weight of ten grains <note>about 0.6 grams</note>.

However, it is called the "Quintessence of Gold" <term>quintessence: the fifth element or purest essence extracted from a substance</term> whenever a red tincture has been drawn from it and separated from its "body" <note>the physical dross or metallic residue</note>. Indeed, the active power of any substance resides in its tincture. The dose for this Quintessence of Gold is three grains; it is mixed at various times with good *aqua vitae* <note>original: *aquæ vitæ*; "water of life," usually high-proof distilled alcohol or brandy</note> or some other highly refined water, and taken in the morning, at noon, and in the evening as the medicine requires.

When this gold or "sulfur of gold" <note>the combustible or "soul" principle of the gold</note> enters the body and is taken up by our internal balsam <note>a Paracelsian term for the body’s innate healing force</note>, it then purifies the balsam of the blood from the "smoke" of malevolent stars <note>harmful astrological influences thought to cause disease</note>. If a disease should be in any principal organ, this sulfur must be fermented into a "specific" form; otherwise, it would have no power to act upon those members. These "specifics" transmute this gold from one form into another. For the nature of the balsam in the blood is one thing, while it is another in the brain, another in the heart, and another in the spleen. A physician must know and observe all these things.

When it is administered in potable form, you shall take an amount the size of a pea and place it inside a boiled egg from which the yolk has been removed, so that the hardened part is dissolved; you shall usefully give this to the sick person to drink, for it strengthens by itself. However, everyone must diligently observe that true philosophical gold, as soon as it is dropped into wine or simple water, will gild any silver vessels or instruments it touches. If, however, it has not been prepared according to the true art, it will not gild them, but will only coat them with a dark brown blackness. The hard gold of the philosophers—that is, the "coagulated" form—in two or three grains, while vi- <note>original catchword: *dum vi-*; likely continuing "while it lives" or "while it is vigorous"</note>

<header>ON MEDICINES</header>

...while the strengths of the human body are applied or used, it produces many wonders, even in all ailments, when administered with one scruple <note>a small unit of weight, about 1.3 grams</note> of better theriac <term>theriac: a famous ancient "universal" medicine and antidote made from dozens of ingredients</term> or with certain other medicines, as any wise person will provide. Cardanus <note>Girolamo Cardano, a famous 16th-century Italian polymath</note> writes in Book 5 of *On the Subtlety of Things*: "Gold," he says, "is a truly mysterious and most perfect thing, of an equal temperament, and composed with a wonderful proportion of elemental powers, to which no mixed body can be compared: a wound made with it does not become inflamed."

The common sort of doctors, with great simplicity, quench golden chains, coins, and such like in liquid, or they attempt to make a certain decoction <note>a concentrated extract made by boiling</note> even in simple water, in some cloudy potion, in honey, in some broth or wine for the strengthening of the spirits and the principal organs: and they call that liquid in which it was quenched by the fictional name *apobamma* <note>original: "apobamma," a Greek term for a liquid in which red-hot metal has been dipped</note>. But how would it strengthen the powers of the heart, since only the filth of the handling hands, collected and adhering to those coins, is removed in this way?

Many also, persuaded by ointment-sellers <note>apothecaries or street-side pharmacists</note> and common physicians, swallow gold reduced to powder by a file, as if they truly had the stomachs of ostriches capable of digesting iron. Some people, in electuary confections <note>medicinal pastes made with honey or sugar</note> and many other medicines—such as in *Diathamaron* <note>a medicine usually containing fruit juices</note> according to the description of Nicolaus, in the *Electuary of Gems*, in the Galenic <note>referring to the system of Galen, the ancient Greek physician</note> "confections of joy" for the heart, and in the "Golden Alexandrians"—not only delight in eating it but also in eating and drinking from golden vessels.

But since anything incorruptible cannot be changed in a man’s stomach, and therefore seems unable to provide any virtue to the principal organs (as was said above); however, the "gold of the philosophers" <note>refined alchemical gold</note> and that which is philosophically prepared has innumerable virtues. It similarly heals hot and cold [imbalances] and many other diverse defects, as any learned physician will faithfully judge for himself through his own erudition. Above all, it resists epilepsy <term>epilepsy: referred to here as the "falling sickness" (*caducum*)</term> and contractures <note>the permanent tightening of muscles or joints</note>, both by preserving health and by curing.

**Against the Falling Sickness.**

For contractures, the dose of potable gold <term>potable gold: *aurum potabile*, a liquid form of gold believed by alchemists to be a universal cure</term> is 1 scruple each time. Above all, it strengthens the substance of the heart and the principle of life; it has the power both to comfort and to cheer the heart; in doses of 4 or 8 grains. For it can be very easily transferred through the mesenteric veins <note>original: *venas mesaraicas*; the veins draining the intestines</note> to the liver, then to the heart, and from there through the entire body. Furthermore, it dries up the superfluity of all other dregs from the substance of the heart, illuminates the spirits with its own brightness, strengthens them with its solidity, and by its own temperament balances the blood. It preserves against rot, cleansing the blood, and by its own weight causes superfluities to move toward the parts of expulsion <note>aiding the body's natural waste removal</note>. It tames melancholy and mania: it restores exhausted powers and spirits. Youth...

### ADDITION

A true description of diaphoretic gold <term>diaphoretic gold: a preparation of gold designed to induce sweating as a means of purging the body of disease</term>. Make an amalgam of Sun <note>original: "Sole," the alchemical name for gold</note> and Mercury, and mix it with the powder of flowers of Sulfur, the weight of which should be triple that of the amalgam. Place all these together in a strong dish over a small heat for one hour. Afterward, ignite the Sulfur so that it is entirely burned away, and you will find your gold to be very spongy. You shall pulverize this carefully upon a marble slab, and while grinding, sprinkle this powder with highly rectified aqua vitae <term>aqua vitae: literally "water of life," referring to concentrated distilled alcohol</term>. When you have mixed it well, set fire to the aqua vitae so that it all blazes up, and thus you will find the gold calcined <note>reduced to a fine powder through heat</note>; you should do this three times. Grind it again upon the marble and add a little honey and prepared common salt. Afterward, place it into an earthen dish, pour in hot water, and stir it; let it rest for a while, then filter and wash it until no more honey or salt remains, and it will be so fine that you can write with it. Then you shall incorporate it with triple its weight of oil of tartar, dry it, and place it in the fire until it becomes red-hot. Afterward, place it upon the marble, and the Sun [gold] along with the salt will be dissolved into a deep red color. If it does not dissolve the first time, you must repeat the process for the portion that remains undissolved. Place this oil in a matrass <note>a long-necked glass flask used for distillation or digestion</note> with the best aqua vitae, and place it in a bath <note>a water bath or "bain-marie"</note> for eight days, and for another eight in hot ashes, and you will find your oil to be red like a ruby. Afterward, draw off the aqua vitae through a filter so that the salt of tartar is separated. Wash it frequently with aqua vitae and ignite it; keep the oil that remains for use. 

The virtues of this potable gold <term>potable gold: "aurum potabile," a legendary alchemical medicine thought to be a universal cure</term> are so great that I can hardly count them. First, in the greatest pains of the stone <note>original: "calculi," referring to kidney or bladder stones</note>, by drinking 5 or 6 drops with white wine or some suitable medicinal water, it immediately soothes the pains; and after one hour, it dissolves the stone and casts it out. In the plague, when the heart is laboring greatly, it repels the pestilential poison. Against all kinds of poison, it is a most excellent remedy; it cures apoplexy <note>a sudden loss of consciousness or a stroke</note>, restoring a person to their former health in a short time. It heals cancer and cures all ulcers and internal abscesses; it is a remedy against all desperate diseases abandoned by physicians, provided that the vital moisture <note>original: "humidum," referring to the "radical moisture" or the essential life-force of a person</note> in the man has not been completely extinguished.

### *PARACELSUS ON GOUT.*

In the beginning, let the gout sufferer be purged with a full and perfect cleansing. Treat him with the **coralline arcanum** <term>arcanum corallino: A "secret" alchemical remedy, likely a red mercurial or coral-based preparation</term>, that is, with the color separated and abstracted from the substance by the spirit of wine. Through its intervention, the "flows" of gout are drawn out, so that no further place is left for the disease. In this coralline secret, which is derived from the essence of gold, there is such great power and virtue that it is impossible for a physician to grasp it unless this purging is performed first. This purging should be done six or seven times, depending on the age, severity, or nature of the gout. Paracelsus, by means of the **quintessence of the sun** <note>The "quintessence of the sun" refers to the purified essence of gold.</note> and its oil, removes leprosy along with all other diseases; it renews and restores the body. Furthermore, it strengthens the sight and makes it clear. 

Potable gold should be taken in electuaries <note>A medicinal paste made by mixing powders with honey or syrup.</note>, or against the "universal disease"—also called the Spanish disease <note>original: "morbum catholicum, seu Hispanicum," referring to syphilis.</note>—using 8 grains in wine, or one drachm <note>original: "ʒ j."</note> of theriac water <term>theriac: A legendary herbal concoction used as a universal antidote.</term> in the morning on an empty stomach for 10 continuous days. For it is a diaphoretic <note>A medicine that induces sweating.</note> medicine, purging away superfluous sweats and all harmful humors of the entire body. It is conducive for those with consumption <note>original: "phthisicis," or tuberculosis.</note>, chronic fevers, spleen disorders, and for those with cancerous, devouring, lupous, or fistulous ulcers. It preserves the entire human body from putrefaction and decay until the day destined by the most high God. 

Indeed, it is even able to cure any new symptoms of disease that emerge or arise from the ointments and fumigations of "living gold" <note>original: "auri vivi," often meaning quicksilver or mercury in this context.</note> or common mercury, as well as from precipitates, sublimates, cinnabar, and other absurd medicines of the unskilled (who offer or hand out lethal poison instead of a remedy). 

The dose of precipitated gold is half a denarius weight for younger people, and a full denarius weight <note>A "denarius" here refers to a specific medicinal weight, roughly equivalent to a scruple or about 1.3 grams.</note> for adults. It cures the plague when taken with theriac, and it drives away "water under the skin" <note>A form of dropsy.</note>, elephantiasis, and other diseases difficult to cure, and it unlocks obstructions of the internal organs. It helps those who have swallowed poison. Likewise, it is taken internally for curing malignant ulcers in the "French disease" <note>original: "morbo gallico," another name for syphilis.</note>. 

<term>Recipe:</term> Take one denarius of precipitated gold and mix it with one ounce <note>original: "℥ j."</note> of electuary of rose juice. Also, take five scruples <note>original: "℈ v."</note> of the "species of gems" <note>A medicinal powder made from ground precious stones.</note>. Mix them together and let it be given as is customary; let it be taken two, three, or four times. It promises that the plague will be extirpated in a short time. Then, for external use, it is successfully mixed into purging ointments and plasters to treat filthy and cavernous ulcers—though not the "creeping" <note>original: "serpentia," likely referring to spreading skin infections like shingles or erysipelas.</note> kind.

The administration and use of the **tincture of the sun** according to Paracelsus is as follows: 

<term>Recipe:</term> Let one drachm <note>original: "ʒ i."</note> of the tincture of the sun or gold be mixed with one ounce <note>original: "℥ i."</note> of the best Venetian theriac. Let one scruple <note>original: "℈ j."</note> of this mixture be given to the patient to drink on an empty stomach at dawn. Sweating should be commanded and encouraged with blankets in bed. The process of this administration is to be repeated until the ulcer ejects blood, or any other bloody humor, as usually happens, perhaps by the twelfth day.

### ON THE MOON AND PHILOSOPHICAL SILVER

Philosophical silver <note>In alchemy, "the Moon" (Luna) and "Silver" are synonymous.</note> is a sweat-inducing agent <note>original: "diaphoreticum"</note> for diseases arising from inflammation of the brain, convulsion of the nerves, the "thunderstruck" disease <term>morbus attonitus: an old medical term for a stroke or apoplexy, where a patient is suddenly "struck" unconscious</term>, the Cosmopolitical or Spanish disease <note>A common early modern name for syphilis</note>, mania or insanity, and delirium. It is a singular remedy for defects and obstructions that have arisen in the liver, the spleen, or the menses. For it expels the corrupt qualities of the human body through the pores without any fear, danger, weakening, dissolution, or feebleness of strength; it comforts the principal organs <note>original: "membra principalia"</note>, the vital spirits, and restores the entire human body to its former health. Silver leaves or shavings <note>original: "ramenta"</note> are commonly mixed into the **Electuary of Gems**, Galen’s "cheering" medicines <note>remedies intended to lift the spirits and treat melancholy</note>, and the golden medicines of Alexandria to treat mania, melancholy, and to strengthen the brain itself. The "white body" and the remaining fixed silver is reduced into Mercury within a few days; it is precipitated by its own feverish heat and turns into a powder, of which 8 grains are administered against dropsy <note>edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</note>.

Finally, place it in a reverberatory furnace <note>a furnace that reflects heat onto the substance being treated</note> in the heat of the flame for 24 hours. When this is finished, grind it again and place the whole thing in a damp place, and it will dissolve into an oil. To separate the oil from the tartar, pour on enough lukewarm water, shake it together, and leave the oil to sink to the bottom. Separate the water from the tartar with a filter; the oil of the silver will remain at the bottom, which you shall wash until the water no longer tastes of tartar. ### ADDITION.

If you layer iron plates layer upon layer with pumice stone and reverberate them, then extract its tincture with distilled vinegar, once the vinegar has evaporated, you will find a red salt. If you cohobate <note>to repeatedly distill a liquid over the solid remains of the previous distillation to concentrate it</note> it more often, it will become an oil of wonderful virtue.

## ON SATURN OR PHILOSOPHICAL LEAD, and its powers.

Saturn <term>Saturnus: the alchemical name for Lead</term> or philosophical lead is useful for all burns caused by fire, water, or oil. It heals hemorrhoids, restrains the growth of ulcers, and opposes cancerous and putrid ulcers, whether used by itself or mixed with other things. It heals "Persian Fire" <note>ignis Persicus: a historical name for various skin conditions, likely anthrax or shingles</note> or "Sacred Fire," as they call it, benefits those with skin eruptions <note>impetiginosis: relating to impetigo or similar scabby skin conditions</note>, fills in cavities in the flesh, and stops bleeding. Oil of Saturn or lead is dissolved in a damp place, and when mixed with oil of Turpentine, it is a most excellent medicine and a precious balsam for filling with flesh and curing any malignant and desperate wounds and ulcers in a short time and within a few days. It is also excellent for stopping ophthalmia <note>inflammation of the eye</note> accompanied by discharge and inflammation, provided that it is first very well sweetened <note>dulcoretur: likely meaning washed or neutralized of its corrosive acidity</note>. Likewise, when rubbed on convulsed or paralyzed limbs, it restores them quickly. Similarly, it dissipates tumors born from hot imbalances when mixed with chamomile and olive oils. Furthermore, it checks inflammations of any origin and any burns if a blue cloth soaked in it is applied. But for those suffering from the "colic passion" <note>severe abdominal pain</note> and other intestinal pains, 3 or 4 grains are given to drink in some liquid.

Let these things now suffice regarding the manifold powers of minerals and metals. When they are reduced to a liquid by a subtle preceding preparation, they are found to have wonderful effects; however, according to the preparation of common apothecaries and many other unskilled people, they have almost none. This is because natural heat <note>the body's digestive and metabolic heat</note> is not so powerful and strong that it can break down and transmute the Sun <term>Sol: Alchemical Gold</term>, the Moon <term>Luna: Alchemical Silver</term>, and other metals, so that, changed into blood, they can nourish the human body and strengthen the vital spirits, or be able to perform the other tasks granted to them by nature, as long as they remain in their harder substance. This is a matter for all natural philosophers and physicians alike...
