For just as a hen warms with heat and hatches her eggs, so also you should warm and perfect, both extracting and irrigating with divine waters in the sun; and in warm places roast with a gentle fire, with virgin’s milk <note>original: *lacte virgineo*; a term for a white mercurial liquid or precipitate</note>, and beware of smoke.

In the underworld <note>original: *inferno*; the bottom of the alchemical vessel where the "death" of the matter occurs</note> however, hide them, and move them cautiously, until their preparation becomes more solid and does not flee from the fire; then let it be extracted from it. When the soul and spirit are joined and become one, then cast it into the "body of the moon" <note>silver</note>, and you shall have the "sun" <note>gold</note>, which the storehouses of kings did not possess. Behold the secret of the Philosophers, for which our fathers bound us by oath not to reveal it, that it might have a divine form and operation. For it is divine, because joined with divinity, it makes divine substances, in which the spirit becomes body, and the dead are animated, receiving the spirit coming forth from them; and they are held in turn, and they hold.

Just as, on the other hand, the dark spirit, full of vanity and sadness, prevents bodies from being whitened <note>original: *dealbentur*; the *albedo* stage of purification</note>, or from receiving the beauty and color which they had from the Creator. For they are sick—both body, spirit, and soul—because of the spread darkness: but when that dark and destructive spirit is removed, so that neither the scent nor the color of darkness appears, then the body and soul are illuminated, and the spirit rejoices when the blackness is absent from the body, and the soul calls the illuminated body...

Taking <term>sandarac</term> <note>Realgar, a bright orange-red arsenic sulfide mineral</note>, <term>calcanthum</term> <note>Blue vitriol or copper sulfate</note>, arsenic, <term>native sulfur</term> <note>original: *sulphur vivum*; natural, unrefined sulfur</note>, and cinnabar, grind them all together. Making a sticky mixture, cast it into a clean, narrow-necked glass vessel and block the opening with clay. Heat it for a day with a fanned fire; afterward, removing the clay lute, you will find a dry material with a thickness similar to pitch. Grinding this again, store it in an earthen vessel, and place the whole thing in the fire; when the lid is removed, you will find it has turned yellow, and so on. Indeed, if you take white <term>magnesia</term> <note>In alchemy, this often refers to a primitive form of manganese or a "materia prima" rather than modern magnesium</note> and an equal weight of very well-prepared sand, and afterward grind both together and cook them in radish oil, you will have that which serves as gold in the furnaces.

But if it should not be shining in color, let the things mentioned above be rubbed with salt, and let them be ground with <term>mysy</term> <note>A yellowish mineral, likely a basic copper or iron sulfate</note> and <term>saffron of iron</term> <note>original: *ferri croco*; iron oxide or rust used for its red pigment</note>. With these things communicating their powers, you will produce a gold more radiant than the golden sands of the <term>Pactolus</term> <note>A river in Lydia (modern Turkey) famous in antiquity for the gold dust found in its waters</note>. 

If you already have gold and wish to double its weight without losing any of its quality, take medicine weighed out to twice the amount. Mix filings of mysy and <term>beryl</term> <note>original: *berilli*; possibly referring to a crystalline mineral used as a flux</note> so that there is four times the amount of the gold; when these two are combined and mixed or tempered, join them to the gold. When you have cast these into a crucible and made them white-hot, draw them out, and you will find yourself twice as rich. 

But our purpose was not to discuss the polishing or the increasing of gold, but rather its making. I shall therefore provide this, even though my discourse has digressed slightly to look at these other arts in passing.

Therefore, cinnabar and the "golden flower of copper" <note>original: *aureus flos aeris*; likely copper scales or copper oxide formed by heating</note>, acting as natural forms cast into "lunar matter" <note>In alchemy, "luna" or lunar matter refers to silver</note>, create a golden body. If, therefore, you temper the medicines by mixing them while melting silver, "luna" will be made for you; and if you follow such a path, you will find the color and the silver turned into gold for every use of gold. And silver indeed makes gold, but the "sun" <note>Gold</note> does not make silver; for the sun alone possesses light from within, and it serves not only the moon, but even the great light.

It was perhaps when Paris had seen such a Venus that he preferred her over Juno and Pallas.

Devise something of this kind for me also—not stirring the air, nor lifting me on high, but by some reason show me the "super-celestial good" upon the earth: for it is nowhere, yet everywhere, and in any part of the universe. The discovery is hidden from many, and that which is within us, we seekers look for wandering in the heavens. But teach me how it is near, and how it is farther away—not distant in place, but approaching nearer in disposition, that which is farther off. Tell me, what is the reason for the defense of the intellect? Then, descending to such a point, how does it ascend again? In short, lead me by the hand to God. ## A SUMMARY DECLARATION OF THOSE THINGS,
### *which have been said thus far from Democritus, through enigmas.*

What does it mean to despoil, to humble, to corrupt, to dissolve, and to <term>mortify</term> <note>original: *mortificare*; in alchemy, the "killing" or chemical breakdown of a substance to its base components to prepare it for transformation</note>, and to extract all matter, so that while the spirit broods and reveals, that which has the power of <term>tinting</term> <note>original: *tingendi*; the power of the alchemical "tincture" to change the nature and color of a base metal into gold</note> the body might be known? Let the response be suited to the perfection of the quest. For this is prompt and fit for a perfect completion: by ascending from speculations that fall under the senses to those which are perceived by the intellect alone, and by gazing upon the great celestial ornament. 

When you have contemplated the beauty of these things, raising your mind above all things, and considering the great and sufficiently shining glory of the angels, and such great joy, do not turn back thereafter to the material notion of this humble and abject science of making gold, which has now been revealed; but raise yourself entirely to higher things. Lifting the wings of the mind to the splendor of the supernal substances, gazing upon their innumerable and arduous beauties with intent and internal eyes, wondering, and laying aside all works in the world, contemplate in your mind an <term>elected death before its time</term> <note>original: *electam ante tempus mortem*; a spiritual or ascetic practice of dying to worldly desires to achieve union with the divine</note>, and mortifying your body with you. Moreover, indeed, denying your own soul, glorifying and praising the King of all and the Lord of glory with clear hymns, and struck with trembling and fear, contemplate the omnipotent power in your mind, and His goodness, which surpasses all goodness, and how all things were produced through His unutterable wisdom. 

The tongue grows numb, the mind also cannot bear, or thoroughly investigate, or recount, what great works of the Almighty God are truly stored up for the contemplating mind. Considering all these things within ourselves, let us also strive so that with all people, like brothers through faith and delight, we may be united, and assimilated, as much as possible, to the Word of God who loved us. ...that we may be filled with grace <note>original: *gratia*; completing the word from the previous page</note>, and with the light of that wisdom which illustrates all nature and illuminates every mind. To Him be praise forever.

These things the Patriarch Xiphilinus <note>John VIII Xiphilinus, an 11th-century Patriarch of Constantinople known for his interest in law and scholarship</note> wrote to Michael Psellus <note>A prolific Byzantine monk, philosopher, and historian (c. 1017–1078) who wrote extensively on alchemy and the occult</note>, who, returning the favor, says: Take one part of **chrysolite** <note>original: *chrysolithi*; here referring to yellow arsenic or orpiment rather than the modern gemstone</note>, and three parts of the **magnesia of cinnabar**; grind them together until the substances are joined and mixed, and no more "living sulfur" <note>original: *sulphuris vivi*; native or unrefined sulfur</note> appears. For it becomes very black, like writing ink; after three days, casting it into a bath, pour in an equal portion of the liquid that is accustomed to washing, and wash away every tincture that is released, etc.

**Chrysolite** is arsenic, as you know, or the "aethesian stone." The **magnesia of cinnabar** is <term>chalcopyrite</term> <note>a copper iron sulfide mineral</note>, and is also called lead. The "liquid of the bath" is the <term>radical vinegar</term> <note>highly concentrated or "rooted" vinegar</note> of our radish root, with its own salt, drawn from it through <term>cohobation</term> <note>the process of repeatedly distilling a liquid over the solid matter left behind to increase its potency</note> into a dissolving agent. Wash it, he says, until its rust <note>original: *rubigo*</note> comes out, and thus nothing of the copper remains in the lead. This is the "great solution" through evacuation, <term>aerugination</term> <note>the process of turning metal into a green rust or verdigris</note>, blackening, washing, etc. Proceed as you know. Taking the mentioned evacuation, leave it to settle in vessels, and pressing out the liquid, dry that which subsides; you will find this to be like writing ink, which you must grind until it becomes perfectly yellow, or white first. In this manner, let it be ground by drying with a continuous fire until it whitens and becomes the most brilliant white. See to it, therefore, that you do not grow weary during the time of whitening; for negligence happens because that beauty is not yet seen. Since through this whitening the copper becomes "without shadow," casting away all its earthly superfluity and thickness. If, therefore, the copper is whitened, it becomes spiritual, and finally nothing is left behind, nothing is lacking, except for the rising of the mist and the water. Zozimus <note>Zosimos of Panopolis, a 3rd-century Greco-Egyptian alchemist and one of the earliest known practitioners</note> says: I know one order having two works: first, that it flows through the resin (understand this as the purgatory); second, that the moisture of <term>Saturn</term> <note>the alchemical name for lead</note> is dried out through a rising into a light powder. 

Therefore, place an equal part of the "light stone" with the purified material, and grind it by washing and evacuating with vinegar extracted through an <term>alembic</term> <note>a chemical apparatus used for distillation, consisting of two retorts connected by a tube</note>, until it whitens, until it becomes brilliant white. See to it, therefore, during the time of whitening, as mentioned above, etc. Thus sweetening the medicine and drying it, set it aside, and balance the medicine: three parts of **Calcanthum** <note>copper sulfate or "blue vitriol"</note>, one part of magnesia, and another part of the medicine; grind them together, moistening them in the sun with white vinegar for six days, and afterward, drying it, place it in cow dung <note>a traditional alchemical method for providing a gentle, steady heat for "digestion"</note>, and allow them to be "burned" for two or three days. Removing it from the heat, you will find gold tinted like blood: this is the **Cinnabar of the Philosophers**, and a clear yellow copper. Why do you (says the Senior) <note>likely referring to "Senior Zadith," an influential figure in Latin alchemical texts</note> occupy yourselves with a forest of many things?
